New read-only management route `GET /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/run-chain` (handler in plugin `api.rs`) and CLI subcommand `harvest workflow run-chain <exec_id> [--json]` return `{ head_unknown, workflow_id, runs: [{ exec_id, run_id, sequence, state, started_at, completed_at, outcome, continued_to_exec_id }] }` — `sequence` is zero-based over the ordered chain and `continued_to_exec_id` is `null` for the tail (AC2). **Additive back-link, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, zero replay-determinism impact**: two nullable columns on `harvest_workflow_executions` — `continued_from_exec_id` (immediate predecessor) and `first_exec_id` (chain origin) — are stamped at the existing `persist_workflow_continue_as_new` successor-insert site; migration `20260710000002_harvest_workflow_continue_chain` is additive/nullable only, with partial indexes on both columns. **Design decisions**: (1) the dual-column back-link records both the immediate predecessor and the chain origin, so `first_exec_id` gives O(1) head resolution and a single indexed query (`WHERE id = head OR first_exec_id = head`) fetches the whole chain from any member — no per-hop history loads on a post-feature chain, hitting the p99 < 100 ms / N ≤ 100 success metric. (2) Pure core module `run_chain.rs` (`RunChainRecord`/`RunChainResponse`, `assemble_run_chain`, ordering + `head_unknown` derivation) is unit-tested without a database; ordering is bounded and cycle-safe (a `continued_from` linked-list walk with a deterministic `(started_at, exec_id)` fallback). (3) The `head_unknown` flag has a crisp rule — set when the resolved head lacks a back-link **and** participates in a continue-as-new chain **and** is not a confirmed origin (`head_lacks_backlink && head_participates_in_can && !confirmed_origin`), and additionally set when the resolved head declares a predecessor that is missing from the gathered set (e.g. a retention-pruned origin, from the correctness review). (4) **Graceful legacy degradation (AC5)**: pre-feature runs (which have no back-link columns populated) are forward-walked via the existing `WorkflowContinuedAsNew` events and the head is flagged `head_unknown: true` rather than ever returning a 500. **Shard-local by construction**: routing uses `db_conn_for_execution` (never `iter_shards`), and the legacy forward-walk reuses the held connection so the route is pool-size-1-safe (the #601 F4 precedent). The route is registered read-only across all four parallel plugin registries (`management_api_routes()`, request-fields, response-fields) plus `docs/api-contract.json` and the three `audit.rs` route lists (`CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` ReadOnly / `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` `None` / `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`), with a `contract_regression` pin test guarding the classification. **No mutation, no task claims, no `WorkflowEvent` appended, no macro impact.** Out of scope (per issue): parent→child spawn lineage (#621), reset-fork tree branching (#148/#538), cross-shard fan-out, merging chain event histories, and Vantage UI chain navigation. Tests: 14 pure `run_chain` unit tests (four canonical cases plus ordering/sequence/serialization/pruned-origin), 6 plugin integration scenarios in `run_chain_integration.rs` (404 + JSON body, 400 malformed id, 4-run chain resolved from head/middle/tail, standalone single run, legacy `head_unknown`, partial-shard) — compile-checked in this sandbox (no Docker) and executed by CI under Postgres, per the repo's #543/#544/#601 precedent — plus CLI mapping, contract-coverage, and contract-regression pin tests. Local CI mirror green (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, 1264 no-default-features + 1659 all-features lib + 442 plugin lib + 271 CLI + 18 contract_regression); testcontainers/HTTP tests compile-checked only where Docker is unavailable. **Review hardening (post-review):** (1) `head_unknown`/`continued_to_exec_id` no longer synthesize a false continuation across a retention gap — per-execution legal hold (#747) can delete a *middle* run while a held head and tail survive, so a direct head→tail `continued_to` link is no longer fabricated across the hole and `head_unknown=true` is flagged on **any** gathered row whose `continued_from_exec_id` names a predecessor missing from the gathered set. (2) Legacy (pre-feature) chains queried from the tail or a middle run — which carry no back-link columns — reconstruct from the tail via shared `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` plus `WorkflowContinuedAsNew`-event linkage (id-reuse-safe by construction: a run sharing the `workflow_id` but pointing at a different successor is excluded; bounded by `MAX_LEGACY_CANDIDATES`, else served best-effort with `head_unknown=true`), and the candidate scan is scoped to the queried row's `shard_id` so a shared-physical-database topology never pulls another logical shard's same-id rows into the walk (shard-local by construction). Post-feature origins keep the cheap single-query fast path. (3) A non-partial `(workflow_name, workflow_id, shard_id)` index `idx_harvest_wfx_workflow_identity` backs that candidate scan — the pre-existing pair index is partial and excludes terminal `CONTINUED_AS_NEW` predecessors, exactly the rows the reconstruction needs. (4) The two additive nullable columns are `continued_from_exec_id` (immediate predecessor) and `first_exec_id` (chain origin). (5) The testcontainers `run_chain_integration` suite was wired into `ci.yml` — added to the plugin `--no-run` compile allowlist and given a dedicated Docker-backed Linux run step, mirroring the `timeline_integration` (#739) sibling.
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): Cancellable / renewable durable timers — see issue #768. Author-controlled durable timers that can be **cancelled** and **reset** (re-armed) without leaving orphaned firings — the missing complement to the fire-once `ctx.timer`/`ctx.sleep_until` primitives, for idle-session timeouts and sliding-window debounces. New `WorkflowContext::start_timer(id, secs) -> TimerHandle<'_>` arms a durable timer via a **non-suspending bookkeeping command** (returns immediately, does not park the coroutine); `TimerHandle` exposes `cancel()`, `reset(secs)`, and `await_fire() -> HarvestResult<TimerOutcome>` (`TimerOutcome::{Fired, Cancelled}`). `ctx.cancel_timer(id)` / `ctx.reset_timer(id, secs)` are the untyped equivalents. `TimerHandle`/`TimerOutcome` re-exported from `lib.rs` and the prelude. **Design (Option C — bookkeeping arm, non-suspending):** the worker has no mixed-batch suspension (`handle_suspended_workflow` only recognizes single-shape batches), so a suspending arm could never be cancelled in-flight. Arm/cancel/reset are modelled as **bookkeeping commands** (`WorkflowCommand::ArmTimer`/`CancelTimer`, no `result_tx`), exactly like `CancelRaceLosers`/`RecordMarker`. The durable side runs in **two phases** inside the persist transaction at every persist site (sibling of `apply_race_loser_cancellations`): `worker::plan_timer_lifecycle` performs the `harvest_timers` row mutations (`ArmTimer` upserts the row and resolves a `TimerStarted` only when newly created — dedup, incl. within one batch, mirrors `persist_started_timer`; `CancelTimer` deletes the pending `fired = false` row via `queue::delete_pending_timer` and resolves `TimerCancelled`) and returns the resolved events **aligned to command indices** plus the minimum armed `fires_at`; `worker::build_suspension_events` then **interleaves** those `TimerStarted`/`TimerCancelled` events into the single suspension event batch at their `ArmTimer`/`CancelTimer` command-emission positions — exactly like `ChildWorkflowSpawnedDetached` — so `replay`'s strictly positional `match_timer_arm` sees the same order the live cycle emitted. (An earlier revision appended timer-lifecycle events at the *end* of the batch, which nd-blocked a `start_timer` + `side_effect`/`new_uuid`/`system_now` same-cycle run on first resume, since `drain_early_signals` does not skip `SideEffectRecorded`/`MarkerRecorded` and the cursor landed on them ahead of the positional timer-arm match.) A bookkeeping-only batch that armed a timer reschedules the workflow task to the armed `fires_at` (via `persist_bookkeeping_and_requeue_workflow`) so the armed timer actually wakes the workflow — unless a wake raced the park (`had_wake_requested`), in which case the task is woken now rather than deferred to the deadline. `await_fire` observes the outcome by re-arming idempotently (the durable row is deduped by `timer_id`) and parking (`park_until_dropped`); the next cycle resolves `Fired`/`Cancelled` by recorded-history order. On a **terminal cycle** an `ArmTimer` **skips only the `harvest_timers` row insert** but **still emits the `TimerStarted` event** at the `ArmTimer` command's position (via the pure `worker::terminal_arm_timer_events`), so a `start_timer`/`reset` that arms a timer and then completes in the **same** task replays deterministically. **One new `WorkflowEvent` variant** — `TimerCancelled { timer_id }`, appended at the END of the enum; adjacently-tagged serde is automatic, and pre-#768 histories deserialize unchanged. **No migration** — the `harvest_timers` row deletion is the fire-suppression mechanism, and `delete_pending_timer` (filtering `fired = false`) already existed and is race-safe; recorded-history order (`TimerFired` vs `TimerCancelled`) decides the observed outcome (AC3). **Replay (`replay.rs`):** new `match_timer_arm(id, dur)` (positional, consumes `TimerStarted` like a marker), `match_timer_cancel(id)` (forward-scan claim of `TimerCancelled`), and `match_timer_or_cancel(id) -> TimerFireMatch { Fired, Cancelled, NoMatch }`; `TimerCancelled` is a command-bearing event that can interleave into unrelated scans, so a **transparent, non-consuming** skip-arm was added to every forward scan that could step over it (`scan_activity_terminal`, `match_timer_strict`, `match_signal_or_timer`, `is_timer_started_next`, `match_signal`, `match_external_cancel`, `peek_u64_marker`, `match_saga_marker`) — leaving the event claimable by its own matcher. `TimerFireMatch` re-exported from `lib.rs`. **Non-determinism classification:** new `NonDeterminismKind::TimerCancelMismatch` (`testing.rs`) — an unconsumed `TimerCancelled` is classified precisely; a renamed timer id surfaces as the ordinary `TimerMismatch`. **Test harness (`WorkflowTestEnv`):** `ArmTimer` records `TimerStarted` + defers a `TimerFired` (idempotent re-arm no-ops); `CancelTimer` records `TimerCancelled` and retain-filters the deferred fire — so both branches are driven deterministically with no real sleep. **No worker-suspension-shape change** (arm/cancel are bookkeeping added to every `extract_*`/predicate ignore-list; `await_fire` parks with an idempotent re-arm, routed through the existing `only_bookkeeping_commands` → `persist_bookkeeping_and_requeue_workflow` path). Example `autumn-harvest/examples/cancellable_timer_sla.rs`. **Composition note:** composing an armed handle with a signal wait in one `select!`-style call is a documented follow-up — use `ctx.receive_signal_timeout` (#476) for the two-branch signal-or-deadline shape today. **Post-review hardening (Codex, PR #1010) — one P1 + three P2s (reset-interleaving / terminal-cycle family):** **P1 (worker.rs terminal persist)** the initial FINDING-6 cut passed `skip_arm_inserts = true` to `plan_timer_lifecycle`, dropping the `ArmTimer` **entirely** — a workflow that armed a timer and completed in the same task committed a terminal history with **no** `TimerStarted`, diverging strict replay; fixed by splitting the two effects (skip only the row insert, still emit the event via the pure, unit-tested `worker::terminal_arm_timer_events`). **P2 (match_timer_strict)** the `ctx.timer` fire scan skipped an interleaved `TimerCancelled` but stopped on the reset's paired `TimerStarted` → `TimerStarted` added to the transparent skip branch. **P2 (match_signal)** a `wait_for_signal` polled before a same-cycle `reset()` stopped on the re-arm → `TimerStarted` added to the transparent branch. **P2 (reset.rs `apply_event_to_pending`)** the pending-side-effect scan inserted on `TimerStarted` and closed only on `TimerFired` → a `TimerCancelled` now closes the pending arm. **Symmetry audit:** every forward-scan loop transparent to an interleaved `TimerCancelled` must also be transparent to the reset's paired `TimerStarted`; `scan_activity_terminal`/`peek_u64_marker`/`match_external_cancel`/`ctx.race()` scan already handled both; `match_timer_strict`/`match_signal` fixed; `match_saga_marker` got `TimerStarted` added; `scan_local_activity_terminal` got both added (closing the same class for a reset interleaved with a *retrying local activity*); `match_timer_or_cancel`/`match_child_workflow` already transparent; `is_timer_started_next` legitimately stops at `TimerStarted`. **Round 2 (Codex 3× P2):** **(context.rs `await_timer_fire`)** same-cycle cancel-then-await re-armed a cancelled timer — fixed with a per-context logical timer-lifecycle map (`cancellable_timer_state: HashMap<timer_id, Armed|Cancelled>`): `await_fire` consults recorded history first (`match_timer_or_cancel`) and only on `NoMatch` falls back to the logical state, resolving `Cancelled` without re-arming. **(testing.rs)** an armed timer fired during a mixed non-timer suspension — fixed by gating the deferred `TimerFired` on a new `is_competing_suspension` check. **(worker.rs history hard-cap preflight)** timer-lifecycle events uncounted near `event_hard_cap` — fixed with the new pure `worker::timer_lifecycle_event_count` folded into `pre_suspension_event_count`. **Round 3 (Codex 2× P2):** **(context.rs `start_timer`)** a duplicate ACTIVE `start_timer` diverged on replay — fixed by making a duplicate arm of an already-`Armed` id a true idempotent no-op (no second `match_timer_arm`, no second `ArmTimer`); new helper `timer_logically_armed`. **(testing.rs)** an already-armed timer never fired on a later bookkeeping-only `await_fire` — fixed by splitting the `already_armed` guard so an `ArmTimer` for a timer already active in *history* fires on a bookkeeping-only batch. **Round 4 (Codex 2× P2) + semantic clarification** — a cancellable timer's deadline is now measured from when it is **awaited** (`await_fire`), not from `start_timer`; arming records only `TimerStarted` and inserts no row, the row is created at `await_fire`. **(worker.rs `plan_timer_lifecycle`)** an armed-but-unawaited timer fired spuriously and broke a later `reset()`/replay — fixed by inserting the row only on the `await_fire` path via a new `for_await: bool` field on `WorkflowCommand::ArmTimer` (renamed the emission helper to `arm_timer_events`, used on all paths; the previous `skip_arm_inserts` flag subsumed and removed). **(worker.rs `persist_started_timer`)** a classic `ctx.timer` re-using a just-cancelled cancellable id could reschedule to a deleted row — fixed defensively by moving the classic timer's `existing`/`is_new`/`fires_at` resolution into the transaction after `plan_timer_lifecycle`. **Round 5 (Codex 2× P2):** **(context.rs `start_timer`)** a duplicate ACTIVE `start_timer` with a DIFFERENT duration silently changed the live deadline — fixed by carrying the recorded duration in `TimerLogicalState::Armed(u64)` (a duplicate active `start_timer(id, new_dur)` returns a handle preserving the RECORDED duration and ignores `new_dur`; a genuine change goes through `reset`). **(replay.rs `match_timer_or_cancel`)** the `await_fire` timer-outcome scan crossed intervening command events (replay-soundness false-negative) — fixed by making the crossable set EXPLICIT (only `is_consumed` events plus a bounded allowlist of genuinely transparent/interleaved events), STOPPING at any UNCONSUMED command-bearing event not on the allowlist. **Round 6 (Codex 2× P2):** **(replay.rs `match_timer_cancel`)** the cancel scan crossed intervening command events — fixed by sharing `match_timer_or_cancel`'s exact crossable set via the new `HistoryMatcher::timer_scan_cross_or_stop` helper; `cancel_timer`/`reset_timer` now surface the resulting `NoMatch` in strict replay via `check_strict_replay_no_match`. **(context.rs `await_timer_fire`)** the `Armed` logical state was not cleared when a fire was consumed, so a loop reusing the timer id lost its fresh arm — fixed by clearing the logical state (`clear_timer_logical_state`) on a consumed fire (the `Cancelled` path is deliberately NOT cleared). **Timer-matcher lifecycle audit** closes the scan-past-a-command class across all four timer replay matchers. **Round 7 (Codex 2× P2) + a completeness pass:** **(worker.rs `plan_timer_lifecycle`)** an `await_fire` raced by a same-task `cancel` rescheduled the parked task to a deleted row instead of waking now — fixed by excluding any id cancelled in the same batch from `min_fires_at` via the pure, unit-testable `plan_timer_lifecycle_pure(commands) -> (events_by_index, armed_indices)`. **(timeline.rs `derive_timeline`)** cancelled/reset timers were left open forever, distorting the rollup — fixed by adding a `TimerCancelled` arm that closes the OLDEST still-open step for that id as `StepOutcome::Cancelled` (FIFO-by-id pairing). **Timer-event-consumer audit (closing the class):** every consumer outside the already-fixed `replay.rs` matchers and worker persist path was checked for `TimerCancelled`-handling completeness — `replay.rs` matchers already fixed (rounds 5/6); `worker.rs` `plan_timer_lifecycle` FIX A this round; `timeline.rs` `derive_timeline` FIX B this round; `history_export.rs` already handles it (payload-field filter + human-label match); `reset.rs` `rebuild_pending` already handles it (`TimerFired | TimerCancelled` resolve identically, with a test); `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/ui.rs` `human_label` had a cosmetic gap → FIX C this round (added "Timer cancelled"); `analyzer.rs` `SuspiciousTimerRule` inspects individual `TimerStarted { duration_secs }` only (no change); `context.rs` already handles it; `testing.rs` `WorkflowTestEnv` `final_now()` sums `TimerStarted` incl. cancelled (test-harness virtual clock, deliberate — revised in round 8); `simulator.rs` never emits cancels (revised in round 14); `store.rs`/`erase.rs`/`executor.rs` are test fixtures / event-type-name only. **Round 8 (Codex 2× P2) — duration/clock accounting:** **FIX A (`context.rs await_timer_fire`)** used the awaiting handle's stale cached duration — now reads the CURRENT armed duration from the logical state map (`timer_logically_armed`) for both the live deadline and `advance_timer_clock`. **FIX B (`testing.rs` `final_now`/`elapsed`)** the virtual clock counted non-fired arms — new pure `fired_timer_duration_secs(events)` sums only `TimerStarted`s paired with a matching `TimerFired` (per id, FIFO; a `TimerCancelled` discards the earliest pending arm uncounted). **Round 9 (Codex 1× P2)** reset-then-await in one task must arm the durable row in the transaction that recorded the reset — `plan_timer_lifecycle_pure`'s contribution rule is now order-sensitive (a `for_await: true` arm for id X contributes iff the last establish/cancel op for X is not a trailing cancel), satisfying both reset-then-await and cancel-then-await shapes with one rule. **Round 10 (Codex 2× P2):** **Fix B (replay.rs)** the timer outcome/cancel scans now stop at an UNCONSUMED SAME-id `TimerStarted` — `timer_scan_cross_or_stop` is now **id-aware** (only a FOREIGN-id `TimerStarted`/`TimerCancelled` stays crossable). **Fix A (reset boundary scanner) DEFERRED pending maintainer decision** — a lazy cancellable arm records a `TimerStarted` without a durable row, yet `reset.rs::apply_event_to_pending` treats every open `TimerStarted` as unresolved; the correct history-based fix is an additive `cancellable: bool` field on `TimerStarted`, deferred (breaks ~109 exhaustive-binding sites); SAFE (refuses valid resets, never a wrong fork), left as a documented known limitation. **Round 11 (Codex 1× P2)** `plan_timer_lifecycle` contributes a firing row for a `for_await: true` arm only when no same-id `CancelTimer` follows it in the batch (forward) AND the timer is not sitting cancelled-without-reset before it (backward, round 9) — replacing round 10's end-of-batch-liveness rule, which was wrong for an `await_fire()` polled BEFORE a sibling `reset()` in the same task (armed a firing row off the stale await duration). **Round 12 (Codex 1× P2)** a blocked cancellable-timer scan (stopped at an unconsumed command with the recorded `TimerCancelled`/`TimerFired` still ahead) is now treated as a non-determinism divergence in NORMAL worker replay too (via `HistoryMatcher::timer_scan_stopped_at_command()`), not only under strict `WorkflowReplayer` mode — closing a silent-corruption path where issue #603 should have nd-blocked. **Round 13 (regression fix)** round 7 made `match_signal` skip interleaved timer events unconditionally, so a `wait_for_signal` over a history with a STRAY unconsumed `TimerStarted` and NO matching signal ran off the end and parked forever instead of nd-blocking — fixed by making `match_signal` diverge (not swallow to `NoMatch`) when the scan reaches end-of-history after crossing one or more UNCONSUMED interleaved timer/detached-spawn commands; an already-consumed reset's timers still suspend correctly. **Round 14 (Codex 2× P2):** **Fix 1 (`simulator.rs`)** `WorkflowSimulator` now handles `ArmTimer`/`CancelTimer` (previously fell through the wildcard arm → deadlock/omitted events), mirroring `WorkflowTestEnv`. **Fix 2 (`replay.rs`)** foreign (sibling) `TimerFired` is crossable in the timer outcome scan (`tokio::join!(slow.await_fire(), fast.await_fire())` no longer diverges) while a SAME-id `TimerFired` stays the target/anchor and a genuine command still stops the scan. **Command-consumer audit** re-confirmed `ArmTimer`/`CancelTimer` handling across `worker.rs`/`testing.rs`/`context.rs`/`executor.rs`; `simulator.rs` was the sole gap. **Round 15 (Codex 2× P2):** same-id collision across the two timer APIs now fails fast (was: silent event drop → replay corruption) — `WorkflowContext::timer` returns a clear `HarvestError::Config` when `timer_id` is held by a LIVE, un-cancelled cancellable timer (state `Armed`), before pushing any `StartTimer`; a defensive persist-time guard `same_batch_uncancelled_arm_start_collision` backs it. And `WorkflowTestEnv` now fires concurrent awaited timers in DEADLINE order (was: poll/command order). **Round 16 (Codex 3× P2):** **Findings 1 & 2 — comprehensive bidirectional, order-independent namespace disjointness** (enforced at the source in `WorkflowContext`): a given `timer_id` belongs to at most ONE timer API per run — `classic_timer_ids` set populated by `ctx.timer`/`sleep_until`; `start_timer(id)` records a deterministic deferred nd error (→ #603) when `id` is already a classic timer id (reverse of round 15's cancellable-first rejection), the worker backstop scans the WHOLE batch, and `cancel_timer(id)`/`reset_timer(id)` are pure NO-OPs when `id` is a classic timer id (so `delete_pending_timer` can never delete a classic `ctx.timer` row out from under its parked waiter). **Finding 3 — concurrently-armed timers advance the test clock to the MAX deadline, not the SUM** (test-harness fidelity only) — each cancellable arm records a deadline anchor (`TimerLogicalState::Armed { anchor_secs }`) and the clock advances to `anchor + duration` via a monotonic `fetch_max`; concurrently-armed timers share an anchor → MAX, sequential timers still SUM. All fixes: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration. Falsifiable success bar `reset_1000_times_replays_with_bounded_history` (1000 GENUINELY DISTINCT fixtures, every third interleaving a same-cycle `new_uuid()` side effect; plain fixtures pin 2 events/reset, interleaved 3 events/reset; all `ReplaySucceeded`, all ≤1 `TimerFired`), plus the full Armed/Cancelled logical-state matrix fixture-covered.
- **Phase 3.52** (implemented): Handler-panic containment at the dispatch boundary — see issue #782. Before, a `panic!()` in a `#[workflow]` or `#[activity]` handler body (a stray `unwrap()` on `None`, an out-of-bounds index, an arithmetic overflow) was **not** contained: the handler runs inside a fire-and-forget spawned tokio task, so the panic unwound past the DB state-transition boundary without ever reaching the completion/failure code and left the `harvest_task_queue` row stuck `RUNNING`. Because the worker *process* survives (the panic is isolated to one async task), the poison-pill reclaimer (#367) — which only reclaims rows whose worker has **no live heartbeat** — never touched it, so an un-timed workflow task could sit `RUNNING` indefinitely and the eventual operator signal (a DLQ `PoisonPill` entry / consumed `crash_strikes`) told the wrong story for an ordinary code bug. Now the panic is caught at the dispatch boundary via `catch_unwind` and routed into the engine's existing clean failure paths, the same way returning `Err` does; the worker process stays up and the task leaves `RUNNING` within one poll interval. **Activity / local-activity panic** → converted to a retryable typed `ActivityFailed` (`error_type = "HandlerPanic"`, panic message captured as the failure detail) that follows the activity's **existing retry policy**, then fails terminally — no DLQ row, `crash_strikes` never consumed. **Workflow-body panic** → caught in the executor and surfaced through a new internal `WorkflowOutcome::Failed { handler_panic }` flag into a bounded, configurable panic-retry gate in `process_workflow_task` (an in-process per-execution strike map + capped-exponential backoff); after the budget is exhausted the execution fails terminally via the existing `WorkflowFailed` event (`error_type = "HandlerPanic"`); budget `WorkerConfig::workflow_panic_max_attempts` (default **3**; `0` = terminal on first panic); #523 workflow-level retry is explicitly skipped for a panic terminal so a panicking workflow is not double-retried. **Two panic-distinct counters** for alerting on handler-panic rate separately from process-crash quarantine: `harvest.activity.panic` (labels `activity`, `queue`) and `harvest.workflow.panic` (labels `workflow`, `queue`), each getting a panel under the "Handler panics" row of `docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`, catalogued in `docs/telemetry.md` and ADR-0001 §7, and enforced by the anti-drift `dashboard_pack_docs.rs` coverage gate (`execution.id` stays span-only). **Determinism preserved**: a workflow-body panic is treated like any other workflow-task failure on replay. **Documented caveats surfaced by review:** the inline-append-before-terminal limitation is inherited from the ND-block work (#603), not introduced here (a workflow-body panic re-dispatches under the panic-retry budget, so a hotfix that changes replay-relevant history *structure* before an already-committed inline event may re-diverge that in-flight run into a non-determinism *block* rather than data corruption; the common case — fixing the panicking line without reordering — replays cleanly and resumes); **containment requires `panic = "unwind"`** (a binary compiled with `panic = "abort"` aborts the process instead, so the stuck-`RUNNING` row is recovered by the poison-pill reclaimer's missing-heartbeat path); a **repeatedly-panicking activity trips its circuit breaker (#369) exactly like a repeated `Err(String)`, by design**. **Post-review hardening (Codex bot, PR #1012): contain panics during future *construction*, not just poll.** The initial `catch_unwind` boundaries wrapped only the *future* returned by a handler, but a handler `fn` is *called* (constructed) first — so synchronous work a hand-written `WorkflowInfo`/`ActivityInfo` handler does before returning its `Box::pin(...)` future still unwound the spawned worker task uncaught, bypassing the `HandlerPanic` conversion, the panic metric, and leaving the task on the old `RUNNING`/poison-pill path. (Macro-generated `#[workflow]`/`#[activity]` handlers can't hit this; the public `handler` fields and `WorkflowReplayer::register_fn` are a supported hand-written surface.) Closed uniformly by wrapping the synchronous handler *call* itself in `catch_unwind` (new `pub(crate) crate::error::catch_construct`) at every invocation site — activity (`worker.rs`), local activity (`worker.rs`), the shared workflow drive/strict/canary cycle (`executor::run_workflow_handler_cycle`), and both query-replay drives (`executor::drive_query_replay`, `handle::execute_query_in_process`); a construction panic maps to the same contained path as a poll panic. `AssertUnwindSafe` is sound — on a construction panic the future is never produced and the borrowed context is dropped without reuse. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant and no migration** — contained panics reuse the existing `ActivityFailed` / `WorkflowFailed` events, preserving the append-only invariant. Files: `builder.rs`, `executor.rs`, `failure.rs`, `metrics_rs_adapter.rs`, `queue.rs`, `telemetry.rs`, `testing.rs`, `worker.rs`, plus the new `tests/integration/panic_containment_tests.rs` (and a one-line `workflow_panic_max_attempts` field added to the `WorkerRuntimeConfig` literals across ~14 existing integration-test files). Tests: `catch_construct` unit tests (`error.rs`), a construction-panic workflow unit test (`executor.rs`), a construction-panic query-replay test (`query_terminal_tests.rs`), an activity construction-panic envelope test (`worker.rs`), and 4 integration tests in `panic_containment_tests.rs` (`activity_handler_panic_is_contained_and_retried_then_terminal`, `local_activity_handler_panic_is_contained_and_retried_then_terminal`, `workflow_handler_panic_is_re_dispatched_then_terminal_within_budget`, `workflow_panic_max_attempts_zero_is_terminal_on_first_panic`) asserting the worker process stays up, the task leaves `RUNNING` within a poll interval, activities retry per policy, the workflow fails terminally after the bounded budget, and no spurious crash-strike / poison-pill entry — run against a real local Postgres 16; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings`, and the 1704 library unit tests green locally. Out of scope (per issue): unbounded retry-the-workflow-task-forever mode, any change to poison-pill process-crash semantics (#367), hung/infinite-loop detection (#494/#703), operator force-fail (#765).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Tiered / summary retention — see issue #752. When the history-retention janitor (issue #737) hard-deletes a terminal execution, it can now optionally **demote** it into a compact, queryable `harvest_execution_summaries` row instead of losing all trace of the run — a "tiered" retention policy where full histories expire on one horizon and lightweight summaries live (far longer, or forever) on a second, decoupled horizon; the summary answers "did this run exist, when, and what did it produce?" in one management-API call at ~<1 KB/execution, long after the event log is gone. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no replay impact** — a summary is a retention-time projection of terminal state, never part of the append-only event contract (AC8). **Configuration (AC1):** new `RetentionConfig.summary: Option<SummaryPolicy>` (`policy.rs`/`retention.rs`); `None` (default) is byte-for-byte identical to pre-#752 behavior (hard delete, no summary). `SummaryPolicy { retention: SummaryRetention, capture_payload: bool, max_payload_bytes: usize }` with `SummaryRetention::{For(Duration), Unbounded}`; builders `SummaryPolicy::for_days(u64)`/`::for_duration(Duration)`/`::unbounded()`, chained `.with_payload_capture()`/`.with_max_payload_bytes(usize)`, and on `RetentionConfig` `with_summary_retention(...)`/`with_summary_retention_days(u64)`/`with_summary_retention_unbounded()`; default payload cap `DEFAULT_SUMMARY_PAYLOAD_CAP` = 4 KiB; `validate()` bounds the summary horizon by the same `[MIN_MAX_AGE, MAX_MAX_AGE]` range as `max_age`; `enabled()` returns `true` for an overrides-only or summary-only config. **Atomic demotion in the delete transaction (AC2/AC7):** summarization happens inside `delete_candidate_execution`'s existing `FOR UPDATE` transaction, *after* the #747 legal-hold re-check and *before* the execution-row delete (the select is widened to fetch `output`/`error`/`search_attrs`/timing/shard/identity/state); the `INSERT` (with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`) is atomic with the delete — no window where both the execution and its summary are absent, and a rolled-back delete leaves no orphan summary; a legally-held execution is never summarized until released; summary disabled ⇒ no `INSERT`. **Opt-in capped payload with typed markers (AC3):** captured `result`/`error` payloads are opt-in (default off ⇒ identity + timing + search-attrs only) and byte-bounded; pure helpers `cap_result_payload`/`cap_error_text` store the value **verbatim** (codec-encoded form preserved, matching history-export *Full*) except an offload reference envelope (#524) becomes `{"_harvest_omitted": true, "reason": "offloaded"}` (never store a blob ref whose backing blob may be GC'd out from under the summary), an oversized value becomes `{"_harvest_omitted": true, "reason": "too_large", "bytes": N}`, and oversized error text becomes `[omitted: too_large, N bytes]`. Migration `20260710000001_harvest_execution_summaries` adds the table (`execution_id` PK, `workflow_name`/`workflow_id`/`state`, `started_at`/`completed_at`/`duration_ms`, `shard_id`, `search_attrs` JSONB, `result` JSONB, `error` TEXT, `parent_id` UUID, `summarized_at`) with a `(completed_at, execution_id)` GC/keyset index, a `(workflow_name, completed_at DESC)` filter index, a GIN index on `search_attrs`, and a partial `(parent_id) WHERE parent_id IS NOT NULL` index for the erase cascade. **Codec caveat:** the summary stores the `output`/`search_attrs` *columns* verbatim (the same codec-encoded columns #608 decodes on read), so encryption-at-rest is preserved. **Horizon caveat:** the summary horizon should exceed the history horizon to be useful (a bounded summary window at or below the history window means the summary is GC'd almost immediately); `RetentionRuntime::spawn` logs a one-time non-fatal warn when a bounded `summary_age() <= max_age()`. **Read-only list route (AC4):** new admin-guarded `GET /api/harvest/workflows/summaries` (handler `list_workflow_summaries`), registered **before** `/workflows/{id}` (per the #544 precedent) so axum does not capture `summaries` as a path param; filters mirror `GET /workflows` (`workflow_name`, `workflow_id`, `state` repeatable/CSV, `completed_after`/`completed_before` RFC 3339, `search_attr` repeatable `key:value` JSONB containment, and `order=asc|desc` default `desc` — any other value → `400`), same keyset-cursor pagination keyed on `(completed_at, execution_id)` (`limit` default 50 / max 500); cross-shard fan-out + k-way merge via `retention::list_execution_summaries` + `load_summaries_from_shards`; each item carries the summary columns plus `summarized: true` and `history_available: false`; registered in all four plugin registries, `docs/api-contract.json` (read-only, `workflow` category), and `autumn_harvest::audit` (`CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` ReadOnly / `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` None / `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`), with a pinned `workflow_summaries_route_is_classified` test. **Summary GC pass + metric (AC5):** second GC pass `purge_expired_summaries(...)` folded into `RetentionRuntime::spawn`, selecting by `completed_at < now - summary_age` (deterministic, anchored on the original run window — not `summarized_at`; `Unbounded` never GCs; batched `DELETE ... RETURNING workflow_name`), emitting the new `harvest.retention.summary_deleted{workflow}` counter (`METRIC_SUMMARY_DELETED`, `record_summary_deleted` no-op default on `MetricsRecorder`, bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter`); `summarized_count` added to `RetentionTickResult`/`ShardTickOutcome` (real deletes only) and surfaced on `GET /admin/retention`. **PII erasure scrubs the summary too (AC6):** `erase_workflow_payloads` (#495) now also scrubs a matching `harvest_execution_summaries` row in the same transaction via `erase_execution_summary`, tombstoning `result` and `search_attrs` with `{"_harvest_erased": true}` (error kept, consistent with #495); erase **succeeds when only the summary remains** (the full execution row already retention-deleted → terminal gate returns `NotFound`, but the summary scrub reports success); `EraseOutcome.summary_scrubbed` reports the outcome. **Child-summary erase cascade (structural fix):** a terminal child workflow is independently retention-eligible, so it can be demoted into a summary and have its execution row deleted before its parent is erased; since `harvest_execution_summaries` is keyed only by `execution_id` and the child's execution row is gone, the pre-existing `parent_id`-based cascade could never reach the child summary — fixed with the new `parent_id` column (captured at demotion from the child's own `FOR UPDATE`-locked row) and a unified downward erase traversal that, for each node, unions child ids from **both** `harvest_workflow_executions` **and** `harvest_execution_summaries` (deduped, `visited`-guarded) and recurses; the parent-delete's terminal-child `parent_id` null-out is skipped when summary retention is enabled so the demotion lineage survives deletion regardless of processing order. **CLI:** `harvest workflow summaries [--workflow-name --workflow-id --state --completed-after --completed-before --search-attr --limit --cursor --json]`. **Tests:** pure `SummaryPolicy` builder/validate + cap-helper unit tests and `enabled()`/`summary_gc_active()` truth tables (`retention.rs`); metric no-op + adapter bridge tests; erase pure-tombstone tests (`erase.rs`); DB integration tests in `tests/integration/retention_summary_tests.rs` (atomic demotion, legal-hold exemption, payload cap/marker, GC-by-`completed_at`, erase-scrubs-summary, `erase_parent_scrubs_a_demoted_child_summary`, `erase_parent_recurses_into_grandchild_summary`); plugin HTTP integration tests in `tests/workflow_summaries_integration.rs` (list-with-flags, filter-by-name/state/completed-range/search-attr, keyset pagination round-trip, admin-guard 401, malformed-param 400, summary-only erase → 200 + tombstoned fields). **Post-review hardening:** child-summary erase cascade (above, the major fix); the summary GC drain loop breaks on `n == 0` and compares against the *effective* clamped `LIMIT` (`i64::try_from(n) < batch`) so a degenerate `batch_size == 0` can't spin forever; `order=asc|desc` parity (previously silently ignored); `cap_result_payload` fail-safe emits the `too_large` marker on a (near-impossible) serialize failure; NITs (`for_days` uses `saturating_mul`, `duration_ms` clamped `.max(0)`, a root-only-offload-envelope invariant comment). **Success metric:** after a GC tick that hard-deletes a run's history, one management-API call (`GET /workflows/summaries?workflow_name=…`) returns that run's identity, terminal state, timing, and (opt-in, capped) result in well under a second, at ~<1 KB/execution.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Declarative DAG signal/approval gate nodes — see issue #746. A unified `#[dag]` can now **pause on a named signal** between graph nodes, with an optional durable timeout — the declarative way to insert a human approval or external-event wait without abandoning the DAG surface for a hand-written `#[workflow]`. A **gate node** is a `DagTask` whose new `signal: Option<DagSignalGate>` field is `Some`; it has no activity dispatch, its node identity (`activity_name`) is the signal name, and it composes like any other node (`.upstream(&gate)`, `.map_activity(f).over(&gate)`, `.condition(...)`). Fluent `DagBuilder::signal_gate(name)` and `signal_gate_with_timeout(name, timeout, on_timeout)` return a `DagTaskRef`; new public types `DagSignalGate` and `GateTimeoutAction` (`FailRun` | `Continue`). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration** — gates lower onto the existing #476 `receive_signal_timeout` / `wait_for_signal` machinery, reusing `TimerStarted` / `TimerFired` / `SignalReceived`, so a gated run is durable and replays deterministically (whichever of the signal or the deadline is recorded first in history wins on every replay). **Semantics.** Signal arrives → node `Succeeded` with the payload as output; `on_timeout = Continue` deadline → `Succeeded` with `Value::Null`; `on_timeout = FailRun` deadline → `Failed` (the run fails). **AC2 "continue to a named branch" is expressed declaratively** — there is no bespoke branch-target mechanism; under `Continue`, the gate's null-vs-payload output *is* the branch selector via a downstream `.condition(...)` (e.g. `.condition(|ups| ups[0].is_null())` for the timed-out branch). A signal delivering a JSON array fans out a downstream `.map_activity(f).over(&gate)` node with zero map-lowering change (Gap B). Deliver the unblocking signal with the ordinary standalone `POST /workflows/{id}/signal/{name}` route (AC3). **Level isolation** (highest-risk design point): the worker requires homogeneous suspension batches, so a `WaitForSignal` command must not share a batch with a level's `ScheduleActivity` dispatches — a `DagBuilder::build()` post-pass splits each Kahn level so each gate occupies its own singleton execution level; when a DAG contains no gates the level vector is returned byte-for-byte unchanged. **Single-sourced walker:** the macro previously emitted two byte-approximate copies of the level walker (which had already drifted on error handling in the collect-all map branch); both now shrink to a call into one core helper `dag::run_unified_dag(ctx, input, levels, tasks)`, fixing the drift bug (adopting the propagating, fail-fast-consistent behavior). **Classic-DAG rejection (AC6):** new `validate_classic_dags_have_no_signal_gates()` in `try_build` rejects any DAG with `workflow_handler.is_none()` containing a gate, with `HarvestBuilderError::DagSignalGateRequiresUnifiedExecution { dag, signal }`. **Graph-view (AC4):** `dag_graph::DagRunNode` gains `kind: DagNodeKind` (`Activity` | `Gate`) and `DagNodeStatus::Waiting`; `build_run_graph` classifies a gate the same way as an activity's reachability (`dag_skip` marker → `Skipped`; recorded `SignalReceived` → `Succeeded`; fired race timer → `TimedOut`; unresolved gate → `Waiting` only when the walker actually reached it, else `Pending`); the race-timer id is parsed exactly (`__signal_timeout:{seq}:{name}`), not by suffix match. **MCP restoration (Gap A):** `DagInfo::consumes_signals()` reports whether a unified DAG has ≥1 signal-gate node; `McpWorkflowDescriptor` gains a `consumes_signals` flag; the `signal_{dag}` tool suppression (issue #597) is refined from a blanket `is_dag` to `is_dag && !consumes_signals`, so a signal-capable DAG regains its `signal_{dag}` tool while an activity-only DAG still suppresses it. Docs: "Signal / approval gates" section in `docs/getting-started/08-dags-and-schedules.md`. Example: `autumn-harvest/examples/dag_approval_gate.rs` (extract → approval gate → load, with a `FailRun` primary and a `Continue` + `.condition` named-branch fallback; four embedded `WorkflowTestEnv` + `WorkflowReplayer` tests). Tests: pure builder-API unit tests (gate metadata, timeout/action, level isolation, upstream/map composition, classic-DAG rejection) and unified `WorkflowReplayer` money tests (signal-first and timer-first histories replay deterministically) in `tests/integration/dag_signal_gate_tests.rs`; graph-view gate tests in the plugin `dag_graph`; the new `collect_descriptors_signal_capable_dag_keeps_its_signal_tool` mcp_tools unit test.
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): Non-blocking signal drain for the aggregator pattern — see issue #775. Five synchronous, **non-suspending** signal-consumption methods on `WorkflowContext` that make the canonical aggregator / entity-workflow pattern (collect N events via signals, batch-process, `continue_as_new`) O(1) tasks + O(N) replay instead of O(N) tasks + O(N²) replay. Before this, collecting a batch required one blocking `receive_signal` call per signal — each in its own workflow task, each replaying the whole growing history. **New public API** (all `fn`, not `async fn` — they never `.await` and never push a `WaitForSignal` command, so they can never suspend): `try_receive_signal::<O>(signal_name) -> HarvestResult<Option<O>>` (the oldest buffered, not-yet-consumed signal, FIFO recorded-history order, or `None`), `drain_signals::<O>(signal_name) -> HarvestResult<Vec<O>>` (consumes and returns **all** currently-buffered signals in recorded-history order; typed = untyped + `serde_json::from_value`, fail-fast — the first undeserializable payload aborts with `HarvestError::Serialization`), `drain_signals_collect::<O>(signal_name) -> HarvestResult<Vec<Result<O, String>>>` (the poison-tolerant sibling — per-slot `Result<O, String>` so a single malformed payload never discards its good siblings; mirrors the fan-out fail-fast/collect pair), `try_wait_for_signal(signal_name) -> HarvestResult<Option<serde_json::Value>>` (untyped sibling of `try_receive_signal`), and `drain_signals_raw(signal_name) -> HarvestResult<Vec<serde_json::Value>>` (untyped sibling). **Matcher engine (`replay.rs`):** `drain_signals_raw` reuses the existing `HistoryMatcher::claim_pending_signal` (the cursor-bound, race-reserved-skipping FIFO drain built for issue #546) verbatim; `try_*` adds a new `pub(crate) fn try_claim_pending_signal(...) -> Option<Value>` that mirrors `match_signal`'s fast path but adds the two guards it lacks (runs `prepare_match()` first and skips `race_reserved_signal_events`) and never falls through to a suspension. **Determinism / ordering contract** (documented on all four methods): a signal recorded *after* an activity/timer the workflow has not yet reached in this replay cycle is invisible until the workflow's own `match_*` call for that event advances the cursor past it (mirroring `wait_for_signal`'s history-order contract); claimed events are marked consumed so a later `receive_signal`/`wait_for_signal`/push handler never re-sees them (no double delivery in either direction); a signal reserved for an **open** `receive_signal_timeout`/`wait_for_signal_timeout` race (issue #476) is never resolved by a drain (so a drain can never silently flip an open race's outcome), while a signal that already *lost* a resolved `TimerWon` race is fair game; history order is authoritative. **All four route through `match_history(|m| ...)`** so the `pump_signal_handlers` post-hook keeps push-handler ordering consistent. **`WorkflowTestEnv`/`WorkflowSimulator` faithfulness:** both no-DB harnesses now mirror production's task-preparation ingest (`worker::load_workflow_replay_state` → `ingest_due_timers_and_signals` appends all pending signals into history **before** the workflow handler runs for each task pickup) — a **task-prep ingest** drains every currently-queued signal (all names, queued order) into history at the top of each run-loop iteration, so a workflow that *starts* with a non-blocking `drain_signals_raw`/`try_receive_signal` (no prior blocking `wait_for_signal`) sees its pending signals; the now-redundant `WaitForSignal`-gated promotion was removed from both harnesses (`WorkflowSimulator::signals_to_send` also changed from `HashMap<String, VecDeque<Value>>` to a single `Vec<(String, Value)>` to preserve cross-name queued order). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no shard-semantics change** — the methods only consume already-recorded `SignalReceived` events (`claim_pending_signal`'s behavior is untouched; the `race_reserved_signal_events` guard is preserved on both the drain and try paths). **Tests, TDD red→green→refactor:** 6 `replay.rs` unit tests for `try_claim_pending_signal`, 13 `context.rs` unit tests (drain-raw-in-order, typed-deserialize-each, fail-fast → `Serialization`, drain-signals-collect per-slot poison-tolerant, try-receive-oldest-then-none, try-receive-emits-no-commands, drain-then-wait-no-double-delivery, drain-skips-race-reserved, push/pull first-claim-wins in both directions, signal-after-a-drain observable by a subsequent drain), 4 `WorkflowTestEnv` integration tests (`test_drain_signals_returns_all_queued_in_order` — the literal AC; `test_drain_1000_signals_returns_all_in_one_task` — the falsifiable success metric asserting the RETURNED batch count == 1000; `test_single_wait_with_extras_queued_returns_first_signal`; `test_try_receive_signal_none_when_nothing_queued`), and 2 `WorkflowReplayer` fixtures (`replay_drain_signals_interleaved_with_activity_is_deterministic` over 3 cycles; `replay_drain_n_signals_in_one_task_consumes_all` — 1000 buffered signals drained in ONE task). Example `autumn-harvest/examples/signal_aggregator.rs`. This is a no-DB (`testing`/`--no-default-features`) feature; all tests executed.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Activity execution interceptors — see issue #680 (merged as PR #1025). Register an ordered middleware chain that wraps **every** activity execution on the worker — regular (task-queue-dispatched) *and* local (inline) — so applications add cross-cutting behavior (structured logging, custom metrics, header propagation, input/output shaping, test fault-injection) **once** at registration time instead of editing every `#[activity]` function. New core module `interceptor.rs`: the object-safe `ActivityInterceptor` trait (generic over a lifetime only, stored as `Arc<dyn ActivityInterceptor>`; no `async_trait` — manual `Pin<Box>` alias `ActivityInterceptorFuture<'a>` mirroring `PayloadStore`/`HistoryArchiver`/`CompletionCallbackDeliverer`), the `ActivityInvocation<'a>` read-only metadata carrier (`name`/`is_local`/`queue_name`, private fields + accessors), the `ActivityInterceptorNext<'a>` continuation (`.run(input)` proceeds to the next interceptor or the terminal handler; not calling it short-circuits so the handler never runs), and the shared `pub(crate) dispatch_with_interceptors` helper (zero-overhead direct handler call when the chain is empty — the default path is byte-for-byte unchanged). **First-registered interceptor is the OUTERMOST wrapper**, the activity handler is innermost. Registration: `HarvestBuilder::activity_interceptor(impl ActivityInterceptor)` (repeatable, push-order = registration-order = index-0-outermost; mirrors `history_archiver`), threaded through both `into_worker_parts`/`into_worker_parts_with_extra_state` into `HandlerRegistry::with_activity_interceptors`. Both worker dispatch sites — the regular `process_activity_task` handler call and the local `run_local_activity_inline` per-attempt call — build the execution future through `dispatch_with_interceptors`. **Error / panic / retry / circuit-breaker transparency by construction:** an interceptor future resolves to the *exact* `Result<serde_json::Value, String>` `Output` of `ActivityHandlerFn`, so its error rides the same internal String channel the handler uses (an interceptor `Err(String)` is treated identically to a handler error — normal retry → circuit-breaker `on_result` → terminal `ActivityFailed`, no special-casing; typed failures via `ActivityFailure::retryable/non_retryable(...).into_error_payload()`), and a **panic** in an interceptor (construction or poll) is caught by the same `catch_construct` + `catch_unwind` guard that contains handler panics (issue #782) → retryable `HandlerPanic` → worker survives, no poison-pill / DLQ row. Interceptors run **after** the per-activity circuit-breaker admit gate; the local-activity chain runs **inside** the per-attempt local timeout (interceptor time counts against `start_to_close` — the one documented behavioral difference). **Replay safety, no schema cost:** interceptors live only on the worker dispatch path; the replay engine never invokes activity handlers, the value the chain returns *becomes* the recorded activity result, so replay reads it back and interceptors are never re-invoked for a completed activity; input reaches an interceptor already-decoded. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no event-schema change** — a worker with no interceptors registered is byte-for-byte identical to before. Re-exported from `lib.rs` and `prelude.rs`. Testing surface (feature `testing`): `ActivityInvocation::for_test` + `run_interceptor_chain_for_test`. Example `autumn-harvest/examples/activity_interceptor.rs` (a `LoggingMetricsInterceptor` recording a per-activity `harvest.user.activity.duration_ms` histogram + structured logs, registered once across two `#[activity]` functions). Tests: 6 pure no-DB unit tests in `interceptor.rs` (outermost-first ordering, input transform, result transform, short-circuit-without-next, error transform, empty-chain fast path) + an object-safety assertion; 7 DB/worker integration tests in `tests/integration/activity_interceptor_tests.rs`. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2) — transactional-activity consistency.** A transactional activity (`ctx.run_transactional`) atomically commits its `ActivityCompleted` event and marks its task `COMPLETED` *inside the user's transaction* — before an outer interceptor regains control from `next.run` — so an interceptor transforming the result after `next` cannot change the recorded history, yet the worker was consuming that discarded post-interceptor result for its per-attempt metrics **and** the per-activity circuit breaker (an interceptor mapping a committed `Ok` to `Err` would trip the breaker and record `Failed` on an outcome history records as `ActivityCompleted`). Fix, in two parts: **(A)** the inherent limitation is now documented — an interceptor **observes but cannot transform** a transactional activity's recorded outcome; **(B)** `ActivityContext` carries an interior-mutable self-commit flag (`transactional_commit_occurred`, set only on a successful `run_transactional` commit), and after the interceptor chain resolves the worker reads it: a self-committed activity records the attempt as `Completed`, feeds the circuit breaker `Success`, and skips the finalize/retry path entirely (a single `tracing::warn!` still surfaces the misuse). Byte-for-byte unchanged for the no-interceptor / observe-only / non-transactional cases. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** Tests: 2 new DB/worker integration tests — `interceptor_error_transform_on_transactional_activity_does_not_trip_breaker` (committed `Ok`→`Err` interceptor leaves the breaker closed, records `Completed`, seals history as `ActivityCompleted`, no retry/DLQ; fails pre-fix) and `interceptor_result_transform_on_transactional_activity_is_observably_ignored`.
- **Stack endpoint pending-local-activity fold — read fields at the correct JSON depth** (production fix, PR #1022, issue #773): the `pending_local_activities` fold in the workflow `/stack` endpoint handler (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`) read `activity_id` and `name` from the **top level** of `harvest_events.event_data`, but that column stores the full adjacently-tagged event envelope `{"type": ..., "data": {...}}`, so an event's own fields live under `.data`, not at the top level. Root cause: the top-level `.get("activity_id")` was always `None`, so every `LocalActivityScheduled`/`LocalActivityCompleted`/`LocalActivityFailed` event fell through the fold's catch-all arm and nothing was ever inserted — `pending_local_activities` was always `[]` (the `type` key was read correctly since it genuinely lives at the top level via the DB `event_type` column; the sibling failure-map query already decodes via `serde_json::from_value::<WorkflowEvent>(data)` and was unaffected). Fix: read `activity_id` and `name` under `.data`, restoring the issue-#773 behavior that a backing-off/flapping local activity surfaces its `last_failure` on `/stack`. The test `stack_pending_local_activity_surfaces_last_failure` now passes (it was masked on `trunk-dev` because CI fail-fast aborted the read-path-decode suite before reaching it when the earlier typed-failure #767 INIT_SQL step failed). No public API change, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration. Verified against a fresh local Postgres 16 (the single test passes ×3, full `read_path_decode_integration` suite green 20/20).
- **Stack endpoint — remove exhausted local activities from the pending list** (production fix, PR #1022, issue #773): follow-up to the same-PR depth fix. Correctly inserting entries activated a latent bug (Codex P2): the fold's SQL filter selected only `LocalActivityScheduled`/`LocalActivityCompleted`/`LocalActivityFailed`, and its remove arm only removed on `LocalActivityCompleted`, so it never consumed the terminal `LocalActivityExhausted` event. Root cause: a local activity that exhausts its retry budget records `LocalActivityScheduled + N×LocalActivityFailed + LocalActivityExhausted` and no `LocalActivityCompleted`; if the workflow *catches* that terminal failure and keeps running, the exhausted activity stayed in `pending_local_activities` forever. Fix: add `LocalActivityExhausted` to the SQL `eq_any` filter and to the remove arm alongside `LocalActivityCompleted` (both are terminal closes → remove the pending entry); `LocalActivityFailed` handling is deliberately unchanged (a bare mid-retry `Failed` still stays pending, per #773). No public API change, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration. Verified TDD red→green against a fresh local Postgres 16 — the new `stack_exhausted_local_activity_is_not_pending` FAILS without the remove-arm change and PASSES with it; full `read_path_decode_integration` suite green (21/21).
- **Stack endpoint — decode `last_failure` only for surviving pending local activities** (production fix, PR #1022, issue #773 / #608): follow-up to the fold-insert/remove fixes. Correctly activating the local-activity path surfaced a Codex P2 read-path-decode audit-fidelity bug: the fold decoded each entry's `last_failure` error **inline in the `LocalActivityScheduled` arm** — before a later terminal-remove arm could drop the entry. Root cause: when the read-path decoder (#608) is admin-active and a still-RUNNING workflow has a local activity that failed with a stringified codec envelope and then EXHAUSTED (caught-and-continued), the Scheduled arm decoded and merged that failure into `decode_outcome` (touching the audit accumulator) before the `LocalActivityExhausted` arm removed the entry — so the response contained no such pending local activity yet `audit_decoded_read` wrote a spurious `payload.decode_read` audit row for data that never left the handler, violating the #608 contract "decode/audit exactly what is surfaced." Fix: defer `last_failure` decoding until after the fold — the `LocalActivityScheduled` arm now attaches the **raw (undecoded)** most-recent failure, and once the fold has applied all terminal removals a single post-fold loop over the **surviving** `pending_local_activities` decodes each entry's `error` inline and merges into `decode_outcome`. The regular (task-queue) pending-activity `last_failure` path is unaffected (it decodes over already-surviving rows). Localized change — no restructure of the #608 decoder/audit plumbing, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration. Verified TDD red→green against a fresh local Postgres 16 — the new `stack_removed_local_activity_failure_is_not_decoded_or_audited` FAILS without the fix and PASSES with it; full `read_path_decode_integration` suite green (22/22).
- **Trunk hotfix — add missing legal-hold migration to typed-failure test schema** (test-fixture fix, PR #1022): restored a green `trunk-dev`. Two `db_handle_surface` tests in `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/typed_workflow_failure_tests.rs` failed their `assert!(matches!(err, HarvestError::WorkflowFailed { .. }))` assertion because `handle.result_raw()`/`result_snapshot()` on a sealed-`FAILED` execution returned `HarvestError::Database("column harvest_workflow_executions.legal_hold_set_at does not exist")` instead of the typed `WorkflowFailed`. Root cause: the `db_handle_surface` tests build their testcontainers schema from a hand-rolled, ordered `INIT_SQL` list of migration `up.sql` files rather than running `diesel migration run`; that list omitted `20260709000001_harvest_legal_hold`, so the four `legal_hold_*` columns PR #1008 (issue #747) added to the `WorkflowExecution` read struct were absent from the test schema — and once `WorkflowExecution::as_select()` began selecting them, loading any execution row against the stale schema errored (PR #1008 swept many sibling test files' `INIT_SQL` but missed this file, which PR #995 for issue #767 had introduced only hours earlier). Fix: add the one missing migration to the `db_handle_surface::INIT_SQL` include list in timestamp order. **Not a production regression** — a test-fixture omission only; no production code change, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration added or altered. Verified: reproduced RED against a fresh local Postgres 16 (verbatim `Database("column ... legal_hold_set_at does not exist")`); after the fix both tests pass.
- **Phase 3.5x** (implemented): Durable await of external workflows (`ctx.await_external_workflow`) — see issue #757. `ctx.await_external_workflow::<T>(target: ExecutionId) -> HarvestResult<T>` (typed) and `ctx.await_external_workflow_value(target) -> HarvestResult<Value>` (untyped) let a running workflow durably block until an arbitrary, independently-started sibling execution reaches a terminal state, then hand back its typed result or terminal cause. It is the third verb of the external-workflow family (signal #244 / cancel #492 / **await #757**), a close architectural mirror of the cancel primitive. Callable from any `#[workflow]` body with **no feature flag**. **Semantics** (the key differences from cancel #492): target `COMPLETED` → resolves with the **deserialized output**; target `FAILED`/`TIMED_OUT`/`CANCELLED`/`TERMINATED` → returns a typed `Err` carrying the target's terminal cause as an **outcome** (not a transport error) — a `FAILED` target surfaces as `HarvestError::WorkflowFailed { name: "external-workflow:{target}", .. }`, the SAME typed error a failed child surfaces as (issue #767), so `err.workflow_error_type()`/`workflow_details()`/`is_workflow_non_retryable()` are all readable; target `RUNNING`/`PAUSED` → the caller parks durably and resolves within one outbox poll interval after the target reaches any terminal state; **self-await** (`target == own ExecutionId`) → immediate `HarvestError::ExternalAwaitFailed { reason_code: "self_await" }`, records no history (nil-UUID sentinel); an **unknown target** still unknown after the configured grace window → `HarvestError::ExternalAwaitFailed { reason_code: "target_unknown" }` (a transport failure, distinct from the terminal-cause outcomes; `err.external_await_reason_code()` reads it). Await is **observe-only** — it never establishes parent/child linkage, cancels, triggers `ParentClosePolicy`, or has any lifecycle effect on the target. **No new migration.** Three new append-only `WorkflowEvent` variants appended at the **END** of the enum (opaque adjacently-tagged JSON; pre-upgrade histories deserialize/replay unchanged): `ExternalAwaitRequested { await_id, target }`, `ExternalAwaitResolved { await_id, output }` (carries the target's inflated output), `ExternalAwaitFailed { await_id, reason_code, message?, error_type?, details?, non_retryable? }` (the optional typed fields are `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; carry the target's typed `WorkflowFailure` for a `FAILED` target). New `ExternalAwaitId(Uuid)` newtype (exact clone of `ExternalCancelId`, re-exported from `lib.rs`), new `HarvestError::ExternalAwaitFailed { await_id, target, reason_code }` transport variant + `external_await_reason_code()` accessor. **Implementation mirrors the cancel primitive throughout.** `replay::HistoryMatch::ExternalAwaitInProgress`/`ExternalAwaitFailed` variants + `StashedExternalAwait`/`StashedAwaitTerminal` stash + `pending_external_awaits` field; `HistoryMatcher::match_external_await(target)` (returns `Matched { output }` carrying the real output value); the await event triplet is stashed transparently in all ten scan loops (`scan_activity_terminal`, `scan_local_activity_terminal`, `drain_early_signals`, `match_external_activity`, `match_external_signal`, `match_timer_strict`, `timer_scan_cross_or_stop`, `match_signal`, `match_signal_or_timer`, `match_child_or_timer`) plus the `match_external_cancel` sibling scan and the two `matches!` skip-lists, and tracked in `has_buffered_history`/`has_non_lifecycle_unconsumed`. `WorkflowContext::await_external_workflow(_value)` + `dispatch_await_command` (suspension whose value is recovered from the appended terminal event on the resumed drive, never the channel). `WorkflowCommand::AwaitExternalWorkflow` dispatched through the worker's generalized `SignalBatchItem::Await(AwaitExternalWorkflowRun)`: `extract_signal_external_workflow`/`split_mixed_signal_batch`/`resolved_external_ids`, all classification guards (`should_requeue_signal_wait`, `extract_started_timer_for_suspension`'s valid-command set, the mixed-batch `is_mixed`/`any(...)` guards, the pure-external `all_resolved`+reconstruct), and `persist_signal_wait_park`'s post-park self-wake re-check. `persist_external_signal_inline` Await arm resolves a **same-shard** target inline via the new `execution::read_external_await_outcome` (which follows a `CONTINUED_AS_NEW` chain to the true terminal, reads the target's `WorkflowFailed` event for the typed cause, and is **observe-only** — never mutates the target or creates linkage); a cross-shard or still-running target leaves the bare `ExternalAwaitRequested` and re-parks. `timeout::enforce_external_awaits_outbox` (folded into `enforce_timeouts_once` right after the cancel outbox) resolves cross-shard + still-running targets, applying the grace-window `target_unknown` rule (mirrors `enforce_external_cancels_outbox`). The resolved output is stored **INFLATED** (not offloaded) into the awaiter's own history in both the inline and outbox paths — correct, replay-deterministic, and free of any awaiter-owned blob-GC hazard (an offload-aware awaiter copy is a possible future optimization). `testing.rs`: `WorkflowTestEnv::with_external_await_result`/`with_external_await_failure` + a `process_command` Await arm, a `WorkflowSimulator` arm, and `NonDeterminismKind::ExternalAwaitMismatch` (+ `classify_kind` `"external await"` arm, also closing the cancel gap). **No metric added** (optional per the issue). Example: `autumn-harvest/examples/await_external_workflow.rs` (a fan-in coordinator awaiting three independently-started legs by id in one line each, branching on a leg's typed terminal cause). Tests: event round-trip + pre-#757 back-compat unit tests in `event.rs`; 6 `match_external_await` matcher unit tests in `replay.rs` (incl. the concurrent-with-activity stash regression); 6 context unit tests (live-command, self-await-no-history, replay-resolved, replay-failed-typed-`WorkflowFailed`, replay-`target_unknown`, ND-wrong-target); 3 `WorkflowTestEnv` coverage tests; 5 `WorkflowReplayer` fixtures in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs` including the falsifiable **1000-pass determinism** bar (mirroring the #476 precedent), a failed-target typed-branch fixture, a concurrent-with-activity fixture over both interleaved orderings, and an `ExternalAwaitMismatch` detection fixture; 7 DB integration tests in `tests/integration/cross_workflow_await_tests.rs` (completed-inline → Ok, failed-target → typed error surfaces, running-then-outbox-resolves, cross-shard via outbox, self-await immediate-Err-no-park, unknown-target grace-window, observe-only-target-unchanged) — **run green against real Postgres 16** and wired into `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`.
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): Inline-resolved mixed timer + external op wakes immediately — see issue #678. Fixes a latency bug where a `select!{ timer(3600s), signal_external_workflow(target) }` (or `request_cancel_external_workflow(target)`) whose external target lives on the **same shard** could park its timer for up to the full timer duration (an hour) instead of resolving on the external branch that already completed. **Root cause.** For a mixed `[StartTimer, SignalExternalWorkflow/RequestCancelExternalWorkflow]` suspension batch, the drive-loop mixed arm strips the external commands (`split_mixed_signal_batch`) then delivers them inline (`persist_external_signal_inline`) — which for a same-shard target appends `ExternalSignalDelivered`/`ExternalCancelDelivered` to history **in this decision cycle** and returns them in `new_events`. The remaining `StartTimer` then reaches `persist_started_timer`, whose `is_mixed` detection uses a SQL probe for **unresolved** `External*Requested` events. Because the request was resolved inline, that probe finds nothing, the parked row is **not** tagged `mixed_signal_suspension`, and neither `wake_workflow_task`'s primary re-pend (which requires that tag) nor the existing post-park recheck (which only inspects incoming pending **signals**) ever self-wakes the task. It sleeps until `fires_at`. **Fix (Option 1 — thread the resolution ids, self-wake).** New pure helper `resolved_external_ids(new_events: &[WorkflowEvent]) -> ResolvedExternalIds` collects the resolved signal/cancel ids by scanning the `External{Signal,Cancel}{Delivered,Failed}` terminals in `new_events` — the events `persist_external_signal_inline` appended for this batch, which contain exactly this batch's `External*Requested` events plus any inline terminal, so the resolved-id set is derivable from `new_events` alone (no batch-item correlation, no payload clone). `Failed` counts as resolved; any non-terminal event (a `Requested` with no matching terminal — cross-shard / `NotFound` → outbox route — or a marker) contributes nothing. The mixed arm computes it right after `persist_external_signal_inline` returns and threads the result — via a new `ResolvedExternalIds` field on `SuspendedWorkflowContext` and a new by-value parameter on `persist_workflow_outcome` — down to `persist_started_timer`. There, `if !resolved_inline_external.is_empty() { is_mixed = true; }` marks the parked row `mixed_signal_suspension` (wakeable), and a new post-commit self-wake block — mirroring `persist_signal_wait_park`'s #492 external self-wake — calls `queue::wake_workflow_task` **unconditionally** (the inline terminal is guaranteed already durable this cycle, so no history re-check is needed), so the worker re-claims the task immediately and re-runs the workflow, which now observes the external terminal in history and takes the signal/cancel branch → `COMPLETED`. **Correctness guard.** The self-wake fires **only** from `resolved_inline` — ids resolved in **this** decision cycle, threaded from the arm — never from a blanket history scan. A pure `ctx.timer()` sleep threads `ResolvedExternalIds::default()` (empty) and can never false-wake, even in a workflow that performed an earlier, fully-observed external op. Every suspension path other than the mixed timer + external arm passes the empty default, so their behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. No new events are appended by the fix, so the suspension shape / `suspended_command_event_count` is unaffected. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no replay-determinism change** — the fix is entirely in the worker's suspension/self-wake bookkeeping. **Tests.** No-DB unit tests for `resolved_external_ids` in `worker.rs` (matches delivered signal / delivered cancel / requested-without-terminal is empty / counts `Failed` terminals / partial resolution / empty events — `db`-feature gated, since `worker.rs` is `db`-only). Two DB integration tests in `tests/integration/cross_workflow_signal_tests.rs` (`test_mixed_timer_suspension_signal_resolves_inline_wakes_immediately`, `test_mixed_timer_suspension_cancel_resolves_inline_wakes_immediately`): the target is started **first** and confirmed `RUNNING` so the caller's external op resolves inline, and a tight 30 s bound proves the caller wakes immediately on the inline terminal rather than sleeping out the 3600 s timer. The existing `test_mixed_timer_suspension_signal_wakes_timer` control (caller started first → `NotFound` → outbox path) is unchanged and still passes, confirming no regression to the unresolved/outbox route.
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): Inline-resolved external op wakes every standard mixed-suspension shape immediately — see issue #1034. Follow-up to #678 / PR #1033. Closes the remaining latency (and, for one shape, indefinite-hang) bug where a workflow that races an external op — `signal_external_workflow` / `request_cancel_external_workflow` — against a **non-timer** branch in one decision cycle, with the external target on the **same shard**, failed to wake on the inline-resolved external terminal. **Before.** #678 fixed exactly one suspension shape: a mixed `[StartTimer, SignalExternalWorkflow/RequestCancelExternalWorkflow]` batch. For a same-shard target, `persist_external_signal_inline` appends `External{Signal,Cancel}{Delivered,Failed}` to history **in this decision cycle**, so the terminal is already durable — but the self-wake that re-claimed the parked task lived inside the timer-only `persist_started_timer` path. Any other mixed shape got no wake: **signal-wait** (`select!{ signal_external_workflow(target), wait_for_signal("other") }`): the task parked on the signal wait and **hung** until the *other* signal arrived — potentially forever. **scheduled-activity** (`select!{ signal_external_workflow(target), execute_activity(slow) }`): the task waited out the **full activity** before noticing the already-resolved external branch. **After.** The workflow wakes **immediately** on the inline-resolved external terminal and completes on the external branch right away. This covers every **standard** mixed-suspension park shape whose park leaves the workflow-task row re-pend-eligible: the issue's three named shapes (timer, signal-wait, scheduled-activity) **plus** child-workflow, external-activity-wait, and the child-timeout race (issue #779) — all use the same RUNNING-park / `mixed_signal_suspension`-stamp mechanism, so the single arm-level wake re-pends them uniformly. **How.** Lifted the #678 inline-external self-wake out of the timer-only `persist_started_timer` path up to a single arm-level `queue::wake_workflow_task` in `persist_workflow_outcome`'s `WorkflowOutcome::Suspended` dispatch, gated on `!resolved_inline_external.is_empty()` (so a pure suspension, or a cycle whose externals routed to the outbox / were already observed, never false-wakes). Each shape's park leaves the workflow task `wake_workflow_task`-eligible: RUNNING-parked for signal-wait / scheduled-activity / child-workflow, and `mixed_signal_suspension`-stamped for the timer shape — so one arm-level wake re-pends them via the primary re-pend query. Retired the timer-only special case; **kept** `persist_started_timer`'s `mixed_signal_suspension` stamp (still set from the threaded `resolved_inline_external`) so the arm-level wake re-pends the timer's PENDING row. Runs **inside the enclosing persist transaction**, so park + re-pend commit atomically and the NOTIFY defers to the outer commit — no crash window. **Known limitation (pre-existing, out of scope).** The one uncovered park shape is the issue #768 cancellable-timer `await_fire` `armed_fires_at` bookkeeping remainder — composing an armed cancellable-timer handle with an external op in a single `select!` is documented in #768 as an unsupported follow-up: that path reschedules the workflow row to `PENDING@future` **without** the `mixed_signal_suspension` stamp, so the arm-level wake no-ops for it and the run sleeps to the armed deadline (this is pre-existing #768 behaviour, not a #1034 regression). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no replay-determinism change** — the fix is entirely in the worker's suspension / self-wake bookkeeping; the resolved-id threading and `resolved_external_ids` helper from #678 are reused unchanged. Every suspension path other than the mixed external arm still threads `ResolvedExternalIds::default()` (empty), so their behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. **Tests.** Four DB integration tests added to `tests/integration/cross_workflow_signal_tests.rs`, each starting the target **first** (confirmed `RUNNING`, so the caller's external op resolves inline) and bounding the caller's completion tightly to prove an immediate wake rather than a park-out: `test_mixed_signal_wait_suspension_external_signal_resolves_inline_wakes_immediately`, `test_mixed_signal_wait_suspension_external_cancel_resolves_inline_wakes_immediately`, `test_mixed_activity_suspension_external_signal_resolves_inline_wakes_immediately`, and `test_mixed_child_workflow_suspension_external_signal_resolves_inline_wakes_immediately` (the child-workflow shape, backing the "covers more than the three named shapes" claim above — RED without the arm-level wake, GREEN with it). The activity and child-workflow tests use a 60s slow branch with a 30s completion bound (the buggy path waits out the full 60s → trips the bound; the fixed path completes in ~seconds regardless of the branch length) for robustness on slow CI. The #678 timer-shape tests and the unresolved/outbox control are unchanged and still pass, confirming no regression to the cross-shard / `NotFound` route.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Deadline-aware continue-as-new for long-lived, low-event workflows — see issue #772. A long-lived entity workflow (a subscription, a cart, a device) can run for weeks while recording only a handful of events, so it never approaches the history event-count threshold `ctx.should_continue_as_new()` watches — yet if it declares an `execution_timeout` (#243) for runaway/SLA protection, that hard timeout eventually terminates it mid-flight even though it is healthy. This slice gives `should_continue_as_new()` a **second, independent trigger**: it now *also* returns `true` once the run has consumed at least a configurable fraction (default `0.8`) of its `execution_timeout` budget, so the author can `continue_as_new` **before** the hard deadline truncates the run, carrying state forward into a fresh run with a fresh deadline. Entirely additive, pure `WorkflowContext` + replay logic. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no change to the adjacently-tagged event-JSON contract.** New public `WorkflowContext` accessors, both **pure and replay-safe**: `deadline() -> Option<DateTime<Utc>>` = the recorded `WorkflowStarted` timestamp (`start_time`, no advancing clock) + the effective `execution_timeout`, `None` when there is no timeout or the sum overflows — records **no** event; and `time_until_deadline() -> Option<chrono::Duration>` = `deadline() - system_now()`, measured against the replay-safe recorded wall clock (`system_now()`, #384's `SideEffectRecorded{Now}`), **never** `chrono::Utc::now()`. `time_until_deadline` checks the pure `deadline()` first, so a workflow with **no** `execution_timeout` consults (and records) **zero** side-effects (AC4).
