Registered in `management_api_response_fields()` and `docs/api-contract.json` (kept in sync, guarded by `contract_regression`); nested `sample_execution_ids` is documented in the route description (precedent: `next_retry_at`/`input` on `/stack` live in the description, not the top-level `fields` list). **AC4 — boot-time fail-fast (default warn).** New `[harvest.startup] orphaned_workflows = off|warn|fail` config (env override `AUTUMN_HARVEST_STARTUP__ORPHANED_WORKFLOWS`, case-insensitive), mirroring the `require_shard_readiness` precedent. `start_harvest_runtime` runs the gate **before** `HarvestRunner::start` — before any worker poll loop, scheduler, or scanner is spawned, so no task can be claimed or terminally failed when it fires — computing `registered` directly from the owned `built` (workflow-info names UNION unified-DAG names) and querying the single-shard `workflow_reachability::build_reachability_report_single_shard(registered, pool, filter)` core against the runner-resolved shard-0 pool (selected via the shared `pick_runtime_pool_source` + the read-only `select_runtime_shard0_pool`, which installs no process global). It feeds `(report.orphaned, report.status)` into the pure `startup_orphan_decision(action, orphaned, status) -> StartupOrphanDecision` — the single source of the fail/warn/partial policy (AC4 reads AC3's two fields). `off` skips the check; `warn` (default, non-breaking — a mixed fleet mid-rollout must not crash-loop) logs the orphaned types and continues; `fail` refuses startup with a bare `return Err` — the gate runs before the runner, gate-refresh, and outbox are spawned and before any admission globals are published, so a refused boot has nothing to tear down and leaks no background tasks. A failure of the check *itself* only warns (never blocks boot on its own error). **Crash-loop safety:** `fail` aborts **only** when orphaned types are present **and** the report is `Complete`; an incomplete (`partial`/`unavailable`) report always degrades to `Warn` — a boot loop has no human in the loop, so a transient unreachable shard/DB must never hard-fail startup. This is deliberately **asymmetric** with the CLI gate (`harvest workflow-types reachability`), which fails *closed* (exit 2) on a partial report because a human reads its exit code. Truth-table clarification: only a `Complete` report with `orphaned == false` resolves to `Continue` (a *confirmed* clean boot never warns); an incomplete report always warns (see hardening item (7) below). **Architecture deviation (deliberate):** the gate lives in the plugin (`[harvest.startup]` + `startup_orphan_decision`), not on `HarvestBuilder` — the boot gate is a single-shard *pre-runner preflight* over the owned `built` and the runner's shard-0 pool (the plugin is single-shard-only; multi-shard configs are rejected upstream, so it reads the identical rows the started-runtime cross-shard fan-out would), while the cross-shard `GET /admin/workflow-types/reachability` route (`build_workflow_reachability_report`) stays plugin territory and *is* the programmatic embedder access the AC's "e.g. a `HarvestBuilder` method" refers to (both share the `observe_shard` + `build_report_from_observations` helpers, so they cannot drift). **AC9 — runbook.** `docs/runbooks/safe-deploy.md` gains a "Pre-cutover handler-coverage gate" section ahead of the #512 replay canary: its deploy-ladder position (worker drain #386 → this gate → #512 canary → #480 → #614 → #538/#510), the CLI (exit 2 on orphan/partial) and API single-field `orphaned`/`total_orphaned_executions` gate, the per-group `sample_execution_ids` drill-in, and the boot-time `[harvest.startup] orphaned_workflows` option with its crash-loop-safe partial-shard behavior. Cross-linked to `safe-handler-removal.md` (type-level vs build-id vs `ctx.version()` distinction), with a back-pointer added there. **CI:** wired the plugin `workflow_reachability_integration` suite (previously ALLOWLIST debt, only compile-checked) and the new core `workflow_reachability_samples_tests` module into `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`; removed the now-covered ALLOWLIST entry and lowered `ALLOWLIST_MAX_LEN` 74 → 73. **Tests, TDD red→green:** pure unit tests in `workflow_reachability.rs` (samples cap/merge/empty, orphan summary, `startup_orphan_decision` truth table) and `config.rs` (default/TOML/env/unknown-value on both the env AND TOML paths); core DB `workflow_reachability_samples_tests` (executed against Postgres — includes a `samples_are_oldest_first` test seeding staggered `started_at` values in reverse insertion order to pin the `started_at ASC, id ASC` ordering); plugin HTTP `orphaned_group_surfaces_bounded_execution_id_samples` + `endpoint_exposes_top_level_orphaned_and_total` (testcontainers, compile-checked where Docker is unavailable, executed by CI on Linux, per the #543/#544/#601 precedent). **Post-review hardening (consolidated ship-list, PR #1109):** three review lenses + the Gemini bot returned no blockers; the following polish items were applied. (1) **Sample-cap drift guard** — Diesel `sql_query` cannot interpolate the `REACHABILITY_SAMPLE_CAP` const into the SQL string, so the per-shard slice stays a hardcoded `[1:5]` literal; a DB-free guard unit test now fails if the literal and the const drift apart, an inline SQL comment names the invariant, and the const doc was corrected (it aspirationally wrote `[1:REACHABILITY_SAMPLE_CAP]` while the code hardcodes `[1:5]`). (2) **Boot-gate decision coverage** — new `boot_gate_{fail_aborts,warn_allows,fail_allows_clean}` integration tests drive the exact two-step decision path `start_harvest_runtime` composes (`build_workflow_reachability_report` + `startup_orphan_decision`) against a seeded database, each filtering to a unique workflow type for race-free isolation; the private, config/migration/pool-coupled `start_harvest_runtime` shell (thin task-teardown glue over this decision) is not integration-callable. (3) **Default-boot-query cost + drain-first callout** — `safe-deploy.md` now states the reachability check runs **by default** under `warn` on every boot (a bounded cross-shard `GROUP BY … ARRAY_AGG` aggregate; `off` is the only zero-cost setting, the per-group `LATERAL … LIMIT n` fallback bounds memory), and warns that enabling `fail` refuses boot **fleet-wide** until a persistent orphan drains — so confirm `orphaned == false` via the CLI gate before flipping it on. (4) **Readability** — the boot-gate decision compares against the `ReachabilityReportStatus` alias name to match its parameter type, and the cross-shard sample-dedup rationale was corrected (execution ids are globally unique and each lives on exactly one shard). (5) **P1 — run the boot gate BEFORE workers spawn (Codex).** The AC4 gate originally ran *after* `HarvestRunner::start` had already spawned the worker poll loop, so under `orphaned_workflows = fail` + `worker_enabled` a worker could CLAIM and terminally FAIL an orphaned-type execution (no registered handler → `fail_task_and_execution` → `WorkflowFailed` + `FAILED` state) during the boot window, *before* the after-the-fact abort tore the runner down — defeating the gate's protective purpose (default `warn` was unaffected — nothing aborts). Fixed by moving the gate to run BEFORE `HarvestRunner::start` (right after the multi-shard config pre-flight, before any admission globals are published), so no task can be claimed when it fires and an Abort is a bare `return Err` with no runner/gate-refresh/outbox teardown. The gate now calls a new single-shard report core `workflow_reachability::build_reachability_report_single_shard(registered, pool, filter)` that reuses the existing `observe_shard` + `build_report_from_observations` helpers (so it cannot drift from `build_workflow_reachability_report`) but needs NO started runtime: `registered` is derived directly from the owned `BuiltHarvest` (new `BuiltHarvest::workflow_infos()` accessor, workflow names UNION `dags().filter(workflow_handler.is_some())` names — the DAG union replicating `build_workflow_reachability_report`'s registry-key + `registered_dag_names` union exactly, load-bearing because `registry.workflows` omits unified-DAG names), and `gate_pool` is a clone of `harvest_pool` captured before it is moved into the runner resources. The plugin is single-shard-only (multi-shard configs are rejected upstream), so the single-shard report reads the identical rows the started-runtime cross-shard fan-out would. `build_workflow_reachability_report(&HarvestApiState, query)` and the HTTP route are behaviorally unchanged. Crash-loop safety is preserved: a DB read failure encodes as `status == Unavailable` inside the (now infallible) report, and `startup_orphan_decision(Fail, ., Unavailable) == Warn` (never `Abort`). New tests (env-URL local Postgres): `gate_report_core_needs_no_runtime` (structural proof — the abort decision resolves from just a registered set + pool, no `HarvestApiState`) and `gate_is_side_effect_free_orphan_task_untouched` (a seeded orphan's claimable task stays `PENDING`/unclaimed, its execution `RUNNING`, and no `WorkflowFailed` is appended — the deterministic analogue of "no worker touched the orphan run"). **Known follow-up (not fixed here):** the standalone `HarvestRunner::start` embedder path has no orphan gate at all and carries the same latent leak; a separate issue should add an equivalent pre-worker check inside the runner. (6) **P2 — the gate must query the pool the runner will (Codex).** The pre-runner gate cloned its pool from `harvest_pool`, but `PreparedHarvestRuntime::build` gives `WorkerConfig::with_sharded_pool` PRECEDENCE over `harvest_pool` — so a `HarvestBuilder::with_sharded_pool` deployment had the workers poll one database while the gate queried another; under `fail` the gate could validate the wrong DB, miss an orphan, and the worker would then poll+fail it, bypassing the protection. Fixed by extracting the pool-resolution precedence into a **single source of truth**, `runner::resolve_runtime_storage_pool(resources_sharded_pool, worker_config_sharded_pool, harvest_pool)`, called by BOTH `PreparedHarvestRuntime::build` and the plugin gate (the gate feeds it the exact inputs `build` uses — the runner-level override via the new `HarvestRunnerResources::sharded_pool_override()`, which the plugin never sets; WorkerConfig's sharded pool; the `harvest_pool` clone — and then queries `resolved.clone_inner()`, the same default-shard pool the workers poll), so the `sharded_pool`-over-`harvest_pool` precedence can never drift between them. Pinned by `runner::tests::resolve_runtime_storage_pool_precedence` (DB-free — `max_size`-tagged pools assert WorkerConfig's sharded pool wins over `harvest_pool`, a runner-level override wins over WorkerConfig, none falls back to `harvest_pool`) and `gate_resolves_sharded_pool_not_config_pool` (env-URL Postgres — `harvest_pool` unconnectable, the sharded pool the real DB holding the orphan; the decision resolves to `Abort`, only reachable if the shared resolver read the sharded pool's DB, since querying `harvest_pool` would be `Unavailable` → `Warn`). (7) **P2 — an incomplete report must warn, not silently continue (Codex).** A startup DB blip surfaces the single-shard gate as a **successful** report with `status == Unavailable` and no rows, so `orphaned == false`. The prior `startup_orphan_decision` short-circuited `!orphaned → Continue` for every action, so under `fail` a DB blip *silently continued* — no warning that orphan detection never actually ran, contradicting the documented crash-loop-safe intent (degrade an *incomplete* report to a warning rather than ignore it). The "clean boot never warns" deviation over-reached into the "couldn't-determine" case. Fixed the single-source-of-truth `startup_orphan_decision` to the refined table: `Off → Continue`; `Warn`/`Fail` + **incomplete report** (`Partial`/`Unavailable`) → `Warn` regardless of `orphaned` (never `Abort` — crash-loop safety preserved); `Warn`/`Fail` + **complete report** + no orphans → `Continue` (a *confirmed* clean boot never warns); `Warn`/`Fail` + complete + orphaned → `Warn`/`Abort`. Only the cells `(Unavailable|Partial) × !orphaned × (Warn|Fail)` flip `Continue → Warn`; the `Abort` condition is unchanged (`orphaned && Complete && Fail`). This is distinct from the report-builder-`Err` arm (a DB blip is a successful `status == Unavailable` report, not an `Err`), so the fix lives in the decision function. Pinned by a new `unavailable_report_warns_not_silently_continues` truth-table test (both `warn` and `fail` actions, `Unavailable` and `Partial`, `orphaned ∈ {false, true}` → all `Warn`); the existing `fail_aborts_only_on_orphaned_and_complete` / `fail_warns_not_aborts_on_partial_status` / `warn_never_aborts` / `off_skips_entirely` tests stay green unchanged. (8) **P2/P4 — the boot-gate pool selection must be side-effect-free (Codex).** The P2 fix (item 6) had the gate call `resolve_runtime_storage_pool`, whose single-shard case goes `HarvestDbPool::from` → `ShardedDbPool::single`, which **writes the process global `GLOBAL_SHARDED_POOL`**. So the gate's `Abort` (which returns before `HarvestRunner::start` owns anything) left a global installed — a failed second-runtime startup in the same process would point completion-trigger/timeout code at the aborted runtime's DB, breaking the whole point of the early-gate move (an aborting gate must mutate no process global). Fixed by splitting the resolution into two helpers sharing one precedence source of truth (`pick_runtime_pool_source`): `resolve_runtime_storage_pool` (the **install** path, unchanged, used by `PreparedHarvestRuntime::build` on the normal startup path — still installs the global for the single-shard case as intended) and the new `select_runtime_shard0_pool` (the **read** path — returns the shard-0 `DbPool` handle honoring the same precedence but installs nothing: it reads shard 0 from an already-constructed `ShardedDbPool` via `pool_for`, or returns the `harvest_pool` handle directly, and never calls `ShardedDbPool::single`/`from_map`). The gate now calls `select_runtime_shard0_pool`, so it queries the same DB the workers will (P2 preserved) AND installs no global (P4 fixed); the real global install stays exactly where it was in `HarvestRunner::start`, unchanged for the happy path. `HarvestRunnerResources::sharded_pool_override()` now returns a borrow so the gate's selection clones nothing. Pinned by `runner::tests::select_runtime_shard0_pool_precedence` (DB-free — the read selector honors the same precedence as the install helper) and a dedicated own-binary test `gate_no_global_install.rs` (deterministic global state: a fresh process starts with `GLOBAL_SHARDED_POOL` unset; after `select_runtime_shard0_pool` in both the sharded and single cases the global is unchanged, while the contrast call to `resolve_runtime_storage_pool` DOES install it — proving the gate uses the side-effect-free helper).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Active-workflow population gauge — see issue #770. **Implemented.** New continuously-sampled gauge `harvest.workflow.active` (`METRIC_WORKFLOW_ACTIVE`) reports the count of currently-active workflow executions, labeled by `workflow` (workflow-type name) and `state` (bounded to exactly two values: `running` / `paused`). It is the live in-progress population signal the metric catalogue lacked — a steady rise while `harvest.workflow.terminal` stays flat is the signature of a leak or backlog (starts outpacing completions), distinct from a healthy burst that later drains. **Source & sampling.** A dedicated background sampler `worker::spawn_workflow_active_sampler` (a near-copy of `spawn_history_oversized_sampler`, gated on `metrics.is_enabled()` since it issues SQL) runs on the worker's `poll_interval` and calls `worker::sample_active_workflow_counts`, a shard-local `SELECT workflow_name, state, COUNT(*) … WHERE state IN ('RUNNING','PAUSED') GROUP BY workflow_name, state`. Counts are summed across every shard of the worker's `ShardedDbPool` for a fleet-wide gauge. A read failure on any shard skips the whole tick (never false-clears the gauge during an outage); a `(workflow, state)` pair present last tick but absent this tick is zero-filled so a drained pair falls back to `0` rather than going stale. The emit/skip/ zero-fill decision is the pure, unit-tested `worker::compute_active_gauge_emissions`. **Bounded cardinality.** The `state` label can only ever be `running` or `paused` — enforced by construction via the bounded `worker::ActiveWorkflowState` enum (`from_db_str` maps only `RUNNING`/`PAUSED`, everything else → `None` and is dropped with a debug log as defense-in-depth). Per ADR-0001 §7, `execution.id` is never a label. Total series is bounded by `workflow_types × 2`. `PAUSED` runs (issue #383) count under `state="paused"`; nd-blocked runs (issue #603) stay `RUNNING` and count under `state="running"` — no special handling. **Three-touchpoint metric recipe:** (1) `telemetry.rs` — `pub const METRIC_WORKFLOW_ACTIVE` + `pub const METRIC_LABEL_STATE` + the no-op-default `MetricsRecorder::record_workflow_active(workflow, state: &str, count)` trait method; (2) `metrics_rs_adapter.rs` — the `gauge!` bridge with `workflow`/`state` labels; (3) a real capturing-recorder adapter test asserting the registered gauge key, labels, and `set` value (`5.0`). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no shard-routing/replay change** — read-only over `harvest_workflow_executions.state`, no write path, no event schema surface. **Anti-drift registries:** dashboard panel "Active workflows by type & state" (`docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`, `max by (workflow, state)`), `DASHBOARD_PROMETHEUS_SERIES` + `SERIES_LABELS` (`dashboard_pack_docs.rs`), alert rule `harvest_workflow_population_leak` (`docs/alerts/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`) with a full runbook section (`docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md`), `REQUIRED_ALERTS` + `STABLE_PROMETHEUS_METRICS` (`alert_pack_docs.rs`), README mapping row, ADR-0001 §7 catalogue row, `docs/telemetry.md` call-site + labels tables, `metrics_coverage.rs` `RecordingMetrics` coverage, and a `linux autumn-harvest integration` manifest row for the DB test. **Tests, TDD red→green:** R1 telemetry const/no-op unit tests; R2 bounded-enum `from_db_str`/`as_str` unit tests + R5 `compute_active_gauge_emissions` zero-fill/skip-on-read-failure unit tests (both in `worker.rs`, run under the all-features lib step); R3 capturing-recorder gauge-value bridge test (`metrics_rs_adapter.rs`); R4 DB integration test (`tests/integration/active_workflow_gauge_tests.rs`) asserting the grouped read counts RUNNING/PAUSED per type and excludes terminal executions — executed against a real local Postgres 16.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Chain-scoped workflow lifetime cap — see issue #617. A **chain-scoped lifetime cap** (`chain_execution_timeout`) distinct from the per-run `execution_timeout` (#243): it is anchored at the FIRST run's start and CARRIED VERBATIM across every continue-as-new, so a runaway loop cannot escape the cap by continuing-as-new. Enforced by the existing timeout scanner and the existing `WorkflowExecutionTimedOut` event — **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant**. **Storage** (one additive migration `20260714000000_harvest_workflow_chain_timeout`, mirroring #243's dual-column shape): two nullable columns on `harvest_workflow_executions` — `chain_execution_timeout INTERVAL NULL` (the chain-cap DURATION) and `chain_deadline_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL` (the absolute enforcement deadline, `first_run.started_at + chain_execution_timeout`, copied verbatim into every continue-as-new successor). Partial index `idx_harvest_executions_chain_deadline ON (chain_deadline_at) WHERE state = 'RUNNING' AND chain_deadline_at IS NOT NULL`. Both columns added to `schema.rs`, `WorkflowExecution` (read struct — additive serialized fields on the nested `.execution` describe surface, matching the `deadline_at`/`sla_deadline_at` precedent, non-breaking, no contract-registry change) and `NewWorkflowExecution` (insert struct). **Anchor & inheritance rules** (the core semantic): **Fresh chain-origin start** (HTTP start, scheduler tick/backfill, typed stub, etc.): `chain_deadline_at = target_start_time + effective_chain_timeout`. **Continue-as-new successor** (`worker::persist_workflow_continue_as_new`): CARRY BOTH COLUMNS VERBATIM — copy the predecessor's absolute `chain_deadline_at`, never recompute `now + timeout` (the per-run `deadline_at`/`sla_deadline_at` right above it are re-anchored; the chain deadline is not). **Workflow-level retry (#523)** (`worker.rs`): CARRY — `StartWorkflowParams.inherited_chain_deadline_at = exec_ref.chain_deadline_at` used verbatim (a retry is the same logical run continuing). **Reset fork (#148)** (`reset::insert_fork_execution`): RE-ANCHOR — a fresh chain origin (`chain_deadline_at = now + source.chain_execution_timeout`), consistent with `first_exec_id: None`/`schedule_id: None` (the #488 lineage-break precedent). **Child workflow** (`worker.rs`): a fresh chain origin resolving the child's OWN `WorkflowInfo.chain_execution_timeout` at spawn, exactly as it resolves the child's per-run `execution_timeout`/`sla` — awaited children resolve it (`now + effective`); the detached-child path (which resolves no `execution_timeout` at spawn) gets `None`, matching the existing pattern precisely. **Effective resolution + ceiling (AC4 — a deliberate divergence from #243):** the pure `timeout::effective_chain_timeout(workflow, ceiling)` returns the MIN of all present values, and `None` only if both are absent — so the builder ceiling acts as BOTH a cap AND a fleet-wide DEFAULT (`(None, Some(c)) => Some(c)`). This diverges from #243's per-run ceiling (which only caps a *specified* value, `(None, Some) => None`) so an operator can cap every chain even when a workflow under-specifies. Documented in code and `docs/getting-started/07-reliability-knobs.md`. **Config surfaces (AC4):** `#[workflow(chain_execution_timeout = "7d")]` macro attribute (parsed exactly like `execution_timeout`, added to the "unsupported attribute" list); `WorkflowInfo::chain_execution_timeout` field + `with_chain_execution_timeout` fluent builder; `HarvestBuilder::max_workflow_chain_timeout(...)` ceiling + `max_workflow_chain_timeout_ceiling()` accessor (mirrors `max_workflow_execution_timeout`); `WorkflowSchedule::chain_execution_timeout` field + `with_chain_execution_timeout` builder are **currently inert** (not persisted on `harvest_schedules`, not read at tick — at exact parity with #243's own dead `WorkflowSchedule::execution_timeout`; kept for API symmetry). The *functional* schedule-level chain default reaches scheduled runs through the workflow-type `#[workflow(chain_execution_timeout = "…")]` attribute inherited via `WorkflowInfo` at tick, plus the fleet-wide ceiling. **AC4 fleet-wide ceiling threading** (review fix): the ceiling (which doubles as a fleet-wide default) is applied at these ORIGIN start paths — plain HTTP start, signal-with-start, update-with-start, batch start, trigger-now, and workflow backfill (via `HarvestApiState::max_workflow_chain_timeout()`), and the scheduler tick (both the tick-direct and buffered-drain fire sites, tick-throttle and buffered-throttle included) via a new `HandlerRegistry::max_workflow_chain_timeout` field, since the core scheduler has no `api_state`. Debounce/throttle/batch DEFERRED starts carry the declared cap + ceiling through two additive `DebounceStartOptions` fields (`chain_execution_timeout_secs`, `max_workflow_chain_timeout_ceiling_secs`) resolved at admission and threaded at all four fire sites. **Documented limitation (not covered by the fleet-wide default, parity-consistent with their per-run-ceiling treatment):** completion-trigger starts, the Vantage UI manual schedule trigger, the webhook cross-shard outbox, webhook-subscription starts, and the typed Rust client stub's `signal_with_start`/`update_with_start` pass `None`/`None` — a workflow-type `#[workflow(chain_execution_timeout = "…")]` attribute (or the HTTP route) still caps runs from those paths. DAGs carry NO chain cap (the `#[dag]` macro has no chain attr; DAG start paths pass `None`). `StartWorkflowParams` gains three fields (`chain_execution_timeout`, `max_workflow_chain_timeout_ceiling`, `inherited_chain_deadline_at`), defaulted `None` at every construction site except the retry site and the resolving HTTP/scheduler/typed-stub start sites. `WorkflowHandleClient` and the plugin `HarvestApiState` mirror the ceiling (`with_max_workflow_chain_timeout` / `set_max_workflow_chain_timeout` / `max_workflow_chain_timeout()`), wired from `BuiltHarvest::max_workflow_chain_timeout`. **Deliberately NOT threaded into `WorkflowContext`/`ctx.deadline()`/`should_continue_as_new()`** (issue #772 stays bound to the per-run `deadline_at`) — the chain cap is SCANNER-ONLY enforcement, so a runaway loop cannot "escape" it via CAN. **Not shifted on pause/resume** — `chain_deadline_at` is absolute wall-clock (runaway-protection/compliance reading; chain-deadline extension is out of scope). **Scanner (AC2, timeout.rs):** `enforce_workflow_execution_timeouts` selects `state='RUNNING' AND ((deadline_at < NOW()) OR (chain_deadline_at < NOW()))`; the const `workflow_execution_timeout_query()` string reflects the same disjunct. Per expired row, the pure `classify_workflow_timeout(deadline_at, chain_deadline_at, now) -> (fired, TimeoutKind)` decides which fired with **chain precedence** (a chain-only expiry has no per-run `deadline_at` and is handled without panicking). New additive `TimeoutType::WorkflowChain` enum variant (distinct Display "workflow chain lifetime exceeded"; NOT a `WorkflowEvent` variant) used for chain timeouts' error string. **Metric (AC6):** new counter `harvest.workflow.chain_timeout` (`METRIC_WORKFLOW_CHAIN_TIMEOUT`, labels `workflow`/`queue`; additive no-op default `record_workflow_chain_timeout` on `MetricsRecorder`, bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter`). The scanner emits it for `TimeoutKind::Chain` and `harvest.workflow.timeout` for `TimeoutKind::Run`; both still emit `harvest.workflow.terminal{outcome="timed_out"}` (the chain-vs-run distinction lives only in the two timeout counters). Dashboard panel in `docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`, catalogue rows in `docs/telemetry.md` and ADR-0001 §7, and the anti-drift `dashboard_pack_docs` coverage gate updated (series + label ground truth). **Backward compatible:** `None` default everywhere; a workflow with no chain cap and no ceiling behaves byte-for-byte as before. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no replay-determinism impact.** **Docs/examples:** `docs/getting-started/07-reliability-knobs.md` (run-cap vs chain-cap decision, runaway-loop story, ceiling-as-default, absolute-wall-clock/pause note); `examples/long_running.rs` (run-cap vs chain-cap usage). **Tests, TDD red→green:** pure unit tests in `timeout.rs` (`effective_chain_timeout` truth table incl. the AC4 divergence, `classify_workflow_timeout` chain-precedence/run-only/chain-only-no-panic, query-const chain disjunct, chain metric name), `error.rs`/`telemetry.rs`/`metrics_rs_adapter.rs` (variant Display, metric const, no-op default + bridge), macro parse + `with_chain_execution_timeout` builder tests (`macros_workflow.rs`); DB integration tests in `tests/integration/chain_timeout_tests.rs` (scanner fires on chain cap where per-run cap alone would not; chain-only expiry no-panic; per-run vs chain counter separation; origin anchor; inherited-verbatim; ceiling-as-default and ceiling-caps-min; and the AC7/AC9 worker-driven money test — a real continue-as-new carries `chain_deadline_at` verbatim, falsifying the re-anchor hypothesis).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): `WorkflowIdConflictPolicy` for idempotent plain workflow starts — see issue #685. Splits the single, overloaded `WorkflowIdReusePolicy` into two **orthogonal** axes so an idempotent plain start can express "attach to a currently-running run" without abusing the reuse semantics that were designed for terminal priors: `WorkflowIdReusePolicy` (unchanged, 4 variants) governs **TERMINAL** priors (COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMED_OUT). New `WorkflowIdConflictPolicy` (`types.rs`, re-exported from `lib.rs`) governs **ACTIVE** (RUNNING/PAUSED) priors: `Unspecified` (default — defer to the reuse policy's native active behavior), `Fail` (→ `Err(AlreadyExists)`), `UseExisting` (attach: return the running handle, `created == false`, no new `WorkflowStarted` event, no task enqueued, no cancel), `TerminateExisting` (cancel + start fresh). Wire values `unspecified`/`fail`/`use_existing`/`terminate_existing`. The two axes **compose** in the start-path admission logic: the conflict axis has no effect on a terminal prior, and the reuse axis has no effect on an active prior (except via the `Unspecified` fallback). Because `Unspecified` maps each reuse policy to its exact documented active behavior (`AllowDuplicate`→Attach, `RejectDuplicate`→Fail, `AllowDuplicateFailedOnly`→Attach, `TerminateIfRunning`→Terminate), **every existing caller is byte-for-byte unchanged (AC-6)**. **Core changes (`execution.rs`):** new pure helpers `ActiveConflictBehavior { Fail, Attach, Terminate }`, `is_active_conflict_state(state)` (RUNNING|PAUSED), `effective_active_conflict_behavior(reuse, conflict)` (all `pub`). `start_will_create_new_execution` gains a `conflict_policy` parameter and branches active-vs-terminal first. `StartWorkflowParams` gains a `conflict_policy: WorkflowIdConflictPolicy` field (swept to `Unspecified` at ~123 literal sites workspace-wide). The start transaction's existing-prior `match` was restructured to branch on active-vs-terminal first: an active prior is resolved by the effective conflict behavior; a terminal prior is resolved by the reuse axis exactly as before. **Admission-gate / pre-check interaction:** the two-transaction `TerminateIfRunning` pre-check cancel and its unlocked POINT-1 gate now fire on `terminate_via_pre_check = (reuse == TerminateIfRunning && effective == Terminate)` — identical to the old `reuse == TerminateIfRunning` for `Unspecified`, and correctly excluding `TerminateIfRunning` + `UseExisting`/`Fail` (so a `UseExisting` override never cancels the prior). A conflict-driven Terminate with a non-`TerminateIfRunning` reuse (e.g. `AllowDuplicate` + `TerminateExisting`) is handled **atomically inside** the start transaction (active branch: `inline_cancel` + `replace_execution`), never via a pre-check cancel that would otherwise route the just-cancelled prior through the reuse policy's attach branch. This deviates from the literal spec's "POINT-1 gates on `effective == Terminate`" (which would wrongly block an attach to a terminal prior); the goal — "the gate is applied exactly when a fresh execution WILL be created, skipped for a genuine attach" — is met precisely. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no persisted field** — `conflict_policy` is a request-time caller concern only, exactly like `reuse_policy`. Plugin/CLI/HTTP wiring of the new axis is a follow-up; the plugin's two `start_will_create_new_execution` call sites and the `#[workflow]` typed-stub currently pass `Unspecified` (behavior-preserving). **Tests:** unit matrix in `execution.rs` (`start_will_create_tests` extended with the active-conflict axis + an explicit legacy-truth-table `unspecified_matches_today` regression guard; new `active_conflict_tests` for the helpers). DB matrix in `integration_e2e.rs`: `conflict_use_existing_running_attaches_no_new_run` (attach, prior stays RUNNING, zero new events), `conflict_use_existing_paused_attaches`, `conflict_terminate_if_running_reuse_plus_use_existing_completed_starts_fresh` and `..._running_attaches` (AC-3 corners, proving the pre-check gate fix), `conflict_fail_running_errors`, `conflict_terminate_existing_running_cancels_and_starts_fresh`, `conflict_unspecified_preserves_allow_duplicate_running_attaches` (AC-6 guard), and `conflict_concurrency_race_use_existing_converges` (the success-metric proof — 20 concurrent `UseExisting` starts against one running prior all converge on the same `exec_id`, zero `AlreadyExists`, zero terminations). `setup_test_db` now honours `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` for local-Postgres runs when Docker is unavailable. **Plugin + CLI + HTTP wiring (issue #685, second half)** Exposes and enforces the `conflict_policy` axis on the standalone HTTP start route and the CLI (the core half above landed it behind `Unspecified`-defaulted plugin call sites): **HTTP `POST /workflows/{workflow_name}/start`** (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`): new optional body field `conflict_policy` (`unspecified`|`fail`|`use_existing`|`terminate_existing`), parsed by `parse_conflict_policy` (mirrors `parse_reuse_policy`; unknown value → `400`, echoed). Threaded into **both** the plain and the #808 idempotency-key `StartWorkflowParams`. An attach (`use_existing` over an active prior) returns `200` + `created:false`; a fresh replacement (`terminate_existing`) returns `201`; `fail` over an active prior returns `409`. **`started_fresh` surfacing (AC-4/AC-7):** the no-key success response now includes `started_fresh: Some(start.created)` **only when the request sent a `conflict_policy` field** (even `unspecified`); omitting the field omits `started_fresh` so the response is byte-for-byte identical to a pre-#685/#808 build. **Admin gate (security parity):** the handler's top-of-function admin gate — previously `reuse_policy == terminate_if_running` — now **also** requires admin for `conflict_policy == terminate_existing`, since both can forcibly cancel a live prior. Without admin → `401`. (This closes a privilege gap that would otherwise let `conflict_policy` reach the identical cancel-and-replace behavior without auth.) **Deferred-start mutual exclusion:** a non-default `conflict_policy` combined with a throttle / debounce / batch policy returns `400` (the start is deferred and has no active prior to resolve at request time), mirroring the `idempotency_key`-vs-deferred-start rule. `conflict_policy` + `idempotency_key` compose (allowed). **Contract:** `conflict_policy` added to `management_api_request_fields()` and `docs/api-contract.json` (request field + `401`/`400`/`409` error descriptions + success-note `started_fresh` semantics); `contract_regression` parity guard stays green. **CLI:** `harvest workflow start --conflict-policy <unspecified|fail|use_existing|terminate_existing>` (`autumn-harvest-cli`), mapped 1:1 onto the body field; omitting the flag sends no field. **Docs:** CLAUDE.md "Standalone Start — Conflict Policy" matrix; `docs/getting-started/10-operations.md` "Conflict policies" section. **Tests:** plugin `parse_conflict_policy` unit tests + a DB/HTTP suite `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/conflict_policy_integration.rs` (attach-200, AC-3 terminate_if_running+use_existing corner, fail-409, terminate_existing-201-cancels-prior, omit-preserves-response, unknown-400, throttle-mutual-exclusion-400, no-admin-401, and a 20-way concurrent `use_existing` convergence proof) — wired into `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`. CLI mapping tests (`conflict_policy_tests`) + `contract_coverage` body-field coverage. **Post-review hardening (issue #685 review)** **Capability-precise admin gate (narrowed).** The plugin start handler's admin gate no longer raw-string-matches `reuse_policy == terminate_if_running || conflict_policy == terminate_existing` before parsing. It now parses **both** policies first and requires admin **iff the request can cancel a live run** — i.e. `effective_active_conflict_behavior(reuse, conflict) == ActiveConflictBehavior::Terminate`. This keeps `conflict=terminate_existing` (any reuse) and `reuse=terminate_if_running` + default/omitted conflict admin-gated (unchanged), while **allowing the flagship non-admin idempotent-starter shape** `reuse=terminate_if_running` + `conflict=use_existing` (resolves to *attach*, provably cannot cancel a live run) — previously wrongly forced to require admin. `terminate_if_running` + `fail` (resolves to `409`) is likewise now non-admin. The gate moves after the two policy parses (an invalid value now returns `400` before the gate) and after the #808 committed-replay probe (safe: a replay returns the already-committed run and performs no new cancel, and a non-admin can never commit a Terminate start). New HTTP tests: `terminate_if_running_plus_use_existing_is_not_admin_gated` (RUNNING prior → `200` attach, zero `WorkflowCancelled`; also the HTTP AC-3 RUNNING-prior corner), `terminate_if_running_plus_use_existing_over_completed_is_not_admin_gated` (COMPLETED prior → `201` fresh), `terminate_if_running_without_conflict_still_requires_admin` (no-regression `401`). **AC-2 coverage gap closed.** New core DB tests `conflict_terminate_existing_paused_cancels_and_starts_fresh` (the IN-TRANSACTION `inline_cancel` + `replace_execution` on a PAUSED prior — a path the pre-check-based native `TerminateIfRunning` never reaches: asserts fresh `created`, prior sealed `CONTINUED_AS_NEW`, exactly one `WorkflowCancelled`) and `conflict_fail_paused_errors` (`Fail` over PAUSED → `Err(AlreadyExists)`, `existing_state == "PAUSED"`). **AC-4 strengthened.** `conflict_use_existing_running_attaches_no_new_run` now also asserts at the DB level that a `UseExisting` attach enqueues **no** `harvest_task_queue` row against the allocated-but-unused fresh `exec_id`. **Concurrency note documented.** Concurrent `terminate_existing` starts of the same `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` against one live prior are last-writer-wins; a loser may observe a transient `404 NotFound` (a pre-existing `load_workflow_execution_by_key_for_update` race, more reachable without a pre-check). It does not corrupt data, deadlock, or double-run — retry the start (documented in `execution.rs`, CLAUDE.md, and `10-operations.md`). **Coverage nits.** Mutual-exclusion guard now exercised for **all three** deferred-start legs (`conflict_policy_on_debounced_workflow_returns_400`, `conflict_policy_on_batched_workflow_returns_400`, alongside the existing throttle test). Docstring drift in `start_throttle_integration.rs` updated to the 3-arg `start_will_create_new_execution(_, _, Unspecified)` signature. **Post-review hardening, round 2 (issue #685 review, Codex P2 — concurrent `terminate_existing` convergence)** **Bounded seal-race retry replaces the transient `NotFound`.** The concurrency note above documented a real gap: concurrent `conflict=terminate_existing` (or any replace-type) starts of one live `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` could leave a LOSER with a transient `HarvestError::NotFound` (→ HTTP `404`) instead of a successful idempotent start. The loser's post-INSERT `load_workflow_execution_by_key_for_update` (a single `FOR UPDATE` SELECT) takes its statement snapshot before a concurrent winner commits, blocks on the prior's row lock, and — on the winner's commit — sees the prior filtered out by the load's non-sealed filter (winner sealed it → `CONTINUED_AS_NEW`) while the winner's freshly-inserted replacement row is invisible to that same statement's snapshot → the load returns `None` → `NotFound`. This was a pre-existing race in the shared active-`Terminate` branch, now the PRIMARY path for `terminate_existing` (which has no pre-check cancellation), so newly reachable on a normal concurrent-delivery scenario. **Fix (in-transaction bounded retry).** The active-conflict load is now wrapped in a bounded retry loop (`execution.rs`, `start_or_load_workflow_execution_collect`): under READ COMMITTED each SELECT statement gets a fresh snapshot, so re-issuing the load after the winner has committed picks up the winner's replacement RUNNING row and the start CONVERGES (last-writer-wins) instead of surfacing a transient `NotFound`. The loser holds no conflicting lock after a `None` load (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` never locks the conflicting row; a `None` `FOR UPDATE` locks nothing), and once a row IS found and `FOR UPDATE`-locked the subsequent `inline_cancel` + `replace_execution` cannot be sealed out from under us. Each retry's `FOR UPDATE` naturally blocks on the current lock holder (forward progress, not a busy-loop), so N concurrent contenders serialize and the last loser waits behind at most N-1 winners; the cap (`SEAL_RACE_MAX_LOAD_RETRIES = 64`) is set generously above realistic concurrent-delivery bursts, with a small fixed backoff guarding the pathological "prior sealed without a replacement" case (e.g. a concurrent reset), which falls back to the pre-existing terminal `NotFound`. Scoped to the seal race only (a `None` load after a no-op INSERT) — transparent to every non-racing path and to `UseExisting`/`Fail`/`Attach`. The `idempotency_key` path (`in_outer_transaction = true`, #808) is untouched — its same-key dedup already collapses concurrent same-key retries. **Docs corrected.** The "concurrent terminate_existing … a loser may get a transient NotFound and should retry" note is updated in `execution.rs`, CLAUDE.md, and `docs/getting-started/10-operations.md` to reflect that the transient failure is now handled internally: concurrent `terminate_existing` on one key is last-writer-wins and CONVERGES to a single surviving run via a bounded internal retry — no transient `NotFound` is surfaced. **Test.** New `conflict_terminate_existing_concurrent_converges` (`autumn-harvest/tests/integration/integration_e2e.rs`): seed one RUNNING prior, spawn 20 concurrent `allow_duplicate + terminate_existing` starts on a shared pool (multi-thread runtime), assert ZERO calls errored (no `NotFound`, no `AlreadyExists`) and the storm settled to exactly ONE surviving RUNNING execution with all others sealed. The race is timing-dependent, so the test guards the convergence invariant rather than deterministically reproducing the pre-fix 404. **Docs (contract) — capability-precise start admin gate (Codex P2).** The `POST /workflows/{workflow_name}/start` `401` note in `docs/api-contract.json` (and the `conflict_policy` field note) claimed `reuse_policy=terminate_if_running` unconditionally requires admin. Corrected to describe the gate by the resolved active-conflict behavior: admin is required only when the request can cancel a live (RUNNING/PAUSED) prior — `conflict_policy=terminate_existing` (any reuse), or `reuse_policy=terminate_if_running` with the default/omitted conflict — so the flagship non-admin idempotent-starter shape (`terminate_if_running` + `use_existing`) is documented as non-admin and API-contract-following clients no longer needlessly admin-route it. Docs-only; signal-with-start / update-with-start notes (which lack `conflict_policy`) are accurate and unchanged.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Server-side overdue-schedule detection — see issue #696. Harvest's schedule suite (jitter, overlap policy, calendars, backfill, catchup windows, `end_at`/`max_runs` bounds, HA claim exclusivity #350, failure-driven auto-pause #360) had no answer to the most common cron failure mode: a schedule that should be firing **silently stops** (scheduler loop not ticking, `next_run_at` wedged in the past, an HA claim that never released, all scheduler replicas down, or a config slip). The only prior signal was the starter alert `harvest_schedule_missed_runs`, which *inferred* a problem from the **absence** of `harvest.schedule.runs` (`increase(...runs...[1h]) == 0`) — brittle, forces operators to hand-encode each schedule's cadence into Prometheus, noisy for low-frequency schedules, and unable to name *which* schedule is wedged or *how late*. Since Harvest already stores every schedule's `next_run_at` + cadence in Postgres, it can compute "overdue" authoritatively server-side. **Read/observability slice over existing `harvest_schedules` columns: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, schedules fire byte-identically.** **Pure predicate (AC2, `scheduler.rs`).** New `pub fn schedule_overdue(schedule, next_run_at, now, jitter, tick_interval, is_paused, auto_paused_at, exhausted_at, at_capacity) -> OverdueVerdict` (unit-tested, no DB). A schedule is overdue iff it is *active* AND `now − next_run_at > grace`, where `grace = cadence_step + jitter + tick_interval` — so a healthy schedule caught mid-tick (tick term), deferred by jitter (jitter term), or one full cadence behind (cadence-step term) is never flagged. Cadence step is derived by the private `cadence_step` helper: the interval for `Interval`, and the gap to the next occurrence strictly after the missed slot for `Cron`/`CronInTimezone` (so DST-variable cron steps use the actual upcoming step), reusing the existing `next_run_after`/`interval_period` primitives directly. `pub const SCHEDULER_TICK_INTERVAL` re-exports the scheduler's own 1s tick so read/sampler callers pass the identical grace term. `OverdueVerdict { overdue: bool, overdue_by_secs: Option<i64> }` reports `now − next_run_at` (not `lag − grace`). **AC3 exclusions + §2 false-positive guard.** Intentionally-not-firing states are never overdue: `is_paused`, `auto_paused_at` set (#360), `Schedule::Manual`, and `end_at`/`max_runs`-exhausted (`exhausted_at`, #478/#543). The predicate also takes an `at_capacity` (running ≥ `max_active_runs`) suppression input: the scheduler tick **deliberately** holds `next_run_at` at the past due slot while a schedule is at capacity (`OverlapPolicy::Skip` under catchup retains the overdue slot; the catchup dispatch loop defers remaining slots at the cap), so an at-capacity schedule is deliberately deferring, not wedged. Verified against the tick: in *every other* fire decision (Skip without catchup, all Buffer/Cancel/Terminate policies, the normal dispatch path) `next_run_at` advances forward; jitter deferral is bounded by the jitter grace term; end_at/max_runs deferral sets `exhausted_at`; and backfill (#337) creates independent executions and never touches the live schedule's `next_run_at`. So `running ≥ max_active_runs` is the *only* unbounded-lag-without-a-wedge case, and it is suppressed. The suppression is self-healing: once capacity opens, `at_capacity` drops and a genuine wedge is flagged on the next sample. **Read surface (AC1/AC5).** `ScheduleEntry` gains `overdue: bool` + `overdue_by_secs: Option<i64>`, computed in `schedule_entry_from_row` via the pure predicate. Surfaces automatically on both `GET /admin/schedules` (list) and `GET /admin/schedules/{id}` — no new route, no audit/contract-registry churn — riding the existing #756 cross-shard fan-out and conditional-envelope contract. The read's `at_capacity` is computed **shard-locally** on each schedule's own shard (`load_schedule_at_capacity_by_shard`, keyed by schedule id, using the shared `scheduler::schedule_running_basis`), so the read agrees with the gauge and the tick by construction — never a cross-shard sum that could hide a genuine wedge on a schedule's own shard behind unrelated same-named executions elsewhere. Create/re-register responses pass `at_capacity = false` (a fresh `next_run_at` is never overdue); the PATCH response computes it shard-locally (a non-cadence patch preserves a possibly-stale `next_run_at`). **Metric (AC4).** New gauge `harvest.schedule.overdue{kind, name}` (`METRIC_SCHEDULE_OVERDUE`; `record_schedule_overdue(kind, name, overdue)` no-op default on `MetricsRecorder`, bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter` as `set(1.0/0.0)`). Labels are bounded `kind` (`workflow`/`dag`) + registered `name`; per ADR-0001 §7 the schedule/execution id is never a label. Same-named schedules aggregate (overdue if either). **At-capacity basis (§2 false-positive guard — matches the tick exactly).** Shared `scheduler::schedule_running_basis(conn, name)` replicates `tick_one_workflow_schedule`'s own capacity count byte-for-byte: the shard-local `COUNT(RUNNING|PAUSED)` **plus** the #607 pending-throttle backlog (`throttle::pending_throttle_count_for_workflow`) the tick adds before comparing against `max_active_runs`. Both the gauge sampler and the read call it, so a throttle-deferred schedule at capacity (the tick holds `next_run_at` in the past under Skip+catchup) is correctly suppressed rather than spuriously flagged. **Emission (AC5/AC8).** `scheduler::overdue_schedule_samples(conn, now)` computes the verdict for every schedule on one shard (via `schedule_running_basis`, so `at_capacity` fires exactly when the tick would hold `next_run_at`) and returns per-schedule verdicts. A new worker sampler `spawn_schedule_overdue_sampler` (modeled on the DLQ/queue samplers, gated on `is_enabled()`, iterating every shard pool) OR-aggregates verdicts across **all** shard pools into one `(kind, name)` map before emitting — closing the cross-shard last-write-wins masking window a per-pool `.set()` would leave. It runs on a **coarse** cadence (`max(poll_interval, SCHEDULE_OVERDUE_SAMPLE_INTERVAL = 30s)`, since the overdue signal is minute-scale), on the **worker**, not the scheduler tick, so a wedged tick cannot suppress its own health signal and a dead scheduler is still detected while any worker is alive (a *total* process outage falls back to the tertiary absence-of-runs expression + an `up`/scrape-health signal). `scheduler::sample_overdue_schedules(conn, now, metrics)` is a single-shard emit convenience used by the DB tests. The scheduler tick stays byte-identical (AC8). ALL schedules are sampled every pass (including paused/exhausted, which emit `0`) so the gauge stays fresh; deleted schedules go stale (documented in the runbook — cross-check the read). The predicate's `grace = step + jitter + tick` uses checked addition (an unrepresentable grace is treated as not-overdue, never a panic). **Alert + docs (AC7).** `harvest_schedule_missed_runs` in `docs/alerts/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json` now leads with the precise `max by (kind, name) (harvest_schedule_overdue) > 0`, keeps the skipped-counter expression, and retains the absence-of-runs expression only as a tertiary total-process-death signal (paired with `up`). `docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_schedule_missed_runs`, `docs/telemetry.md` (ADR-0001 §7 catalogue + label table), a new dashboard panel in `docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`, and the `docs/api-contract.json` schedule route descriptions are updated. **Tests (AC6).** Pure predicate table tests in `scheduler.rs` (overdue past grace across interval + hourly/5-min/daily/weekly cron with the correct cadence step; healthy within grace incl. the exact-at-grace boundary; jitter absorbed by grace; every AC3 exclusion + `at_capacity`; manual/none/null-next; and a 100-schedule healthy fleet under varied cadence/jitter/overlap reporting **zero** false positives). DB integration suite `tests/integration/scheduler_overdue_tests.rs` (testcontainers + `full_migrations_sql()` + a `RecordingMetrics` capturing `record_schedule_overdue`): wedged→overdue, healthy/paused/exhausted→not-overdue, at-capacity→not-overdue (§2 guard in the DB path), and the returning helper's `overdue_by_secs` lag. Plugin read-field test in `api_scheduler_integration.rs` asserting `overdue`/`overdue_by_secs` on `GET /admin/schedules` and `/{id}`. One new sorted line in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Dry-run preview for batch operations — see issue #769. `POST /api/harvest/batch-operations` (the fleet-wide Cancel/Terminate/Signal surface, #102/#533) — the single most destructive engine surface, acting on **every** workflow matching a `BatchFilter` across all shards with no preview — gains an additive `dry_run: bool` (`#[serde(default)]` = `false`). Reset, worker drain, schedules, and DAG retry were all previewable; batch now is too, so an operator sees the exact blast radius (count + a bounded sample) before committing. `dry_run: false`/omitted → **byte-for-byte unchanged**: `202` + `{batch_job_id}`, the audit row, and the job lifecycle are all identical to a pre-#769 client. `SubmitBatchOperationRequest` has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so pre-#769 clients that never send `dry_run` are unaffected. `dry_run: true` → resolves the SAME filter across ALL shards and returns `200` with `{ dry_run, action, filter, matched_count, per_shard: [{shard_id, matched_count}], sample: [{execution_id, workflow_name, state}], sample_cap (100), sample_truncated, status, unavailable_shards }`. `matched_count` is an EXACT `COUNT(*)` per shard summed (never derived from the capped sample); `sample` is globally capped at 100 across shards (ordered by `id` ascending, so the sample is deterministic across repeated previews); `sample_truncated = matched_count > sample.len()`. Performs **zero** writes — no workflow transitions, no signals, no `harvest_task_queue` rows, no `harvest_batch_jobs` job row, and **no audit row for any outcome** (a preview is read-only introspection, like the other `preview`/`dry_run` surfaces). **Partial-shard degradation (mirrors `POST /workflows/batch_reset`):** an unreachable shard no longer fails the whole preview with a `500`. Each shard's connect/count/sample errors are caught and folded into `status: "partial"` naming the shard in `unavailable_shards: [{shard_id, reason}]` (`"complete"` + omitted `unavailable_shards` on the happy path). When any shard is unavailable, `matched_count`/`per_shard` cover reachable shards ONLY — a documented **lower bound**. The cross-shard accumulation (sum exact counts, fill the GLOBAL sample cap across shards, compute `sample_truncated`, derive `status`/`unavailable_shards`) is a pure, unit-tested helper `fold_batch_shard_previews(Vec<ShardPreviewOutcome>, sample_cap)` in the plugin `api.rs`, so the multi-shard sum / global-cap / partial-degradation logic is testable without a multi-shard database. An empty/criteria-less filter is rejected in `dry_run` mode with the same `400` guard the real submit uses (the shared `batch::BATCH_EMPTY_FILTER_ERR` constant), writing zero audit rows. **Anti-drift (the load-bearing constraint):** the real target resolver, the dry-run count, and the dry-run sample all build their WHERE clause through ONE shared predicate builder — `batch::apply_batch_filters(query, action, filter)` in `autumn-harvest/src/batch.rs` — extracted from `resolve_targets_on_shard`. The two new `db`-gated functions `count_targets_on_shard` (exact `COUNT(*)`, no cap) and `sample_targets_on_shard` (bounded `SELECT (id, workflow_name, state) LIMIT n`) both call it, so a preview can never drift from what a real submit would act on. Proven by the `dry_run_matches_real_submit_target_count` integration test, which asserts the dry-run `matched_count` equals the real job's resolved `total`. Per-action state defaults (Terminate → `state NOT IN ('CANCELLED','TERMINATED')`; Cancel/Signal → `state IN ('RUNNING','PAUSED')`) are shared identically. **Handler:** `submit_batch_operation` (plugin `api.rs`) widened its return type from `Result<(StatusCode, Json<SubmitBatchOperationResponse>), AutumnError>` to `Result<axum::response::Response, AutumnError>` so the 200-preview and 202-submit bodies differ; the 202 arm's bytes are unchanged. The dry-run branch is placed after the action-parse + `KNOWN_WORKFLOW_STATES` validations (so it can echo the resolved action) and before `submit_batch_job` / the signal-payload cap (a preview is filter-determined and deliberately skips the Signal `signal_name` requirement and payload cap — it reports blast radius, not signal validity). The action-parse and unknown-state early-validation audit writes are guarded by `if !request.dry_run` so a malformed dry-run request writes no audit row either. **CLI (`autumn-harvest-cli`):** `harvest batch submit <action> --filter-json … --dry-run [--json]`. The `--dry-run` flag inserts `body["dry_run"] = true` only when set (a real-submit body stays byte-identical to a pre-#769 client). By default the preview renders as a table (count + per-shard breakdown + sample + a truncation note); `--json` prints the raw preview body. A real submit (no `--dry-run`) falls through to the default JSON renderer unchanged. **Contract/registries:** `dry_run` added to the `POST /batch-operations` request-field registry; the polymorphic response's full set of TOP-LEVEL fields — `batch_job_id`, `dry_run`, `action`, `filter`, `matched_count`, `per_shard`, `sample`, `sample_cap`, `sample_truncated`, `status`, `unavailable_shards` — enumerated in BOTH `management_api_response_fields()` AND `docs/api-contract.json` `success_response.fields` (the `GET /workflows/{id}/stack` + `GET /admin/build-routing` precedent, which the `contract_response_fields_match_code_registry` test cross-checks for exact set equality), with `success_response.notes` reserved for the 202-vs-200 polymorphism and the nested `per_shard`/`sample`/`unavailable_shards` object shapes. Route stays classified `Mutating` (no `audit.rs` change) — `dry_run` is a field on a mutating route, so a `dry_run` preview is admin-only (a read-only principal cannot preview). Runbook: a "Fleet-wide batch: preview before you commit" section added to `docs/runbooks/contain-runaway-execution.md`, including the admin-only, Signal-not-validated, partial-lower-bound, and single-shard-seq-scan caveats. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no shard-routing change, no replay/append-only surface.** New core types re-exported from `autumn_harvest::batch`: `BatchTargetSample`, `BATCH_EMPTY_FILTER_ERR`, `count_targets_on_shard`, `sample_targets_on_shard`. Tests: 4 pure (no-DB) `fold_batch_shard_previews` unit tests in the plugin `api.rs` test module (2-shard count sum, GLOBAL sample cap ≠ per-shard, `sample_truncated` boundary at/over cap, one-shard-errored → `status=partial` + lower-bound `matched_count`); 10 plugin integration tests in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/batch_operations_integration.rs` (matched_count + capped/truncated sample with full filter echo + UUID-parseable sample ids + `status:complete`, sample-below-cap-not-truncated, `matched_count == cap` boundary → not truncated, `search_attrs`-filter echo, zero-writes, anti-drift count-equals-real-submit, empty-filter-400-no-audit, Terminate-default-excludes-terminal, real-submit-still-writes-job **plus the correlated `batch.submit`/`succeeded` audit row**, and the `Signal --dry-run` without `signal_name` → 200 + zero `harvest_signals` rows) plus the 12 pre-existing batch tests (regression) — executed green against real Postgres 16; 4 CLI request-mapping tests (`--dry-run` sets the body flag; omitting it adds no key; `Signal --dry-run` without `--signal-name` builds a preview request; a non-dry-run `Signal` without `--signal-name` is rejected by the manual `batch_request` guard) plus 4 CLI unit tests (preview table renderer incl. the `per_shard` block; `--dry-run --json` compact raw body; `--json` without `--dry-run` rejected at clap parse via `requires`). The `Signal` `signal_name` arg dropped clap's `required_if_eq` in favor of the manual guard so a `Signal --dry-run` may omit it. The batch suite's `setup_database()` now honors `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` (creating a fresh per-test database off the admin URL) with a testcontainers fallback, and is registered in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt` (Docker-backed Linux run).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Synthetic liveness canary — see issue #796. **Opt-in built-in synthetic liveness canary** that continuously probes the *live* `start → dispatch → activity → durable-timer → complete` execution path so a wedged pipeline (workers polling but never completing, a stalled scheduler tick, a write-blocked shard) is detected within one probe interval — before any customer workflow misses its SLA — with zero operator-authored workflow code. **Distinct from the #512 replay canary**, which validates *code changes* by replaying in-flight histories; this validates *the running pipeline* by actively executing a throwaway workflow end to end (the two share only the word "canary"; no symbol collision — `is_canary_workflow`/`CANARY_*` vs `run_workflow_canary`/`canary_mode`). **Opt-in and byte-identical when off (AC1):** `HarvestPlugin::synthetic_canary(CanaryConfig::new(interval))` enables it; absent that call the canary is entirely off and the runtime is byte-for-byte identical. The reserved names/predicates live in the core crate (`autumn_harvest::canary`: `CANARY_WORKFLOW_NAME_PREFIX = "__harvest_canary_probe"`, `CANARY_ACTIVITY_NAME`, `is_canary_workflow`, `is_reserved_canary_name`); the plugin (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/canary.rs`) owns registration (hand-built `WorkflowInfo`/`ActivityInfo`, per-writable-shard schedule, self-cleaning retention) and the opt-in `CanaryConfig`. **Probe (AC2/AC3):** for each configured probe queue the plugin registers a per-queue probe workflow `{PREFIX}__{queue}` (a real handler that dispatches one genuinely **non-local** activity on the probe's target queue, then waits on a short **durable** timer, then completes) plus one shared reserved canary activity (`is_local = false`, load-bearing). One canary + schedule per queue so a single wedged worker pool is distinguishable from "some queue is draining". **Per-writable-shard coverage (AC4):** a new additive `#[serde(default)]` `WorkflowSchedule::all_writable_shards` flag (set via `with_all_writable_shards()`) is honored in `register_workflow_schedules_for_shard` (upsert on every `router.writable_shards()` shard) and the fire-path exec_id branch (mint `ExecutionId::new_for_shard(current_shard)`), so a single canary schedule definition runs its own probe loop on every writable shard. Single-shard/off is byte-identical. **`harvest.canary.*` metrics + read model (AC5/AC7):** three metrics `harvest.canary.success` / `harvest.canary.failure` (counters) and `harvest.canary.roundtrip` (histogram), labels **`queue` + `shard` only** — `execution.id` is impossible by construction (three-touchpoint recorder methods take `queue: &str, shard: u16`). Emitted at the two primary terminal sites: `worker.rs::process_workflow_task` (success + roundtrip on Completed) and `timeout.rs::enforce_workflow_execution_timeouts` (failure on a per-probe-timeout). New read-only, admin-guarded `GET /admin/canary` reconstructs per-`(queue, shard)` freshness (`last_success_at`, `age`, `last_roundtrip_ms`, success/failure counts, `stale`) by cross-shard fan-out (`shard_fanout`), unioning the writable-shard grid with observed leftovers; an unreachable shard is named in `unavailable_shards` with `status: partial`/`unavailable` (never a hard 500). Registered across the axum router, `management_api_routes()`/`response_fields()`, `docs/api-contract.json`, and all three `audit` route lists (`RouteClass::ReadOnly`). Dashboard panels + `docs/telemetry.md` catalogue rows added. **Business-observability exclusion (AC8):** a canary probe emits **only** `harvest.canary.*` and contributes to **no** `harvest.workflow.*` business SLO counter. Routed airtight through a single choke point `telemetry::emit_workflow_terminal` (generic over `&(impl MetricsRecorder + ?Sized)`) that skips `is_canary_workflow` probes; **every** `record_workflow_terminal` call site across the engine (worker completion/failure, execution-timeout, poison-pill quarantine, event-batch, execution cancel/terminate ×7, debounce, throttle, and the plugin batch-cancel) routes through it, so a canary can never leak `harvest.workflow.terminal` no matter which terminal path it reaches during exactly the distress the canary exists to detect. `harvest.workflow.started`/`.duration`/`.history_size`/`.continue_as_new` are also gated on `!is_canary` in `process_workflow_task`. `harvest.activity.*`/`harvest.queue.*` are unchanged (the canary legitimately exercises them). The canary is likewise excluded from `GET /workflows` (default list) **and** the stalled-workflow loader (`?no_progress_minutes=N`) unless a caller explicitly filters to a canary `workflow_name`, and from the cross-shard `GET /workflows/count`. `is_reserved_canary_name` is wired into `preflight::required_queues` and `shard_health`'s equivalent so the canary activity's `default_queue: None` never injects a phantom `"default"` required queue (which would flip a healthy non-default-queue deployment to a preflight/readiness failure). **Self-clean retention (AC9):** `register_canary` adds an aggressive self-cleaning per-workflow retention override so the canary's own history is purged shortly after each run even with no global `max_age`. `CanaryConfig::effective_retention` is floored at `max(2 × staleness_window, 1h)` in **every** config path (an explicit `with_retention` below the floor is raised with a warning), so the last success row always outlives the freshness check that reads it — no false-positive stale alert on a healthy pipeline — and is clamped within the core `RetentionConfig` validator's bounds so `try_build()` can never fail. **Config guardrails (AC6):** `CanaryConfig::new` clamps an interval below `MIN_CANARY_INTERVAL` (10s) up (with a warning); the derived `per_probe_timeout` is always in `[PROBE_MIN_RUNTIME (5s), interval - 1s]` — above the probe's own minimum runtime (a dispatched activity + a 1s durable timer + task wakeups) so a **healthy** probe never false-fails, and strictly below the interval so a wedged probe times out before the next tick (non-blocking). `with_per_probe_timeout` clamps out-of-range overrides (0, `>= interval`) into the same band. 30s is the recommended interval. **Deliberate design decision (probe-queue polling):** `register_canary` does **not** force the local worker to poll the probe queue — the probed queue must be polled by some worker in the fleet built from this builder (the fleet whose liveness is being tested). Auto-adding a probe queue to the local worker would make it claim a dedicated remote fleet's real customer tasks and could report a false-"healthy". The default `"default"` queue is already polled by the builder's default worker, so the out-of-the-box config works with no extra wiring; probing any other queue requires the operator wire a worker (local `with_queues` or a separate process) for it. **AC10 — no engine-schema cost:** the canary is registered as an ordinary `#[workflow]`/`#[activity]` on the standard execution path — **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no replay-determinism change**. The `all_writable_shards` flag is an additive `#[serde(default)]` schedule field with a back-compat deserialize test. **P3 behaviors (documented):** an orphaned non-DAG `all_writable_shards` canary schedule left on a shard removed from `writable_shards` keeps firing probes there until the row is manually cleaned; its executions are bounded by retention (self-cleaning), so it is wasted probing, not unbounded growth. A probe queue with no live poller in the fleet under test simply times out — correctly flagging "this queue has no live pollers". **Tests:** core `is_canary_workflow`/`is_reserved_canary_name` predicate unit tests; the `telemetry::emit_workflow_terminal` choke-point record-vs-skip unit test; plugin `CanaryConfig` interval/timeout/retention clamp unit tests, `register_canary` registration + `try_build` unit tests, and pure `build_canary_report` read-model unit tests (fresh/stale/never-succeeded/empty-shard/unreachable-shard/mixed-grid); `GET /admin/canary` HTTP integration + admin-guard tests; the three-metric dashboard/contract/audit anti-drift guards. New DB-backed core suite `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/canary_tests.rs` (RecordingMetrics) drives a real worker completing a probe (asserts `harvest.canary.success`/`roundtrip`, no `harvest.workflow.*` for the probe — AC5/AC8), a backdated-deadline execution-timeout (asserts `harvest.canary.failure`, no terminal/timeout — AC6/AC8), and a normal workflow still recording `harvest.workflow.terminal`; wired into `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt` (one sorted line, ci_run_coverage green), compile-checked in-sandbox and RUN by CI's Docker-backed Linux step.
- **Phase 3.52** (implemented): Workflow run metadata via `ctx.info()` — see issue #698. **Before:** a `#[workflow]` body could read its author-supplied business key (`ctx.workflow_id()`) and type (`ctx.workflow_type()`), but **not** its system-generated `execution_id` — the exact identifier every operator surface keys on (the management-API path `/api/harvest/workflows/{exec_id}/...`, the DLQ, reset/pause/cancel, and the ADR-0001 `execution.id` span attribute). A workflow could log `workflow_id = "cart-42"` but an operator paging from that line had no run UUID to open the execution or build a correlated trace query; authors also couldn't mint run-scoped idempotency keys, and a child workflow couldn't identify the parent that spawned it. **After:** one read-only, replay-safe accessor `WorkflowContext::info() -> WorkflowExecutionInfo` bundles the run's system metadata: `execution_id`, `workflow_id`, `workflow_type`, `start_time`, `history_event_count`, `is_replaying`, and `parent_execution_id` (`None` for a top-level run, the spawning parent's id for a child). Two sibling `const fn` accessors are added — `start_time()` (the **raw** frozen `WorkflowStarted` timestamp, deliberately **not** the advancing virtual clock that `now()` moves under the test harness) and `parent_execution_id()`. **Design.** `info()` is the single source of truth built from the existing accessors (`execution_id()`/`workflow_id()`/`workflow_type()`/`start_time`/ `history_event_count()`/`is_replaying()`/`parent_execution_id`), so it stays consistent with each of them and adds no new logic. `WorkflowExecutionInfo` is a `#[non_exhaustive]`, `Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Eq` struct co-located in `context.rs` (leaving the `ActivityExecutionInfo` name free for the activity-side slice, issue #783), re-exported from `lib.rs` and the prelude so it is usable from any `#[workflow]` body **with no feature flag**. **Parent threading.** `WorkflowExecuteSpanMeta` gains a `parent_execution_id: Option<ExecutionId>` field; the worker populates it from the execution row's `parent_id` column (`prepared.execution.parent_id.map(ExecutionId::from_uuid)`), and the executor threads it into the live `WorkflowContext` alongside `workflow_name`/`workflow_id`/`build_id`/`execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` in both live construction chains (`run_workflow_with_state_history_policy_and_caps` and `run_workflow_with_state_advancing_clock`). The query/update throwaway (`new_for_handler`), replayer, and bare-test contexts default it to `None`. **Invariants.** Reading `info()` appends **zero** `harvest_events` and emits **zero** `WorkflowCommand` (same leave-no-trace property as a query handler), and returns byte-identical values on every worker and every replay pass — all fields derive from already-recorded state. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no shard-semantics impact.** Additive public API (minor bump). Out of scope (per the issue): mutable search-attr reads, a workflow-level `attempt` counter / continue-as-new run-count, nominal scheduled fire-time (#508), and the `ActivityContext` equivalent (#783). **Tests (TDD red→green).** Unit tests in `context.rs`: all-fields on `new_test`, graceful `new_for_handler`, `start_time()` raw-vs-advancing-clock trap, configured vs. default parent, zero command/event footprint, `execution_id` string round-trip through `ExecutionId`'s `FromStr` (AC4 core), and the Success-Metric replay-determinism property test (**N = 1,000** rebuilds from one fixture yield byte-identical `info()`, 0 divergences). No-DB `WorkflowTestEnv` integration tests (via the new `WorkflowTestEnv::with_parent_execution_id` builder): a parent-reading workflow reports the configured parent and replays deterministically (`ReplaySucceeded`), and a top-level run reports `null`. DB/worker integration test `tests/integration/ctx_info_tests.rs` (testcontainers): a real spawned child reports the parent's `execution_id` via `ctx.info().parent_execution_id` end to end (worker → executor → context), while the top-level parent reports no parent. Example `autumn-harvest/examples/ctx_info.rs` (logs `execution_id`, mints a run-scoped `charge-{execution_id}` idempotency key, reads the parent) with embedded `WorkflowTestEnv` tests. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2s).** (A) `info()` must be a genuinely read-only snapshot: it previously read `history_event_count()`, which routes through `match_history()` whose `pump_signal_handlers()` post-hook (issue #546) dispatches push signal handlers and claims a reachable `SignalReceived` — so a read-only `ctx.info()` would fire a registered signal handler, mutate handler-captured state/control flow, and consume the signal, violating the AC5 zero-footprint contract. (The pre-existing `info_emits_no_commands_and_no_events` test used a context with no handlers, so it passed vacuously.) `info()` now reads `event_count`/`is_replaying` by locking the `HistoryMatcher` directly, bypassing the post-hook; a doc note on the public `history_event_count()` accessor flags that it still runs the pump. New regression test `info_does_not_pump_signal_handlers_or_claim_signals` (registers a handler + a reachable `SignalReceived`, asserts `info()` neither fires the handler nor consumes the signal — a later flush still delivers it). (B) `parent_execution_id` is now threaded through the DB `export_history` → `HistoryExportDocument` → `replay_from_json` path (retention archives / offline replay), mirroring `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` exactly: `parent_id` is a row column absent from every `WorkflowEvent`, so a parent-aware child exported through this path previously deserialised parent = `None` and false-reported non-determinism. New top-level `parent_execution_id: Option<ExecutionId>` field (additive `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, never redacted) on both `HistoryExportRequest` and `HistoryExportDocument`; `export_history_decoded` populates the document from the request, round-tripping into `HistorySnapshot.parent_execution_id`. Threaded core-side through the retention archive path (`CandidateExecution.parent_id` + both candidate SELECTs) and the `handle.rs` query-hydration replay context (`replay_from_db`-style). Tests: `HistoryExportDocument` round-trip + legacy-back-compat (no-parent field → `None`) unit tests in `history_export.rs`, and end-to-end `parent_aware_child_replays_clean_through_export_document_round_trip` (+ its no-parent negative control) in `replayer_tests.rs` — a parent-aware child exported via the document replays `ReplaySucceeded` through `replay_from_json` with **no** manual `with_parent_execution_id` override. (C) **Plugin HTTP export handlers threaded (completing the full #1040 mirror).** `parent_execution_id` is now carried through **all three** export producers — single, batch, and retention — exactly the way `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` are, so `replay_from_json` reconstructs the spawning parent for a child exported by **any** path. The two `HistoryExportRequest` construction sites in the plugin's HTTP export route (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`) set the field from the row/candidate `parent_id` column: the single-execution handler (`export_history_for_execution`) uses `execution.parent_id.map(ExecutionId::from_uuid)`, and the batch handler (`export_history_for_candidate`) uses `candidate.parent_id.map(ExecutionId::from_uuid)`. The plugin-local `HistoryExportCandidate` struct gained a `parent_id: Option<Uuid>` field and the batch candidate SELECT (`HISTORY_EXPORT_CANDIDATES_SQL`) now selects `w.parent_id` (added to the `GROUP BY` too), mirroring how it already SELECTs the columns backing `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at`. With this, live HTTP single and batch exports carry the parent (previously they round-tripped parent = `None`); the core round-trip unit test and the `retention_archive_carries_parent_execution_id` DB test cover the assertion end to end. (D) **`history_event_count` is the replay-STABLE consumed position, not the total loaded snapshot length (Codex P2).** `info()` previously reported `matcher.event_count()` — the total loaded history snapshot, which **grows across workflow tasks** (a run replayed on task 2 loads a larger history than it did live on task 1), so the same `info()` call at the same code position returned a different value live vs. replay, a false non-determinism violating AC3. `info()` now reports the matcher's **consumed cursor position** (`matcher.position()`, a pure non-pumping read consistent with the existing non-pumping `info()` read path) — a pure function of how far the workflow's own code has advanced through history at the call site, so it is byte-identical across replay passes and workers. The public `history_event_count()` accessor is **left as the total** because `should_continue_as_new()` needs the whole-history size for its checkpoint decision (the internal history-cap logic in `worker.rs` uses `events.len()` directly); the `WorkflowExecutionInfo.history_event_count` field doc now states it is the consumed position, replay-stable, and NOT suitable for continue-as-new history-size decisions. New decisive regression test `info_history_event_count_is_consumed_position_replay_stable` (two contexts for the same execution driven to the SAME cursor, one loaded from a short history and one from a longer one, assert EQUAL `history_event_count` — RED pre-fix: 3 vs 4). (E) **`parent_execution_id` threaded through ALL remaining replay/handler-context paths (closing the Codex parent-threading surface).** The field is now threaded at **every** context-construction site that sources the sibling row-only columns `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` from the execution row — the exact same class, since `parent_id` likewise lives on the row, absent from every `WorkflowEvent`: worker dispatch (`WorkflowExecuteSpanMeta`), the executor strict/canary/live construction chains, `WorkflowReplayer`/`replay_from_json` (strict + canary), `WorkflowTestEnv`, the history-export document + retention archive + all three plugin HTTP export handlers, the typed-client query-replay path (`handle.rs`), and — **new this pass** — the plugin's `hydrate_ctx_for_query` query-replay context (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`, `.with_parent_execution_id(execution.parent_id.map(ExecutionId::from_uuid))`) and the declarative `#[update]` handler contexts (both the `register_declarative_update_handler` registration wrapper and the `invoke_update` declarative fallback in `context.rs`, which copy the parent's `workflow_id`/headers/deadline into the throwaway `new_for_handler` context but previously dropped `parent_execution_id`). Query handlers run against the main `self` context (`h(self, args)`), so they already inherit the parent; signal handlers likewise dispatch in the main context. New regression test `update_handler_inherits_parent_execution_id` (a declarative update handler invoked on a child run reads `ctx.info().parent_execution_id == Some(parent)` — RED pre-fix: `None`). No CLI, scheduler, `ActivityContext`, event, schema, or migration changes. (F) **`is_replaying` documented as observability-only (Codex P2, doc-only).** The `WorkflowExecutionInfo` struct/`info()`/field docs, the standalone `is_replaying()` accessor doc, CLAUDE.md, and the example now carve `is_replaying` out of the byte-identical/branch-safe guarantee: it is the replay indicator itself, so it intentionally differs live-vs-replay and must never drive workflow commands or be included in an activity input (doing so records different commands live vs replay → non-determinism). It remains identical between two replay passes of the same history. No runtime-logic change.
