That stray edge is a *structural* effect the earlier "silently ignored" framing hid, so the binding is now rejected rather than swallowed. Use `.upstream()` to add a gate dependency deliberately. **Test evidence — 17 tests (9 unit + 8 integration), TDD-verified.** Unit tests in `dag.rs` cover single/merged binding storage + auto-added edge, activity-name vs. alias keying, all four build-error guards (incl. the empty-binding guard for both `input_from_all(&[])` and `input_from_aliased(&[])`), and that a binding *appends* its edge without reordering prior `.upstream()` edges — so a `.condition(|ups| …)` sees `ups[0]` determined by builder call order (asserted both on the stored `upstreams` vector and via `dispatch_decision`). Integration tests in `tests/integration/dag_input_binding_tests.rs` (`unified-dag-execution` + `testing`, no DB) cover a bound node receiving the raw upstream output live (AC2), a merged binding delivering a keyed object, a bound-to-skipped-upstream yielding null (AC6, condition-skip branch), a bound-to-**failed**-upstream yielding null (AC6, failed branch — live plus a deterministic `WorkflowFailed` replay of a hand-built `ActivityFailed`-without-`ActivityCompleted` history), an unbound DAG staying byte-identical (AC3, regression guard), a bound ETL history replaying deterministically (AC5), a 2-source **1000-replay sweep** with randomized within-level completion order, and a stronger 3-source **1000-replay sweep** rotating the within-level completion order through all 6 permutations — both asserting `ReplaySucceeded` (and thus correct merged keys regardless of completion order) on every iteration. Example `autumn-harvest/examples/dag_data_flow.rs` (a three-stage ETL plus a fan-in merge) carries three additional embedded `WorkflowTestEnv`/`WorkflowReplayer` self-check tests. Docs: "Passing data between nodes (node input binding)" in `docs/getting-started/08-dags-and-schedules.md`.
- **Phase 3.57** (implemented): Live workflow output streaming via `ctx.publish_progress` — see issue #791. **Before:** a workflow author building an AI agent, a long-running import, or any interactive flow had **no way to push incremental, author-defined business output** to a waiting client while the run is in flight. The only surfaces were a query handler (pull, snapshot-only), `set_current_details` (a single overwriting status string, #473/#593), or — for operators only — the admin-gated engine-event SSE tail (#324), which streams `ActivityScheduled`/`ActivityCompleted` *machinery*, not the author's content. Streaming tokens / reasoning steps / per-item progress to an end user meant standing up an external message bus. **After:** one replay-safe method — `WorkflowContext::publish_progress(chunk: impl serde::Serialize) -> HarvestResult<()>` — emits an ordered, author-defined chunk from live workflow code, delivered to a subscriber on the new SSE route `GET /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/stream` over the existing Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY plumbing. **Ephemeral, best-effort, product-UX channel** — not an audit record: chunks are dropped when no subscriber is connected; the durable workflow *result* remains authoritative. **Determinism / append-only invariant — the load-bearing property.** The call is a **pure side effect gated on `is_replaying()`**: on a replay pass it returns `Ok(())` immediately with **no `WorkflowCommand` pushed and no seq consumed** (mirrors `set_current_details`), so a workflow that publishes N chunks produces a **byte-for-byte identical `harvest_events` history** to one that publishes none. Chunk content **MAY be non-deterministic** (LLM tokens, wall-clock timestamps, sampled values) *precisely because* it is never recorded or replayed. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no shard-routing change.** **Core (`context.rs`).** Live path: serialize the chunk to `serde_json::Value` (serialize error → `Err`), cap serialized bytes at `PROGRESS_CHUNK_MAX_BYTES = 7000` (Postgres `NOTIFY` hard limit 8000, with envelope headroom); an oversize chunk is **replaced** — never silently dropped — with the truncation marker `{"_harvest_progress_truncated": true, "bytes": <original_len>}`, preserving the ordered slot and signalling truncation to the client. Pushes a **bookkeeping** `WorkflowCommand::PublishProgress { seq: u64, chunk: Value }` (no `result_tx`, non-suspending; joins the `SetCurrentDetails` family at every exhaustive-match and bookkeeping-classifier site in `worker.rs`, excluded from `executor.rs::is_replay_significant_command`, `Ok(false)` no-op in `testing.rs::apply_command`). **Monotonic seq (AC6):** `seq = (epoch << 24) | (local_index & 0xFF_FFFF)` (`encode_progress_seq`), where `epoch` is the loaded-history length at cycle start (read by locking the matcher directly, the `info()` trick, to avoid the `pump_signal_handlers` side effect) — constant within a cycle and strictly growing across cycles — and `local_index` is a per-cycle `AtomicU64`. seq is therefore lifetime-monotonic (reconnect gap detection) and **idempotent on a crash-retry of the same cycle** (best-effort duplicates are dedupable by seq). Epoch shift uses `saturating_mul`; `local_index` saturates at `2^24 - 1` (no overflow panic). **Notify (`worker.rs` + `notify.rs`).** `notify_progress_from_commands(conn, exec_id, &commands)` fires `notify::notify_workflow_progress(...)` on the worker's **persist connection**, co-located right after every `persist_current_details_from_commands` call site (5 sites: suspension, terminal, local-activity pre-run, 2 panic-strike paths) — so progress flushes on both suspension and terminal cycles, in the same transactional context as the `current_details` write (pg NOTIFY delivers on commit → a rolled-back+retried cycle re-fires live; the deterministic seq makes any autocommit-mode duplicate dedupable). A notify failure is **logged and swallowed**, never fails the workflow — progress is disposable. `notify.rs` adds the per-execution channel `workflow_progress_channel(exec_id)` (`harvest_progress_{32-hex}`, < 63-char `NAMEDATALEN`), `ProgressNotifyPayload { seq, chunk }`, `notify_workflow_progress`, and `WorkflowProgressListener` (`connect` / `wait_for_progress` / `wait_for_progress_timeout` → `ProgressWaitOutcome::{Chunk, TimedOut, ChannelClosed}`), mirroring `WorkflowEventListener` (tokio-postgres driver task + mpsc). All `pub` under `autumn_harvest::notify`. **Plugin SSE route (`api.rs`).** `GET /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/stream` (`text/event-stream`). Frames: `event: progress` (`id:` = seq, `data:` = the raw chunk JSON, **not** re-wrapped in the adjacently-tagged envelope) in publish order; `event: end` (`data: {"reason": <terminal-state>}`) on terminal; `event: error` (`data: {"error": "listen_connection_closed"}`) on channel loss. **Auth (AC5): deliberately NOT `require_admin`** — it is an end-user-facing read path (an app's users stream their own workflows), distinct from the admin engine-event tail (#324). It inherits the general `api_with_auth` middleware the other management routes use; **open if no auth is configured** — the default posture is documented in `docs/streaming-progress.md`, and embedders MUST front untrusted end-users. Clean-close mechanics: `LISTEN` is established **before** the existence check (so a chunk published in the check→listen window is not missed); the pooled DB connection is **dropped** before streaming (SSE streams never hold pool connections — the listener owns its own dedicated `tokio-postgres` connection, shard-resolved via `sse_notification_url(shard)`); an already-terminal execution emits a single `end` frame and closes immediately; on each keepalive `TimedOut` tick the producer polls terminal state (bounding close latency to one keepalive) and detects an idle-disconnected client via `tx.is_closed()`; `ChannelClosed` emits `error` and ends rather than hanging. Read-path decode (#608) does **not** apply — progress chunks are ephemeral author-supplied JSON, never codec-encoded. **Contract / audit registration (AC9).** Route registered in `harvest_api_router`, `management_api_routes()`, `management_api_response_fields()`, `docs/api-contract.json`, and `autumn_harvest::audit`: `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` (**ReadOnly**), `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` (op **None**), `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`. Pinned classification tests in **both** `audit.rs` and plugin `contract_regression.rs` (the audit exhaustiveness cross-check stays green if a route is dropped from BOTH lists, so both are pinned independently). **Out of scope (per issue):** durable persistence / replay of chunks (that is the durable per-execution logs primitive, #790); at-least-once / exactly-once delivery, cross-reconnect ordering guarantees, or buffering for late subscribers (best-effort only); final-result delivery (#527) and snapshot reads (query handlers / `set_current_details`); client→workflow streaming (that is signals/updates); cross-shard fan-in of one logical stream (a stream is scoped to a single `exec_id` on its owning shard). **Docs / example.** `docs/streaming-progress.md` (API, determinism contract, best-effort delivery model, SSE wire format + `seq` semantics, auth default posture, 7000-byte cap + truncation marker, out-of-scope list, cross-links to #473/#593/#324/#527). `autumn-harvest/examples/streaming_agent.rs` (an AI-agent-shaped workflow publishing per-step chunks interleaved with a mock activity across decision cycles, one intentionally non-deterministic chunk with a SAFE-because-never-replayed comment, a documented `curl -N` consumer, and embedded `WorkflowTestEnv` tests asserting completion + zero-event-footprint + `ReplaySucceeded`). **Tests, TDD red→green.** Core: 5 inline `context.rs` unit tests (replay-suppressed, live-emits-bookkeeping-command, per-cycle local-index increase, oversize→truncation-marker); 2 no-DB integration tests (`publish_progress_leaves_zero_event_footprint` — identical event-type sequence to a no-progress sibling; `publish_progress_replays_with_zero_divergence` — ReplaySucceeded against an activity-only history, AC2); 2 new `notify::` unit tests (progress channel payload round-trip). Plugin: DB integration (`progress_stream_delivers_ordered_chunks_and_ends_on_terminal`, `progress_stream_on_already_terminal_execution_closes_immediately`, `progress_stream_unknown_execution_returns_404`) and no-DB registration/auth-posture tests (`sse_stream_tests.rs`), plus the pinned classification tests. All core no-DB surfaces run green in-sandbox; DB/HTTP suites (`progress_stream_integration`) run under the Docker-backed CI step registered in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`.
- **Phase 3.x** (implemented): replay: only cross this signal's own deadline timer in `match_signal` — see issue #1071. Follow-up correctness fix on the merged PR #1084 (issue #1071), caught by Codex review. `HistoryMatcher::match_signal`'s interleaved-sibling arm — added by #1084 so a plain `wait_for_signal` tolerates a sibling deadline timer's `TimerFired` recorded before the awaited signal — crossed **any** reserved `__signal_timeout:*` deadline timer *without a rewind*, keyed only on the reserved **prefix** (`signal_timeout_race_name(...).is_some()`). So when a plain `wait_for_signal("a")` runs concurrently with a `receive_signal_timeout("b", …)` in one mixed batch and b's deadline fires before a arrives, the `match_signal("a")` scan advanced the cursor past a **foreign** signal's deadline events (`TimerStarted(__signal_timeout:1:b)` + `TimerFired(...)`) without setting `first_interleaved_command`. The "b" branch's positional `match_signal_or_timer("b")` could then no longer re-anchor on its own `TimerStarted`, so strict replay diverged with `NonDeterminismDetected{EarlyCompletion}` even though both waits genuinely resolved. **Fix (one-line guard narrowing):** the guard changes from name-agnostic `.is_some()` to name-matched `== Some(signal_name)`, so the cross-without-rewind arm fires **only for THIS signal's own** reserved deadline timer. A foreign-name reserved timer instead falls through to the existing generic `TimerStarted` rewind arm (as does a genuine user `ctx.timer` sibling), which sets `first_interleaved_command` so the sibling race re-anchors and resolves `TimerWon` after the win. Behavior is **byte-identical** for the same-name #1071 case (`interleaved_sibling_signal_after_deadline_timer_fired_replays_succeeded`) — `Some("go") == Some("go")` still matches — and the park-forever guard (`matcher_signal_scan_parks_on_lone_open_deadline_timer`) is untouched. The arm's comment, which described (and over-claimed for) the old name-agnostic behavior, is rewritten to state that it only crosses this signal's own deadline timer and that a foreign one is deliberately left to its own race matcher via the rewind path. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration** — a strictly narrowing change to one replay-matcher arm that diverts foreign-name reserved timers to the existing generic rewind path. Regression test `interleaved_two_signal_race_foreign_deadline_timer_replays_succeeded` (in `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`) encodes Codex's exact composition (`tokio::join!(wait_for_signal("a"), receive_signal_timeout::<Value>("b", 5s))`, "a" polled first, history `[WorkflowStarted, TimerStarted(__signal_timeout:1:b), TimerFired(__signal_timeout:1:b), SignalReceived(a)]`); it **fails pre-fix** with `NonDeterminismDetected(kind=EarlyCompletion, event_index=4)` and **passes post-fix** with `ReplaySucceeded`. Verified green at the pinned CI toolchain 1.97.0: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p autumn-harvest --no-default-features --features testing --test integration` (961 passed), and `cargo test -p autumn-harvest --all-features --lib` (2138 passed).
- **Phase 3.x** (implemented): Enforce the start-route capability-precise admin gate before the fail-closed runtime check — see issue #685. Heals the no-DB plugin security test `eris_unauthenticated_start_workflow_terminate_if_running_is_blocked`, which began failing on trunk-dev after #1100 (issue #685) narrowed and **reordered** the `POST /workflows/{name}/start` admin gate. **Root cause (not a live-deployment security hole).** Pre-#1100 the admin gate was a raw-string match placed at the top of `start_workflow`, before the fail-closed `api_state.runtime()` check. #1100 replaced it with the capability-precise gate `effective_active_conflict_behavior(reuse, conflict) == Terminate && !admin` and moved it to *after* both policy parses — which sit after the runtime check and the #808 committed-replay probe. In a **running** deployment the gate still correctly returns `401` for every request that can cancel a live run, so there is no live security hole. But in the no-DB `unauthenticated_app()` harness the runtime is unset, so `api_state.runtime()` returns `Config("harvest runtime is not started")` → `400` *before* the gate is reached. The test's `401` assertion now saw `400`. More importantly the reordering made the start-route auth gate **un-observable** in the no-DB harness: a gate-present and a gate-removed build both return `400`, so a test that accepted `400` would catch no regression. **Fix.** Add a surgical, additive, **lenient early auth gate** before the runtime check that reproduces the exact capability-precise condition on the two pure request-body policy strings (no runtime, no DB needed). It is lenient — an unparseable policy string makes the `Ok`/`Ok` guard fail, deferring to the authoritative gate (so #808's "committed replay returns `200` despite an invalid string" and "fresh invalid string → `400`" are preserved). Only a cleanly-parsed `Terminate`-capable combo by a non-admin returns `401`. The authoritative gate after the two parses is kept unchanged as a belt-and-suspenders backstop (reachable only for requests the early gate let through — admin, or non-`Terminate`). This restores the pre-#685 property that a cancel-capable unauthenticated start is rejected with `401` regardless of runtime readiness (defense in depth: authorize before the fail-closed resource check; `401` now precedes the registry `404`, removing an existence oracle — exactly the pre-#1100 ordering), and keeps #1100's narrowing intact: the flagship non-admin idempotent-starter `reuse = terminate_if_running` + `conflict = use_existing` (→ `Attach`) and `+ fail` (→ `Fail`) stay non-admin. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route change.** Running deployments are unaffected (same outcomes, `401` merely enforced earlier). **Tests** (`autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/security.rs`): the previously-failing test now asserts a clean `401` again; four new no-DB cases encode the narrowed contract so a regression in either direction is caught — `conflict_policy = terminate_existing` → `401`; and `terminate_if_running + use_existing`, `terminate_if_running + fail`, `conflict_policy = use_existing` are each `!= 401 && != 403` (allowed past the auth gate). **Also heals inherited trunk-dev Lint red** (out of this change's scope but blocking the `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest-plugin --all-targets` gate): #1100's `StartWorkflowParams` literal sweep missed `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/progress_stream_integration.rs` (added by #1098), which failed to compile with `missing field conflict_policy`. Added `conflict_policy: WorkflowIdConflictPolicy::Unspecified` matching the sweep's convention. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2): the early gate now defers idempotency-keyed requests.** The early gate above rejected any cleanly-parsed `Terminate`-capable combo by a non-admin with `401` — with no regard for an idempotency key. But the #808 committed-replay claim is keyed on `(workflow_name, idempotency_key)` **alone** — independent of the reuse/conflict policy and the caller's auth — so a keyed `Terminate` start committed by an **admin** can legitimately be replayed by a later **non-admin** retry carrying the same key, which must return the #808 `200` no-op. The early gate's own comment (and the authoritative gate's) claimed "a non-admin can never have committed a `Terminate` start, so no committed replay exists" — flawed reasoning, since the committer and the retrier need not be the same principal. **Fix:** narrow the early gate to fire only when **no** idempotency key is present (a cheap presence-only boolean — header `Idempotency-Key` present, or a non-empty body `idempotency_key`; no validation here, so the downstream resolver still `400`s an empty/over-long key unchanged). Any keyed request defers past the early gate to the downstream path, preserving BOTH #808 outcomes: a committed-replay hit returns its `200` at the committed-replay probe (caller/body-independent), while a genuinely-fresh keyed `Terminate` by a non-admin is still `401`'d by the authoritative gate — which runs **after** that probe, so the narrowing opens no hole. Both misleading comments are rewritten to state the correct invariant (the early gate is an observable, key-absent-only auth check; keyed requests defer downstream). New no-DB regression tests (`eris_keyed_terminate_if_running_defers_past_early_gate`, `eris_keyed_terminate_existing_conflict_defers_past_early_gate`) assert a keyed cancel-capable request is no longer early-`401`'d (in the no-DB harness it fails-closed at the runtime check → non-`401`), contrasted against the unkeyed cases which still assert `401`.
- **Phase 3.x** (implemented): `harvest new <name>` project scaffolding — see issue #692. New local CLI subcommand `harvest new <name> [--path <DIR>] [--force] [--template minimal]` in `autumn-harvest-cli` that scaffolds a complete, compiling, runnable autumn-harvest project so a first-time evaluator reaches one durable workflow execution in **≤ 3 post-scaffold commands** (`docker compose up -d` → `AUTUMN_PROFILE=dev cargo run` → `curl … /workflows/{name}_workflow/start`). The one metric the engine is judged on — time from `cargo add` to first executed workflow — finally has an owning command. **CLI-only, additive.** No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no event-schema or macro-path change, no library API change. `harvest new` is a **local** command (early-return in `run_cli` before the API dispatch path, exactly like `det-check` #778): pure local file generation, no database, no network. **Design decisions:** **Command surface**: `harvest new <name>` only this slice (AC-1's "and/or" is satisfied by `new`; `harvest init` and an ephemeral-Postgres `--demo` mode are noted follow-ups). `ScaffoldTemplate` value_enum ships one `minimal` template. **Embedded templates**: `include_str!` from `autumn-harvest-cli/templates/minimal/` — the first `include_str!` in `src/`; zero runtime fetch. `{{crate_name}}` / `{{ident}}` / `{{workflow_fn}}` / `{{activity_fn}}` / `{{queue}}` placeholders (double-brace so they never collide with Rust `{}`), substituted by a tiny tested `apply_substitutions` helper. **Generated project shape** mirrors `examples/quickstart`: `Cargo.toml` (crates.io **version** deps `autumn-harvest = "0.4"` + `db` feature, `autumn-harvest-plugin = "0.4"`, `autumn-web = "0.5"` — never path deps, since the generated project lives outside the workspace; `edition = "2021"` for the broadest floor), `src/main.rs` (one `#[workflow]` `{ident}_workflow` calling one `#[activity]` `{ident}_activity`, `HarvestPlugin` wiring, a tiny `#[get("/")]` landing route since autumn-web requires ≥1 HTTP route, worker polling the single `["{ident}"]` queue — a workflow start enqueues the workflow task on the worker's first queue and the activity (`queue = "{ident}"`) is enqueued there too, so one queue services both), `README.md` (the ≤3-command runbook + `AUTUMN_PROFILE=dev` auto-migration note, satisfying the DB-bootstrap AC without a manual `diesel migration run`; the result-observing step polls `GET /workflows/{execution_id}` for `.execution.state` and offers the real `harvest … workflow get <id>` subcommand), `compose.yaml` (postgres:16), `autumn.toml`, `.gitignore`. Every emitted identifier is a pure function of `<name>` — no example identifiers survive (AC-5). **Clean identifier derivation**: `derive_crate_ident` lowercases, maps `-` → `_`, collapses runs of `_`, and trims leading/trailing `_`, so any spec-valid name yields a warning-free `snake_case` ident with no double underscore (`my-app` → `my_app`, `MyApp` → `myapp`, `trail-` → `trail`). Only the derived idents are normalized; name **acceptance** is unchanged (keyword/reserved collision is checked against the raw `-` → `_` form), so an uppercase package name like `MyApp` stays accepted per `cargo new` parity (only cargo's own cosmetic uppercase warning), while the generated `main.rs` uses the clean lowercase ident. **Fail-safe** (AC-6): a non-empty target directory without `--force` returns an error and writes **nothing** (validation + full render happen before any file is written); `--force` overwrites but never removes files it did not write (no `rm -rf`). An existing **non-directory** at the target (a plain file) is rejected up front with a clear "is not a directory" message instead of an opaque `create_dir_all` OS error. **Name validation**: rejects empty / over-64-char / non-`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$` / Rust-keyword-resolving / reserved names before any write, so an invalid name can never produce an invalid `Cargo.toml`. **Scaffold-rot guards (AC-8):** A **content-parity** unit test ties the template's `main.rs` wiring tokens to the CI-compiled `examples/quickstart/src/main.rs` (read at test time), so template drift from the shape CI actually builds fails the test. A Linux-only `scaffold-smoke` CI job **generates, builds, and runs** the scaffold to a terminal state — the literal AC-8 assertion. It builds the generated project against the **published** crates.io deps (no `[patch.crates-io]`) — exactly what a real user gets — behind a `postgres:16` service whose user/password/db match the scaffold's generated `autumn.toml`, boots the app (`AUTUMN_PROFILE=dev` auto-migrates), POSTs a workflow start, and polls `GET /workflows/{id}` until `state == COMPLETED`, failing the job on a bad terminal state or timeout. This closes the earlier "runtime execution deferred to a fast-follow" gap: the headline metric (scaffold → first executed workflow) is now asserted end to end in CI against the published API. **Mechanism note.** The end-to-end run lives in a dedicated CI job with a `postgres:16` service (rather than an in-crate integration test registered in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`) because it must scaffold, build, and run a *generated standalone cargo project* as a subprocess — which does not fit the in-crate cargo-test harness and would be far heavier on disk. **Tests (TDD red→green→refactor):** 22 integration tests in `autumn-harvest-cli/tests/integration/new_cli.rs` (derive names, substitution, no-placeholder-survives across every file, crates.io-deps-no-path, identifier substitution in `main.rs`, hyphenated/uppercase/repeat-separator names → clean `snake_case` idents in `main.rs` with no double underscore, README 3-command path, README result-observing commands, quickstart wiring parity, writes-all-files, fail-safe-non-empty, `--force` overwrite preserving unrelated files, existing-file target rejection, `--path` creates missing dir, over-length + reserved-name rejection, invalid-name-no-write) + 7 lib unit tests (`clap` parse of `Commands::New` with flags and defaults, clean `derive_crate_ident`, keyword rejection, valid-name acceptance, uppercase cargo-new parity). **Local end-to-end verification.** The scaffold was built against the published `autumn-harvest 0.4.0` / `autumn-harvest-plugin 0.4.0` / `autumn-web 0.5.0` (registry sources, no patch) and driven to `COMPLETED` (output `hello, World!`) against a local Postgres, confirming both the published-deps build and the single-queue wiring.
- **Phase 4** (implemented): Replay tolerates interleaved sibling terminals in forward-scan matchers — see issue #1071. Fixed a pre-existing **core** replay limitation (shared by the Postgres engine, surfaced by the SQLite backend work #1068/#1069): an *ideal, correct* workflow history that interleaves a sibling terminal event next to the event a matcher is scanning for would falsely fail replay with `NonDeterminismDetected(EarlyCompletion)`. The canonical case is a timer-first mixed suspension batch — `tokio::join!(ctx.timer(...), ctx.execute_activity(...))` with the timer command emitted first — recording `WorkflowStarted, TimerStarted, ActivityScheduled, ActivityCompleted, TimerFired`: `HistoryMatcher::match_timer_strict`'s forward `TimerFired` scan **broke at the still-unconsumed `ActivityScheduled`**, never recognized the timer as fired, skipped the re-arm, and diverged. The mirror `join!(activity, timer)` (activity first) happened to replay fine. **Fix (matcher-scan logic only, in `impl HistoryMatcher`, `autumn-harvest/src/replay.rs`):** each intolerant forward-scan matcher now tolerates an interleaved sibling terminal at its recorded position — the same non-consuming-skip / rewind template `match_signal_or_timer` (#476) already uses — across all four documented manifestations: **`match_timer_strict`** — a rewind arm for interleaved unconsumed sibling *commands* (`ActivityScheduled | LocalActivityScheduled | MarkerRecorded | SideEffectRecorded`) plus transparent non-consuming skip arms for interleaved sibling *terminals* and *foreign `TimerFired`* (a `TimerFired` whose id ≠ this timer's belongs to a sibling). Fixes manifestation #1 (timer-first mixed batch) and #4 (reversed multi-timer same-batch fire order). **`scan_activity_terminal`** — added `LocalActivityScheduled` to the interleaved-command arm and a transparent skip for `TimerFired (any id) | ChildWorkflow{Completed,Failed} | LocalActivity{Completed,Failed}`. Fixes manifestation #2 (sibling timer fires before an activity's terminal). **`match_signal`** — transparently crosses a sibling deadline timer's `TimerStarted`/`TimerFired` recorded ahead of the awaited signal; a reserved `__signal_timeout:{seq}:{name}` timer (a concurrent `receive_signal_timeout` race, #476) is crossed without a rewind so the signal-win advances the cursor past it (no false `EarlyCompletion`), while a genuine user `ctx.timer` sibling keeps its rewind. Fixes manifestation #3 (deadline timer fired before an awaited plain-wait signal). **Contract-preserving by construction: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no change to event emit / suspension-batch command ordering** — the persisted contract is untouched; this only changes how the matcher *reads* an existing history. Foreign events are never marked consumed, so each crossed sibling stays claimable by its own matcher in program order. **Tolerance does not over-swallow — genuine non-determinism still diverges:** guarded by `interleaved_sibling_multi_timer_wrong_one_fires_still_diverges`, `interleaved_sibling_signal_stray_timer_fired_still_diverges`, `interleaved_sibling_signal_stray_timer_started_still_diverges`, the matcher-unit `matcher_signal_scan_parks_on_lone_open_deadline_timer` (a lone open deadline timer parks rather than being falsely nd-blocked), and the retained `replay_activity_history_for_timer_workflow_detects_timer_mismatch` (a genuine timer-id mismatch still diverges via the untouched positional anchor). **Known limitation (pinned + documented):** composing a plain `wait_for_signal` with a cancellable timer (#768) in one `join!` where the cancellable `TimerFired` is recorded before the `SignalReceived` still diverges on strict replay (self-heals live; use `ctx.receive_signal_timeout` #476 for the supported signal-or-deadline shape) — pinned by `known_limitation_signal_wait_composed_with_cancellable_await_fire_diverges_on_reversed_order`. **Cross-crate pin flip:** one now-obsolete `autumn-harvest-sqlite` known-limitation control (`reversed_timer_fire_order_breaks_core_replay`) is renamed to `reversed_timer_fire_order_replays_on_core_after_1071` with its assertion flipped from `NonDeterminismDetected` to `ReplaySucceeded` — the core fix makes that reversed multi-timer history replay-succeed, so the stale pin would otherwise fail the `cargo test -p autumn-harvest-sqlite` CI step. No sqlite workaround *logic* changed (the `arm_seq` fire-order tie-break is retained but is no longer a replay-*correctness* prerequisite). The sqlite `join!(activity, timer)` "activity branch first" and plain-`wait_for_signal`-with-deadline guidance become unnecessary and are flagged for a follow-up docs cleanup (not changed here); the WASM branch #1072 inherits the same core matcher. Tests: `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs` gains the four manifestation replay-succeeds tests (`interleaved_sibling_timer_first_mixed_batch_replays_succeeded`, `interleaved_sibling_timer_fires_before_activity_terminal_replays_succeeded`, `interleaved_sibling_signal_after_deadline_timer_fired_replays_succeeded` + `interleaved_sibling_signal_after_plain_user_timer_fired_replays_succeeded`, `interleaved_sibling_multi_timer_reversed_fire_order_replays_succeeded`), the child-workflow coverage variant `interleaved_sibling_child_workflow_terminal_before_timer_replays_succeeded`, the divergence guards above, and the known-limitation pin; `replay.rs` gains the `matcher_signal_scan_parks_on_lone_open_deadline_timer` unit test. CI reproduced at cargo 1.97.0: integration `960 passed`, all-features lib `2071 passed`, clippy `-D warnings` + fmt clean, sqlite `125/125`.
- **Phase 4** (implemented): Vantage UI: DAG run-graph page (issue #957) + execution timeline/Gantt page (issue #960) — see PR #1085. Adds the two remaining Phase 4 Vantage dashboard pages, both server-rendered inline SVG in `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/ui.rs` (the Workers #142 / DLQ #226 precedent — no JS, no client-side charting library), both read-only except one already-audited mutation. **No new backend endpoint, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no core change.** The only `api.rs` touch is a shared-impl extraction (below). Diff confined to `ui.rs`, `api.rs`, and `tests/ui_integration.rs`. **DAG run-graph page (issue #957)** New DAG run-graph rendered on the per-DAG detail page (`GET /api/harvest/dags/{dag_name}`). `dag_detail_ui` now derives topology, per-node status, and timings **solely** from `dag_graph::build_run_graph` — the same in-process derivation the #690 API handler calls — so the picture and the #366 retry action can never disagree about what "failed" means. The previous UI-side status fork (`map_node_states`/`DagNodeState`/`dag_node_state_label`/`merge_dag_task_state`/`infer_skipped_node_state`/`parse_dag_skip_marker_index`) is **deleted** (its unit tests deleted with it; grep for every symbol is empty), satisfying #957's "must not fork its own node-status derivation" AC. Topology renders as level-by-level inline SVG (`build_graph_layout`, one `<line>` per `depends_on` edge), each node filled **and** icon-marked per status (`succeeded`/`failed`/`timed_out`/`cancelled`/`running`/`pending`/`skipped`) so status is distinguishable without color (accessibility), with `role="img"`+`aria-label` and per-node `<a>`/`<title>`. Node index alignment (`nodes[i]` ↔ `tasks()[i]` ↔ `execution_levels()`, all from one `DagDefinition`) is pinned by a regression test. Geometry is fully clamped/guarded — no panics on zero-node, cyclic-impossible, or huge-fan-out runs; ≥ 200 nodes fall back to a scrollable container. Click-through node detail panel shows `status`/`started_at`/`finished_at`/`attempts`/`error_type` + truncated error first line. A failed node offers **"Retry from this node"** whose confirmation names the exact widened node set (#366's level + downstream-closure semantics) before commit. **`api.rs` change (the only one): `retry_dag_run`'s handler body extracted into `pub(crate) retry_dag_run_inner` + `DagRetryFailure` (with `human_message` + `into_http_response`).** The HTTP `retry_dag_run` handler delegates to it, preserving the #366 wire contract byte-for-byte (every original status/body arm reproduced). The UI dry-run confirm and the commit both call the same audited `retry_dag_run_inner` (`OP_DAG_RETRY`, `source = SOURCE_UI`); the whole `/dags/{dag_name}/runs/{run_exec_id}/retry` route (GET confirm + POST commit) is `require_admin`-gated to match the API, so the UI adds no unaudited mutation path. **Behavior changes:** classic (non-unified) DAG runs — which #690 rejects with `400` — now render the explicit "no topology available for classic DAG runs" degraded message (required to source statuses solely from `build_run_graph`); and an explicitly-provided-but-unknown `?run=` now returns the 404 message (AC7) instead of silently falling back to the first valid run (an omitted `?run=` still defaults to the latest run). **Execution timeline / Gantt page (issue #960)** New **Timeline** tab on the execution detail page (route `GET /workflows/{id}/timeline`, read-only, non-admin — parity with the #739 API). `workflow_timeline_ui` calls `derive_timeline` in-process (the same shipped #739 function — not a forked history-derivation). Renders one horizontal span per step on a shared wall-clock axis, lane-grouped by `step_kind`, colored by `outcome`, with the `wait_ms`/`exec_ms` split drawn as two segments **only when #739 provides it** (a single undivided span otherwise — never fabricating a split). Gantt geometry is clamped/guarded (`x_scale` clamps to axis width; `GanttAxis::new` forces `end > start`; zero/open spans use a min-width; casts are bounded) — no panics on never-started, still-running, clock-skew, or null-split histories; in-flight steps render as open-ended spans to "now". Uniquely versus every competitor, engine interventions render as first-class bands because those states are durable columns: operator **pauses** (#383) render as a full-height shaded band with reason/actor (active pause only); **ND-blocks** (#603) render as a distinct marker with the block reason. The rollup header shows `total_wall_clock_ms`/busy/wait and highlights + scroll-focuses (`#slowest`) the slowest step. Runs > 500 steps truncate with a note. The nondeterminism-block runbook is surfaced as non-clickable `code` text (a repo path, not a served URL — matching the `docs/runbooks/safe-deploy.md` convention), never a dead relative `<a href>` that would 404 during triage. **Deferred #739/#690 data gaps (honored, not patched with a UI-side history parse)** Per both issues' "file the gap against the data API, never patch in the UI" clause, four ACs are honored only to the extent the shipped derivations expose data, each recommended as a #739 follow-up: (1) per-span deep-links (#960 AC7) — a `TimelineStep` carries no child/activity exec_id; (2) adjacent-attempt spans (#960 AC3) — a step has an `attempt` count but no per-attempt timestamps, so retries render as one span + `×N` badge; (3) historical/resolved pause windows (#960 AC4) — `StepKind` has no `Pause` variant and the row keeps only the active pause; (4) interactive axis zoom (#960 AC8) — deliberately no-JS, min-span-width compression only. Analogously, #957 AC3's "link to underlying task/activity detail where one exists" is honored by the "where one exists" conditional (the #690 `DagRunNode` carries no per-node exec_id, so no link target exists). **Tests** Pure `ui.rs` render tests (status fill/icon/label coverage, `build_graph_layout` levels, SVG nodes/edges/fills/glyph embedding, `render_dag_node_panel`, `node_retry_offered` matrix, `resolve_dag_run_selection`, `dag_detail_relative_url` encoding, timeline lanes/`span_segments`/`x_scale`/rollup/slowest/pause-band/nd-marker/HTML-escaping, step-cap) run under `cargo +1.97.0 test -p autumn-harvest-plugin --lib` (582 passed). `tests/ui_integration.rs` testcontainers tests (mixed-status graph, node detail, retry confirm/commit/audit/admin-gate, classic-DAG + unknown-run degraded, 220-node timed render, real `dag_skip` skipped-node distinctness, index alignment; timeline four-affordance fixture, split-only-when-present, slowest highlight, in-flight open span, 404, 200-step timed render) are compile-checked and run Docker-backed in CI via the registered `ui_integration` suite. Multi-angle review: 0 P1, ~6 P2 all fixed (`run`-param redirect encoding, dead ND-block runbook links → code text, untested 100-node perf metric, unexercised pending-vs-skipped, unasserted status-icon-in-render, unknown-run silent-fallback → 404).
- **Phase 4** (implemented): Scoped API tokens + rotation for the management API — see issue #942. Adds a first-class, least-privilege credential layer for the Harvest management API: create / list / revoke scoped, optionally-expiring, individually-revocable API tokens, with every mutating operation attributable to a named actor. Entirely a `autumn-harvest-plugin` auth layer plus **one additive config-table migration** — **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, zero replay-determinism impact, no change to `harvest_events`** (AC9). The deterministic execution core is untouched. **What shipped** **Token table (`harvest_api_tokens`, migration `20260713000000`)** — a small, Postgres-only, shard-agnostic control table (`id`, `name`, `token_hash`, `scope`, `created_at`, `expires_at?`, `last_used_at?`, `revoked_at?`, `created_by`), mirrored into core `schema.rs`/`models.rs` exactly like `harvest_audit_log`. Verified on the **default (control) shard**; rows carry no `shard_id`. **Wire format & secret hygiene (AC2)** — a token secret is opaque `hvst_<base64url(32 random bytes)>`. Only `token_hash = hex(SHA256(secret))` is stored (UNIQUE-indexed); the plaintext is returned **exactly once** at creation and never persists. Verification hashes the presented secret and does one indexed `SELECT` — **no in-Rust hash comparison** (a 256-bit random hash is not an iterable timing oracle), so no constant-time-compare crate is added. `GET /admin/tokens` returns a **metadata-only** `TokenView` DTO that structurally cannot hold the hash/secret (the #695 redaction-view pattern, exhaustive-destructure guard); `MintResult`/`NewApiToken` redact the secret/hash in `Debug`. Uses `sha2`/`base64`/`rand` — all already workspace/core deps. **Scope from route classification (AC3/AC4)** — a token carries `read` or `mutate`, derived from the existing `audit::CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` (the #776 single source of truth — **no second route taxonomy**). The scope gate is `deny_readonly_mutation` over `classify_route`, which **fails closed**: an unclassified path resolves to `Mutating` and is denied to a `read` token. A `read` token gets **403 on 100% of `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES`** and reaches 100% of read-only routes (the 100%/0% success-metric sweep). **Enforcement layer (`api_token::enforce_token_scope`)** — a `from_fn_with_state` layer installed on the nested `harvest_api_router` **only** under the new `HarvestPlugin::enable_api_tokens()` opt-in (default off → byte-identical, AC7). A bearer that does not start with `hvst_` (or an absent bearer) is passed through untouched — token auth **composes with**, never replaces, `api_with_auth` (AC7). A claimed `hvst_` bearer that cannot be verified (store unavailable) is rejected 503, never trusted unverified. **Rotation & expiry (AC5)** — optional `expires_at`; an expired or revoked token is rejected 401 on the **next request** because there is **no grant cache** (every request re-queries the table; bounded TTL = 0). Rotation is create-replacement → cut over → revoke old, over the existing routes. **Actor attribution (AC6)** — on a verified token the layer strips any inbound `x-harvest-actor` and injects `token:{id}`, so every audited mutation is attributed to the token (never the secret/hash) and a caller cannot spoof a different actor. The `token:` audit-actor namespace is **reserved**: on the pass-through path (no/invalid `hvst_` bearer, incl. OPTIONS) the layer also strips any inbound `x-harvest-actor` whose value starts with `token:`, so a caller admitted by some *other* means (a session admin, or any request under an embedder admin boundary) cannot forge a token-namespaced actor and impersonate a minted token. Non-`token:` actor values pass through untouched — legacy embedder-authed requests keep the documented `x-harvest-actor`/`anonymous` fallback. A verified `TokenPrincipal` extension lets `require_harvest_admin` admit a token-authenticated request in standalone-token mode. **Routes (AC1)** — `POST /admin/tokens` (create, 201, audited `token.create`), `GET /admin/tokens` (list, metadata-only, read/no-audit), `DELETE /admin/tokens/{id}` (revoke, audited `token.revoke`), all admin-gated and registered across every registry: `harvest_api_router`, `management_api_routes()`/`_request_fields()`/`_response_fields()`, `docs/api-contract.json`, and core `audit` (`CLASSIFIED_ROUTES`, `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES`, `AUDITED_OPERATIONS`, `OP_TOKEN_CREATE`/`OP_TOKEN_REVOKE`/`TARGET_TOKEN`, `EXCLUDED_ROUTES` for the GET), with a dedicated `token_routes_are_classified_and_audited` pin. **MCP composition** — a token-aware `enforce_token_scope_mcp_mutation` layer (mirroring `enforce_read_only_mcp_mutation`) is provided in `api_token` to hard-deny a `read`-scoped token the mutating generated MCP tool routes. `enable_api_tokens()` installs the management-router `enforce_token_scope` layer; wiring the MCP-tool gate onto the app-level generated tool routes is a follow-up composition (the generated MCP routes live outside the nested management router). **CLI (AC8)** — `harvest token create|list|revoke` (plus a `rotate` client-side convenience that mints a replacement via the create route). The `--token` bearer was already sent; the new layer consumes it. **Single source of truth for hashing** — the pure token-secret helpers (`mint_secret`, `hash_secret`, `looks_like_harvest_token`, `TOKEN_PREFIX`) live in **core** (`autumn_harvest::api_token`, no `db` feature — they use only the non-optional `base64`/`sha2`/`rand` core deps). The plugin's mint route re-exports and calls them, and the offline `harvest token bootstrap` CLI calls the same functions, so the server mint path and the offline seed path can **never drift** on how a secret is generated or hashed. `sha2`/`base64`/`rand` were removed from the plugin's own `Cargo.toml` (they now live only in core). **First-token bootstrap — standalone (tokens-only) mode** **The problem (Codex P1).** In pure standalone mode — where scoped API tokens are the *only* auth, with no embedder `api_with_auth` admin boundary — there is a chicken-and-egg gap: `POST /admin/tokens` is an admin-gated mutation, so minting a token requires an admin `TokenPrincipal`, which only a *previously-minted* token can provide. There is no way to mint the **first** token via the API. (Composed mode — tokens layered on the embedder's own admin auth — is unaffected: an existing admin caller mints the first token normally.) **The fix — `harvest token bootstrap` (offline seed CLI).** A new local-only CLI subcommand generates a fresh token, prints the plaintext secret **exactly once** (same "shown once — store it now, it cannot be recovered" framing as the create route), and prints the exact `INSERT INTO harvest_api_tokens (...) VALUES (...)` statement for the operator to run against their database out-of-band. It opens **no** DB connection and issues **no** HTTP request (print-only). The printed SQL embeds **only the hash** (never the secret), with `id`/`created_at` taking the column defaults (`gen_random_uuid()`/`NOW()`) and every user-supplied string single-quote escaped (`'` → `''`) to neutralize injection through a crafted `--name`/`--created-by`. `--expires-at` is validated as RFC 3339 before any SQL is emitted. `--scope` defaults to **mutate** (a seed token must be able to mint the rest via the API). Usage: `harvest token bootstrap [--name <name>] [--scope mutate|read] [--expires-at <rfc3339>] [--created-by <who>]`. The operator (who already has DB access — the trust anchor) runs the printed SQL once to seed a single `mutate` token, then mints every further token through the API. **Why option (a) — offline seed CLI — over the alternatives.** (a) keeps **zero new server-side auth surface** and anchors trust in the DB access the operator already has (the same trust anchor the migration itself requires), leaving composed mode byte-identical. A server-side bootstrap secret (b) would add a *static, long-lived credential* the operator must provision, guard, and eventually rotate — a standing liability for a one-time ceremony. A docs-only "insert a row by hand" note (c) would ship an advertised standalone mode that is effectively unusable out of the box and would force operators to hand-derive the `hex(SHA256(secret))` hash correctly (the exact drift hazard this feature removes). The CLI reuses the shared core hashing helper, so a bootstrap-seeded token authenticates **byte-for-byte identically** to a route-minted one — proven by a dedicated parity integration test. **`last_used_at` is debounced** — the best-effort last-used bump runs off the request critical path (fire-and-forget) **and** is skipped when the token's `last_used_at` is newer than 60 s, so a high-rate token client (the intended CI-fleet case) does not turn every read into a write or double the pool-checkout pressure. **Operational caveats** **Standalone-token mode should sit behind a rate-limiting proxy.** With `enable_api_tokens()` as the *only* auth (no reverse proxy / `api_with_auth`), any request whose `Authorization` begins with `hvst_` triggers one indexed token lookup before authentication — inherent to any bearer-token scheme. In that deployment shape, front the management API with a reverse proxy / load balancer that rate-limits (per-source) to bound unauthenticated lookup floods; the lookup is a single cheap indexed `SELECT` per probe and the connection is released promptly, but the mitigation is deployment-level. **Incident response for a compromised `mutate` token must audit `created_by` lineage.** A `mutate` token can reach `POST /admin/tokens`, so it can mint replacement tokens (the 2-level read/mutate model has no scope that grants mutation but withholds token management — fine-grained RBAC is explicitly out of scope). Revoking a leaked `mutate` token is therefore insufficient on its own: also audit the `created_by` provenance and revoke the entire lineage of tokens the compromised token minted. **Tests** Pure unit tests (core `api_token.rs`): hash determinism/hex, secret mint prefix/entropy, minted-secret-round-trips-through-hash, `hvst_` discrimination. Pure unit tests (plugin `api_token.rs`): `MintResult`/`TokenView` redaction, the scope-from-class decision (deny-mutating / allow-readonly / fail-closed), expiry predicate (exercising the re-exported core helpers). Audit pin (`audit.rs`). No-DB HTTP layer tests (`security.rs`): pass-through of absent/non-`hvst_`/OPTIONS, 503-on-claimed-token-without-store, default-router-unchanged. DB integration (`token_auth_integration.rs`): create-returns-secret-once/stores-only-hash, list-metadata-only, verify-authenticates, unknown-401, revoke-denies-next-request, expired-401, the read-token 403/read sweep, mutate-token standalone admin access, `token:{id}` actor attribution (spoof-proof on the token path), a pass-through anti-spoof test proving a non-token caller cannot forge a `token:`-namespaced audit actor (AC6, reserved-namespace strip), create/revoke audited, plus the **bootstrap parity test** (`bootstrap_seeded_token_authenticates_identically_to_route_minted`): proves the mint route stores exactly `hash_secret(secret)` and that a row seeded offline with the shared core helpers authenticates + audits as `token:{id}` identically to a route-minted token. CLI unit tests (`token_bootstrap_tests` in `lib.rs`): builder emits a `hvst_` secret + hash-only INSERT SQL (secret never embedded), default scope `mutate`, invalid-scope rejected, flag-values flow through, RFC-3339 expiry validated/embedded, single-quote escaping. CLI mapping + contract-coverage tests.
- **Phase 5.0** (implemented): `autumn-harvest-sqlite` companion crate — see issue #1068. New workspace member `autumn-harvest-sqlite`: an embedded, single-writer **SQLite** backend for the workflow engine, targeting edge / local-first deployments. It productizes the R&D feasibility spike (issue #966 / PR #1066) into a real crate following the separate-companion-crate recommendation (option ii) — the Postgres path is **completely untouched**. **What it reuses vs. reimplements.** The crate depends on `autumn-harvest` with `default-features = false`, pulling in only the pure, backend-neutral determinism core (`run_workflow`, `WorkflowEvent`, the replay engine, `WorkflowContext`) — no Diesel/Postgres. It reuses that core **wholesale** (the decision loop calls the pure `run_workflow_with_state_history_policy_and_caps(...)` entry point with plain values — no connection, no trait object — threading the real registered `workflow_name` so `ctx.info().workflow_type` matches the Postgres worker; see the FIX C entry below) and reimplements only *persistence* on `rusqlite` (`bundled`, so no system SQLite and **no Docker** for tests): the event store (`store.rs`), the task queue + durable timers (`queue.rs`), and the worker pass (`worker.rs`), wired by `SqliteRuntime` (`runtime.rs`). **No in-crate `StorageBackend` trait** — the core is already reusable as a library. **Single-writer / single-server contract** (documented in the crate docs): `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` replaces `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (exactly-once by construction under one writer); polling replaces `LISTEN`/`NOTIFY`; restart = drop the runtime + re-open the file, with an orphan-reclaim on `open()` flipping any crash-stranded `RUNNING` task back to `PENDING` (activity execution is **at-least-once** — bodies should be idempotent). Durable timers use the **real wall clock**: a timer's absolute deadline (`now + duration`) is stored at arm time, so timers are naturally monotonic across restarts with **no virtual clock to persist or reset**; the public drivers use `Utc::now()`, and `*_as_of(now)` variants inject an as-of time so restart/timer tests are deterministic without sleeping. **The load-bearing correctness work — decision-cycle persistence atomicity as a CLASS invariant.** The spike prototype left the append-then-mutate ordering non-transactional (an open Codex P1). Every persist site in this crate wraps its event append(s) **and** its durable-row mutation(s) in ONE `conn.transaction()`, so a crash (or a mid-write drop) can never leave the event history and the durable rows observably out of sync across a reopen: **start** — execution-row insert + `WorkflowStarted` append. **dispatch** — the whole decision cycle's `ActivityScheduled`/`TimerStarted` appends + task/timer row inserts (a mid-batch unsupported command rolls the whole cycle back — no half-written cycle). **drain** — the activity body runs *outside* the transaction (a SQLite write lock cannot be held across arbitrary user I/O — hence at-least-once), but the terminal `ActivityCompleted`/`ActivityFailed` append + task-row completion (or the retry requeue + attempt audit) commit together. **timer fire** — `TimerFired` append + mark-timer-consumed in one transaction (a crash between them would otherwise double-fire the timer and leave a stray non-lifecycle `TimerFired` in history). **signal delivery** — `SignalReceived` append + the `harvest_signals` delivered-flag update ride the same cycle transaction. **terminal** — `WorkflowCompleted`/`WorkflowFailed` append + execution-state → terminal in one transaction. The cycle's drained bookkeeping commands (see below) are appended **before** the terminal event, in command order, inside that same transaction (mirroring the Postgres worker's `persist_terminal_outcome_commands`); any non-bookkeeping command in a terminal drain is rejected loudly with `SqliteError::Unsupported`, rolling the whole terminal transaction back. **bookkeeping** — a `RecordSideEffect` command (from `ctx.system_now`/`new_uuid`/`random_*`/`side_effect`) is persisted as a `SideEffectRecorded` event, and `RecordMarker` as `MarkerRecorded`, **never silently dropped** — whether it rides a suspending batch (via `apply_commands`) OR is emitted in the cycle that completes/fails the workflow with no further suspension (e.g. `ctx.new_uuid()` right before `Ok(..)`, persisted on the terminal path above). Both cases join the same atomic cycle transaction, so replay never re-mints a different value and a history written here always replays byte-identically on the core `WorkflowReplayer`. `ctx.set_current_details(...)` (issue #593) and a re-park `WaitForActivity` are benign **no-ops** (they append no event and gate no control flow) rather than `Unsupported` errors, so a workflow that publishes an operator status breadcrumb is not wedged. **timer re-arm** — a timer id may be RE-ARMED under the same name after a prior fire (the poll-loop idiom `loop { ctx.timer("tick", 1).await?; … }`, which the core supports via cursor-based per-id FIFO pairing). Arm idempotency keys on OCCURRENCE (`store::pending_timer_arms` = recorded `TimerStarted` minus `TimerFired` for the id), NOT the bare id, and `enqueue_timer` uses `INSERT OR REPLACE` so the fresh arm supersedes the spent (`fired = 1`) row — a bare-id guard would wrongly match the prior fired arm and wedge the re-arm at `Stuck`. **Determinism / cross-backend guarantee.** A history written here is byte-identical **per event** to one the Postgres backend would write (both serialize `WorkflowEvent` via the shared adjacently-tagged `#[serde(tag = "type", content = "data")]` form), so it replays unchanged on the core `WorkflowReplayer` — including a deterministic side effect emitted in a terminal (completing/failing) cycle, which is now persisted (see the terminal/bookkeeping bullets above). The claim is *per-event encoding byte-identity + replay-equivalent event SETS*, not identical event streams: the Postgres engine appends an `ActivityStarted` on claim that this backend never writes, and the two replay identically because `HistoryMatcher::scan_activity_terminal` skips `ActivityStarted`. Retryable activity failures go to a `harvest_activity_attempts` audit table + the task-row `attempt` counter (mirroring the Postgres `requeue_for_retry`), so only terminal outcomes ever reach the replayable event log. **Signals are pull-only (documented non-goal).** A staged signal reaches history (`SignalReceived`) only when a workflow reaches a pull primitive that consumes it. The supported pull surface is the plain waits (`ctx.wait_for_signal` / `ctx.receive_signal`) **and** the signal-or-deadline waits `ctx.wait_for_signal_timeout` / `ctx.receive_signal_timeout` (issue #476) — see the Codex #1069 P2 fix below. The push-handler and non-blocking drain APIs — `register_signal_handler` (#546), `drain_signals` / `try_receive_signal` (#775) — depend on the Postgres task-preparation ingest that promotes *all* pending signals into history up front, which this single-writer backend does not implement; restrict to the pull primitives here (push-based signal *handlers* are a follow-up). **Codex #1069 review — P2: handle `CancelRaceLosers` so `wait_for_signal_timeout` completes.** A workflow using `ctx.wait_for_signal_timeout(...)` / `receive_signal_timeout(...)` suspends on a `StartTimer` + `WaitForSignal` race. When the **signal wins**, the determinism core pushes a `WorkflowCommand::CancelRaceLosers { timers: [<deadline timer>], .. }` (issue #476/#600) to durably delete the losing deadline timer. Both command-drain sites — `apply_commands` (a teardown riding a suspending batch) and `persist_terminal_pending_commands` (the common `let s = ctx.wait_for_signal_timeout(..).await?; Ok(s)` terminal-drain shape) — previously treated it as `SqliteError::Unsupported("Unknown")`, so *after* `SignalReceived` was already committed the next cycle errored and the execution could never complete — wedging every normal pull-style signal workflow that adds a timeout. Both sites now delegate to a shared `apply_cancel_race_losers` (mirroring the Postgres `worker::apply_race_loser_cancellations`): it deletes each losing timer's still-pending `harvest_timers` row (new `queue::delete_pending_timer`, returning whether a row changed so the idempotent re-push on later replay cycles reports no progress and the decision loop still converges) and, for a race over activities, cancels each losing still-open task row (new `queue::cancel_activity_task`) and appends the synthetic `ActivityFailed { error: "lost race to a sibling branch", non_retryable: true, .. }` the core records — only for a row it actually cancelled, so an activity that genuinely completed first keeps its real terminal. All teardown joins the same cycle transaction (atomic with the winner/terminal event). A non-empty `children` set (a child-workflow race — `StartChildWorkflow` is outside the single-writer subset, so it can never have been dispatched here) is still rejected loudly rather than silently dropping a loser the core would cancel. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no schema change** (the `CANCELLED` task state is terminal for the claim query, which only selects `PENDING`). Regression tests (`tests/signal_timeout.rs`): signal-wins completes with the payload and the losing deadline timer row is actually deleted (verified via a raw connection) and the history replays on the core `WorkflowReplayer`; deadline-wins returns the timeout branch (`None`); and a typed `receive_signal_timeout` with a trailing activity exercises the suspending-batch (`apply_commands`) site. The two signal-win tests fail against the pre-fix code and pass after. **Codex #1069 review — P1: engine non-determinism must NOT seal FAILED / poison history.** When replay detects workflow-code drift (a bad deploy), the determinism core returns `WorkflowOutcome::Failed { non_deterministic_details: Some(_) }`. The `drive_one_cycle` terminal `Failed` arm previously ignored that field and persisted a normal `WorkflowFailed` event + `FAILED` state — sealing an engine bug as an author failure and poisoning history against the rolled-back build. The arm now branches on `non_deterministic_details`: `None` (a genuine author `Err`) fails terminally, unchanged; `Some(_)` (an engine-detected divergence) **discards the whole divergent decision cycle** — appends NO terminal event, persists NONE of the cycle's pending bookkeeping commands (a marker from the bad build would poison history), and does NOT transition state — leaving the execution `RUNNING`/resumable and surfacing the new `SqliteError::NonDeterministic { execution_id, details }`. Because the `?` never runs, `harvest_events` is byte-identical to before the drive; a later drive with a corrected (compatible) handler resumes from the same unchanged history and completes. Propagating the error out of the drive also terminates the decision loop, so `run_until_blocked`/`poll_once`/`run_until_idle` cannot spin — the operator fixes/rolls back and re-drives. This is the minimal-correct mirror of the Postgres engine's issue #603 gate (which additionally does an automatic block-with-backoff — a documented follow-up here). Regression test (`tests/runtime_robustness.rs::engine_nondeterminism_is_nonterminal_and_resumable`): a phase-1 workflow arms a durable timer (records `[WorkflowStarted, TimerStarted]` and blocks); flipping an injected drift flag makes the SAME workflow schedule an activity at that command slot; re-driving the unchanged history surfaces `NonDeterministic`, appends NOTHING (no `WorkflowFailed`, history byte-identical, execution still `RUNNING`), and after restoring the compatible build the run resumes and completes — plus `author_error_still_seals_failed` pins the `None` arm. Both fail against the pre-fix code (the drive returns `Ok(RunState::Failed)`). **Codex #1069 review — P2: an unregistered-activity claim is released, not stranded.** `queue::claim_next_ready_task` commits a task to `RUNNING` *before* the worker resolves its handler; if the activity name has no registered body, the drain previously returned `UnregisteredActivity` with the row left `RUNNING` — invisible to later drains (which only re-claim `PENDING`) until a full DB close+reopen ran the orphan reclaim (`UnregisteredActivity → Stuck` until a reopen). `drain_ready` now RELEASES the claim back to `PENDING` (new decrement-free `queue::release_claim`, guarded on `state = 'RUNNING'`, consuming no attempt and not advancing `run_at` — the body never ran) before surfacing the error, so a later drain re-claims it once the body is registered in the SAME runtime, no reopen. Regression test (`unregistered_activity_releases_claim_and_is_reclaimable`): after the error the task row is `PENDING` (verified via a raw connection), and registering the body + re-driving completes the workflow — fails pre-fix (task stranded `RUNNING`). The pre-existing `durability.rs::orphaned_running_task_is_reclaimed_and_body_reruns` test used the unregistered-activity path to *fabricate* a stranded-`RUNNING` orphan; it now fabricates that genuine crash-BEFORE-finalize state directly (raw `UPDATE ... SET state = 'RUNNING'`), keeping its real orphan-reclaim / at-least-once intent intact. **Codex round 8 — activity-panic containment.** A registered activity body that `panic!()`s (rather than returning `Err`) would unwind past the finalize/requeue branch AFTER the task row is already `RUNNING`, so no failure/requeue ever commits and the run wedges permanently (the claim query only re-selects `PENDING`; a single-process design has no live-peer poison-pill net). `drain_ready` now wraps the body invocation in `std::panic::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(...))` and converts a caught panic into the crate's NORMAL retryable-activity-failure path — treated exactly like `Err(msg)`: `finalize_activity_result` records the attempt and follows the retry policy (requeue if attempts remain, else terminal `ActivityFailed`). `AssertUnwindSafe` is sound (the body ran outside any transaction; on a caught panic its result is discarded). Mirrors the Postgres worker's handler-panic containment (issue #782), using the shared `autumn_harvest::error::panic_message` extractor. Regression tests: `panicking_activity_is_contained_and_exhausts_to_terminal` (a body that always panics, `max_attempts = 2` → both attempts caught+recorded → terminal `ActivityFailed`/`WorkflowFailed`, task never stranded `RUNNING`) and `panicking_activity_retry_then_succeeds` (panic on attempt 1, succeed on attempt 2 → the workflow completes, no terminal `ActivityFailed` in the log, the panic recorded only in the per-attempt audit). Both fail pre-fix (the panic unwinds through the tokio test). **Codex round 8 — mixed timer + activity batch.** A single decision cycle emitting BOTH a `StartTimer` and a `ScheduleActivity` (`tokio::join!`) is dispatched correctly: `apply_commands` already appends a cycle's schedule events in COMMAND order (a `for cmd in commands` loop), so **no drain-order change was needed** — the Codex "went Stuck" symptom is a poll-order concern, not a schedule-order one. Regression test (`mixed_timer_activity_batch_completes_and_replays`): with the activity as the first joined future (`join!(activity, timer)`), the batch dispatches both, the activity completes, the run blocks cleanly on the still-armed timer (not Stuck), a later drive fires the timer, the workflow completes, the two schedule events are in command order, and the resulting history replays byte-identically on the core `WorkflowReplayer` — proving the core matcher tolerates the interleaved sibling terminals (`ActivityCompleted` then `TimerFired`). **Documented CORE limitation (not a backend bug):** the REVERSE order — `join!(timer, activity)`, the timer polled first — is unsupported by the *core* determinism engine itself. `HistoryMatcher::match_timer_strict` (replay.rs) breaks its forward `TimerFired` scan at an unconsumed `ActivityScheduled` (it skips consumed siblings, child workflows, signals, external, update, and cancellable-timer events, but stops on an unconsumed activity); verified directly — the core `WorkflowReplayer` rejects even an ideal timer-first history with `NonDeterminismDetected(EarlyCompletion)`. This is shared with the Postgres engine and out of scope for this backend to change; put the activity branch first in a mixed `join!`. On this backend a timer-first mixed batch does not silently loop forever — the driver's `MAX_ITERATIONS` bound surfaces `SqliteError::Stuck` — but it is not a supported shape. **Codex #1069 review (commit `524823a`) — P1: a late signal must not beat an expired timeout.** When a workflow is parked in `wait_for_signal_timeout` / `receive_signal_timeout`, the decision cycle consumed any staged signal (`apply_commands`'s `WaitForSignal` branch, previously `store::take_pending_signal`) BEFORE `worker::drain_ready` appended the due `TimerFired` later in the same cycle. If the deadline passed while the runtime was idle and a signal arrived AFTER that deadline but before the next poll, history recorded `SignalReceived` first, so the timeout wrongly resolved as an approval — even though the core models a late signal as `TimerFired` **then** `SignalReceived` (so the late signal remains observable to a later plain wait). Fixed by mirroring the Postgres `merge_wake_events` arrival-time ordering: `harvest_signals` gains a `received_at` epoch-second column (set by `stage_signal`; a new doc-hidden `send_signal_as_of(exec, name, payload, now)` seam injects it deterministically, paired with the `*_as_of` drivers, while `send_signal` uses the wall clock). The `WaitForSignal` branch now delegates to `worker::ingest_awaited_signal`, which peeks the oldest pending signal's `received_at` and, via `queue::due_timers_before_signal`, fires every due deadline timer whose `fire_at <= received_at` **first** (ties to the timer, matching `received_at < fires_at` ⇒ signal-first), then appends the `SignalReceived`; a due timer whose deadline is *after* the signal arrived is left for the ordinary `drain_ready` pass to fire *after* the signal, so an on-time signal still wins even when the run is only driven past the deadline. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant** (this is a brand-new crate, so the additive column needs no migration). A plain `wait_for_signal` (no deadline timer) and any wait driven before its deadline are unchanged — a pending signal only ever interleaves with a deadline timer that is already *due* at drive time, so the three pre-existing `signal_timeout.rs` tests (which deliver before the deadline) are unaffected. Regression tests (`tests/signal_timeout.rs`): `late_signal_does_not_beat_expired_timeout` (signal delivered after the deadline → the run resolves `auto_rejected`, `TimerFired` precedes the still-recorded `SignalReceived`, and the history replays on the core `WorkflowReplayer`) and `on_time_signal_still_wins` (signal delivered before the deadline but driven past it → the approval wins, `SignalReceived` precedes the later-fired `TimerFired`). The first fails against the pre-fix ordering (the late signal wins). **Codex #1069 review (commit `524823a`) — P1: a workflow-handler panic must not seal FAILED on the first strike.** `run_workflow_with_state` distinguishes a caught **workflow-handler** panic (`Failed { handler_panic: true }`, distinct from an activity-body panic — that already had containment) from an author `Err`. The `drive_one_cycle` terminal `Failed` arm treated it like an author `Err(...)`: it appended `WorkflowFailed` and sealed `FAILED` on the FIRST strike, permanently closing a transiently-panicking or hotfix-able run. A new gate — placed beside the non-determinism gate, BEFORE any terminal side effect — now contains it (issue #782 analog). A per-execution consecutive-panic strike counter (`SqliteRuntime.workflow_panic_strikes`, in-process, cleared on any non-panic outcome so only *consecutive* panics count) is bounded by the new `WORKFLOW_PANIC_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` const (mirroring the Postgres worker's default). Under budget the panicked cycle is **discarded** — no terminal event appended, none of its (already-empty) pending commands persisted, state stays `RUNNING` — and surfaced as the new `SqliteError::WorkflowPanicked { execution_id, details }`, which propagates out of the drive loop (mirroring the non-determinism gate) so a hotfix/rollback can re-drive the UNCHANGED history to completion; only at/over budget is the run sealed with the typed `HandlerPanic` error (as a normal `RunState::Failed`). A genuine author `Err(...)` carries no panic flag and still fails terminally on the first strike, unchanged. Regression tests (`tests/runtime_robustness.rs`): `workflow_handler_panic_is_not_sealed_on_first_strike` (a workflow whose body always `panic!()`s stays `RUNNING` with no terminal event under budget and seals `WorkflowFailed` only after the budget is exhausted — never on the first strike) and `workflow_handler_panic_then_hotfix_resumes` (panic on the first drive, flip an injected hotfix flag so the corrected handler completes → the run completes `42`, and the history is exactly `[WorkflowStarted, WorkflowCompleted]`, proving the panicked cycle persisted nothing). Both fail against the pre-fix code (sealed on the first strike). **Codex #1069 review (commit `524823a`) — FIX C: thread the real `workflow_name` into the executor (cross-backend fidelity).** The decision loop called `run_workflow_with_state(exec, history, handler, input, empty_shared_state(), None)` — the trailing `None` is span-metadata, so the core built the `WorkflowContext` with an EMPTY `workflow_name` (the `workflow_name` param that populates `ctx.info().workflow_type`, issue #698, is separate from `span_meta.workflow_name`, which feeds only the OTel span this backend has no worker for). A workflow that used the documented replay-safe `ctx.info().workflow_type` — in an activity input, an idempotency key, or a branch — therefore recorded/replayed `""` here while the Postgres worker injects the real handler name: a divergence on the very byte-identity guarantee the crate makes. Fixed by driving through the pure, already-`pub` caps-carrying entry point `executor::run_workflow_with_state_history_policy_and_caps(...)`, passing the registered `workflow_name` (available from the execution row) in the dedicated load-bearing parameter and reproducing `run_workflow_with_state`'s own defaults for every other argument (`WorkflowHistoryPolicy::default()`, no declarative handlers, the `DEFAULT_MAX_*`/`DEFAULT_CURRENT_DETAILS_CAP_BYTES` caps, empty context headers, no offload, `NoOpMetrics`; `span_meta` stays `None`). **No core change** — the entry point and the cap consts were already `pub`. Regression test (`tests/cross_backend.rs::workflow_type_reaches_ctx_info_and_replays_on_core`): a workflow reads `ctx.info().workflow_type`, routes it through an activity input, and returns it — the run completes with the real registered name (NOT `""`), the recorded activity input carries it, and the history replays `ReplaySucceeded` on the core `WorkflowReplayer`. Fails pre-fix (records/returns `""`). **Codex #1069 review (commit `1e346f1`) — P2: `send_signal` rejects unknown / terminal targets.** `send_signal` staged a signal row unconditionally, and `harvest_signals` has no FK/state check, so a typoed `ExecutionId` or a signal to an already-`COMPLETED`/`FAILED` run returned `Ok(())` while the wakeup was silently lost — no live pull primitive (`wait_for_signal` / `receive_signal[_timeout]`) will ever consume it. `send_signal` (via `send_signal_as_of`) now validates the target BEFORE staging, mirroring the Postgres `signal::send_signal` rejections (and the crate's own `outcome()` not-found pattern): an unknown id → `SqliteError::ExecutionNotFound`; a terminal execution (per `autumn_harvest::erase::is_terminal_state`) → the new `SqliteError::WorkflowNotRunning { execution_id, state }`; a `RUNNING` execution stages (and later consumes) the signal exactly as before. The single-writer runtime holds SQLite's only write handle, so the state read and the stage cannot race a concurrent transition. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no schema change.** Regression test (`tests/runtime_robustness.rs::send_signal_rejects_unknown_and_terminal_targets`): an unknown id → `ExecutionNotFound` with zero staged rows; a `COMPLETED` execution → `WorkflowNotRunning` with zero staged rows; a `RUNNING` execution stages and drives to completion consuming the payload. The two rejection cases fail against the pre-fix code (which returned `Ok(())` and staged an unconsumable row). **Codex #1069 review (commit `1e346f1`) — P2: "fire expired timers before draining activities" assessed and DECLINED (a replay regression for the only reachable shape).** The finding proposed reordering `worker::drain_ready` to fire due `TimerFired` events *before* running ready activity bodies, so an activity-vs-timeout race that is only driven past the deadline records the deadline first. This was implemented, tested end-to-end, and **reverted**: for the *only* mixed activity+timer suspension expressible in this crate's subset — `tokio::join!(activity, timer)` with the activity polled first (the documented "Codex round 8 — mixed timer + activity batch" shape; the reverse order is already an unsupported core limitation) — the reorder produces a history the **core** determinism engine cannot replay. The core's `HistoryMatcher::scan_activity_terminal` (replay.rs) skips `TimerStarted`/`TimerCancelled` mid-scan but **breaks its forward `ActivityCompleted` scan at an unconsumed `TimerFired`** (`_ => break`), so `[…, TimerFired, ActivityCompleted, …]` leaves the activity permanently in-progress → the run wedges at `SqliteError::Stuck`. Verified directly on the core `WorkflowReplayer`: the current (activity-first) drain order `[…, ActivityCompleted, TimerFired]` replays `ReplaySucceeded`, while the finding's proposed order `[…, TimerFired, ActivityCompleted]` replays `NonDeterminismDetected`. The finding's premise ("replay resolves the activity branch even though the deadline passed") presupposes an order-tolerant activity-vs-timeout **race** matcher (the analog of `match_signal_or_timer`, which is why the sibling late-*signal* ordering fix in `ingest_awaited_signal` is sound); no such matcher exists for activity+timer, and `ctx.race()` explicitly rejects a mixed activity+timer shape (`HarvestError::Config`, pinned by the core's own `race_rejects_mixed_activity_and_timer_shape`). Correcting the finding would require a core change to `scan_activity_terminal` (out of scope — no `autumn-harvest/src/` changes) plus a new activity-vs-timer race primitive — far beyond a minimal faithful fix. The current drain order is therefore left unchanged. **Durability & concurrency pragmas.** `open()` sets `PRAGMA synchronous = FULL` (fsync on every commit — the conservative durability the crash-then-reopen tests rely on), `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` (the idiomatic single-writer + occasional-reader embedded choice; a harmless no-op on an in-memory database), and `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000` (a second connection racing the writer's `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` claim retries briefly instead of failing instantly with `SQLITE_BUSY`). WAL + FULL is fully durable. `run_until_idle()` returns the new `SqliteError::Runaway` when the fleet driver never quiesces within its iteration safety bound, rather than swallowing it as a clean `Ok(())` a caller could not distinguish from genuine quiescence (mirroring `run_until_blocked`'s `Stuck`). **No import/seed API** — the cross-backend guarantee is export-shaped (a SQLite-produced history → the core `WorkflowReplayer`) and needs none; a future edge → hub ingest path that rebuilds derived task/timer rows from open scheduled work (or rejects such histories) is a follow-up. **Public API.** `SqliteRuntime::open(path)` / `open_in_memory()` (reopen-safe — all state in the DB), `register_workflow(&WorkflowInfo)`, `register_activity(&ActivityInfo, body)` (the audited, declared-default-driven path — the analog of `register_workflow`) / `register_activity_raw(name, ActivitySpec)` (the hand-made escape hatch, no audit — the analog of `execute_activity_raw`), `start_workflow(name, input) -> ExecutionId`, `send_signal(exec, name, payload)`, `poll_once()` / `run_until_idle()` / `run_until_blocked(exec)` (+ `*_as_of` test seams), `load_history(exec) -> Vec<WorkflowEvent>`, `activity_attempts(exec, name)`, and the `outcome(exec)` accessor. Typed `SqliteError`/`SqliteResult` (thiserror). `RunState` / `ExecutionOutcome` / `ActivitySpec` / `ActivityBody` / `ActivityAttempt` are re-exported. **Known limitations (documented):** a crash *mid activity body* leaves the task `RUNNING` and is recovered by the reclaim on next `open()` (re-running the body — at-least-once); a single-process design has no live-peer heartbeat/poison-pill reclaimer, by design. Signals are pull-only (see above). The `activity_attempts(exec, name)` audit accessor is name-scoped: a workflow scheduling the same activity *name* more than once returns a single merged, attempt-ordered list across those instances (`load_history` remains the per-instance source of truth).
