Because Postgres's own clock decides `> NOW()` fresh on every query, a TTL expiring reverts the effective rate to the declared baseline the very next claim/debit/read — zero background sweeper, zero worker-side caching, zero restart. **Two symmetric admin route pairs** (both `require_admin`-gated, both fan out across every shard the same way `set_rate_limit`/`declare_compat` already do): `POST`/`DELETE /admin/rate-limits/{activity_name}/override` (body `{refill_rate?, burst?, ttl_secs}`) and `POST`/`DELETE /admin/start-throttle/{workflow_name}/override` (body `{refill_per_sec?, burst?, ttl_secs}`) — at least one of the two rate fields is required, both optional independently (overriding only `burst` leaves the declared `refill_rate` in effect, and vice versa, via the per-field `COALESCE`). **Validation, all pre-write:** a non-finite or non-positive `refill_rate`/`refill_per_sec`, a `burst < 1.0`, or a `ttl_secs` of `0` or over the server cap (`queue::MAX_PACING_OVERRIDE_TTL_SECS = 86_400` = 24h, via `pacing_override_expiry`) → `400`; an unregistered activity/workflow, or one that declares no rate limit/throttle at all → `404`; a **dynamically per-key-keyed** policy (issue #699's `rate_limit(key = ...)` / a throttle with a `key_expr`) → `409 Conflict` — a pacing override targets a single static bucket and has no defined meaning against a policy that fans out into many per-tenant buckets at runtime. `DELETE` is idempotent: clearing an activity/workflow with no active override still returns `200` reporting the declared baseline (`override_active: false`); the same `404`/`409` registry-lookup validation applies. **Audit.** Four new operation constants distinct from the pre-existing, unrelated `OP_RATE_LIMIT_OVERRIDE` (issue #332's *permanent* baseline-write route) — `OP_RATE_LIMIT_PACING_OVERRIDE_SET`/`_CLEAR` (`"rate_limit.pacing_override.set"`/`.clear`) and `OP_START_THROTTLE_PACING_OVERRIDE_SET`/`_CLEAR` (`"start_throttle.pacing_override.set"`/`.clear`), registered in the audit-op inventory and dispatch table alongside a new `TARGET_THROTTLE` audit target (pairing with the pre-existing `TARGET_RATE_LIMIT`). Every set/clear across every shard writes exactly one audit row per call. **Read surface.** `PacingOverrideResponse { key, declared_refill_rate, declared_burst, override_refill_rate, override_burst, override_active, effective_refill_rate, effective_burst, expires_at }` is both the `POST`/`DELETE` response body AND the shape `GET /admin/rate-limits` and `GET /admin/start-throttle` extend their existing rows with, registered in `management_api_response_fields()`. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, zero replay/determinism impact** — the override columns hold only dispatch/admission pacing state, never written to `harvest_events`; a replay of any execution that ran under an active override is byte-identical to one that never had one. **CLI:** `harvest rate-limit override <activity_name> [--refill-rate] [--burst] --ttl-secs <n>` / `harvest rate-limit clear <activity_name>` and the symmetric `harvest throttle override <workflow_name> ... / harvest throttle clear <workflow_name>` (aliases `rate-limits`/`throttles` preserved from the pre-existing `Status`/`Set` subcommands). **Tests, TDD red→green→refactor:** pure unit tests for the `COALESCE`-rendering helpers and the `EffectiveRateLimit` resolution struct (`queue.rs`, gated `#[cfg(feature = "db")]` since the sole caller, `throttle::resolve_backlog_bucket_state`, is itself DB-only); 16 DB integration tests in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/pacing_override_integration.rs` — rate-limit override activates on the very next claim/debit with no worker restart and reverts automatically at TTL expiry (the headline success-metric proof, driven through a real `Worker::run` poll loop rather than a direct SQL assertion), the same activation/TTL-revert pair via the real `POST /workflows/{name}/start` route for the throttle side (with a `clear_throttle_backlog` helper accounting for `reserve_or_defer`'s FIFO-backlog fast path, which defers a new admission for a key with a still-pending backlog entry regardless of the token bucket's current state), `DELETE` reverting an override before its TTL elapses (both rate-limit and throttle), an undeclared-activity/workflow `404` and a dynamically-keyed-policy `409` (both sides), an invalid-TTL/non-positive-rate `400` sweep (both sides) plus a dedicated burst-boundary test (`burst < 1.0` rejected, `burst == 1.0` accepted) and an `override_expires_at`-reflects-TTL-and-reverts-to-null-on-`DELETE` assertion against the raw response shape, the new read-only `GET /admin/start-throttle/{workflow_name}/override` route (AC5's dedicated companion, surfacing an active override even with no current deferred-start backlog) reflecting live state across a set/delete cycle plus its own 404/409 validation, and two audit-record tests confirming every set/clear (both rate-limit and throttle) writes exactly one row retrievable via the real `GET /admin/audit` route — registered in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt` for Docker-backed CI execution, and run repeatedly (both `--test-threads=1` sequential and default parallel) against a real local Postgres 16 to rule out cross-test state collision. Also: 5 no-DB auth-boundary tests in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/security.rs` (`eris_require_auth_blocks_*`) proving all 5 routes 401 without admin. **Out of scope (per issue):** runtime overrides for retry policies/timeouts/concurrency limits, creating brand-new rate limits/throttles at runtime for undeclared activities/workflows, cross-shard-coordinated global rate control, and Vantage UI surfacing (API + CLI only). **Post-review hardening (4 Codex rounds on PR #1220, all fixed):** **Round 1** (1 P1 + 1 P2) — `token_accrual_expr` computed accrued tokens with a single flat "currently effective" rate across the whole elapsed interval rather than a piecewise two-segment expression bounded by the override's actual expiry, so a TTL lapsing mid-interval retroactively applied the reverted baseline rate to the portion of the interval an override was still governing — producing a phantom token refill the instant the TTL expired. Fixed by splitting accrual into segment 1 (the override's rate up to `LEAST(override_expires_at, NOW())`) + segment 2 (the baseline rate for whatever remains), wired into `effective_available_tokens_expr`, `refund_rate_limit_token`, `claim_task_query`, and `oldest_pending_ages_query`; plus reordering the four admin handlers so the audit row is written before the not-found/dynamic-key early returns, matching every other admin route's audit-on-every-outcome contract. Tests: `rate_limit_override_expiring_mid_interval_accrues_piecewise_not_the_reverted_baseline_across_the_whole_interval`, `rate_limit_override_expiring_mid_interval_does_not_phantom_refill_the_dispatch_gate`. **Round 2** (2 P2s) — `GET /admin/start-throttle/{name}/override` silently degraded a total shard outage into a bare `200 {"override_active": false}` (an incident-response status read lying during an outage is worse than an explicit failure); now `503` on total outage / `207` naming the unreachable shard(s) on a partial one, mirroring the SET/DELETE routes' existing partial-write semantics. And every SET/GET/CLEAR response reported `declared_*` from the live registry instead of the bucket row's actually-*persisted* `refill_rate`/`burst`, which can diverge from the registry via the separate, permanent `POST /admin/rate-limits/{key}` route (issue #332/#699) independently rewriting a bucket's baseline. Tests: `rate_limit_override_reports_persisted_baseline_not_registry_after_legacy_permanent_change`, `throttle_override_reports_persisted_baseline_not_registry_after_legacy_permanent_change`, `get_start_throttle_pacing_override_returns_503_on_total_shard_outage`, `get_start_throttle_pacing_override_returns_207_on_partial_shard_outage_and_reflects_reachable_shard`. **Round 3** (1 P1 + 1 P2) — the throttle scanner's `fire_due_on_conn` candidate-selection CTE computed token availability from the raw baseline `refill_rate`/`burst` columns only, bypassing `effective_available_tokens_expr` entirely, so an operator raising a workflow's override rate specifically to unstick its already-deferred backlog could never make the scanner's own candidate pre-filter admit those rows — even though the downstream debit (`try_consume_rate_limit_token`, reached via `fire_claimed_throttle_row`) was already correctly override-aware and would happily fire them if only they got that far. Fixed by routing the CTE's token check through the shared `effective_available_tokens_expr("b")` helper, matching every other token-availability call site in the codebase. Test: `throttle_scanner_honors_active_override_in_its_candidate_gate` (drives the real `fire_due_throttled_starts` scanner directly, asserting `fired_count == 1` where the pre-fix baseline-only gate would leave the row permanently un-admitted at an effectively-frozen 1/hour rate). Plus a documentation-only fix: `docs/api-contract.json` never described the `207`/`503` partial/total-shard-outage response shapes any of the five pacing-override routes can return, undocumented since the feature shipped; added `success_response.notes` (the established Pattern-B convention this repo already uses for genuine-207-status write/read fan-out routes, e.g. `POST/DELETE /admin/queues/{queue}/pause|resume`) plus refined `error_responses[].description` distinguishing total-outage from audit-write-failure `503` sub-causes, across all five routes. **Round 4** (2 P2s) — the GET route's cross-shard "representative" pick chose the reported row by lowest raw `tokens` count, a proxy metric unrelated to override state: when shards genuinely disagree about an active override (a documented partial SET/DELETE outcome), the wrong shard could win the pick and the endpoint would silently report `override_active: false` in a plain `200` even though the override is live elsewhere, or the reverse. Fixed by collecting every reachable shard's raw row, deriving `override_active`/value disagreement from an explicit per-shard tally (shards disagreeing on the active/inactive boolean, OR all-active shards disagreeing on the actual `override_refill_rate`/`override_burst`), preferring an ACTIVE row whenever any shard has one (an incident-response check must never silently answer "no" while a live override still governs dispatch somewhere), and escalating to `207` with a new `shard_disagreement: bool` field plus a full `shards: {shard_id: PacingOverrideResponse}` breakdown whenever shards disagree — even when every shard is fully reachable, which previously never triggered `207` at all. And `evaluate_eligibility_for_shard` (the `/admin/eligibility` saturation diagnostic) re-derived "tokens available right now" in Rust via a flat `elapsed * effective.refill_rate` applying whichever rate is effective *at read time* to the *whole* elapsed interval — exactly the round-1 phantom-refill class, now reachable in a second place: an override expiring mid-interval with no intervening write could make this diagnostic disagree with what `claim_task` is actually enforcing, in either direction. Fixed by delegating the whole computation to `queue::effective_available_tokens_expr` — the same expression the claim gate, dispatch debit, and refund all use — so this diagnostic is structurally unable to drift from real enforcement. Tests: `get_start_throttle_pacing_override_reports_disagreement_across_live_shards` (two genuinely independent, fully-reachable shard databases with a live override on only one — distinct from round 2's outage-only `207` tests). Also fixed a genuine compile error hit while writing round-4's test coverage: diesel's blanket `RunQueryDsl` impl for every type shadows `Vec<T>::first()` via Deref-to-slice method-resolution order (`Vec<T>` is checked as a candidate receiver before deref-to-`[T]`, and diesel's trait method wins since `Vec<T>` has no inherent `.first()` of its own), so a bare `.first()` call on a plain in-memory `Vec` in a diesel-importing scope resolves to the wrong trait method (`RunQueryDsl::first`, a DB query method) and fails to compile — worked around with `.iter().next()` plus a documented `#[allow(clippy::iter_next_slice)]` (clippy's own suggested `.first()` fix reintroduces the exact error). **Round 5** (2 P2s) — `list_rate_limits` (`GET /admin/rate-limits`, the fleet-wide LIST route) deduplicated each key's per-shard rows down to a single "fewest remaining tokens" representative and never compared shards for override disagreement at all — round 4's disagreement detection only ever reached the single-key `GET /admin/start-throttle/{name}/override` deep-dive, so an operator scanning the LIST route for "which keys are currently overridden?" could have a live override on one shard silently hidden behind a different, non-overridden shard that happened to have fewer raw tokens and won the dedup. Separately, round 4's own disagreement check on the single-key GET route compared only the RAW `override_refill_rate`/`override_burst` columns across shards — missing the case where those columns are byte-identical (e.g. `refill_rate` overridden, `burst` left `None` on both shards, falling back to each shard's own baseline) while the underlying persisted BASELINE has diverged across shards via a partial legacy `POST /admin/rate-limits/{key}` (issue #332) fan-out, so the RESOLVED EFFECTIVE burst genuinely differs even though the raw-column check reported agreement. Both closed by extracting one shared, pure `queue::pacing_shards_disagree(effective: &[EffectiveRateLimit]) -> bool` (comparing exact-value active/inactive state plus resolved `refill_rate`/`burst`; `#[allow(clippy::float_cmp)]`-justified since both sides are either byte-identical copies of one resolved DB column or genuinely diverged persisted values, with no arithmetic imprecision in play) and wiring it into BOTH call sites: `list_rate_limits` now collects every reachable shard's row per key (not just the worst-case pick) into a new `build_rate_limit_bucket_view` helper, which computes disagreement over the resolved effective values and picks the representative row preferring an ACTIVE override (falling back to the pre-existing lowest-tokens heuristic only among a homogeneous active/inactive set) — `RateLimitBucketView` gains an additive `shard_disagreement: bool` field (`false` for the pre-existing single-shard `From<RateLimitBucket>` conversion, since only the new multi-shard path has the context to set it); and `get_start_throttle_pacing_override` replaces its round-4 raw-column comparison with the shared function over each shard's `resolve_effective_rate_limit`-resolved value (including a declared-baseline fallback for a reachable shard with no bucket row yet). Tests: 7 pure unit tests for `pacing_shards_disagree` (empty/single-shard never disagrees, all-inactive agrees, all-active-identical agrees, active-state-mismatch disagrees in both orderings, an all-active pair with a genuinely different raw `refill_rate` disagrees, a deliberate boundary that two all-INACTIVE shards with different baselines are NOT flagged — baseline-consistency-when-nothing-is-overridden is explicitly out of scope for this override-consistency check — and the round-5 money test `pacing_shards_disagree_active_but_diverged_baseline_disagrees` — byte-identical raw override columns on both shards but a deliberately-diverged baseline burst (20.0 vs 30.0) resolves to genuinely different effective values and IS flagged) plus `list_rate_limits_reports_disagreement_across_live_shards` (two genuinely independent shard databases: shard 0 carries a live ACTIVE override seeded with MORE tokens than shard 1's inactive row — deliberately defeating the old "fewest tokens wins" pick, so the assertion can only pass if disagreement detection, not lucky token counts, is what now surfaces the override on the LIST route).
- **Per-tenant resource quotas on executions, history, and DLQ** (implemented) — see issue #946. Harvest already bounds per-key **rate** (`ThrottlePolicy`, #607) and per-key **parallelism** (`ConcurrencyPolicy`, #247), but nothing capped a tenant's aggregate *footprint* — how much a single misbehaving or malicious caller could accumulate before anyone noticed. New `QuotaPolicy` (core module `quota.rs`) declares up to **three independent, optional caps** per resolved tenant key, checked in a fixed deterministic order (`ActiveExecutions` → `HistoryBytes` → `DeadLetters`): `max_active_executions` (count of non-terminal RUNNING/PAUSED executions sharing the key), `max_history_bytes` (aggregate `harvest_events` payload bytes across the key's active executions, summed via `pg_column_size` against the existing `idx_harvest_events_exec` index), `max_dead_letters` (count of `harvest_dead_letters` rows sharing the key). **No second key resolver (AC1)** — `resolve_quota_key(expr, input)` delegates to the EXISTING `concurrency::resolve_concurrency_key` dot-path resolver (issue #247); an unresolvable key (missing/null/non-object input) **fails open** (no policy enforced for that admission) rather than blocking a start on a config that never matched, mirroring the concurrency/throttle precedent. Declarable via `#[workflow(quota(key = "input.tenant_id", max_active_executions = 100, max_history_bytes = "10MB", max_dead_letters = 50))]` (macro attribute, `key` required, `max_history_bytes` parsed as a validated byte-size string) or `WorkflowInfo::with_quota(QuotaPolicy)`; `#[dag]` deliberately has NO `quota` attribute (DAGs bypass registry-aware admission gates entirely, an intentional pre-existing boundary shared with concurrency/throttle/debounce).

  **Enforcement point — one choke point, no new `StartWorkflowParams` field.** Quota is checked entirely inside `start_or_load_workflow_execution_collect` — the function nearly every registry-aware start path funnels through — via `enforce_quota_admission` (the fresh-insert branch, and each of `replace_execution`'s three internal call sites) and the P1-fix `enforce_quota_before_terminate_pre_check` (below). The declared policy is resolved from `completion_trigger::GLOBAL_WORKFLOW_METADATA` (the same process-global mirror `concurrency`/`sla`/`retry_policy` already use to reach core-crate code with no access to the plugin's live handler registry), and the tenant key is resolved from the request's own input — so no new `StartWorkflowParams` field was needed. Enforcement runs under a transaction-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock` (`lock_quota_key`, a `"quota:{workflow_name}:{key}"`-namespaced lock disjoint from #247's concurrency-lock namespace) serializing check-then-admit for the same key, closing the identical concurrent-overshoot race #247 already closes. `load_quota_usage` is a SINGLE indexed round-trip (AC7 — never a full-table scan): the just-inserted row's own RUNNING state is subtracted back out (`.saturating_sub(1)`) so `current` always reports usage *before* this admission — the success metric's "capped at exactly 100" requires the 100th admission to observe `current=99`, not `100`.

  **P1 fix — the two-transaction `TerminateIfRunning` hazard.** `start_or_load_workflow_execution_collect`'s pre-existing `TerminateIfRunning`-over-an-active-prior path runs an UNWRAPPED, already-committed "Transaction 1" (cancel the prior run) BEFORE the wrapped `conn.transaction()` "Transaction 2" (the actual quota-checked insert). Enforcing quota only inside Transaction 2 meant a quota-blocked `TerminateIfRunning` request would still irreversibly cancel the prior execution in Transaction 1 and THEN reject with no successor — silently destroying work, strictly worse than simply rejecting the request. `enforce_quota_before_terminate_pre_check` closes this by checking quota BEFORE the pre-check cancellation runs, mirroring the file's pre-existing "POINT 1" admission-gate ordering pattern ("so a blocked start never cancels the prior run first") verbatim. Its self-exemption semantics differ deliberately from the fresh-insert helper: it subtracts 1 only when the ABOUT-TO-BE-CANCELLED prior's own `quota_key` equals the new request's resolved key (`existing_quota_key == Some(key)`) — that row is about to VACATE its slot, not occupy a freshly-inserted one — versus the fresh-insert helper's unconditional `.saturating_sub(1)` for the row it just inserted.

  **Cross-type continue-as-new (#803) interaction.** A `continue_as_new_as`/`continue_as_new_as_type` successor re-resolves its OWN quota key from its target type's declared policy against the fresh input (never inherits the predecessor's verbatim) — a target type with no declared policy CLEARS the key rather than carrying the predecessor's forward, consistent with how #803 already re-resolves `execution_timeout`/`sla`/concurrency/owner metadata on a type change. A same-type continue-as-new (`ctx.continue_as_new`) propagates the key unchanged.

  **Typed error, structured 429, never silent, never 500 (AC4).** `HarvestError::QuotaExceeded { workflow_name, key, resource, limit, current }` (a `#[non_exhaustive]` `QuotaResource` enum: `ActiveExecutions`/`HistoryBytes`/`DeadLetters`, `.as_str()` → `"active_executions"`/`"history_bytes"`/`"dead_letters"`). All THREE registry-aware HTTP fresh-start entry points — plain `POST /workflows/{name}/start`, `POST /workflows/{name}/signal-with-start` (#244), `POST /workflows/{name}/update-with-start` (#479) — carry a bespoke `QuotaExceeded` arm mapping to `429 Too Many Requests` via one shared `quota_exceeded_body(workflow_name, key, resource, limit, current)` helper (byte-identical JSON shape + a `STATUS_FAILED` audit row across all three), never falling through to the generic `map_error` 500 path. **Every deferred/scanner-fired start path also handles it explicitly rather than propagating a bare `?`** (found and closed while extending test coverage): the batch/debounce/throttle/event-batch/completion-trigger scanners all catch `QuotaExceeded` BEFORE their generic non-transient-error arm and RE-DEFER (leave the row, refund any reserved rate-limit token, bump the retry deadline with backoff) rather than dropping the pending start or letting the `?` abort the WHOLE scanner-tick transaction — an uncaught propagation would roll back every OTHER already-processed row in the same tick and starve every LATER scanner duty (history-ceiling enforcement, broken-session/mutex-lease reclaim, start-idempotency sweep, …) for as long as one quota-blocked tenant sits at the head of the claim queue: the exact runaway-tenant scenario #946 exists to contain, turned into a fleet-wide scanner stall instead. The metric is recorded exactly ONCE per rejection, at the single `enforce_quota_admission`/`enforce_quota_before_terminate_pre_check` choke point — every outer scanner arm passes the SAME `metrics` handle through rather than re-emitting, so a re-deferred row is never double-counted on a later retry (mirrors the pre-existing `Blocked`/`QuotaBlocked` no-double-count precedent in `completion_trigger.rs`).

  **`GET /admin/quotas` (AC5).** Admin-gated, read-only, `shard_fanout`-based cross-shard fan-out (the same `/admin/concurrency`/`/admin/debounce`/`/admin/start-throttle` pattern) reporting usage-vs-declared-limit per resolved `(workflow_name, quota_key)` pair, with `complete`/`partial`/`unavailable` degradation on an unreachable shard (never a hard 500). Per-shard counts are summed into a fleet-wide convenience total but the FULL per-shard breakdown is always listed too — quota enforcement is shard-local (AC8), so the same key can carry genuinely independent usage on every shard a tenant's traffic happens to land on, and collapsing to one number would hide which shard a tenant is actually capped on. Declared limits are resolved from the CURRENT registered `WorkflowInfo.quota`, never a stale usage-time snapshot.

  **Metric (AC6).** `harvest.quota.rejected{workflow, resource}` (`METRIC_QUOTA_REJECTED`, `record_quota_rejected(workflow, resource)` — two parameters, deliberately excluding the resolved tenant key, which would be unbounded cardinality; per-key visibility is via `GET /admin/quotas` only), bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter.rs`.

  **Sharding scope (AC8).** `quota_key` is a plain, denormalized column on BOTH `harvest_workflow_executions` (nullable, indexed `(workflow_name, quota_key, state) WHERE quota_key IS NOT NULL`) AND `harvest_dead_letters` (`workflow_name`/`quota_key` denormalized rather than joined through the owning execution — DLQ entries are the durable long-term failure record and routinely outlive their execution's retention window, issue #737; a join would silently under-count once the execution row is retention-collected). A tenant spread across N shards effectively gets a `limit × N` aggregate cap unless pinned to one shard via issue #697's `residency_key`; `docs/sharding.md` documents this explicitly, cross-referencing #697. Migration `20260725000000_harvest_workflow_quotas` is purely additive (two nullable columns + two partial indexes across the two tables) — a no-quota workflow's rows carry `quota_key = NULL`, excluded by the partial indexes, paying zero storage/index overhead (AC9). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no replay-determinism impact** — `quota_key` is resolved once at admission time and never recorded as an event or read on replay.

  **Tests, TDD red→green→refactor.** 18 DB integration tests in `tests/integration/quota_enforcement_tests.rs` (core crate) covering per-resource cap enforcement, per-key and per-workflow-type isolation, the no-policy/no-caps/unresolvable-key no-op paths, cap release on completion, the #803 continue-as-new interaction (same-type propagate / cross-type re-resolve / cross-type-to-no-policy clear), the P1 regression across all three `replace_execution` call sites (`AllowDuplicateFailedOnly` resurrection, `TerminateIfRunning` over a terminal prior, `TerminateIfRunning`'s NEW-request-key resolution) plus a control proving `replace_execution` paths still succeed when under cap, and the issue's own success-metric scenario (`concurrent_runaway_tenant_is_capped_while_a_second_tenant_is_unaffected`, driven with GENUINE concurrency via `tokio::spawn` racing on separate connections — not a sequential loop — scaled from the issue's literal 10,000-starts/100-cap to a 60-attempt burst against a 20 cap for CI runtime, since the admission-time SQL path under concurrency is scale-invariant; asserts tenant A capped at EXACTLY the declared limit with every overflow attempt receiving the typed `QuotaExceeded`, and every one of a concurrently-racing tenant B's attempts succeeding, unaffected). 12 HTTP integration tests in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/quota_admin_integration.rs` covering the plain-start 429 body shape + audit row + under-cap success + no-policy pass-through, all 6 `/admin/quotas` scenarios (usage-vs-limit, per-key isolation within one workflow type, DLQ counting, cross-shard sum + per-shard breakdown, partial-shard degradation, admin-auth requirement), and — closing a P2 test-coverage gap found during review — the `signal-with-start`/`update-with-start` 429 body-shape + zero-phantom-execution-row assertions (neither route needs a registered signal/update handler to exercise the quota-rejection arm: the check runs inside the shared core admission primitive before any signal/update-specific validation is even reached for an unmatched name). Contract parity verified via the plugin's `contract_regression` suite (38/38 green, including `management_routes_match_contract`, `contract_request_fields_match_code_registry`, `contract_response_fields_match_code_registry`, `every_management_route_is_classified`). All suites verified green against a real local Postgres 16 (Docker unavailable in this sandbox; CI runs Docker-backed).
- **Phase 3.x** (implemented): Operator early-warning for workflow history bloat near the cap — see issue #704. Before this, the only signal that a still-running workflow's recorded event history was approaching its optional `event_hard_cap` (`WorkflowHistoryPolicy`) was the hard cap itself — the run would eventually reach it, terminally force-fail, and land in the DLQ, with zero prior warning. This ships two complementary, purely additive surfaces: a discovery filter to *find* offending live executions on demand, and a counter that *pages* the moment one crosses a configurable soft fraction of the cap. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, one additive nullable-column migration, no shard-routing change, no replay-determinism impact** — this is a read-path discovery filter plus a post-commit telemetry emission over already-recorded state.

  **Discovery filter (AC1/AC2/AC6/AC7).** `GET /api/harvest/workflows?history_bloat_min_events=<N>` restricts the response to **live (non-terminal)** executions whose current recorded `harvest_events` count is `>= N`, fanned out across every shard via the existing `observe_shards`/`iter_shards()` scaffold and globally sorted by history size descending (`build_history_bloat_fanout`: a pure, unit-tested merge that concatenates every shard's *unbounded* per-shard result set — no per-shard `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` — sorts once at the merge stage, then truncates to `limit`, so the global top-K-across-shards ordering is correct by construction). Each row carries its current `history_event_count` (AC2) so an operator can rank/triage without a second call. `history_bloat_min_events` is its own dedicated discovery path — it rejects composition with `cursor`/`page_size`/`order` pagination with `400` (the computed sort has no keyset cursor, so silently mis-ordering or ignoring the request would be worse than a clear rejection), and rejects a non-numeric or negative value with `400` and a JSON error body (AC7) — never a `500`, never a silent empty match. `0` is a well-defined boundary (matches every live execution, not a "disabled" sentinel). The "live (non-terminal)" filter derives from `erase::TERMINAL_STATES` — the engine's existing single source of truth for terminal-state classification — rather than a second hand-maintained literal, so it can never silently drift from the states `is_terminal_state`/`resolve_execution_id_by_workflow_id` (issue #805) already recognize as terminal. Registered in `docs/api-contract.json` (AC6) and exposed via `harvest workflow list --history-bloat-min-events <N>` (`autumn-harvest-cli`), with `contract_coverage`/`request_mapping` test coverage. **`history_bloat_min_events` is a deliberately distinct query parameter from the pre-existing, general-purpose `min_history_events` filter (issue #493)** — see "Post-review hardening" below for why the two must never share a name.

  **Soft-threshold counter (AC3/AC4).** `harvest.workflow.history_bloat` (`METRIC_WORKFLOW_HISTORY_BLOAT`, bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter.rs`) fires **at-least-once** — a rare crash-window duplicate is possible and deliberately accepted over a permanently lost signal, see "Post-review hardening" below — the moment an execution's recorded history first crosses `history_bloat_warn_fraction * event_hard_cap`, on either of two paths: (1) a still-`RUNNING` execution mid-decision, or (2) the SAME decision that also reaches the event-count hard cap in one inline append batch and terminally fails the execution (`fail_workflow_for_history_cap`), based on the durable post-failure event count — labeled by `workflow` (the registered `#[workflow]` type name) only, per ADR-0001 §7's cardinality rule (`execution.id` is never a label). The soft fraction is configurable via `HarvestBuilder::history_bloat_warn_fraction` / `WorkflowHistoryPolicy::with_history_bloat_warn_fraction` (clamped `[0.0, 1.0]`, default `DEFAULT_HISTORY_BLOAT_WARN_FRACTION = 0.75`); `0.0` (or an unconfigured `event_hard_cap`) is a documented, test-covered no-op (AC4). The pure decision function `history_bloat_threshold_crossed(current_history_event_count, cap, fraction, already_warned) -> bool` performs the inclusive `>=` comparison with truncating cast (`(cap as f64 * fraction) as u64`) and is unit-tested at the exact boundary plus zero-cap/negative-fraction/fraction-1.0 edge cases. Persistence follows the codebase's established "compute pure decision before the transaction, act only in the post-commit `Persisted` arm" discipline (the same pattern `harvest.update.completed`/`failed`/`harvest.signal.unhandled`, issue #684, already use): `should_warn_history_bloat` is computed at the top of `process_workflow_task` — gated on `!is_canary` (issue #796's synthetic liveness probe contributes to no `harvest.workflow.*` business signal, mirroring the sibling `record_workflow_completed`/`history_size`/`continue_as_new` gates) and `matches!(&outcome, WorkflowOutcome::Suspended { .. })` — and only marked/emitted after a successful commit, so a paused-park discard, an ND-block (#603), or a persist failure can never mark an execution "warned" for a decision cycle that never became durable. The at-least-once, idempotent-per-crossing guarantee is enforced by a single guarded `UPDATE harvest_workflow_executions SET history_bloat_warned_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1 AND history_bloat_warned_at IS NULL` (`store::mark_history_bloat_warned`, returning whether *this* call performed the transition) against a new nullable `history_bloat_warned_at TIMESTAMPTZ` column (migration `20260716000000_harvest_workflow_history_bloat_warn`; deliberately unindexed — it is read/written only by exact-row PK operations, never filtered in a `WHERE`) — race-safe by construction (a single atomic statement, not select-then-update), and correctly reset-to-`NULL`-by-default for continue-as-new successors and reset forks (each is a fresh row tracking its own history from zero).

  **Alerting/dashboards/docs (AC5).** A starter alert `harvest_workflow_history_bloat` was added to `docs/alerts/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json` (ticket severity, `sum by (workflow) (increase(harvest_workflow_history_bloat_total[15m])) > 0` — alerting on any increase within the window rather than a sustained rate, since this is a per-run crossing event, not a rate signal) with a `first_action` pointing at `harvest workflow list --history-bloat-min-events <threshold>` and a full runbook stanza at `docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_workflow_history_bloat`. Dashboard panel, ADR-0001 §7 catalogue row, and `docs/telemetry.md` entries were added and are enforced by the existing anti-drift tests (`dashboard_pack_docs.rs`, `alert_pack_docs.rs`) so the metric/alert/panel triad cannot silently drift apart.

  **Success metric.** Operator MTTD for a runaway-history workflow drops from "never, until the hard cap force-fails it to the DLQ" to the soft-threshold crossing instant — bounded below one poll/telemetry-flush interval, well under the issue's <1 minute target — since the counter fires the moment the crossing is durably committed.

  **Out of scope (per issue, unchanged):** the existing hard-cap terminal-fail/DLQ behavior; auto-`continue_as_new`; per-execution gauges (would be unbounded label cardinality); retroactively emitting history-size for already-terminal runs. (The per-shard discovery query's row-scan cost was initially left unbounded — see "Post-review hardening" below, finding C, for the fix that bounds it per shard.)

  **Tests, TDD red→green→refactor, then multi-angle review (replay-determinism, AC-completeness, cardinality/security, shard-fanout correctness, docs/usability) with all findings closed.** Pure unit tests for `history_bloat_threshold_crossed` (worker.rs, 6 cases incl. the exact-threshold boundary, disabled fraction, negative fraction, zero cap) and `build_history_bloat_fanout` (api.rs, merge/sort/truncate). DB integration in `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/metrics_integration.rs`: `history_bloat_counter_fires_once_when_a_still_suspended_execution_crosses_the_soft_threshold` (real worker + Postgres transaction, cap=8/fraction=0.5 exact-threshold crossing, plus a direct second `mark_history_bloat_warned` call proving the SQL guard is race-safe), `history_bloat_counter_never_fires_when_the_soft_threshold_is_disabled` (AC4, end-to-end through the real registry/worker path), and — added during the review pass to close the one real coverage gap the review surfaced — `history_bloat_counter_fires_exactly_once_across_two_real_live_suspension_cycles`: a dedicated probe workflow that suspends on a short (1s), genuinely-firing timer, is woken for a real *second* live decision cycle by the worker's own timeout scanner, and re-suspends on a long timer; the test polls for a durable `TimerStarted("history-bloat-second-suspension")` event to prove cycle 2 actually ran, then asserts the counter recorder shows **zero** new emissions after that cycle — a stronger, genuinely end-to-end proof than the sibling test's direct second function call. HTTP integration in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/history_bloat_integration.rs` (8 tests, since renamed to `history_bloat_min_events_*` — see "Post-review hardening" below): sorted-descending + `history_event_count` presence (AC1/AC2), full terminal-state exclusion across all six `erase::TERMINAL_STATES` values including `CONTINUED_AS_NEW`, non-numeric/negative `400` rejection (AC7), pagination-combo `400` rejection, a `history_bloat_min_events=0` boundary test, and — the other genuine review-surfaced gap — `history_bloat_min_events_merges_and_sorts_globally_across_shards`: a real **two-Postgres-database** test (mirroring `workflow_filter_integration.rs`'s `setup_sharded_databases`/`build_two_shard_pool` pattern) seeding above/below-threshold rows on both shards plus a large terminal row, proving the HTTP path performs a genuine global sort across shards rather than concatenating each shard's already-sorted page. All DB/HTTP suites were executed green against real Postgres 16 (not merely compile-checked), registered in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt` for the Docker-backed Linux CI run, and the full workspace quality gate (fmt, clippy `-D warnings` on all three touched crates, the full no-DB core suite, plugin lib suite, and CLI suite) was re-verified green after the review-fix batch.

  **Post-review hardening (PR #1139 review, two findings, both fixed).** **P1 — query-parameter name collision (correctness/regression).** The initial cut triggered the discovery path above on the existing, shipped, general-purpose `min_history_events` filter (issue #493, landed independently before this PR) — silently breaking every caller who combined `min_history_events` with `state=`, `order=`, or cursor pagination, since the new dedicated path forces "live (non-terminal) only, sorted by size, no pagination" onto a parameter that previously composed freely. This is the same "semantic merge conflict" failure class this repo has hit before: no line-level `git` conflict exists (the two features were developed independently and never touch the same lines), so only careful review caught it. Fixed by renaming the AC1 discovery trigger to a new, dedicated query parameter, `history_bloat_min_events` — `min_history_events` (issue #493) is restored to its original, unmodified, freely-composable behavior across every call site: `WorkflowFilters` gains a distinct `history_bloat_min_events: Option<u64>` field alongside the untouched `min_history_events: Option<u64>`; the query-string parser gains a new `"history_bloat_min_events"` match arm (the pre-existing `"min_history_events"` arm and its two downstream consumers in `load_workflows`/`load_stalled_workflows` are byte-for-byte unchanged); `list_workflows`'s routing branch now checks `filters.history_bloat_min_events.is_some()`; and the CLI, `docs/api-contract.json`, both starter-pack JSON files, `docs/telemetry.md`, and `docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md` were all updated to the new name (`harvest workflow list --history-bloat-min-events <N>` / `?history_bloat_min_events=<N>`). Regression-proofed with three new HTTP integration tests exercising the *restored* `min_history_events` (#493) behavior directly: `min_history_events_composes_with_state_including_terminal` (the exact composition the collision broke — `?state=COMPLETED&min_history_events=N` must return a matching **terminal** row, which the AC1 dedicated path would always exclude), `min_history_events_composes_with_page_size_pagination`, and `min_history_events_composes_with_order_pagination` (both proving `min_history_events` + pagination returns `200` with the paginated object shape, not the `400` `history_bloat_min_events` deliberately produces for the same combination). **P2 — a `history_bloat_warn_fraction` of exactly `1.0` silently disables the counter.** The public builder API (`with_history_bloat_warn_fraction`) accepted the full `[0.0, 1.0]` range, but `process_workflow_task`'s unconditional hard-cap force-fail check runs *before* the warn-fraction crossing calculation and short-circuits with an early return whenever `current_history_event_count >= cap` — the exact condition a fraction of `1.0` requires to cross. So `harvest.workflow.history_bloat` could never fire for a `1.0`-configured workflow, silently contradicting the documented "only `0.0` disables it" contract. Fixed by clamping the public config surface's upper bound below `1.0` rather than reordering `worker.rs`'s hard-cap/soft-warn control flow (the two live in separate code paths — the hard-cap teardown and the post-commit warn-emit — and reordering them was judged more invasive than tightening the input range): new `MAX_HISTORY_BLOAT_WARN_FRACTION: f64 = 0.999` constant in `context.rs`; `with_history_bloat_warn_fraction` now clamps to `[0.0, MAX_HISTORY_BLOAT_WARN_FRACTION]` (was `[0.0, 1.0]`). This is a deliberate divergence from the sibling `DEFAULT_CONTINUE_AS_NEW_DEADLINE_FRACTION` knob (issue #772), which safely clamps to the full `[0.0, 1.0]` because it has no competing hard-cap early-return race — the two mechanisms are structurally different and the divergence is intentional, not an inconsistency. Existing unit tests in `context.rs`/`builder.rs` asserting the old "clamps to `1.0`" behavior were updated to assert clamping below `1.0`, plus a new explicit `1.0`-input case pinning the fix. No `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change from either fix — the P1 fix is a query-parameter rename plus doc updates, and the P2 fix is a config-surface input-range tightening.

  **Post-review hardening (PR #1139 review, second pass, four findings, all fixed).** **Finding #1 (P1) — the soft-threshold warning never fired on the hard-cap terminal-fail path.** `should_warn_history_bloat` was computed and emitted only inside the `Persisted` arm for a still-`Suspended` outcome, but every one of `process_workflow_task`'s six `fail_workflow_for_history_cap` early-return sites (local-activity-inline, external-signal-inline, mixed-batch, and the primary suspension check) short-circuits *before* that arm whenever `current_history_event_count >= cap` — precisely the scenario a soft-threshold crossing exists to warn about *before* it happens, and by construction the fraction is always `< event_hard_cap` (the P2 clamp above guarantees `fraction <= MAX_HISTORY_BLOAT_WARN_FRACTION < 1.0`), so a decision that reaches the hard cap has *always already* crossed the soft threshold in the same instant — meaning the counter silently never fired for the single most important case: a workflow whose history bloat is severe enough to trip the hard cap in one decision, rather than being caught earlier while still healthy. Fixed by extracting the mark+emit logic (previously inline in the `Persisted` arm only) into a new shared helper, `emit_history_bloat_warning_if_crossed`, called from **both** the `Persisted` arm and the new choke point inside `fail_workflow_for_history_cap` itself (which every one of the six call sites already funnels through) — so the two call shapes can never independently drift. `fail_workflow_for_history_cap` gained a `registry: &HandlerRegistry` parameter (threaded through all six call sites) to resolve `history_bloat_warn_fraction`; the mark+emit runs *before* the terminal DLQ transition, gated on `!is_canary_workflow(...)` (mirroring the sibling `Suspended` gate) and the same pure `history_bloat_threshold_crossed` decision function, so a canary probe is still excluded and the guard column is still exactly-once. **Finding #2 (P1) — the mark-then-emit ordering was not crash-recoverable.** The original ordering called `store::mark_history_bloat_warned` *before* emitting the counter; a worker crash in the narrow window between the two would leave the guard column stamped `NOT NULL` with the counter never actually emitted — a *permanent, silent* loss of the signal, since the guard column exists precisely to make the crossing a one-shot event with no future retry to fall back on (unlike this codebase's other best-effort telemetry emissions — `run_deferred_schedule_counter`, `emit_update_result_metrics`, `emit_unhandled_signal_metrics` — which recur and self-heal on a later cycle). Fixed by reversing the order inside the new shared helper: **emit the counter first, mark the guard column second**. A crash in the window between the two now leaves `history_bloat_warned_at` `NULL`, so a future retry of the same decision cycle (this codebase's existing crash-recovery mechanism — no new machinery introduced) re-detects the still-unmarked crossing and re-emits, rather than the mark permanently silencing a signal that was never delivered. This is a deliberate, documented divergence from the mark-then-emit convention used elsewhere in this codebase: it trades a rare crash-window duplicate emission (an accepted cost for a best-effort early-*warning* signal, not a durable audit record) for eliminating a permanent-loss failure mode that is uniquely severe for a one-shot, non-recurring gate. `docs/telemetry.md`, `docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md`, and `docs/alerts/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json` were all updated to describe the corrected at-least-once (not exactly-once) delivery semantics and the new dual emission sites, including runbook guidance that a lone duplicate-looking page for an already-warned execution is the benign crash-retry case, not evidence of a second distinct crossing. **Finding #3 (P2) — `failure_cause` was silently ignored by the history-bloat discovery loader.** `list_workflows` parses and applies `failure_cause` on the general-purpose `load_workflows`/`load_stalled_workflows` paths, but the dedicated `load_history_bloat_workflows` loader never consulted it at all — so `?history_bloat_min_events=N&failure_cause=non_determinism` silently ignored the second filter and returned every above-threshold row regardless of its recorded cause, rather than narrowing to the ones the caller actually asked for. Fixed by applying the identical `search_attrs @> {"failure_cause": <cause>}` JSONB-containment predicate (`sql::<Bool>("search_attrs @> ").bind::<Jsonb, _>(...)`) inside `load_history_bloat_workflows`, immediately after the shared `apply_search_attr_filters` call. **Finding #4 (P2) — `no_progress_minutes` and `history_bloat_min_events` silently let one filter win when combined.** These are two separate, mutually-exclusive discovery paths (stalled-workflow discovery, issue #486, vs. history-bloat discovery, this issue) that each sort by a *different* computed value the other loader neither computes nor honors — `list_workflows` checked them in sequence with no interaction guard, so combining both params in one request silently dropped whichever filter's branch ran second rather than telling the caller. Fixed by rejecting the combination up front with a clear `400` (`AutumnError::bad_request_msg`), mirroring the existing `history_bloat_min_events` + pagination precedent, so a caller who accidentally combines the two discovery paths gets an explicit error instead of a silently mis-filtered page (AC7's "never a silent, mis-filtered page" contract). Regression-proofed with five new tests: `history_bloat_counter_fires_even_when_the_same_decision_reaches_the_hard_cap` (`metrics_integration.rs`, finding #1 — a real worker + Postgres transaction where `event_hard_cap=4`/`fraction=0.5` makes the SAME decision reach both the hard cap `4 >= 4` and the soft threshold `4 >= 2` at once, asserting the execution terminally `FAILED` via the DLQ path *and* `history_bloat_warned_at` is stamped *and* the counter fired exactly once), `history_bloat_min_events_composes_with_failure_cause` and `history_bloat_min_events_combined_with_no_progress_minutes_returns_400` (`history_bloat_integration.rs`, findings #3/#4, against real Postgres). All DB/HTTP suites were re-executed green against real Postgres 16 (not merely compile-checked), and the full workspace quality gate (fmt, clippy `-D warnings` on both touched crates, plus the no-DB `ci_run_coverage`/`migration_hygiene` guard suites) was re-verified green after this second review-fix batch. No `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change from any of the four fixes — findings #1/#2 are a `worker.rs`-internal control-flow and ordering fix behind the existing metric/guard-column contract, and findings #3/#4 are `api.rs`-internal query-building fixes behind the existing `history_bloat_min_events` parameter contract.

  **Post-review hardening (PR #1139 review, third pass, three findings, all fixed).** **Finding A (P2) — a NaN warn-fraction silently trips the soft-threshold warning on the first suspended cycle of every execution.** `with_history_bloat_warn_fraction`'s clamp (`fraction.clamp(0.0, MAX_HISTORY_BLOAT_WARN_FRACTION)`) does not sanitize `NaN`: `f64::clamp`'s real implementation is a pair of direct `<`/`>` comparisons against the bounds, both of which evaluate to `false` for `NaN` (unlike `f64::max`/`f64::min`, which *do* have NaN-avoidance behavior — `clamp` does not use them), so a `NaN` input passes through unclamped and is stored verbatim. `history_bloat_threshold_crossed`'s decision then computes `(cap as f64 * NaN) as u64`; `f64 as u64` in Rust saturates rather than panicking, and `NaN as u64 == 0` (stable since Rust 1.45), so the soft threshold becomes `event_count >= 0` — trivially satisfied by the very first recorded event of **every** execution using a corrupted `NaN` fraction, regardless of how close the run actually is to its cap. Fixed by explicitly checking `fraction.is_nan()` before the clamp and normalizing to `DEFAULT_HISTORY_BLOAT_WARN_FRACTION` (not `0.0`/disabled — silently turning off the whole feature on a corrupted config value would be a worse failure mode than falling back to the documented default) inside `with_history_bloat_warn_fraction`, the sole (guarded) entry point for this field. A structurally identical, pre-existing `NaN` gap in the unrelated sibling method `with_continue_as_new_deadline_fraction` (issue #772) was deliberately left untouched — it predates this PR, was not flagged by the diff-scoped review, and fixing it here would be unrequested scope creep on a different feature's config surface. **Finding B (P2) — `min_history_events` was silently dropped whenever `history_bloat_min_events` was also supplied.** `load_history_bloat_workflows` (the dedicated AC1/AC2 discovery loader) applied only its own `history_bloat_min_events` count filter and never consulted the pre-existing general-purpose `min_history_events` filter (issue #493) at all, even when the caller supplied both at once — so `?history_bloat_min_events=4&min_history_events=6` silently behaved as `?history_bloat_min_events=4`, ignoring the caller's stricter, explicitly-requested bound. Fixed by composing the two as an additional `AND`-ed `>=` predicate over the identical correlated-subquery count expression: `count >= a AND count >= b` is exactly `count >= max(a, b)`, so the stricter of the two thresholds always wins regardless of which parameter supplied it — proven symmetric (order-independent) by a two-directional regression test. **Finding C (P1) — the per-shard discovery query loaded every matching live row before truncating, with no per-shard bound.** `load_history_bloat_workflows`'s Step 1 query had no `.limit(...)` at all: it `.load()`ed every non-terminal, above-threshold execution row on a shard — full `WorkflowExecution` structs, including large JSON payload columns (`input`/`output`/`memo`/`search_attrs`) — before the cross-shard fan-out merge (`build_history_bloat_fanout`) truncated to `filters.limit` (default 50, max 200). A shard with a large live population matching the filter could therefore force this endpoint to materialize, transfer, and JSON-decode thousands of full rows just to discard all but a few dozen of them — a memory/DB-pressure risk with no bound relative to the caller's actual `limit`. Fixed by restructuring the query into a single pass that computes the current `harvest_events` count via one reusable correlated-subquery constant (shared identically by the count-threshold filter(s), the `ORDER BY`, and the `SELECT`, so the three can never read divergent values), orders by that count descending with an `id` ascending tie-break — matching `build_history_bloat_fanout`'s own cross-shard merge order exactly — and applies `.limit(filters.limit)` **before** any full row is loaded, folding the previously-separate Step 2 batch-count query into the same `SELECT` (returning `(WorkflowExecution, i64)` tuples directly, eliminating a second round trip entirely). This is a correct top-K-per-partition-then-merge by construction: any row excluded from a shard's own local top-`filters.limit` (under this exact order) necessarily has `filters.limit` other rows on that same shard ranked at or above it, so it can never be part of the true global top-`filters.limit` once every shard's contribution is merged — excluding it at the per-shard query changes nothing about the final, correctly-truncated result. Regression-proofed with three new HTTP integration tests: `history_bloat_min_events_composes_with_min_history_events` (finding B, both parameter orderings, against real Postgres), `history_bloat_min_events_limit_orders_by_history_size_not_insertion_order` (finding C, a single shard with candidates seeded deliberately out of count order, so only a genuinely-correct `ORDER BY ... DESC LIMIT N` — not insertion/PK order or the reverse direction — produces the expected top-2), and `history_bloat_min_events_limit_survives_per_shard_truncation_across_shards` (finding C, the cross-shard correctness proof: two shards each seeded with *more* candidates than the global limit, where the true global rank-3 row lives on the same shard as the global rank-1 row and must survive that shard's own local truncation to reach the merge, while a different shard's own local rank-2 row — globally rank 4 — must still be correctly excluded by the final merge). The pre-existing `history_bloat_min_events_merges_and_sorts_globally_across_shards` test (from the original AC1 implementation) continues to pass unchanged, confirming the restructure preserves prior behavior byte-for-byte on top of the new bound. All DB/HTTP suites were re-executed green against real Postgres 16 (not merely compile-checked), and the full workspace quality gate (fmt, clippy `-D warnings` on both touched crates plus the `mcp,unified-dag-execution`/`metrics`/`webhooks` plugin feature combos, the core NaN-normalization unit tests, the `metrics_integration.rs` DB suite, and the no-DB `ci_run_coverage`/`migration_hygiene` guard suites) was re-verified green after this third review-fix batch. No `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change from any of the three fixes — finding A is a `context.rs`-internal input-sanitization fix behind the existing builder-method contract, and findings B/C are `api.rs`-internal query-building fixes behind the existing `history_bloat_min_events`/`min_history_events`/`limit` parameter contracts.

  **Post-review hardening (PR #1139 review, fourth pass, two findings, both fixed).** **Finding (P2) — the hard-cap preflight's soft-threshold decision could be based on a PROSPECTIVE, never-persisted event count.** `fail_workflow_for_history_cap`'s `should_warn_history_bloat` was computed from its `event_count` parameter — whatever value tripped the hard cap at the call site — but for the `WorkflowOutcome::Suspended` preflight branch that value can be purely prospective: `suspended_command_event_count` *predicts* how many events a batch of still-pending, not-yet-persisted commands (e.g. a wide activity fan-out proposed in one decision) would produce if actually appended, and `fail_workflow_for_history_cap` never persists them — the whole point of the hard-cap preflight is to reject the batch and fail the execution terminally instead. A run sitting at, say, 10 durably recorded events that merely *proposed* 90 more against a cap of 100 would satisfy `event_count >= cap` (100 >= 100) and stamp a permanent soft-threshold crossing off a count that never lands in `harvest_events` — leaving a terminal execution the live (non-terminal) discovery filter (AC1/AC2) can never find, and a counter that fired for a run whose actual recorded history stayed nowhere near the threshold. Fixed by switching the crossing decision to `terminal_count` — a value the function already computed (from `next_event_id`, the running count of events genuinely appended so far this cycle) and already trusted for the `harvest.workflow.history_size` metric — since that is exactly what will be durably recorded once the `WorkflowFailed` event is appended below. At every OTHER call site (a batch that genuinely already appended its events before hitting the cap, e.g. local-activity or external-signal inline persistence) `terminal_count` and `event_count` coincide by construction, so this is a strict correctness fix with zero behavior change there; the DLQ's own `HistoryCapExceeded { count: event_count, .. }` reason is deliberately left unchanged, since reporting the prospective batch size there is exactly the useful diagnostic ("this decision would have produced N events against a cap of C"). Regression-proofed with a new DB test, `history_bloat_counter_does_not_fire_off_a_prospective_pending_command_count` (`metrics_integration.rs`): a probe pre-seeded with only `WorkflowStarted` (1 durable event) proposes 8 pending `RecordSideEffect` bookkeeping commands plus a fresh timer arm in one live decision against `event_hard_cap=8`/`fraction=0.75` (threshold 6) — the prospective count (10) trips the hard cap, but the durable post-failure count (2: `WorkflowStarted` + the terminal `WorkflowFailed`) never reaches the threshold, so the counter must NOT fire and `history_bloat_warned_at` must stay unset even though the execution IS terminally `FAILED` via the DLQ; the test additionally re-loads the final history and asserts it contains exactly those 2 events, proving the 8 proposed side effects and the proposed timer were genuinely never persisted. Verified as a genuine TDD red before the fix (a temporary revert to `event_count` makes the new test fail with the exact `history_bloat_warned_at` assertion this fix targets) and green after restoring it, alongside the four pre-existing `history_bloat_*` DB tests in the same file (unaffected — each of their scenarios already has `terminal_count == event_count` by construction, so the fix changes nothing observable for them). **Finding (P2) — the ADR row, dashboard panel description, and this changelog's own opening summary still described "exactly once" / "still-RUNNING only" delivery, contradicting the corrected semantics `docs/telemetry.md` and this changelog's own "Post-review hardening, second pass" section above already document accurately.** The round-2 fix (finding #2 above) changed delivery to at-least-once (emit-before-mark, so a rare crash-window duplicate is possible) and added a second, terminal emission path (the hard-cap preflight) — `docs/telemetry.md` was updated correctly at the time, but `docs/adr/0001-otel-trace-contract.md`'s `METRIC_WORKFLOW_HISTORY_BLOAT` catalogue row, the `harvest_workflow_history_bloat` panel `description` in `docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`, and this changelog's own opening "Soft-threshold counter" paragraph were all left stating the pre-fix "exactly once per still-RUNNING execution" contract, so an operator reading any of those three surfaces could misread a benign crash-retry duplicate — or a legitimate hard-cap-terminal emission — as evidence of an implementation fault. Fixed by rewording all three to state at-least-once delivery (with the crash-window-duplicate rationale) and the dual emission path (still-`RUNNING` mid-decision, or the same decision terminally hard-cap-failing the execution) explicitly, matching `docs/telemetry.md`'s already-correct wording; no anti-drift test asserts the exact prose of any of the three (`dashboard_pack_docs.rs` only checks the metric-name/label ground truth, unaffected), so this is a documentation-only correction with no code, contract, or schema surface. No `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change from either fix — the first is a `worker.rs`-internal decision-input fix behind the existing metric/guard-column contract, and the second is prose-only across the ADR, dashboard JSON, and this changelog file.

  **Post-review hardening (PR #1139 review, fifth pass, three findings, all fixed).** **Finding (docs-only) — the runbook wrongly described `event_hard_cap`/`history_bloat_warn_fraction` as per-workflow-type tunable.** `docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md`'s `harvest_workflow_history_bloat` section repeatedly said "tune the fraction or the cap per workflow type" / "raise `event_hard_cap` ... for that type," but `HandlerRegistry.history_policy` is a single, non-keyed `WorkflowHistoryPolicy` field (`registry.history_policy()` takes no workflow-name parameter) — every workflow type registered on a given worker shares the identical cap and warn fraction; there is no per-type override, and `HarvestBuilder::history_event_hard_cap`/`history_bloat_warn_fraction` configure it once at worker-registry construction time. Following that guidance as written would have led an operator to attempt (and fail to find) a per-type config knob that does not exist, or to raise the cap not realizing every other workflow type sharing that worker is affected too. Fixed by rewriting all four misleading passages (the opening paragraph's configuration-method claim, the "Likely causes" bullet, the "False positives" phrasing, and "Safe actions" step 3) to state the registry-wide scope explicitly, name the actual `HarvestBuilder` methods, and add operator guidance for the divergent-footprint case (confirm the new value suits every type sharing the worker, or run the outlier type on a separate worker/`HandlerRegistry` with its own cap). Documentation-only; no code, test, or contract surface. **Finding (P2) — `history_bloat_threshold_crossed` truncates the fraction*cap product instead of rounding up, firing the warning before the configured percentage is actually reached.** The threshold computation was `(cap as f64 * fraction) as u64` — a truncating cast. Whenever `cap` is not evenly divisible by the fraction's denominator the product is non-integral (e.g. `cap=10, fraction=0.75` → `7.5`), and the truncating cast rounds *down* to `7`, so the soft-threshold counter fired at the 7th recorded event — 70% of the cap — instead of the first integer count that actually reaches or exceeds the configured 75% (the 8th event, 80%). The fraction's entire purpose is to warn at-or-past the configured percentage, never noticeably before it, so this silently undercut the operator-facing contract by up to one full percentage-point-of-cap on any non-exact cap/fraction pair (the overwhelmingly common case — only exact-dividing pairs like the pre-existing tests' `cap=100/fraction=0.75=75.0` or `cap=100/fraction=1.0=100.0` were exempt, which is why no existing test caught it). Fixed by switching to `(cap as f64 * fraction).ceil() as u64` — the smallest integer count satisfying `count >= cap * fraction`. Regression-proofed with a new unit test, `history_bloat_threshold_crossed_rounds_a_non_integral_product_up_not_down`, covering two distinct non-exact cap/fraction pairs (`cap=10/fraction=0.75` → threshold 8, not 7; `cap=7/fraction=0.5` → threshold 4, not 3, guarding against a fix that happens to work only for one numerator/denominator) plus an exact-product control (`cap=8/fraction=0.75=6.0` — unaffected by switching floor→ceil, confirming the pre-existing exact-division tests and the DB-backed counter-emission tests stay green). Verified as a genuine TDD red before the fix (temporarily reverting to the truncating cast makes the new test fail at `assert!(!history_bloat_threshold_crossed(7, 10, 0.75, false))`) and green after restoring it, alongside all six pre-existing `history_bloat_threshold_crossed_*` unit tests (unaffected, since every one of them uses an exact-dividing cap/fraction pair). **Finding (P2) — the history-bloat discovery loader's generated SQL repeated the correlated event-count subquery redundantly across clauses.** `load_history_bloat_workflows` shared one `HISTORY_EVENT_COUNT_SUBQUERY` string constant across the WHERE filter(s), `ORDER BY`, and `SELECT`, but a shared *Rust* string constant does not make Postgres share one *SQL* evaluation — each clause independently re-evaluated the correlated `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM harvest_events WHERE workflow_exec_id = ...` subquery per candidate row, so a single row could re-run the count query up to four times (two WHERE instances after finding B's `min_history_events` composition, one `ORDER BY`, one `SELECT`) before this fix, and up to three times even without `min_history_events` supplied. Fixed two of those four redundant evaluations without a full `LATERAL`/CTE rewrite (judged too invasive — see finding C, third pass, above, for why the query still uses `.into_boxed()` dynamic-filter composition rather than hand-assembled raw SQL): (1) the two separately-ANDed WHERE predicates (`>= history_bloat_min_events` and `>= min_history_events`) are now collapsed into a single evaluation by precomputing `effective_min_events = min_history_events.map_or(min_events, |m| m.max(min_events))` in Rust before the query is built — `count >= a AND count >= b` is exactly `count >= max(a, b)`, so this is a pure evaluation-count reduction with identical semantics to the finding-B fix it supersedes structurally; (2) `ORDER BY` now references the `SELECT`'s output alias by bare name (`HISTORY_EVENT_COUNT_ALIAS = "history_event_count"`) instead of re-stating the subquery text — Postgres documents that a bare, simple-name `ORDER BY` expression matching an output column resolves to that output column (falling back to a same-named input column only when no output alias matches), so the two clauses now share exactly one evaluation of the subquery per candidate row. The remaining WHERE-vs-SELECT/ORDER-BY split (Postgres evaluates WHERE before the SELECT list/ORDER BY in logical processing order, so a bare subquery text cannot be shared across that boundary without a `LATERAL`/CTE restructure) is left as a known, documented residual — the fix reduces the per-row evaluation count from up to four to at most two, without touching the `.into_boxed()` composition machinery the ~15 conditional filters rely on. Regression-proofed by re-running the full pre-existing 16-test `history_bloat_integration.rs` suite unchanged (all pass), with particular attention to the three tests that directly stress the restructured `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT`/composition logic — `history_bloat_min_events_limit_orders_by_history_size_not_insertion_order`, `history_bloat_min_events_limit_survives_per_shard_truncation_across_shards`, and `history_bloat_min_events_composes_with_min_history_events` — none of which needed modification, confirming the restructure is behavior-preserving. All DB/HTTP suites were re-executed green against real Postgres 16 (not merely compile-checked), and the full workspace quality gate (fmt, clippy `-D warnings` on both touched crates using the exact CI invocations) was re-verified green after this fifth review-fix batch. No `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change from any of the three fixes — the runbook fix is prose-only, the rounding fix is a `worker.rs`-internal pure-function correction behind the existing metric contract, and the SQL fix is an `api.rs`-internal query-building optimization behind the existing `history_bloat_min_events`/`min_history_events` parameter contracts.
- **Phase 3.x** (implemented): DAG-level `execution_timeout`/`sla` attributes — see issue #743. A `#[workflow]` has had a hard `execution_timeout` deadline (issue #243, Phase 3.12) and a soft `sla` breach signal (issue #487, Phase 3.28) since long before unified DAG execution existed. A `#[dag]` had neither: a scheduled nightly ETL DAG that hung on a stuck upstream had no engine-level ceiling at all, and there was no way to alert an operator when a DAG run was merely running slower than usual. This closes that gap with **pure propagation, zero new machinery** — since Harvest 0.3 (`unified-dag-execution`, on by default) a `#[dag]` already executes as a `#[workflow]` under the hood via a shadow `WorkflowInfo` (issue #256, Phase 3.9), so `execution_timeout`/`sla` declared on `#[dag]` are copied verbatim onto that shadow `WorkflowInfo` and enforced by the **exact same scanners** a plain workflow already uses: `timeout::enforce_workflow_execution_timeouts` (#243) and `timeout::enforce_workflow_sla_breaches` (#487). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no new scanner, no migration.**

  ```rust
  #[dag(schedule = "0 6 * * *", execution_timeout = "4h", sla = "3h")]
  fn nightly_reconciliation(dag: &mut DagBuilder) {
    let extract = dag.activity(extract_ledger);
    let _reconcile = dag.activity(reconcile_accounts).upstream(&extract);
  }
  ```

  **Macro (`autumn-harvest-macros`).** `DagAttrs` gains `execution_timeout:
  Option<String>` and `sla: Option<String>` (`dag.rs`), parsed at
  macro-expansion time via the same `::autumn_harvest::task_duration(…)` call a
  `#[workflow]` uses, and threaded into both the `DagInfo` and (when
  `unified-dag-execution` is enabled on the proc-macro crate) the shadow
  `WorkflowInfo` companion's `quote!` templates. The duration-string validator
  `is_valid_task_duration` — previously private to `workflow.rs` — was hoisted
  into a new shared `attr_util::is_valid_task_duration`, so `#[dag]` and
  `#[workflow]` share one duration-parsing/validation implementation rather
  than duplicating it. `emit_workflow_companion` was refactored from 9
  positional arguments down to `(fn_name, fn_name_str, &DagAttrs)` to stay
  under clippy's `too_many_arguments` threshold once the two new attributes
  were added.

  **Core (`autumn-harvest`).** `DagInfo` gains `execution_timeout:
  Option<Duration>` and `sla: Option<Duration>` fields (`info.rs`).
  `DagInfo::as_workflow_info()` — the function `HarvestBuilder::dags(...)` calls
  to auto-register a unified DAG's shadow `WorkflowInfo` — copies both
  **verbatim** onto the shadow `WorkflowInfo` it builds, alongside the
  pre-existing `chain_execution_timeout: None` (DAGs carry no chain-scoped
  lifetime cap, issue #617; unrelated to this feature). This is the
  core-crate-level runtime propagation point; the macro-level `quote!` threading
  into the DAG macro's OWN, separately-emitted shadow-`WorkflowInfo` companion
  function (`emit_workflow_companion`, used for direct
  `__autumn_workflow_info_{name}()` introspection/`workflows![]`-macro use, not
  by `HarvestBuilder::dags(...)`) is covered in the "Macro" section above — both
  sites are driven from the identical compile-time-parsed attribute string, so
  they can never disagree for a given `#[dag(...)]` declaration, and both are
  independently test-covered. Because the shadow
  `WorkflowInfo.execution_timeout`/`.sla` are the *exact same fields* a plain
  workflow populates, every downstream mechanism composes automatically with
  no DAG-specific branch anywhere in the engine:

  - **Hard deadline (AC1-AC2).** `deadline_at = started_at + execution_timeout`
  is set at start time (issue #322's existing per-run deadline machinery);
  the #243 scanner transitions an overrun DAG run to `TIMED_OUT` exactly like
  an overrun plain workflow, classified via the pre-existing
  `TimeoutType::WorkflowExecution` variant (no DAG-specific timeout kind was
  introduced).
  - **Soft SLA (AC3-AC4).** `sla_deadline_at = started_at + sla` is set at
  start; the #487 scanner emits `harvest.workflow.sla_breached{workflow,
  queue}` **exactly once** when a DAG run passes it and keeps the run going
  — zero lifecycle effect, same as a plain workflow's soft SLA.
  - **Clamp (AC5).** A DAG declaring `sla` larger than `execution_timeout` is
  clamped down to `execution_timeout` at start via the pre-existing
  `effective_sla = sla.min(hard)` arithmetic in `execution.rs` (the hard
  timeout would otherwise kill the run before the soft signal could ever
  fire) — the identical code path a plain workflow's clamp already runs
  through, not a DAG-specific reimplementation.
  - **Fleet-wide ceiling (AC6).** `HarvestBuilder::max_workflow_execution_timeout(…)`
  caps a DAG's declared `execution_timeout` identically to a plain
  workflow's, since both flow through the same `WorkflowInfo.execution_timeout`
  field the ceiling clamps at start.
  - **Zero regression (AC7).** A DAG declaring neither attribute gets `None`
  on both `DagInfo` fields; `deadline_at`/`sla_deadline_at` stay `NULL` at
  start and neither scanner ever inspects the run — byte-identical to a
  pre-#743 build.

  **Compile-time validation (AC8, AC10).** `#[dag(execution_timeout = "4
  hours")]` (a malformed duration string) is rejected at compile time with
  `error: invalid execution_timeout duration; expected e.g. "30s", "5m", "4h",
  "2d"`, mirroring the existing `#[workflow]` diagnostics rather than deferring
  to a runtime `.expect(...)` panic. `#[dag(bogus_attr = "…")]`'s
  "unsupported attribute" error now lists `execution_timeout` and `sla`
  alongside every other recognized `#[dag]` attribute name.

  **Management API (AC9, `autumn-harvest-plugin`).** `GET /admin/schedules`
  (list) and `GET /admin/schedules/{id}` (single) surface each schedule's
  *effective* `execution_timeout_secs`/`sla_secs` — resolved from the
  registered workflow, or the DAG's shadow `WorkflowInfo` for `kind: "dag"`
  schedules, and already clamped per AC5 — so an operator can see what a
  scheduled run will get without cross-referencing source. New
  `resolve_schedule_deadline_secs(registry, name)` (pure: looks up
  `registry.workflows.get(name)`, applies the same `clamp_info_default_sla`
  helper the start path uses) is resolved **once per request** (not once per
  row) in `list_schedules`/`get_schedule`, and threaded through
  `schedule_entry_from_row`'s new `registry: Option<&HandlerRegistry>`
  parameter, `create_workflow_schedule`, and the PATCH `update_schedule_handler`
  so a freshly created or edited schedule's response reflects it too. A
  `None` registry (e.g. no live runtime installed) or an unregistered workflow
  name resolves to `(None, None)` rather than panicking or guessing a stale
  value.

  **Test evidence.** TDD red-then-green throughout; all suites below were
  actually executed (not merely compile-checked) against a locally provisioned
  Postgres 16 in this sandbox, plus real `rustc`/`trybuild` compile-fail
  subprocess runs — no Docker was needed since the plugin's own DB integration
  test compiles clean and CI runs it Docker-backed.

  - 3 new inline unit tests in `autumn-harvest/src/info.rs`
  (`dag_as_workflow_info_propagates_execution_timeout`,

  - 6 new DB integration tests in the new
