  **No migration. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. No public API change.** The
  core MSRV stays 1.88, and `rustls` 0.23.46 builds on it. The
  `wasm-activities` feature still needs Rust 1.95, as `wasmtime` 48 does.

  **Checks.** `cargo deny --all-features check` with cargo-deny 0.20.2, the CI
  version, reports `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`. Before
  the change it failed on the 15 advisories above. The `autumn-harvest`
  library suite passes with `wasm-activities` on 48.0.6: 4865 tests, 122 of
  them wasm tests. `autumn-harvest` with `tls`, `autumn-harvest-cli` and
  `autumn-harvest-redis` build on `rustls` 0.23.46.
- **Fix** (implemented): A refusal after the idle-wait snapshot still arms the capacity wake — see issue #1787. Before an idle wait, the leader claim loop reads `capacity_bound()`. When it is false, the wait does not wake on a released permit, because a release cannot unblock a claim. With the default two claim loops, a follower could record a refusal just after that read:

  - its poll found a pool full, so the gate refused a kind
  - its claim skipped an activity type at its adaptive limit

  The follower then parked. When the permit or the limit slot freed, nothing
  woke the leader, so the refused backlog waited for the leader's timer or
  listener. That is up to one `poll_interval`, 500 ms by default. Nothing was
  lost.

  Now each idle wait that can wake on a released permit takes a
  `CapacityWait`. It registers for a refusal before it reads
  `capacity_bound()`. `record_gate_refusal` and `claim_exclusions` fire
  `refusal_recorded` when their flag turns on. An unbound wait then waits for
  a released permit or a freed limit slot, as a bound wait does. A refusal
  alone does not end the wait, because a poll right after it meets the same
  full pool or limit. A release that `capacity_freed` stored before the
  refusal still ends the wait at once, as it ends a bound wait.
  `refusal_recorded` uses `notify_waiters`, so it stores no wake for a wait
  that starts later. The single-pool leader, the multi-shard round with and
  without listeners, and the single-shard drain use `CapacityWait`. A
  multi-shard drain still leaves the wake to its round.

  A wake on `capacity_freed` now clears `limit_refused` as well as
  `pool_refused`. The poll after the wake sets `limit_refused` again while a
  type is at its limit. Before, a limit refusal that the wake had already
  served also bound the next wait.

  The single-pool leader now sleeps the NOTIFY settle delay after its select,
  not inside it. A capacity or deferral wake can no longer cut that delay
  short. `wait_on_shard_listeners` already worked this way.

  The race was found in review of autumn-foundation/autumn-harvest#2153,
  after it merged.

  **Known gap, not changed here.** A permit that only a sibling poll holds
  goes back without a wake on `capacity_freed`. The leader's gate can refuse a
  kind because of that hold. The backlog then waits up to one `poll_interval`.
  A wake on every returned poll permit would loop under saturation, so this
  change leaves it.

  **No migration. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. No public API change.**

  **Tests.**

  - `a_refusal_after_the_snapshot_arms_the_wake_on_a_released_permit` and
    `a_limit_refusal_after_the_snapshot_arms_the_wake_on_a_freed_slot` fail
    before the fix.
  - `a_refusal_right_after_the_read_still_arms_the_wait` records a refusal in
    a hook that runs with the read. It fails when the wait registers after
    the read.
  - `an_earlier_refusal_does_not_arm_a_later_wait` and
    `an_earlier_limit_refusal_does_not_arm_a_later_wait` fail when
    `notify_one` replaces `notify_waiters`.
  - `a_bound_wait_ends_on_a_released_permit_without_a_refusal` and
    `a_bound_wait_ends_on_a_released_permit_only` pin that a released permit
    ends a bound wait, and that a refusal does not.
  - `a_released_permit_does_not_cut_the_settle_delay_short` pins the settle
    delay after a NOTIFY, with paused time.
- **Fix** (implemented): Agent adapter: failed-edit keys, tick input cap, final-turn delivery, follow-up size — see issue #2050. This fix closes four open items of #2046.

  - **Failed memory edit.** `InMemoryMemoryStore::apply` now keeps the first
    result of an `EditKey`, an error included. A retry returns that error. It
    cannot remove an entry that another run added after the crash. The
    `MemoryStore::apply` contract says the same for durable stores.
  - **Tick input cap.** `HeartbeatTask::max_request_bytes` reaches
    `AgentTask`. A large tick request ends as `TranscriptFull`, not as
    `PayloadTooLarge`.
  - **Final turn only.** Delivery uses the text of the turn that ended the
    segment. An empty final turn sends nothing. An empty `output_capped` turn
    sends the notice.
  - **Follow-up size.** The 2 000 character limit counts the untrimmed prompt.

  **Replay.** The final-turn rule and the raw follow-up length rule sit
  behind the `agent_final_turn_rules` patch marker. A history recorded before
  the marker replays under the old rules.

  **No migration. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant.** `HeartbeatTask` gains an
  optional field that is absent from JSON when unset.

  **Tests.** `a_retried_failed_edit_returns_its_first_error`,
  `a_tick_carries_the_worker_input_cap`,
  `an_empty_final_turn_does_not_deliver_an_earlier_aside`,
  `an_empty_capped_final_turn_sends_the_notice_only` and
  `padding_counts_toward_the_prompt_limit`. Each failed before its fix.
  Items 1 and 5 of the issue shipped in #2046.
- **Phase 3.x** (implemented): codec column follow-ups — see issue #2054. Three follow-ups from the review of issue #1979.

  **Duplicate starts ignore the codec.** `start_workflow` held the encode error
  of `input` and `memo` until a branch writes a run. A start that attaches to
  an existing run, or is refused as a duplicate, no longer fails when the
  active codec fails. It probes for the existing run before the insert, so the
  placeholder payload is never stored. A start that needs a new run still
  returns the codec error. Tests: `start_duplicate_codec_failure_tests` covers
  each reuse policy, the replace branches and the terminate branches.

  **Admin column reads keep the second decode pass.** `decode_column_lossy`
  still decodes a business value that is shaped like an envelope. The strict
  engine read returns it as written. The code comment and
  `docs/operations/read-path-decode.md` state the difference. Test:
  `an_operator_read_decodes_a_business_envelope_that_the_engine_read_keeps`.

  **The column sweep cursor is per runtime.** The process-global cursor map and
  its database-identity key are gone. `PayloadCodecs` now holds the cursor for
  each shard, shared by its clones. Two runtimes with separate registries never
  share a cursor, even when a Unix socket hides the server address. Do not share
  one registry across databases or schemas. No migration and no
  new event variant. Tests: `column_cursor_tests` in `codec_rotation.rs`.
- **Fix** (implemented): The worker runs admitted declarative updates — see issue #2035. The worker now runs each pending update and records its result. Before this change the HTTP edge appended `UpdateAdmitted` and woke the workflow task, but no engine code ran the handler. A caller with `wait=completed` got `504`.

  **Where an update runs.** An update runs after the workflow body, at the end of
  the same decision cycle, in history order. Replay never runs the handler. It
  returns the recorded result. Update events are transparent to command matching,
  so the order cannot cause a divergence. `docs/design/DESIGN-2035.md` holds the planning
  record.

  **Mechanism.** `WorkflowContext::with_update_dispatch` marks a context for
  dispatch. Only the worker cold path sets it, so a replay gate never runs a
  handler. After `classify_cycle`, `update::dispatch_pending_updates` lists the
  updates with no result. It runs each handler and adds a `RecordUpdateResult` to
  the cycle commands. The worker already persists that command on the suspend
  path and before a terminal event.

  A suspended, completed, continued-as-new or errored-body cycle dispatches. A
  divergent, panicked or deadlocked cycle does not, because the worker discards
  its commands.

  **Bounds.** Each handler runs under `UPDATE_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` (5 seconds). A
  panic or a timeout records `UpdateFailed`. The panic text goes to the log, not
  to history. A body that already ran the same update with
  `execute_admitted_update` does not run it twice.

  The cycle runs under the workflow-task budget. A handler starts only while a
  full handler limit is left in half of the remaining budget. The first update of
  a decision always runs. A re-drive of the same decision runs no update past the
  window. Every handler stops at half of the budget that is left. A task with no
  budget gets a fixed 30 second window. When updates remain,
  `DriveResult::updates_deferred` is set, and the worker wakes the task so the
  next cycle runs them. A cycle that defers an update is not kept resident, so
  the next cycle replays cold and runs the dispatch. A burst of slow updates
  therefore cannot cancel the cycle or cost poison-pill strikes.

  **Limits.** Delivery is at least once. Any path that discards the cycle after
  the handlers ran runs them again: a crash, a deadlock retry, an event-id
  conflict, a pause, a lost claim and a capability-miss release. A handler has no
  dedupe key. An admit does not wake a task that waits on a timer. A handler
  cannot await an activity or a timer.

  **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. No migration.** This change adds no writer of
  `harvest_events` rows. `harvest_events` stays append-only.

  **Tests.** Unit tests in `update.rs` cover dispatch, replay, panics, timeouts,
  ordering, terminal cycles, divergence, a panicking body and the dispatch window.
  `declarative_update_tests` runs the worker on Postgres, including a local
  activity and a closed window. The two `mcp_tools_integration` update tests lose
  `#[ignore]`.
- **Feature** (implemented): Agent payload-budget follow-ups — see issue #2040. `autumn-harvest-agent` now keeps a run inside the engine payload caps in four more cases. Items 4 and 6 of the issue shipped earlier, in the always-on PR.

  **What shipped.**

  - **Round budget (item 1).** A tool round measures the whole next request: the
    transcript, the assistant turn and an answer for each call. It builds that
    request once, with a placeholder for each answer. A result replaces its
    placeholder. The placeholder is the longest fixed answer, so any fixed answer
    fits in its place. The request also holds the labels and releases that this
    turn can add. When the placeholders exceed the cap, no call runs.
  - **Model reply cap (item 2).** The model-turn activity fits its reply to the
    result cap. It cuts each decision reason to 256 bytes first. A reply that
    still exceeds the cap becomes a turn with `oversized` set. The loop ends the
    run under the new stop `reply_too_large`. The activity no longer fails with a
    non-retryable `PayloadTooLarge` after the paid call. It logs a warning with
    the sizes.
  - **Zero cap (items 3 and 5).** A cap of zero is no cap, as in the engine.
    `exceeds_bytes`, `max_tool_result_bytes` and the error result follow the
    rule. `AgentTask::max_request_bytes(0)` no longer ends a run before its
    first model call.
  - **Narration.** A round that ends the run as `transcript_full` no longer
    makes the model text the report answer. The text can claim work that did not
    run.

  **Payload store.** A worker with a payload store offloads a value over the
  store threshold, and the engine skips its cap for it. The adapter cannot see
  the store. Set `AgentTask::max_request_bytes` and `AgentHarness::max_result_bytes`
  to zero for such a worker. Before this change, a zero cap broke both limits.

  **Limits.** The round budget is exact for the result text and for the flow
  state that the turn records. A delegation adds the labels and usage of its
  child, which the round cannot know in advance. The loop measures the next
  request again before it sends it, and ends the run as `transcript_full` if it
  exceeds the cap. A result that does not fit is still dropped after its call
  ran.

  **Replay.** The round budget changes which tool calls a round schedules near
  the cap. The zero-cap rule changes whether a run sends its first request.
  `AgentTask::whole_request_budget` gates both. `AgentTask::new` turns it on. A
  task recorded before this change has no field. It keeps the results-only
  measure, reads a zero cap as a limit of zero bytes, and replays as it ran. A
  heartbeat tick builds its task at run time, so `HeartbeatTask` records the
  same flag, and `HeartbeatTask::new` turns it on.

  **Invariants.** No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. No migration. No route change.
  `ModelTurn::oversized` and `AgentTask::whole_request_budget` are left out at
  their defaults, so a recorded value encodes as before. The text of the
  fixed "did not run" and "dropped" answers changed. They reach only the report
  of a run that has ended.

  **Breaking changes.** `ModelTurn`, `AgentTask`, `HeartbeatTask` and
  `eval::TurnDecision` gain a public field. A struct literal of one of them
  needs the new field. `AgentStop` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so
  the new stop is not a break. A reader built before this change cannot decode
  `reply_too_large` in a recorded report. `exceeds_bytes(_, 0)` now returns
  `false`, and `max_tool_result_bytes(0)` returns `usize::MAX`.

  **Eval.** `eval::evaluate` follows a worker. A turn that exceeds the result cap
  is cut or dropped. A dropped reply ends the candidate run under
  `reply_too_large`. The run no longer fails. `TurnDecision::dropped` marks the
  turn, and a dropped reply reads as a `stop` divergence.

  **Tests.** Each behaviour change has a test that failed first. The `types`
  guards and one zero-cap budget test passed at red, because the stubs held the
  shape. Later tests pin behaviour that already held, and a mutation run showed
  that they fail when the code is wrong. The tests cover:

  - a round that cannot fit, and a round charged against a large history;
  - the round budget to the byte, with a follow-up tool in the request;
  - a label that a call adds to the next request;
  - a reply over the cap, a huge policy reason, and a child that drops its reply;
  - a zero cap in the request check, the round and the tool results;
  - a task and a heartbeat tick recorded before the change, with a zero cap;
  - the eval cap, which measures the ids that the provider gave.
- **Feature** (implemented): sandboxed code activities on Firecracker microVMs. The new `sandbox-activities` feature lets an activity run code that an agent writes at run time. The code can be Python, Node, shell or any program in the guest image. It is off by default. The guide is `docs/sandbox-activities.md`, and the design record is `docs/design/DESIGN-sandbox-activities.md`.

  - **The request and the outcome.** An agent sends a `SandboxRequest` as JSON:
    a runtime, the code, files, stdin, arguments, variables, output paths and
    limits. Unknown fields are an error. A `SandboxPolicy` checks each request
    against runtimes, limit ceilings and size bounds. A non-zero exit, a signal
    or a timeout is an outcome. The outcome keeps a head and a tail of each
    stream, and a NUL byte becomes U+FFFD before it reaches `jsonb`.
  - **Failures.** `SandboxDenied` and `SandboxProtocolViolation` are
    non-retryable. `SandboxUnavailable` and `SandboxCancelled` are retryable.
  - **The Firecracker backend.** Each run gets a new, single-use microVM behind
    the jailer with cgroup v2. The microVM has a read-only root, a vsock device
    and a virtio-rng device. It has no network device, no metadata service and
    no serial console. Teardown kills the process, then the cgroup, then
    removes the jail, on every path. A lease file and a stale sweep remove the
    microVMs and cgroups of a crashed worker.
  - **Speed.** A warm pool boots microVMs ahead.
    `FirecrackerLauncher::create_golden_snapshot` makes a golden snapshot for
    `BootMethod::Snapshot`. Each run carries fresh host entropy and the host
    clock, so clones of one snapshot do not share random state or a stale
    clock.
  - **Host checks.** The first launch refuses a Firecracker or jailer version
    with a known escape CVE. `verify_host` also checks KVM, KSM, nested KVM,
    CPU vulnerabilities, cgroup v2, the jail base and the confinement.
  - **The guest agent.** The new `autumn-harvest-sandbox-guest` crate builds
    the agent that runs as init in the microVM. It serves one run over vsock,
    then reboots. Each run gets a cgroup in the guest, so `cpu_seconds` and
    `memory_mib` bound the whole run. `scripts/sandbox/build-guest-image.sh` builds the guest
    image.
  - **The process backend.** For development and CI, it runs the same executor
    as a host process. The run gets rlimits, a private work directory, no host
    environment, no new privileges and an empty network namespace. The default
    policy refuses it.
  - **The activity and the tool.** `HarvestBuilder::sandbox_activity`
    registers a normal activity. Its `start_to_close` covers the queue wait,
    the wall clock, the overhead and the cleanup grace. The handler passes the
    time left in the attempt, so a retry does not overlap a live run. The code
    gets `HARVEST_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` and `HARVEST_ATTEMPT`. The `sandbox` feature
    of `autumn-harvest-agent` adds `SandboxTool` (`run_code`).

  No migration, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, and no worker change other than
  the adaptive-limit list. History records the request and the outcome, and
  replay never runs the code again.

  Evidence: the sandbox unit tests run on every OS in `test-nodb`, with a fake
  VMM, fake `firecracker` and `jailer` scripts and a fake API server. The new
  `Sandbox (KVM)` workflow boots real microVMs, and it runs the `root_` tests
  with sudo. The `sandbox_activities_docs` guards check the guide and the
  design record against the code.
- **Feature** (implemented): SQLite: cancellable timers, workflow mutex, local activities, execution timeout and workflow retry — see issue #2029. Five primitives sealed a SQLite run `FAILED` with `UnsupportedFeature`, or panicked at registration. Code that used any of them could not move from Postgres. Each one now works on SQLite and records the Postgres events, so its history replays on the core `WorkflowReplayer`.

  **What shipped**

  - **Cancellable timers (#768).** `ArmTimer { for_await: false }` appends
    `TimerStarted`. `ArmTimer { for_await: true }` inserts the `harvest_timers`
    row once, so the deadline counts from the first await. `CancelTimer`
    deletes the unfired row and appends `TimerCancelled`. A terminal batch
    records the events and arms no row. `store::pending_timer_arms` now
    subtracts `TimerCancelled`, so a cancelled id can arm a `ctx.timer`.
  - **Workflow mutex (#691).** New tables `harvest_mutex_locks`,
    `harvest_mutex_waiters` and `harvest_mutex_seq`. A grant goes to the first
    run in the FIFO queue of a free key. It mints a new `lock_seq` and appends
    `MutexGranted`. A waiting run returns the new `RunState::WaitingMutex(key)`.
    `lock_seq` fences `ReleaseMutex`. Every terminal state setter releases
    the run's locks and queue places. A release that frees a lock is progress,
    so `run_until_idle` drives the waiter. An acquire must be the only
    awaitable in its batch, as on Postgres. This backend also rejects a timer
    await beside an acquire, because a timer that fires first breaks the replay
    of the grant. A run that stops waiting gives up its queue place.
  - **Local activities.** `register_activity` accepts `local = true`. A local
    activity that declares `schedule_to_close` panics at registration, as
    Postgres rejects it. The cycle appends `LocalActivityScheduled`. The body
    runs after the commit, with the local `ActivityContext`. Each attempt
    appends `LocalActivityFailed` or `LocalActivityCompleted`. A terminal
    failure adds `LocalActivityExhausted`. The per-attempt budget is
    `start_to_close`, capped at 60 seconds. Under Tokio a body past it is
    dropped, as on Postgres. A closure body is checked after it returns.
    The workflow deadline also bounds an attempt.
    A retry backoff parks the run in `local_retry_at`, and the drive does not
    sleep. A batch with a durable awaitable ends the run `FAILED`, as on
    Postgres (issue #950). This backend also rejects a second local activity
    in one batch. A typed `retry_after` hint wins over the policy backoff.
  - **Execution timeout (#243).** A start stores `execution_timeout_ms` and
    `deadline_at`. Each cycle checks the deadline first, and again after the body runs.
    The deadline also bounds the activity drain and an update. A late run gets
    `WorkflowExecutionTimedOut`, ends `TIMED_OUT` with the Postgres error text,
    and loses its open rows and locks. The drive returns the new
    `RunState::TimedOut(error)`. `ctx.deadline()` reports the same deadline,
    because `WorkflowStarted` carries the run's start instant. A signal, an
    update, a cancel or a terminate after the deadline seals the run first and
    gets `WorkflowNotRunning`. A signal by workflow id does the same. A
    signal-with-start replaces the overdue run with a new one.
  - **Workflow retry (#523).** A start freezes the policy and
    `workflow_attempt = 1`. An author failure that the policy allows starts a
    retry in the failure transaction. The retry gets the same input, the next
    attempt, its own exec id as its `workflow_id`, and every signal of the
    failed run, undelivered. The failed run gets `WorkflowRetryScheduled`. The
    retry waits for its backoff in `start_at`, and a cancel ends it at once.
    `SqliteRuntime::successor` now returns a retry too. The jitter seeds are the
    Postgres ones.
  - **Schema.** `harvest_executions` gains `execution_timeout_ms`,
    `deadline_at`, `start_at`, `workflow_attempt`, `retry_policy_json`,
    `retry_of_exec_id` and `local_retry_at`. `schema::migrate` adds them to an old file.

  **Core.** `ActivityContext::new_embedded_local` is a new hidden constructor
  for an embedded local-activity context. `WorkflowReplayer::replay_from_events`
  and `replay_from_snapshot` now replay a history that ends in
  `WorkflowExecutionTimedOut` as an
  in-flight run up to the seal. The engine seals such a run while the body is
  parked, so no command follows the last recorded event. A divergence before
  the seal still reports.

  **Invariants.** No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. `harvest_events` stays
  append-only. The SQLite schema change is additive.

  **Tests.** `autumn-harvest-sqlite/tests/integration/` gains
  `cancellable_timers.rs`, `workflow_mutex.rs`, `local_activities.rs`,
  `execution_timeout.rs` and `workflow_retry.rs`. Each runs a workflow that
  was rejected before, and replays its history on `WorkflowReplayer`. Unit
  tests pin the mutex FIFO and fence, the column migration, and the replayer
  seal rule.
- **Fix** (implemented): cap the interval schedule period — see issue #2048. `validate_schedule` accepted any non-zero whole-second `Schedule::Interval`. The scheduler adds the period to a timestamp to find the next run. chrono panics when the sum passes year 262143. A period of about 8.2e12 s or more made `next_run_after` panic. The management API accepted `interval:9000000000000000`, so a registration or a scheduler tick could panic.

  `validate_schedule` now rejects a period over `policy::MAX_INTERVAL_PERIOD`
  (100 years of 365 days). The error starts with "interval schedule period must
  not exceed" and names a manual schedule as the remedy.
  `HarvestBuilder::try_build` returns it as
  `HarvestBuilderError::InvalidWorkflowSchedule`, for a workflow schedule and
  for a DAG schedule. The runtime registration and update functions return
  `HarvestError::Config`. The management API returns 400.

  Upgrade: an app that registers an interval over 100 years now fails at
  build, and `HarvestBuilder::build` panics with the error. Use
  `Schedule::Manual` for a schedule that must never fire. Use a period of at
  most `MAX_INTERVAL_PERIOD` for a far-future schedule. Before this change,
  such a period panicked or never fired in practice.

  A row stored before this change can keep an interval over the cap. The
  scheduler reads it without validation. Pause, resume and delete still work.
  An update that leaves `schedule_expr` unset returns `HarvestError::Config`
  (the management API returns 400). Send a period within the cap, or `manual`.

  Design decisions:

  - Reject at validation, as issue #1967 did for a fractional period. The
    caller gets a typed error at registration, not a panic at the first tick.
  - 100 years matches the value that `throttle::compute_expiry` uses for an
    absurd duration. It is far above any real cadence and far below the chrono
    limit.
  - The runtime does not trust validation alone. A row stored before this
    change, an embedder that skips validation and a reference near the end of
    chrono time can still reach the addition. `next_run_after` now uses
    `checked_add_signed` and returns `None` on overflow, as for a zero
    interval. `plan_backfill_timestamps` stops its walk. Every caller
    terminates.
  - `CanaryConfig::new` clamps an interval over the cap down, with a warning.
    Issue #1967 rounded a fraction up for the same reason: a canary must
    always build.
  - The stored form, the API shape and the CLI do not change.

  No migration. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant.

  Tests: these failed before the fix.
  `interval_schedule_over_the_cap_is_rejected`,
  `next_run_after_huge_interval_is_none_not_a_panic`,
  `next_run_after_interval_at_the_end_of_time_is_none`,
  `plan_backfill_timestamps_huge_interval_returns_only_the_first_slot` and
  `plan_backfill_timestamps_interval_stops_at_the_end_of_time`.

  These tests cover the cap boundary and each path that calls
  `validate_schedule`: `interval_schedule_cap_is_100_years`,
  `next_run_after_sum_stops_exactly_at_the_last_date`,
  `stored_huge_interval_walks_end`,
  `harvest_builder_rejects_workflow_schedule_over_the_interval_cap`,
  `harvest_builder_rejects_dag_schedule_over_the_interval_cap`,
  `a_huge_canary_interval_still_builds`,
  `invalid_merged_schedule_writes_nothing` and
  `parse_schedule_expr_with_tz_interval_over_the_cap_is_rejected`.
- **Phase** (implemented): SQLite: list and describe executions, search attributes and memo — see issue #2027. The SQLite runtime read one execution at a time by id. It had no list, no filter and no describe. `upsert_search_attrs` sealed the run `FAILED`. The agent daemon read `harvest_executions` with its own SQL.

  **What shipped**

  - `SqliteRuntime::list_executions(&ExecutionFilter)` returns one page of runs,
    newest first, with no payloads. `next` is the cursor of the next page.
  - `visit_executions` passes the same rows with their payloads, one row at a
    time. `describe(exec)` reads one run.
  - `SqliteReader::open(path)` has the same three reads. It opens the file
    `READ_ONLY` and takes no writer lock. It reads a file that an older version
    wrote: a missing column reads as `Null`.
  - `ExecutionFilter` filters by workflow name, execution id, exact workflow
    id, workflow id prefix, states, a start-time range and search-attribute
    equality. The search-attribute filter uses JSON1. Numbers compare as
    numbers. A filter number of magnitude 2^63 or more is refused, because
    JSON1 reads a stored integer of that size as a float. A filter holds at
    most 64 states and 64 search attributes.
  - One state filter seeks on the new `idx_harvest_executions_state` index.
  - Each field is a `Stored<T>`: `Value`, `Null` or `Unreadable`. One damaged
    row does not fail a page.
  - `ctx.upsert_search_attrs` merges its patch in the cycle transaction, on the
    suspend path and on the terminal path, as on Postgres. It is not progress.
  - `start_workflow_with_options` takes a workflow id, a reuse policy, a memo
    and search attributes. A continue-as-new and a workflow retry copy the
    memo and the search attributes.
  - New errors: `SqliteError::InvalidSearchAttribute` and
    `SqliteError::InvalidFilter`.
  - `StartOptions` has builder methods, as `ExecutionFilter` has.
  - The agent daemon reads executions through `SqliteReader`. Its listing
    decodes each document with the decode `status` runs, so the two views
    agree.

  **Behavior change.** A workflow that upserts search attributes no longer
  ends `FAILED` as `UnsupportedFeature`. `SqliteError` has two new variants. An
  exhaustive `match` on it must add the arms. A `WorkflowStarted` timestamp is
  now cut to the microsecond, so the row and the event hold the same time.

  **Invariants.** No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. The additive `migrate` step
  adds four nullable columns to `harvest_executions`: `started_at`,
  `closed_at`, `search_attrs` and `memo`. Both times are epoch microseconds.
  `started_at` is the `WorkflowStarted` time. The first terminal write sets
  `closed_at`, and a later reuse-policy seal keeps it.

  **Limits.** A row written before this change has no start time, so a time
  filter does not match it. Search-attribute filters test equality only.

  **Tests.** `tests/integration/visibility.rs` covers describe, paging and
  every filter. It also covers upserts on both paths, a rolled-back cycle,
  continue-as-new, the reader beside a live runtime, damaged rows and an old
  file. Unit tests assert that no page query sorts in a temporary B-tree, and
  that one state seeks on its index. A daemon test refuses any source that
  names `harvest_executions` outside a comment. The daemon tests pass.
- **Phase 3.x** (implemented): the AEAD codec covers the short-lived payload copies — see issue #2043. Issue #1979 left the short-lived payload copies in clear. A finished activity task row stays until task retention removes it, and a callback dead letter stays until a redrive removes it. So those copies were not short-lived. This change encodes them.

  - **Columns now encoded.**
    - The activity task row: `harvest_task_queue.input`, `.output` and
      `.heartbeat_details`.
    - `harvest_completion_deliveries.payload`, and the CALLBACK dead letter that
      copies it.
    - `harvest_debounce.last_input`, `harvest_start_throttle.input` and
      `harvest_completion_trigger_outbox.target_input`.
    - `harvest_batch_jobs.signal_payload`. Only a signal job stores a payload. A
      cancel or terminate job stores none.
  - **Columns that stay clear.** The event batch buffer, the cross-shard child
    spec, the schedule input and the context headers are encoded by the
    `issue-2043-remaining-payload-copies` change. Configuration columns stay
    clear, and the coverage table in `docs/security-posture.md` gives a reason
    for each. A session task keeps its session id in clear, because the id is
    not payload.
  - **Readers first.** This release always decodes these columns. An older
    worker runs an activity on the envelope. An older scanner sends the envelope
    to a webhook, starts a run on it, or sends it as a signal. Turn column
    encoding on only after every worker runs this release. If it is on already,
    turn it off, finish the roll, and turn it on again.
  - **Engine reads.** These paths decode first:
    - activity dispatch, the heartbeat read-back of a retry, and session tasks;
    - the callback scanner, before it signs and sends the body;
    - the debounce, throttle and outbox fire paths;
    - the batch executor, before it sends each signal.
  - **Failure policy.**
    - An activity attempt whose input or checkpoint does not decode fails with
      `PayloadDecodeFailed`, and the retry policy applies.
    - The debounce, throttle and outbox scanners move the row back and log a
      warning with no payload text. A throttle row past its deadline is still
      dropped. A throttle row is written and logged once per 30-second window.
    - The batch executor leaves a signal job as it is. A cancel or terminate job
      never reads the payload, so a missing key does not block it.
    - The callback scanner counts a failed attempt, so the delivery backs off.
      After its last attempt, the dead letter keeps the stored body, and a
      redrive sends it.
  - **Heartbeat.** The flusher encodes the checkpoint. A checkpoint that does not
    encode keeps the stored checkpoint, and the flush refreshes the heartbeat
    time only. The flusher then encodes it again on each tick until a newer
    heartbeat replaces it. An unchanged checkpoint reuses its last envelope, so a
    repeat does not spend a new random nonce. A change of the column encoding
    switch or of the active key makes the flusher encode again. A rollback that
    turns the switch off thus stores the plain checkpoint.
  - **One envelope layer.** A dead letter and a requeued task keep one layer for
    every task type. The dead-letter writer takes the input as its source row
    stores it.
  - **New APIs.**
    - `heartbeat::spawn_heartbeat_flusher_with_codecs`.
    - `queue::record_heartbeat_liveness_sent_ago` and `queue::activity_row_output`.
    - `completion_callback::fire_due_completion_deliveries_with_codecs`.
    - `debounce::admit_debounced_start_with_codecs`.
    - `throttle::reserve_or_defer_with_codecs` and
      `reserve_or_defer_or_shed_with_codecs`.
    - `batch::submit_batch_job_with_codecs`.
    - `failure::ERROR_TYPE_PAYLOAD_DECODE_FAILED`.
  - **Breaking.**
    - With column encoding on, a non-admin caller of
      `GET /workflows/{id}/stack` gets the stored checkpoint envelope.
    - `dlq::dead_letter_with_codecs` reads `NewDeadLetterEntry::input` as the
      source row stores it, for every task type.
    - A DLQ replay or redrive of an activity entry encodes its input when column
      encoding is on.
    - The plain writers keep the identity registry and store in clear:
      `admit_debounced_start`, `reserve_or_defer`, `reserve_or_defer_or_shed`,
      `submit_batch_job`, `fire_due_completion_deliveries` and
      `spawn_heartbeat_flusher_with`. Call the `_with_codecs` form.
  - **Rotation.** `codec_rotation::CODEC_COLUMNS` lists each new column. The
    census and the sweep cover an activity task row now. A row written before
    this release can hold a clear value that has the shape of an envelope. The
    sweep reads such a value as an envelope. Drain the activity queues before you
    turn column encoding on, and wait for task retention before you retire a
    key.
  - **Erasure.** Erasure (issue #495) does not reach the task rows or the
    outbox. The security posture page says so.
  - **Invariants.** No new `WorkflowEvent` variant and no migration.
    `harvest_events` gains no new writer.

  **Tests.** `codec_column_coverage_tests` runs a real worker with an AES-256-GCM
  codec. It checks ciphertext at rest. It checks plaintext in the handler, the
  retry checkpoint, the callback body, the started run and the batch signal. It
  also checks that a value which does not decode never reaches a handler, a
  webhook or a start. `codec_rotation_db_tests` seeds every swept column and
  checks the census, the sweep, the budget and the retirement gate. Unit tests
  pin the dead-letter layer rule, the session id read and the doc table against
  `schema.rs`.
- **Phase** (implemented): audit chain verification reuses the keyed HMAC state. `ChainVerifier` sets each key up once and streams the canonical row into the MAC. Verify-only cost over 5,000 rows drops from 176.8M to 139.2M instructions (-21.3%) and from 44,999 to 10,000 allocations (-77.8%). No output, event or schema changes. See `docs/performance-audit-chain-verify.md`.
- **Phase** (implemented): shared optional-duration conversion for typed-stub macros (🪞 Echo clone-class merge). `workflow.rs`'s `start_with_options` (four fields: `execution_timeout`, `max_execution_timeout_ceiling`, `chain_execution_timeout`, `max_workflow_chain_timeout_ceiling`), its `signal_with_start` (the first two of those four), and `update.rs`'s `update_with_start` (the same first two) each hard-coded an identical match converting an `Option<std::time::Duration>` field into an `Option<chrono::Duration>`, rejecting overflow with a `HarvestError::Config` naming the field — eight hand-copied occurrences across two files.

  **What shipped.**

  - `attr_util::optional_chrono_duration_tokens(field_name, source) ->
    TokenStream`, a pure codegen helper parameterized on the field name (for
    the error message) and the source expression — both legitimately
    caller-varying, with no mode/kind/flavor flag.
  - All 8 inline matches now splice its output via a precomputed token
    variable, bound before the enclosing `quote! { ... }` call that builds the
    generated typed-stub source. The two fields `start_with_options` and
    `signal_with_start` share verbatim are computed once and spliced at both
    call sites.
  - Six characterization tests in `attr_util.rs` pin the helper's exact
    token-for-token output against each call site's pre-existing inline text,
    including `update_with_start`'s genuinely different source expression
    (no `.or(info....)` fallback).

  **Evidence.** `jscpd` (`--min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --format rust`, scoped
  to `workflow.rs`/`update.rs`): 4 pairwise matches / 712 duplicated tokens for
  this class before this change, 0 after. `start_with_options`'s own doc
  comment says the chain-cap fields (issue #617) were written "at parity with"
  the pre-existing `execution_timeout` match above them — a first-party
  admission the pattern was deliberately copied. Rule of three clears on
  instance count alone (8), so no missed-fix defect is required as separate
  evidence.

  No public API or behavior change: both touched call sites keep their exact
  signatures and error messages. `cargo test -p autumn-harvest-macros --lib`
  (97/97), `cargo build -p autumn-harvest --all-features`, `cargo build -p
  autumn-harvest-agent`, `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest-macros --all-targets
  -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt -p autumn-harvest-macros -- --check` are all
  clean.
- **Testing** (implemented): Nightly coverage and a ratchet on the critical modules — see issue #1818. CI now measures line and branch coverage every night. A ratchet stops the coverage of seven critical modules from dropping. There is no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration and no change to engine behavior.

  **Nightly job.** `.github/workflows/coverage-nightly.yml` runs the
  `autumn-harvest` lib tests and every `linux` manifest row under
  `cargo llvm-cov --branch`. The DB rows use the shard layout of
  `test-db-linux`.
  `show-env` instruments the plain `cargo test` calls of `run-suites.sh`, so the
  manifest stays the one list of suites. The `report` job merges the shards. It
  publishes per-module line and branch coverage as the `coverage-report`
  artifact and as the run summary. A failed scheduled run opens an issue that
  names the result of each job. A PR that changes the workflow runs the whole
  pipeline.

  **Toolchain.** Branch coverage needs `-Zcoverage-options=branch`, so the
  workflow sets `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` to the nightly that `fuzz-nightly.yml` pins. The
  LCOV exporter of LLVM 23 crashes on `worker.rs`. Each job exports
  `llvm-cov` JSON, and `.github/ci/coverage.py convert` turns it into LCOV. The
  line rule is the one of LLVM `LineCoverageStats`. On `queue.rs`, `erase.rs`,
  `scheduler.rs` and `timeout.rs`, it gives the same lines and counts as the
  LCOV exporter of that nightly.

  **Ratchet.** `.github/ci/coverage-baseline.json` records a line floor and a
  branch floor for `queue.rs`, `worker.rs`, `scheduler.rs`, `timeout.rs`,
  `poison_pill.rs`, `codec_rotation.rs` and `erase.rs`. The run fails when a
  module drops more than the tolerance below its floor, or has no data. The
  ratchet runs only when every test job passed, because a failed test cuts
  coverage short. The summary of such a run shows "Ratchet skipped".
  `coverage.py ratchet --update` raises the floors and never lowers one. The
  first floors come from the first complete PR run. The global tolerance is
  0.5 points. `erase.rs` and `poison_pill.rs` set 1.5, because one branch
  there is worth more than one point.

  **Tests.** `coverage_nightly_wiring.rs` checks the cron, the toolchain, the
  shards, the artifacts, the ratchet step, the alert job and the baseline.
  Mutation self-tests prove that the guard rejects a softened ratchet.
  `coverage.py --self-test` runs in the `lint` job. The Docker pre-pull of
  `test-db-linux` moved into `.github/ci/pull-test-images.sh`, so both
  workflows share it. `docs/testing/coverage.md` tells how to read the report
  and how to raise a floor.
- **Phase** (implemented): Republish tasks shifted by the late resume pass — see issue #2066. `resume_queue` shifts held tasks in two passes. The late pass shifts tasks that the first pass cannot see, such as a task created during the pause. The late pass returned only a count, so the resume published dispatch hints for first-pass tasks only.

  With a `TaskDispatch` worker, the reference of a late task can sit in release
  backoff. The task then waited for the backoff or the reconcile sweep.

  The late pass now ends with `RETURNING id`. `resume_queue` adds those ids to the
  hint set. It publishes the hints after commit, as it does for the first pass.
  The released count is unchanged.

  Tests:

  - `the_late_resume_pass_returns_the_ids_it_shifts` pins the SQL shape.
  - `resume_republishes_hints_for_tasks_created_during_the_pause` drops the
    channel reference of a task created during the pause. It asserts that the
    resume republishes the task.

  No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no new migration, no replay impact.
- **Phase** (implemented): SQLite: schedules, retention and the append-only guard — see issue #2031. The SQLite backend had no schedules and no retention. Its `harvest_events` table had no append-only guard.

  **What shipped**

  - `SqliteRuntime::upsert_schedule(&WorkflowSchedule)` stores a cron or
    interval schedule in the new `harvest_schedules` table. The workflow name
    is the key, as on Postgres. An upsert with the same spec keeps its next
    slot and its pause, so an app can upsert on every open.
  - `poll_once`, `poll_once_as_of` and `run_until_idle` fire each due schedule
    before they drive the fleet. `run_until_idle` fires on its first pass only.
    A schedule that cannot fire keeps its slot due. An unregistered workflow
    or a damaged row only logs a warning. A failed write is returned. One transaction checks the overlap, starts the
    run and moves the slot. The run of a slot has the `workflow_id`
    `sched:<workflow>:<slot seconds>`.
  - Catch-up is off: after a gap, a schedule fires one run and realigns. The
    overlap policies are `Skip` and `AllowAll`. `Skip` counts continue-as-new
    and retry successors, through the new `harvest_executions.schedule_name`
    column. It does not count a run past its deadline or with a pending
    cancel. `jitter` is ignored.
  - `pause_schedule`, `resume_schedule`, `delete_schedule` and
    `list_schedules`. A resume counts the next slot from now.
  - Each other `WorkflowSchedule` field this backend cannot honor is rejected
    by name with `SqliteError::Unsupported`. New errors:
    `SqliteError::InvalidSchedule` and `SqliteError::ScheduleNotFound`.
  - `SqliteRuntime::purge_terminal(older_than)` removes each terminal run
    closed before the window, with its events, tasks, timers, signals and
    attempts, in batches of 256 on a keyset cursor. Only the close time
    counts, as on Postgres. It keeps every `RUNNING` run. A run with no
    `closed_at` stays. New `exec_id` indexes on `harvest_tasks` and
    `harvest_activity_attempts` keep the deletes off a full scan.
  - Two triggers keep `harvest_events` append-only. They refuse every `UPDATE`
    and an `INSERT OR REPLACE` of a stored event. `DELETE` stays open. An
    older file gains them on its next open. A test fixture that must damage
    an event calls the hidden `append_only::with_guard_off`. Two daemon
    fixtures now do.
  - Core: the new `autumn_harvest::schedule_plan` module holds the cron and
    interval slot arithmetic with no `db` gate. The Postgres scheduler calls
    it, unchanged in behavior.

  **Migration**

  Additive, applied on open: the `harvest_schedules` table, the
  `harvest_executions.schedule_name` column, four indexes and two triggers. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant.

  **Test evidence**

  - `schedules.rs` (25 tests): a reopen keeps every slot and the next run
    starts on time; a late fire keeps the cadence; a gap fires once; cron and
    cron-in-zone slots; `Skip`, `AllowAll` and `max_active_runs`; successors,
    overdue and cancelled runs; pause, resume and delete; a slot that has its
    run; a fast clock under `run_until_idle`; unregistered and damaged rows;
    each refused field.
  - `retention.rs` (7 tests): every table is emptied for a purged run; live,
    in-window and pre-#2027 runs stay; an old run of a live chain goes; a
    damaged id is skipped; more runs than one batch. A unit test pins an index
    seek for every delete.
  - `append_only_guard.rs` (5 tests): every `UPDATE` form fails; the replace
    and upsert forms fail; `DELETE` works; an old file gains the guard;
    `with_guard_off` restores it, also after an error.
- **Docs** (implemented): upstream Weaver check for the OTel workflow draft — see issue #2015. `scripts/check-otel-workflow-semconv.sh` runs the upstream OpenTelemetry policy checks on the draft workflow model. It mirrors the upstream `semantic-conventions` `make check-policies` recipe at a pinned upstream commit. It reads the Weaver image digest and the policy package commit from that tree. The model passes, and Weaver reports no warning for it. A negative control with a namespace collision must fail on the upstream naming policy, so a pass is not vacuous.

  **CI.** The new `otel-semconv.yml` workflow runs the script on a ready
  pull request that changes the draft. A weekly job runs it against
  upstream `main`.

  **Model.** The enum `workflow.operation.name` has no `examples`. Upstream
  renders them in each span table, where they contradicted the span value.

  **Submission.** The status stays `pending`. Section 10 adds a step to move
  the pins and run the script before a maintainer files the issue. It lists
  the files that the upstream pull request needs. Section 8 gains two open
  questions.

  **Tests.** `the_weaver_check_script_mirrors_upstream`,
  `the_weaver_check_runs_when_the_model_changes` and
  `the_page_records_the_weaver_check` guard the script, the workflow and the
  page.

  **Invariants.** No migration. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. No engine
  change.
- **Fix** (implemented): codec failures and carried columns — see issue #2065. Follow-up to issue #1979. Three defects, one fix each.

  - **Codec failures.** `HarvestError::Codec` is new. Codec encode and decode
    failures used to be `HarvestError::Config`. `HarvestError::is_codec_failure`
    is true for `Codec`, `UnknownCodecKey` and `UnknownPayloadCodec`. The outbox
    (`attempt_signal_delivery`) and inline delivery (`persist_external_signal_inline`)
    used to record `ExternalSignalFailed { reason_code: "target_terminal" }` for
    any non-database error on an `ExecutionId` target. A codec failure now leaves
    the request pending. A target that is terminal still returns `Config` and
    still fails the signal. The rotation sweep reports `Codec` as `codec_error`.
  - **Continue-as-new.** The successor decodes the predecessor `memo` and encodes
    it under the active key. A clear legacy memo no longer reaches the new row in
    clear.
  - **Reset.** The fork decodes the source `input` and `memo` and encodes them the
    same way. This is option (a) of the issue. With column encoding off, or when
    a registry cannot decode a value, the copy keeps the stored bytes.

  No migration. `HarvestError` gains a variant, so a `match` that lists every
  variant needs a new arm. Code that matched `Config` to catch a codec failure
  must call `is_codec_failure()` now. An HTTP route answers a codec failure with
  `503`, as it does for an unknown key, and no longer with `400`.
  `upgrade_check` reports a codec failure as an undecodable run.

  Tests: `payload_codec::tests` (classification and `recode_column_for_copy`) and
  `codec_column_coverage_tests` (outbox, inline delivery, continue-as-new, reset).
- **Testing** (implemented): seeded interleaving simulation of workflow code — see issue #2033. `WorkflowTestEnv::simulation()` tests user workflow code against the delivery orders that production can produce. The default env lands every result of a suspension in one task, in command order. A simulation holds activity results, child results, timer fires, mid-run signals and a cancel in a pending set. At each task boundary a seed picks which ones land, and in what order.

  **Legal orders only.** Results land after their scheduling event, and each
  attempt's `ActivityStarted` lands first. A timer fires only at its deadline
  on the virtual clock. Equal deadlines from different tasks fire in arm
  order. Each task-prep ingest orders signals and due fires as
  `worker::merge_wake_events` does. A cancel is
  terminal, as on Postgres. A pure differential test ties the model to
  `merge_wake_events`. A Postgres test ties it to the real
  `ingest_due_timers_and_signals`. Each explored history also passes
  `check_legal`.

  **Sweeps.** `Simulation::sweep` runs a seed plan. Each seed runs twice with
  equal traces, replays through `WorkflowReplayer`, and runs again with a crash
  at a seeded task. The crash must not change the outcome. `always!` is a hard
  invariant. `sometimes!` is a reachability target, and a sweep fails when a
  label is never true. A failure prints `HARVEST_SIM_SEED=<seed> cargo test …`.

  **Determinism.** A run seeds `ctx.new_uuid()`, `ctx.random_*` and the
  `ctx.system_*` clock reads, and it starts at a fixed time. The context gains
  a `testing`-only seam for this. Production leaves it unset.

  **Faults and mocks.** `fault_percent` fails activity attempts at a seeded
  rate, and the worker retries them. `FaultPlan` fails a call by ordinal.
  `mock_activity_seeded` gives a mock a seeded generator and the virtual clock.
  `replay_with` replays each history with another build.

  **Worked examples.** `workflow_sim_tests` holds a `ctx.race()` workflow that
  always books the primary carrier. The default env passes it. A sweep finds a
  seed where the backup quote wins, and the replay command reproduces it. A
  second test races a cancellable timer against a later classic timer. The
  default env lets the later timer win, which production cannot do. The sim
  fires the earlier one, and the sweep shows that the history then does not
  replay.

  **Also.** `dst::SeedPlan` gains `parse_named` and `from_env_named`, which
  take a `SeedVars`, so both harnesses share one seed parser. `always!` and
  `sometimes!` live in `sim_probe`, so they compile in every build. The
  default env now dedups a re-emitted `StartTimer` and `StartChildWorkflow` by
  id, as the worker does. Its order is unchanged.

  **Engine findings.** The sim surfaced three engine behaviours that this
  change does not alter. A canary replay of a running activity reports its
  trailing `ActivityStarted` as unconsumed. A cancellable timer await stops its
  scan at an in-flight `ActivityStarted`. A strict replay of a race that a
  queued signal wins at once diverges. The guide lists all three.

  The harness now records a race loser's terminal only for a branch that
  started, as `worker::apply_race_loser_cancellations` does.

  The guide is `docs/testing/workflow-simulation.md`.

  No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no production behaviour change.
  The simulation and the context seam are behind the `testing` feature.
- **Feature** (implemented): SQLite: child workflows, and signal, cancel and await between runs — see issue #2026. Before this change, the SQLite backend rejected composition. A workflow that started a child, awaited another run, or signalled or cancelled another run ended `FAILED` as an unsupported feature. Composition now works on this backend.

  **What changed**

  - **Children.** `StartChildWorkflow` and `SpawnDetachedChildWorkflow` start
    the child in the parent's decision transaction. The child is a full run with
    a parent link. Its `workflow_id` is its execution id. Both
    `ctx.info().parent_execution_id` and the new `SqliteRuntime::parent_execution`
    name the parent. An update replay and a query replay see the same parent link.
  - **Results.** An awaited child's terminal writes `ChildWorkflowCompleted` or
    `ChildWorkflowFailed` to its `RUNNING` parent in the same transaction. A
    typed failure keeps `error_type`, `details` and `non_retryable`. A cancelled
    child reports `child workflow cancelled: <reason>`, and a terminated child
    `child workflow terminated: <reason>`. A due child-timeout
    deadline fires before a late child's result, as on Postgres (issue #779).
    The backend reads the clock again when a body returns. A close and a
    signal to another run use that instant, as Postgres uses `NOW()`.
  - **Parent-close policy.** When a parent ends, each running detached child
    gets its policy. `request_cancel` cancels it with reason `parent closed`.
    `terminate` fails it with `ParentClosed`. `abandon` leaves it running. The
    parent records `ChildWorkflowCascadeApplied`. Every terminal path applies the
    policy. The cap check before a terminal event or a cancel seal counts these
    events, as on Postgres. A worklist carries the cascade down a chain of any depth.
  - **Between runs.** `SignalExternalWorkflow`, `RequestCancelExternalWorkflow`
    and `AwaitExternalWorkflow` take effect in the caller's transaction. A
    cancel is a hard seal, as on Postgres: the target ends `CANCELLED` with
    reason `cancelled by external request`. A signal idempotency key dedups on
    the target, and by workflow id across every run of that id. A keyed signal
    row outlives the close of its run. An unknown target fails at once with
    `target_unknown`, because one file has no other shard to wait for.
  - **Race losers.** The parent cancels a child that loses a `ctx.race()` or a
    `spawn_child_workflow_timeout`. The reason is `lost race to a sibling
    branch`. A losing child that never started is skipped.
  - **Abandoned dispatch.** A failing cycle that drops a fresh child dispatch
    records the `ChildWorkflowStarted` and `ChildWorkflowFailed` pair of issue
    #952. The backend makes no child row.
  - **Driving.** A run that waits on a `RUNNING` child or await target returns
    the new `RunState::WaitingWorkflow(target)`. `run_until_blocked` drives each
    such target in the same call, with a cycle budget per run. The fleet drivers
    treat it as blocked.
  - **Cancel, terminate and continue-as-new (issues #2021, #2023).** The
    cooperative `cancel`, `terminate`, a history cap and every other seal close
    the run, so its parent and detached children get the result. A child that
    continues as new fails with the Postgres text, `continue_as_new is not
    supported in child workflows in this release`. Its last cycle keeps its
    bookkeeping, as any failing cycle does. An await follows a target
    that continues as new to its last run. A `TERMINATED` target gives
    `target_terminated`.
  - **Reuse policy.** `AllowDuplicateFailedOnly` replaces a `CANCELLED` prior,
    as core does.
  - **Core replay fix.** `HistoryMatcher` now resolves a stashed await whose
    terminal lands past a sibling's child or activity events. Before, a
    `join!(await_external_workflow, spawn_child_workflow)` parked permanently on
    both backends.

  **Breaking change.** `RunState` has a new variant, `WaitingWorkflow`. An
  exhaustive `match` on `RunState` needs a new arm. This change updates the
  in-tree agent daemon and `docs/sqlite-backend.md` §7. Tests that used a child,
  an external command, a local activity or a search-attribute upsert as the
  unsupported example now use an external activity.

  **Invariants.** No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. Every event this backend writes
  has the Postgres shape. No write to an existing `harvest_events` row. One
  additive schema step adds two nullable columns and an index:
  `harvest_executions.parent_exec_id` and
  `harvest_executions.parent_close_policy`. An old file gains them on open. A
  signal to another run stores its key in `harvest_signals.idempotency_key`,
  which issue #2028 added, and dedups through the same helpers as
  `send_signal_with_idempotency`.

  **With issue #2029.** A run that passes its `execution_timeout` closes like
  any terminal run. Its detached children get their policy, and an awaiting
  parent records a `ChildWorkflowFailed` with the timeout text, as on Postgres.
  A failed run that retries does not close: its successor starts in the same
  transaction, and its detached children keep running, as on Postgres. A child
  keeps the `execution_timeout` of its type. A detached child also keeps the
  retry policy of its type. An awaited child never retries, as on Postgres. A
  cancel from another run, a race-loser cancel and a `request_cancel` cascade
  record the close time and release the run's mutex, as every terminal path
  does.

  **Known limits.**

  - A run cancelled while it waits ends in a `WorkflowCancelled` that its code
    never saw. Strict core replay verifies a cancelled history in full, so it
    reports that run as still parked. Postgres writes the same bytes and gets
    the same result. The tests replay the events before the cancel in canary
    mode.
  - This backend writes a mixed batch in command order. Postgres writes the
    external events first. Each event is the same, and replay accepts both
    orders.

  **Tests.** `autumn-harvest-sqlite/tests/integration/composition.rs` has 63
  tests. Each test replays every history it asserts on the core
  `WorkflowReplayer`, with the run's ids. They cover:

  - attached and detached children, and a three-level attached chain;
  - typed, uncaught, unsupported and panicking child failures;
  - each parent-close policy, a detached chain cascade, and a detached spawn in
    a failing cycle;
  - signal and cancel by execution id and by workflow id, keyed signals, and
    dedup after a cancel and across runs;
  - await of completed, failed, cancelled, superseded and unknown targets;
  - the child timeout race, and a late child, a long terminal cycle, a long
    cancel cleanup, a long final panic or a late signal that loses to its
    deadline;
  - a reopen, mutual awaits, a blocked target beside a working sibling, and a
    run that its own cancel seals;
  - `join!` of an await and a child in both orders;
  - an operator cancel and a terminate of a child, a terminated await target, a
    child that continues as new, and an await across a continue-as-new;
  - the terminal, cancel, fallback cancel and final panic cap checks with and
    without cascade events, and an update and
    a query on a child that read its parent;
  - a parent that passes its `execution_timeout` and cascades to its detached
    child, a child that times out by its declared timeout, a detached child
    that retries, an awaited child that does not, and a cancelled mutex holder
    that releases the lock.

  Unit tests cover the schema step, a race loser with no row, and the panic
  strikes of runs that another run seals: by a cancel, a terminate cascade, an
  unsupported seal or an error-path cancel. A unit test checks that a hard cancel removes a task
  that a dropped drive left `RUNNING`. The core test
  `match_external_await_resolves_past_a_sibling_child` pins the replay fix. The
  design record is `docs/design/DESIGN-2026.md`.
- **Fixed** (implemented): tenant binding on a raw router mount — see issue #2076. `harvest_api_router` now installs the tenant binding layer. Before, a raw mount whose middleware set `VerifiedTenant` did not confine the caller. Tenant A could read, signal or cancel the run of tenant B by id.

  A mount through `HarvestPlugin`, `HarvestEmbedding` or `StandaloneAdminAuth`
  runs the layer once. The inner copy skips when the outer copy has run.
- **Security** (implemented): Authorizer hook sees the body `workflow_id` — see issue #2081. `AuthzRequest` has two new fields: `workflow_id` and `start_input_present`. Harvest reads them from the body of `start`, `signal-with-start` and `update-with-start` before the hook runs. They are `None` and `false` on every other route. The hook never gets the body.

  - The id is the raw value the handler reads. A body the handler rejects names
    no key, so a hook that confines keys must deny `None`.
  - No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. No migration. `harvest_events` is unchanged.
  - Tests: `authz` unit tests, and `start_family_*` and
    `other_routes_carry_no_workflow_id` in `authz_integration`.
  - `docs/security-posture.md` documents the fields. The keyed-entity section no
    longer advises denying signal-with-start.
- **Fix** (implemented): Exact number literals in `filter` — see issue #2141. A number in `attrs.<key> =`, `!=` or `IN` kept only `i64`, `u64` or `f64` precision. So `12345678901234567890123` and `...124` bound the same value.

  The filter now binds the number as `jsonb` text, with every digit. The text
  loses its leading zeros, a bare `.5` and a trailing `.`, so it stays valid JSON.
  A number outside the `f64` range, or longer than 1024 bytes, still gets `400`.

  The legacy `search_attr_filter` parameter uses the same conversion. It still
  reads `+5` and `.5` as numbers. A token such as `++5`, `+-5` or an over-long number
  stays a string.

  Tests: `number_literals_keep_every_digit_when_bound`,
  `number_literals_bind_as_valid_json`, `number_json_accepts_only_json_digits`,
  `legacy_search_attr_filter_keeps_every_digit` and
  `coerce_scalar_never_builds_invalid_json`.
- **Fix** (implemented): SQLite payload depth cap — see issue #2157. The SQLite backend refuses a start input, memo, signal payload or update input that nests deeper than `MAX_PAYLOAD_DEPTH` (100). Ingress returns the new `SqliteError::PayloadTooDeep` before it persists anything.

  `serde_json` writes any depth but reads at most 128 levels. Before this fix, a
  deep payload was stored and then every drive failed with "corrupt stored
  value". The run stayed `Running`. The cap leaves room for the event wrapping.

  The depth walk uses a heap stack, so a very deep value cannot overflow the
  call stack. No migration. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant.

  Tests: `tests/integration/payload_depth.rs` covers each ingress at and over the
  cap, `signal_with_start`, and a 10,000-level value.

  Breaking: ingress now refuses nesting from 101 to 127 levels too. Those
  values worked before when the wrapper stayed under 128. The cap is stricter
  than Postgres, which has no depth cap. The error enum gains one variant.
- **Fix** (implemented): A signal staged during the final decision is no longer lost — see issue #2079. A task ingests the pending signals at its start. A signal that arrived later stayed unconsumed. If the run then completed or failed, the run sealed over the signal. The sender had seen `signal_delivered: true`, and a retry with the same idempotency key deduped against the sealed run.

  **Fix.** The persist transaction now checks for unconsumed signals before it
  seals a `Completed` or `Failed` outcome. It already holds the execution row
  lock, and `send_signal` takes the same lock. If a signal exists, the engine
  discards the decision, re-pends the task and returns. The next pass ingests
  the signal and decides again. A body that ignores the signal still ends on
  that pass, because the signal is then in history.

  A sender that stages a signal in every pass can delay the end of the run.
  The delay lasts as long as the sender keeps sending.

  Park and continue-as-new needed no change. Park already re-checks signals,
  and continue-as-new moves unconsumed rows to the next run.

  **Keyed entity.** An op sent during a delete decision now reaches the loop.
  [ADR 0006](adr/0006-keyed-entity.md) records the new behavior.

  No migration and no new `WorkflowEvent` variant. `harvest_events` is not
  touched, so the append-only invariant holds.

  **Tests.** `late_signal_completion_tests.rs` runs on Postgres. A body sends
  its own late signal on the first pass. The tests cover a body that reads the
  signal, a body that ignores it, and a body that fails.
- **Fix** (implemented): `upgrade_check` hides a mistyped URL — see issue #2119. The `upgrade_check` command printed a mistyped database URL, password included, to stderr. A URL without `--database-url` reached the unknown-flag error. A URL given to `--database-url-env`, `--limit` or `--format` reached the matching error too. A URL given to `--baseline-structure` or `--candidate-structure` reached the "cannot read" error. A URL given to `--baseline-build` reached the build finding in the report.

  Now `plain` in `upgrade_check.rs` shows a token only when it is a plain word. Any other token shows as `<hidden>`. A bare argument is always hidden. A plain flag name or variable name stays visible. The error text changed from "unknown flag" to "unknown argument".

  The "cannot read" error shows a path only when it holds letters, digits and `_-./+~ `. Any other path shows as `<hidden>`. The build finding no longer repeats the baseline build. The command still accepts every file path and build ID, such as `C:\manifests\old.json` and `sha256:abc`. The check redacts the echo, not the input. A guard on the input rejected valid values. A list of bad spellings missed new ones.

  The example binary reads its arguments lossily, so a non-UTF-8 argument no longer panics.

  This change adds no `WorkflowEvent` variant and no migration.

  Tests, red then green: unit tests in `upgrade_check.rs` and `a_bare_url_is_not_echoed_to_stderr` in `upgrade_check_db_tests.rs`.
- **Phase X.Y** (implemented): Replay-stable `should_continue_as_new()` — see issue #2080. `should_continue_as_new()` compared the loaded history size with the threshold. The loaded size grows from task to task, so a cold replay of a loop could answer `true` where the live run answered `false`. The replay then diverged.

  The history-size trigger now reads the count only at the live frontier. It
  records each answer, `true` or `false`, as a `SideEffectRecorded` event named
  `__harvest_continue_as_new` (`CONTINUE_AS_NEW_SIDE_EFFECT_NAME`). A replay
  reads the event at the same position. The record keeps the positions of a
  signal-driven loop apart, where no other command separates two calls.

  The `__harvest_` prefix is reserved for engine side-effect ids. Author code must
  not use `__harvest_continue_as_new`.

  Older histories have no record. A `WorkflowContinuedAsNew` event at the cursor
  reads as `true`, also after a deadline probe clock read. Any other event reads
  as `false`. No migration is needed, and no `WorkflowEvent` variant is new.

  The entity loop keeps its own checkpoint side effect. It calls an unrecorded
  hint, so it adds no second event. Its test
  `the_checkpoint_decision_is_stable_when_history_grows` now asserts that a naive
  loop replays clean.

  Known limits. An older run that answered `true` and then ran other commands
  before `continue_as_new` replays as `false`. A call in an older history with
  no record, followed directly by `continue_as_new`, replays as `true`. Each call
  now records one small event.

  Tests that built a history with no record for a `true` branch now include the
  record. A recorded position no longer depends on the history policy.
- **Phase X.Y** (implemented): autoresearch capstone example (PR #2190). `examples/autoresearch` runs Karpathy's autoresearch loop as durable Harvest workflows on the SQLite backend. An agent edits `train.py`, a trainer runs it, and a pure keep rule keeps the commit or resets it. The loop runs all night, offline by default: a simulated trainer and a scripted researcher.

  - `research_session` runs setup and a baseline, then one `experiment` child
    per idea. Signals (`hint`, `stop`, `policy`), a `status` query and a
    `whatif` update steer it. A durable pause before each experiment ends the
    drive, so a command lands before the next experiment. It continues as new
    every N experiments. A kept
    idea goes to sibling sessions as an external signal by workflow id. A
    detached `agent_loop` writes the morning report.
  - `experiment` asks an `agent_loop` child for one edit. A saga commits it,
    with `git reset` as the compensation. A workflow mutex per GPU guards the
    training activity. A local activity parses the summary. A crash gets one
    fix proposal. The session holds a mutex per lab for each experiment, so
    two sessions in one lab take turns on their own branches.
  - The agent harness has five lab tools and a policy that gates `rewind`. A
    flow rule gates a write after untrusted input, and the labels follow the
    session. It has a `reviewer` peer, file memory, file delivery, a heartbeat
    precheck and a response cache with its index on disk.
  - Each write is idempotent across a crash. A commit is keyed by its
    trailer, and an edit by its tool call. A row and a training run are keyed
    by the activity idempotency key. The process group of a run dies with it.
  - The CLI has `init`, `run`, `serve`, `status`, `hint`, `stop`, `policy`,
    `approve`, `deny`, `eval`, `verify` and `purge`. Commands find a session
    by its tag. History records the model, and a resume needs the same one. A
    Claude model and a command trainer run the real thing on a GPU. The Claude
    model sends thinking blocks back unchanged.

  No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no engine change.

  Tests: unit and property tests; seeded simulation sweeps (issue #2033) of
  both workflows; SQLite end-to-end tests for each acceptance criterion; CLI
  tests. CI runs them, the clippy step and an offline demo. A nightly job runs
  5000 seeds per sweep. The sweeps found a real bug while the example was
  written: the reserved search attribute `status`. The design record,
  `docs/design/DESIGN-autoresearch.md`, has the acceptance criteria, their evidence and
  the review record.
- **Feature** (implemented): Late stream chunks survive a terminated staged copy — see issue #2128. Activation now copies the source's durable stream chunks whenever the target is not erased. Before, an operator terminate of the staged copy skipped the copy, and the forwarded durable read ended without the late chunks.

  Activation locks the target run row `FOR UPDATE` and reads `input` under that lock. Erasure takes the same lock, so the check cannot race an erasure. An erased target (`execution_input_is_erased`) gets no chunks. The parked task and signal re-pend still need `activated > 0`.

  The append fence of #2042 is not involved. The activation copy uses its own insert path. No migration. No `WorkflowEvent` change. `harvest_events` is not touched.

  Test evidence, all in `shard_rebalance_db_tests.rs`:

  - `activation_copies_late_stream_chunks_over_a_terminated_target` failed before the fix.
  - `activation_copies_no_stream_chunks_over_an_erased_target` covers a finished erasure.
  - `activation_waits_for_an_erasure_holding_the_target_row` covers an erasure in flight.
- **Phase X.Y** (implemented): Monotonic durable stream inserts — see issue #2083. `append_stream_chunks` admits only offsets above the highest stored real offset. Before, a re-run could store an offset below a reader's cursor, and no reader received it. The truncation marker is not a real offset. The shard-rebalance copy has its own insert path and does not change. A per-run advisory lock orders overlapping writers, such as a stale worker after a lease reclaim, so they cannot pass the cap or insert out of order. No migration and no new event.

  Updated tests: `the_cap_holds_when_stored_offsets_are_not_a_prefix` and
  `activation_copies_stream_chunks_written_after_verification`, which now
  expects offsets 0, 2, 3 and 4.

  New tests: `a_hole_behind_the_highest_stored_offset_is_never_filled`,
  `a_dropped_hole_chunk_writes_no_truncation_marker`,
  `an_unordered_first_batch_stores_every_offset`,
  `a_mixed_batch_at_the_cap_marks_only_the_new_chunk`,
  `overlapping_appends_for_one_run_are_serialized` and
  `durable_stream_stores_no_chunk_below_a_live_readers_cursor`.
- **Phase** (implemented): Continue-as-new provenance in `ctx.info()` — see issue #2082. `ctx.info()` now reports `start_source` and `continued_from`. They come from the execution row columns `start_source` and `continued_from_exec_id`. The row never changes after the insert, so the values are replay-stable. A run with no recorded source reports `StartSource::Unknown`.

  `Entity::run` uses them. It drops the input of a start that a caller chose and
  starts from `S::default()`. A continue-as-new, reset or re-run keeps its
  checkpoint, and so does a run with an unknown source. `Entity::initial_state`
  seeds a fresh entity from code. `Entity::trust_start_input` restores the old
  behavior. `Entity::from_input` takes the raw start input and decodes it only
  when the run keeps it. A typed `EntityCheckpoint<S>` workflow input decodes
  first, so a malformed client input fails the start.

  **Design.** No new `WorkflowEvent` field and no migration. The test harness and
  the replayer take `with_start_provenance`, so `replay_check` matches the live
  run. [ADR 0006](adr/0006-keyed-entity.md) and
  [`security-posture.md`](security-posture.md) record the change.

  **Tests.** Unit tests cover the source classifier, the row mapping, the
  `ctx.info()` fields and the entity gate, including `replay_check`.

  **API.** `WorkflowExecutionInfo`, `WorkflowExecuteSpanMeta` and
  `ReplayDeclarativeHandlers` gain a field. An external struct literal of these
  types stops compiling.

  **Upgrade note.** Runs that a caller seeded before the upgrade replay from
  `S::default()`. Drain them, or call `Entity::trust_start_input` first. An
  older worker still trusts the input until the whole fleet rolls. A reset or a
  re-run copies the stored input, so it keeps a forged one. The SQLite backend
  records no start source.
- **Phase 8.x** (implemented): Fairness state bound, preview locks and key spelling — see issue #2097. Four follow-ups to the fairness keys of issue #1976.

  - **Bounded state.** A queue that never drains kept one state row per
    one-shot key. Prune now deletes the old row of every key with no pending
    task, except the clock row. The clock row has the greatest
    `(last_start, key)` of its queue, so `V` never falls and concurrent pruners
    keep the same row. A pruned key loses at most `1/w` of debt, one claim at
    its weight, because `pass - V <= 1/w` after a charge. The idle-queue reset
    now deletes only the last row. `FairClock::prune` models the rule.
  - **Preview without locks.** A preview prunes a temp copy of the state rows,
    so a fair claim never waits for it. The count is the same as a live call,
    because both run one SQL text.
  - **Queue name check.** `queue_fairness::validate_fairness_queue_name` is the
    one check. `WorkerRuntimeConfig::validate` and both public fair claims use
    it. A fair claim on `" q "` or `".."` returns `HarvestError::Config` before
    any statement.
  - **CLI keys.** `harvest queue fairness set|clear` rejects only the literal
    `.` and `..`. Keys such as `%2e` reach the route as `%252e`.

  Tests: `prune_forgives_at_most_one_claim_of_debt`,
  `one_shot_keys_leave_one_row_on_a_queue_that_never_drains`,
  `prune_bounds_one_shot_keys_on_a_queue_that_never_drains`,
  `a_preview_takes_no_lock_on_the_state_rows`,
  `a_fair_claim_refuses_an_unaddressable_queue_name` and
  `queue_fairness_accepts_percent_spelled_keys`.
- **Engine** (implemented): Orphaned payload blob sweep — see issue #2123. None by default. The sweep is opt-in.

  **The leak.** An append uploads its offloaded payloads before it opens its
  transaction (issue #954). A rollback after the upload left the blobs in the
  store with no `harvest_payload_refs` row. Retention finds blobs only through
  those rows, so nothing deleted them.

  **The sweep.** The retention runtime now runs `payload_orphans::sweep_orphaned_blobs`
  once per tick.

  - Turn it on with `RetentionConfig::with_payload_orphan_grace`. The grace
    period is at least one hour.
  - It deletes a blob only when the blob is older than the grace period and no
    shard references it. It checks every database. It checks the age itself and
    does not trust the store to filter.
  - A failed reference check stops the sweep. It never deletes on a guess.
  - Each tick reads at most 100 pages. A cursor carries the listing across ticks.
  - `dry_run` counts orphans and deletes nothing.

  **New trait methods.** `PayloadStore::list(prefix, created_before, cursor)` is
  optional. The default returns `None`, so existing stores compile and the sweep
  stays off for them. The log says so once. `created_at` must be the time of the
  latest `put`.

  `PayloadStore::delete_if_older(key, created_before)` is also optional. It
  deletes a blob only if its latest write is before the cutoff, in one atomic
  step. The sweep uses it when the store offers it, so a writer that re-uploads
  a key after the listing keeps its blob. The default returns `None`, and the
  sweep then falls back to `delete`.

  **Metric.** `harvest.retention.payload_orphans` counts `found`, `deleted` and
  `failed` blobs per `store.id`.

  **Limits.** The store must hold only harvest blobs. Do not share it with the
  agent response cache. Each retention process must pool every shard database,
  or the sweep misses references. A store without
  `delete_if_older` keeps a race open: a re-upload of identical bytes during one
  page of checks can lose to a plain delete. The `list` contract requires `put`
  to refresh `created_at`, which closes the race for earlier uploads.

  **Invariants.** No migration, no `WorkflowEvent` variant and no replay impact.
  The sweep never writes `harvest_events`.

  **Tests.** `payload_orphan_sweep_tests` runs against Postgres: a rolled-back
  append, a blob that only one of two shards references, a young blob with a
  faulty store, a store without listing, the page budget and cursor, `dry_run`,
  and the retention runtime with its metrics.
- **Phase X.Y** (implemented): Cross-backend conformance suite — see issue #2030. A new test-only crate, `autumn-harvest-conformance`, runs one corpus of workflows on Postgres 16 and on SQLite. Each scenario must give the same executions, the same histories after the named comparison rules, the same outcome and the same update results. Each history must replay on the core `WorkflowReplayer`.

  - One test target depends on both backends. The SQLite crate still builds
    the core without `db`, so its own tests do not build Diesel.
  - A scenario is data: a workflow, an input, initial signals and a script of
    steps. Steps wait on history events, never on sleeps.
