  note. A writer-only process also needs a post-commit sender
  (`notify::register_pool`). Without one, the fallback drops each owner note.

  **Tests.** `owner_wake_worker_tests` runs an owner and a non-owner worker in
  owner mode. An activity result, a signal, an update admission, a cancel
  and a timeout scanner write each wake the owner, and the non-owner prepares
  no decision. A pause,
  a reset and a terminate from another connection each evict the owner's
  entry. The next decision replays cold and records no non-determinism. A
  child decided by one owner writes its terminal into a parent that another
  owner holds. That owner wakes and its next decision reads the terminal. A
  lost evict wake still replays cold. `owner_wake_db_tests` checks the wake
  and its evict flag on the partition channel for each writer path it covers. A
  listener of another partition gets no wake. The docs guard
  `foreign_writer_table_cites_real_functions` checks each writer that the ADR
  table cites.
- **Engine** (implemented): Owned workflow-task claims and the owner-mode switch — see issue #2252. Stage 1a of epic #2247. [ADR 0009](adr/0009-decision-owner.md) fixes the protocol. Owner mode replaces the sticky lease for workflow tasks. Activity claims do not change. Owner mode is off until an operator turns it on.

  **Migration.** `20261021151820_harvest_decision_owner_claim` adds the
  nullable column `harvest_task_queue.decision_partition`, the one-row switch
  table `harvest_decision_owner_mode`, the candidate table
  `harvest_decision_owner_candidates` and the function
  `harvest_task_queue_owner_claim_guard`. It creates no trigger. No
  `WorkflowEvent` variant, no replay impact.

  **Switch.** `decision_owner::enable_owner_mode` refuses while a live worker
  lacks the `decision_owner_version` label, while live workers poll different
  queues or run different builds, while live owners register different
  workflow or activity types, or while no owner loop is live. A decision can
  run any activity inline, as a local activity. Each worker advertises a
  fingerprint of its workflow and activity types in the
  `decision_owner_handlers` label. It stamps
  live workflow tasks. Then one transaction installs the claim guard,
  re-pends the legacy claims of dead workers and sets the switch.
  `disable_owner_mode` clears the switch and turns the guard off in one
  transaction.

  **Claim.** In owner mode a worker claims a workflow task only from its own
  partitions, or an unstamped one. The owned claim is a splice on each claim
  text, so the legacy text stays byte-identical. It sets
  `harvest.owner_claim` to the holder token, tests one bit of a 64-byte
  partition mask, and checks the holder of a stamped row in each candidate
  scan. The guard skips a workflow claim
  with no token, so an old binary claims no workflow task. For a stamped row
  it takes the owner row `FOR KEY SHARE SKIP LOCKED` and matches the holder.
  The sticky gate does not apply to a workflow row, and an owned park writes
  no pin.

  **Loop.** Each worker runs one owner loop per database. It scans once a
  second, records itself as a live candidate, renews every TTL / 3, drops a
  tenure at its local deadline, and balances to `⌈512 / live candidates⌉`. A
  joiner takes free partitions. An owner above target + 1 stops claiming the
  extra ones and releases them one scan later. A worker with no workflow
  slot or type is a participant: it claims in the owned form and owns
  nothing. Any owner takes a partition whose
  lease ended over one renewal interval ago. An acquisition re-pends the
  workflow tasks that a dead worker left `RUNNING` there. A graceful stop
  releases every partition after the drain. Colocated shards share one key. A
  worker that covers part of a colocated group refuses owner mode there.

  **Terminal guard.** The extra cold decisions of issue #2007 came from
  `queue::claim_still_held_for_update`, in both modes. A peer claim scans the
  queue head `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and can lock a row just after another
  loop claimed it. Postgres keeps that lock until the peer claim transaction
  ends. The final decision of a run read the lock as a lost claim. It rolled
  back, released the task, and the retry replayed cold. A skip now retries
  once with a blocking lock in a savepoint, bounded by
  `CLAIM_GUARD_LOCK_WAIT` (100 ms). A transfer still reads as lost. The bound
  is far below `deadlock_timeout`, so the guard still ends an ABBA cycle.

  **One fence per transaction.** A decision transaction fenced up to three
  times: at its start, in a nested write and in its event insert, which also
  opened a savepoint. The first fence holds its rows until the transaction
  ends, so the others could not fail. `decision_owner::fenced_scope` marks
  the rest of a fenced transaction. Inside it, a fence of the same connection
  and tenure sends no query, and the event insert needs no savepoint. The
  worker persist transaction uses it. At four claim loops, the extra round
  trips had cost owner mode about 10% of its throughput. After the change,
  owner mode ran 2.6%, 2.0% and 4.9% below legacy at 1, 2 and 4 claim
  loops. The 1 and 2 loop results are within the effect of run order.
  `docs/design/DESIGN-2252.md` section 4 has the runs.

  **Evidence.** Unit tests for the splice, the balance plan, the local
  deadline and the colocated groups. Postgres tests for the guard, the owned
  claim, enable, disable and rebalance. Worker tests for zero extra cold
  decisions under two claim loops and for resident hits across the sticky
  window. The e2e bench gains `HARVEST_BENCH_OWNER_MODE=1` and a decision note.

  **Hit rate.** Each run of the e2e throughput bench makes four decisions,
  and its first decision has no resident state anywhere. So the hit rate over
  all decisions cannot pass 75% in either mode. The bench now also reports
  the continuation hit rate: hits over the decisions after the first of each
  run. The worker test measures that rate across a sticky window.

  **API.** `schema::harvest_task_queue` gains `decision_partition`, and
  `TaskQueueItem` does not. A full-row `.load::<TaskQueueItem>()` on that
  table now needs `.select(TaskQueueItem::as_select())`.
- **Phase** (implemented): PAUSED-run index for the claim gate — see issue #2212. Migration `20261018053859` adds `idx_harvest_we_paused ON harvest_workflow_executions (id) WHERE state = 'PAUSED'`. The claim's PAUSED-run gate read one primary-key page chain per candidate. With more than 32 paused-run tasks at a queue head it read every PAUSED row. Claim buffers (EXPLAIN, total) fall 21% to 34% with 10 paused heads, and 80% to 90% with 50 paused heads at 100k to 1M executions. The claimed ids are identical before and after. The migration takes `SHARE` on `harvest_workflow_executions` for the build and has an out-of-band `CONCURRENTLY` recipe. Harness and numbers: `docs/perf-artifacts/claim-paused-gate/`.
- **Phase** (implemented): SLA-breach scan uses its partial index (Ledger). `timeout::enforce_workflow_sla_breaches` repeats the tail of the predicate of `idx_harvest_executions_sla_deadline`, `(completed_at IS NULL OR completed_at > sla_deadline_at)`, in its `WHERE`. The new clause adds no condition. The first clause already implies it.

  **Why.** Postgres cannot prove that `sla_deadline_at < COALESCE(completed_at,
  NOW())` implies the index predicate, so the partial index was never a
  candidate. Every timeout tick read the whole executions table to flag zero
  rows: 189, 1,887 and 19,887 buffers at 10,000, 100,000 and 1,000,000
  executions. It now reads 1 buffer at every size.

  **Evidence.** `docs/performance-sla-breach-scan.md` and
  `docs/perf-artifacts/sla-breach-scan/`. The flagged rows are identical before
  and after across 14 boundary rows at three table sizes. The existing
  `sla_breach_tests` pass unchanged.

  No `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no schema change, no replay impact.
- **Onramp** (implemented): chapter 3 snippets guarded in CI. Docs tooling only. `scripts/check-durable-timers-examples.sh` extracts the three flagship timer workflows of chapter 3 and compiles them with `cargo check` in CI's lint job. Baseline: 3 snippets, 0 compile errors, 8 min cold. The guard finds no defect today. It keeps the chapter from drifting from the timer API. No public API change.
- **Phase** (implemented): `is_redacted_export` probes one key without a `Value` tree (perf). `debugger::is_redacted_export` reads `payload_policy` with a streaming map visitor instead of parsing the whole history into a `serde_json::Value`. `harvest debug diff` and `ReplayDebugger::trace_json` call it before they parse the same text again. Results are unchanged for every input, including repeated keys, non-object documents and invalid JSON. On a 10,001-event history the probe drops from 514,087,439 to 92,813,673 instructions across two files (-81.9%), and the whole `debug diff` pipeline drops 23.7%. Evidence and the reproduce command are in `docs/performance-debug-diff-redaction-probe.md`. Harness: `benches/debugger_diff_profile.rs`.

  No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no new migration, no replay impact.
- **Phase fork perf** (implemented): count activity occurrences without hashing — see issue #2000. `fork::scheduled_occurrence` found the occurrence number of a scheduled activity with a `HashMap` that hashed every `ActivityScheduled` name before the match. It now finds the activity by id first, then counts earlier events with the same name. The result is unchanged. No event, migration or append-only change.

  Evidence: the new `fork_resolve_profile` callgrind harness resolves a K-way
  fan-out through `resolve_activity` and `settle_holds`. Instructions fall from
  22.68M to 15.29M at K=250 (-32.6%), from 69.23M to 39.93M at K=500 (-42.3%),
  and from 237.10M to 120.45M at K=1000 (-49.2%). The 34 `fork::tests` pass
  unchanged. See `docs/performance-fork-scheduled-occurrence.md`.
- **Testing** (implemented): A fair drain phase for the owner-lease simulation — see issue #2294. The DST nightly failed the owner-lease sweep in all four shards. Each shard stopped at its first failing seed, with "the run did not consume every signal within 400 steps". No invariant failed, and the engine was not at fault. The faults ended the lease every few steps for all 400 steps. No owner makes progress then. The check asked for progress while the faults went on, so a few seeds per million failed.

  A run of `dst::owner` now has two phases, as a world run has. The fault
  phase is unchanged, so a run that ends in it has the same trace as before.
  The drain then injects no fault: no nemesis, no expiry, no release and no
  stall. It is weakly fair, with `owner::FAIR_STEPS` (8). A run must consume
  every signal before the drain ends. `OwnerConfig::drain_bound` computes the
  step bound of a drain. The default limit of 400 steps covers up to 103
  decisions in flight at the drain start. The trace logs that number.

  `OwnerConfig::max_steps` is now `fault_steps`, with a new `drain_steps`.
  `OwnerStats` counts the drains, and the longest drain, wait and enabled
  set.

  The world drain and the owner drain now share one fairness helper,
  `dst::fair::Waits`. The world drain keeps its rule and its traces.

  The replay command did not reproduce the failure. `replay_one_owner_seed`
  failed on an invariant only, and the nightly seeds broke none. The sweep
  and the replay now share one verdict, `OwnerReport::failure`.

  A new rule, R8 of ADR 0010, backs the drain. A fenced commit unloads its
  worker only when the worker still pins the fenced epoch. Its invariant,
  `LiveRowHasAPinnedHolder`, is now in `OwnerLease.tla`, `OwnerLease.cfg`,
  the simulator and the Stateright model. The `unload-on-any-fence` mutant
  breaks it in TLC, Stateright and the simulator. That mutant also stops a
  drain with work left. The old sweep missed it, because the lease churn
  freed the row. Stateright also checks `DrainCanProgress`: each state that
  is not quiescent has a step that is not a fault.

  No migration. No `WorkflowEvent` change. No engine change.

  Tests:

  - `the_seeds_of_issue_2294_converge_in_the_drain`: the four nightly seeds
    fail with no drain and pass with it.
  - `the_drain_converges_fairly_within_its_bound`: the drain starts at every
    third step from 0 to 400, over 12 seeds. Each wait and each drain stays
    within its bound.
  - `the_drain_leaves_the_fault_phase_unchanged`,
    `the_drain_injects_no_fault` and `the_drain_ends_every_stall`.
  - `the_replay_fails_a_run_that_does_not_converge` and
    `the_failure_of_a_run_that_does_not_converge_names_the_drain`.
  - `a_worker_that_unloads_on_any_fence_stops_the_drain`, in the `dst` and
    the `stateright` targets.
  - `dst::fair` unit tests: the fairness rules, and the bound
    `fair_steps + k - 1` while actions come and go.
  - All 20 rows of `formal/tla/models.txt` pass TLC.
  - The 4,000,000 seeds of the failed nightly run pass.
- **Measurement** (implemented): Stage 2 gate: cold decisions and history load — see issue #2257. Stage 2 of epic #2247 is an owner-local disk cache (#2258). It ships only if cold decisions pass 20% of decisions for a week, or the cold p99 passes 50 ms. This change builds the instruments for that gate and records its bench half in `docs/rnd/2026-10-22-stage-2-gate.md`.

  - **`harvest.workflow.resident.duration{workflow, queue, outcome}`.** A new
    histogram, in seconds. The worker records it with each
    `harvest.workflow.resident` count. The clock starts before the history
    load and stops at the end of the first drive. The p99 of
    `outcome="cold"` is the cold p99 of the gate. `MetricsRecorder` gains
    `record_workflow_resident_duration` with a no-op default, so an existing
    recorder still builds. The metrics-rs adapter bridges it.
  - **Dashboard.** The starter pack gains "Stage 2 gate: cold share and cold
    p99".
  - **`examples/history-load-gate`.** A new measurement crate. It times one
    history load from Postgres, through the worker load path, and from a
    local SQLite file, with the schema and query of `autumn-harvest-sqlite`.
    Both sides decode each row through `PayloadCodecs::decode_event`. It
    times the cold load of every live run after an owner restart. It drives
    the real `WorkflowCache` to model the cold share of the 1,000-entry cap.
    It applies the thresholds to fleet values: one trip gives `go`, both
    values with no trip give `no-go`, anything else is `undecided`. With no
    sizes and no runs, it opens no database. CI lints it, runs its unit
    tests, and runs its Postgres test from a `linux` manifest row.

  **Results.** One Postgres read of a 10,000-event history takes 44 to
  64 ms at p50. The cold path reads the history twice, 100 to 138 ms. Its
  p99 passes 50 ms near 3,400 events. A local SQLite read is 2.2 to 3.3
  times faster than one Postgres read. Under a uniform load and owner mode,
  more than 1,250 live runs per owner give a cold share above 20% from the
  cache cap alone.

  **Finding.** The cold path decodes the full history twice. A single read
  would halve it with no new store.

  **Verdict:** undecided until a fleet week gives both values. No migration.
  No new `WorkflowEvent` variant.
- **Engine** (implemented): Owner failover tests: frozen owner, kill -9 and scale-out — see issue #2254. Stage 1a of epic #2247. No migration. No `WorkflowEvent` variant. No new append path, so the append-only invariant keeps its two exceptions.

  **Tests.** `owner_failover_tests.rs` runs the owner as a child process of
  the test binary, against real Postgres. It stops the owner with `SIGSTOP`
  inside a decision and inside an open commit. In both cases the standby
  takes the partition and completes the run. The woken owner writes nothing.
  It kills the owner with `SIGKILL` just after a renewal. The next decision
  on its partitions runs 10.2 s to 10.3 s after the kill, under the 11 s
  bound. It grows the fleet from 4 to 8 workers under load. The fleet
  recovers in 8.4 s to 9.8 s, under the 20 s bound, with no fenced commit
  after the settle. `docs/performance-owner-failover.md` records the results
  beside the stage 1 table.

  **Fixes.** The first runs failed the kill -9 bound and churned on
  scale-out. Four changes fix that:

  - A standby scans again just after the next foreign lease end
    (`decision_owner::next_scan_wait`, `OwnerTick::next_change`).
  - An acquisition wakes an idle claim loop of the worker.
  - A worker acquires at most 32 partitions per scan, adopts them, and scans
    again at once (`OwnerLoop::with_acquire_chunk`, `OwnerTick::more`).
  - A free partition becomes an orphan one TTL after its lease end, not one
    renewal interval (`OwnerLeaseTtl::orphan_after`).

  A tick that stops using partitions still waits a full scan interval before
  the release, so decisions in flight can commit first. ADR 0009 decisions 8 and
  9 and its stage 1 table record the change.
- **Engine** (implemented): Baseline of the claim split, the persist phases and the fence cost — see issue #2248. Stage 1 of epic #2247. The case for a decision owner extrapolated from the formula `1 / (claims × claim latency)`. This change measures the three inputs that the formula did not have. Results: [`docs/performance-decision-owner-baseline.md`](performance-decision-owner-baseline.md). A workflow claim costs about what an activity claim costs (4.33 ms against 4.07 ms at one loop). Event and task inserts take 14% of the persist each, the commit 6%. Owner mode with DR on adds two statements and about 20% to the persist at one writer, so it fails the stage 1b bar of 10%.

  **No migration. No `WorkflowEvent` variant. No replay impact.** The claim
  and persist SQL do not change.

  **Claim kind.** A `claim` sample on `harvest.db.query.duration` has a new
  `kind` label: `workflow`, `activity`, `empty` or `error`. The new trait
  method `MetricsRecorder::record_claim_duration` defaults to
  `record_db_query_duration(DbOp::Claim, ..)`, so a recorder written before
  this change still sees every claim. The shipped panels and alerts sum by
  `op` and `shard`, so the label does not split them. A recorder that wraps
  another recorder and forwards only `record_db_query_duration` loses the
  label, and should forward the two new methods too.

  **Persist phases.** The new histogram
  `harvest.db.persist.phase_duration{phase, shard}` splits each decision
  persist into `fence`, `events`, `tasks`, `notify`, `commit` and `other`.
  Phase timers sit at the chokepoints of each phase. The phases of one
  persist add up to its `persist` sample. A terminal failure write records no
  phase. The metrics-rs adapter and the built-in scrape endpoint render both
  signals. The starter dashboard gains two panels.

  **Fence fix.** With DR fencing on, an owner-mode decision sent the owner
  fence again for each append, through `decision_owner::fence_pinned`. That
  broke the rule of issue #2252: a nested fence of the same connection sends
  no query. `fence_pinned` now checks the fenced scope.
  `a_dr_fenced_owner_decision_sends_one_owner_fence` proves it: 3 fence calls
  before, 1 after.

  **Bench.** `benches/decision_fence_bench.rs` (criterion) times a model
  decision persist with zero, one and two fence rows. It uses the real owner
  row of issue #2251. CI compiles it.

  **Tests.** Unit tests and a property test of the phase split, the default
  of `record_claim_duration`, the adapter and scrape-endpoint renders, a
  worker test of the claim kinds and phases on Postgres, the fence test, and
  the bench-note helpers.
- **Feature** (implemented): Owner-local disk cache, encrypted and disposable — see issue #2258. Stage 2 of epic #2247. A decision owner can keep the history of each live run in a local SQLite file. A memory miss then reads the file and the Postgres delta, not the full Postgres history. See `docs/adr/0012-owner-disk-cache.md`.

  - **Opt-in.** Build with the `owner-disk-cache` feature and set
    `WorkerConfig::with_owner_disk_cache(dir)`. The cache acts only in owner
    mode, on the partitions that the worker owns. A directory set on a build
    without the feature fails the worker start.
  - **Encrypted.** AES-256-GCM seals every row under a node key that lives
    in memory only. The cache stores decoded events, so no codec ciphertext
    reaches the disk.
  - **Disposable.** The worker deletes every cache file at start. A lost
    tenure deletes the file of its partition. A stopped worker deletes the
    files that it wrote. A terminal commit and an evict wake purge the run.
    An erasure sends the owner an evict wake. The owner scan runs a reconcile
    pass at most once in 30 s per shard. It purges each cached run that is
    not `RUNNING`, and each file of an older codec key generation.
  - **Long histories only.** `WorkerConfig::with_owner_disk_cache_min_events`
    sets the fewest events that a run needs before it goes to disk. The
    default is 100. A shorter history loads faster from Postgres.
  - **Validity stamps.** Each file holds the owner epoch and the codec key
    generation. Each run holds its state and the hash of its last event. A
    mismatch or a damaged row purges the entry, and the decision replays
    cold from Postgres.
  - **`harvest.workflow.disk_cache{workflow, queue, outcome}`.** A new counter
    of disk reads: `hit`, `miss`, `stale` or `corrupt`. `MetricsRecorder`
    gains `record_workflow_disk_cache` with a no-op default. The starter pack
    gains a panel.
  - **`examples/history-load-gate`.** The warm-up step also times the disk
    cache. From about 100 events, the next pass after a restart is 1.5 to
    1.9 times faster than a Postgres load. Below that, it is not faster. See
    `docs/rnd/2026-10-23-owner-disk-cache.md`.

  **Tests.** `an_erased_run_leaves_no_local_bytes`,
  `an_erasure_purges_a_run_that_a_missed_purge_left`,
  `a_killed_owner_leaves_no_readable_bytes`,
  `a_retired_codec_key_leaves_no_ciphertext`,
  `a_rotated_codec_key_leaves_no_ciphertext_on_disk` and
  `a_corrupt_file_replays_cold` cover the four red tests of the issue.

  No migration. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. Off by default.
- **Engine** (implemented): Keyed-entity state as history events with a Postgres projection — see issue #2259. Stage 3a of epic #2247. [ADR 0006](adr/0006-keyed-entity.md) records the amendment. The design record is [`docs/design/DESIGN-2259.md`](design/DESIGN-2259.md).

  **Event.** The entity loop records a state snapshot as
  `SideEffectRecorded` with the new kind `SideEffectKind::EntityState`. It
  records one at the start of each run, one after each op, and one before a
  delete ends the run. The value is `{"state": <S>, "stats": <EntityStats>}`.
  Replay adopts each recorded snapshot, so it rebuilds the state from the
  events. A tolerant matcher reads a history from before this change as having
  no snapshot, so old entity histories replay with no change. Upgrade every
  worker before entity runs move to the new release: an older worker cannot
  decode the new kind.

  **Migration.** `20261023015028_harvest_entity_state` adds the table
  `harvest_entity_state`, the function `harvest_entity_state_project` and the
  trigger `harvest_entity_state_projection_trg` on `harvest_events`. The
  trigger runs `AFTER INSERT` with a `WHEN` clause, and writes the latest
  snapshot of each key in the transaction that inserts the event. Every insert
  path keeps the projection in step: a decision, a reset, a fork and a shard
  move. The append-only guard does not change. The partition layout changes
  reinstall the new trigger with the guard.

  **Coverage.** `codec_rotation::CODEC_COLUMNS` lists
  `harvest_entity_state.snapshot`. Erasure tombstones the row of each erased
  run and reports `entity_states_scrubbed`.

  **Caps.** A state past the side-effect cap or the depth cap records an
  `omitted` marker, not the state. The history stays loadable, and a query on
  that run replays.

  **Shard moves.** The target rebuilds the row from the copied events. An
  aborted move gives the row back to the runs that stay, and the cutover
  deletes the row of the sealed source run.

  **Reads.** `autumn_harvest::entity_state` reads a row by key, reads the row
  of a run, and lists the rows of an entity type. The HTTP query routes and
  `WorkflowHandle::execute_query_in_process` answer `harvest.entity.state` and
  `harvest.entity.stats` for a running run from the projection. They replay
  when the run has no full snapshot in the row. A terminal run replays, as
  before.

  **Tests.** `entity::tests` cover the snapshots, replay from snapshots, old
  histories, continued and reset runs, the payload caps and the byte budget.
  `entity_state_db_tests` covers a crash at every step, a worker crash, run
  ordering, an aborted shard copy, a reset of a continued run, erasure, codec
  rotation and each partition layout change. `entity_state_query_integration`
  proves that the HTTP query on a running run does not run the workflow body,
  and that a terminal run still replays.
- **Perf** (implemented): Batched owner acquisition — see issue #2296. `OwnerLoop` now takes the partitions of a scan in one transaction, `decision_owner::acquire_many`. Before, each partition was its own transaction of 6 statements. A join of 512 partitions sent 3,072 statements. Now the statement count of a scan does not grow with its picks.

  - The batch takes the DR generation row first. Then it locks the takeable
    owner rows `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, in ascending partition order.
  - It adds 1 to the epoch of each locked row only. A row that a commit holds
    is skipped and listed as busy. So the drain of ADR 0009 decision 5 holds.
  - A batch never waits for an owner row. One busy row does not delay the rest.
  - `acquire` keeps its single-row form, which waits. Tests and
    `decision_fence_bench` use it.
  - No migration. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. No `harvest_events` write.

  `pg_stat_statements` on Postgres 16.15, one fresh database per run, 512
  acquisitions on one connection:

  | Path | Statements | Buffers | WAL bytes |
  |:--|--:|--:|--:|
  | `acquire` per partition | 3,072 | 6,120 | 151,354 |
  | `acquire_many`, chunks of 32 (the worker default) | 96 | 3,443 | 128,431 |
  | `acquire_many`, one batch of 512 | 6 | 4,205 | 159,275 |

  The issue counted 5 statements per partition. Issue #2254 later added the
  idle bound, so the count is now 6.

  Evidence:

  - `decision_owner_db_tests`: one transaction writes each row of a batch
    (one `xmin`); held and busy rows are skipped with no wait; a stale owner is
    fenced after a batched takeover.
  - `decision_owner_claim_tests`: a joiner takes each chunk in one transaction;
    a batch that names a missing row takes no row.
  - `cross_region_dr_tests`: a fenced region takes no row of a batch, and its
    owner loop adopts nothing; a batch that waits out a bump is all busy.
  - `decision_owner_lock_modes_db_tests`: `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` skips a row
    that a commit holds, with no wait.
  - `decision_owner_sim_db_tests`: the owner simulator passes with batched
    acquisitions.
  - Verus, `owner_fence.rs`: a batch moves each locked row by one acquisition
    and leaves each other row. A row that a commit holds keeps its epoch, so
    the commit still passes its fence.
- **Fix** (implemented): ctutils 0.4.5 and tokio 1.53.3 for RUSTSEC-2026-0385 and -0386 — see issue #2307. The daily advisory scan failed on two new advisories.

  - `ctutils` 0.4.2 builds mask generation code that can branch on secret
    values (RUSTSEC-2026-0385). It is a transitive dependency of the RustCrypto
    `digest` 0.11 family. Version 0.4.5 fixes it.
  - `tokio` 1.53.2 has unsound `AsyncFd` constructors (RUSTSEC-2026-0386).
    Version 1.53.3 fixes it.

  The changes:

  - `Cargo.lock` moves `ctutils` to 0.4.5 and `tokio` to 1.53.3. The new
    `tokio` also changes which `windows-sys` versions some crates resolve to.
    Cargo drops `windows-sys` 0.60 and `windows-targets` 0.53, which nothing
    needs any more. These changes affect Windows targets only.
  - `sandbox/exec.rs` opens its pidfd with `AsyncFd::register_with_interest`.
    `tokio` 1.53.3 deprecates `with_interest`, and clippy denies warnings. The
    `AsyncFd` owns the descriptor, so the `unsafe` contract holds.
  - The workspace `tokio` floor moves from 1 to 1.53.3. A downstream consumer
    reads the manifest, not this lockfile, so only the floor keeps it off
    1.53.2 (as in PR #1303).

  **No migration. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. No public API change.** The
  lockfiles under `docs/assays/apparatus/` are separate. The advisory scan does
  not read them, so they keep their old versions.

  **Checks.** `cargo deny --all-features check` with cargo-deny 0.20.2, the CI
  version, reports `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`. Before
  the change it failed on both advisories.
- **Engine** (implemented): Stage 1b: workflow tasks leave the contended claim path — see issue #2255. Stage 1b of epic #2247. [ADR 0009](adr/0009-decision-owner.md) decision 13 records the design. Owner mode stays off until an operator turns it on. Legacy mode does not change.

  **Migration.** `20261023015935_harvest_owner_decider` adds the partial index
  `idx_harvest_tq_owner_scan` on `harvest_task_queue (scheduled_at) WHERE
  state = 'PENDING' AND task_type = 'workflow'`, and the function
  `harvest_decision_fence`. The index build is guarded, so an operator can
  build it `CONCURRENTLY` first. No `WorkflowEvent` variant, no replay impact.

  **Owner decider.** In owner mode each worker runs one owner decider per
  owned database, beside its claim loops. The claim loops then claim
  activities only. The decider learns of work from the owner wake of a
  partition and from a scan of its partitions by due time. The scan runs at
  each tenure change and after a full scan. It also runs at the next due
  time, at most one poll interval apart. While a listener receives the owner
  wakes, the gap grows to 1 s or one poll interval, whichever is longer. So
  a short poll interval does not scan each partition many times a second.
  A take is the owned
  by-execution claim, so every claim gate, the claim guard and the
  post-claim rechecks still apply. Each take runs in its own future, bounded
  by the workflow permits, and a scan never stalls a take. The task row
  serializes the decisions of one execution. A take that finds nothing backs
  its execution off, from one poll interval up to 30 s. A wake ends the
  backoff. So a refused row cannot hold the head of the scan. The scan index
  leads with the partition, so a scan reads a few rows of each owned
  partition. With owner mode off, the decider sends no query. A decider runs
  only on a database with a wake listener, so a worker with no notification
  URL keeps the owned claim. A worker with queue weights or fairness keys
  runs no decider. It keeps the owned claim of
  issue #2252, so its workflow tasks follow the weighted queue order and the
  fairness lags of issue #1976.

  **Signals.** The decider keeps execution ids only, as hints. It
  acknowledges nothing. A signal is a `harvest_signals` row before
  `send_signal` returns (restate#4566). A new owner scans each partition that
  it acquires. So a signal acknowledged just before an epoch bump reaches
  it, also when the old owner held its wake.

  **Wakes.** The sender keeps a plain owner wake to the writer's own
  partition. Only an evict wake to that partition is dropped. A claim-held
  re-pend that is due now wakes the owner of its partition. So a fenced
  owner's re-pend reaches the new owner at once. Where the decider runs, an
  owner wake does not wake the claim loops.

  **Fence.** With a DR pin, an owner-mode decision fences both rows in one
  statement. The generation row comes first, as ADR 0009 decision 6 orders.
  It waits with no bound, as before. The owner row waits at most 250 ms.
  Inside the fenced scope, an append checks neither row again when the start
  fence took the same generation row. The scope records that row. The signal
  and timer ingest runs in the fenced scope, so it fences once.

  **Metric.** `MetricsRecorder::record_owner_take_duration` times each take
  as `harvest_db_query_duration{op="take", kind, shard}`. A take reads no
  queue head, so it is not a claim. The default records nothing, so a custom
  recorder sees no workflow take until it adds the method. The starter alert
  watches `take`, and the claim-by-kind panel shows it.

  **Evidence.** `owner_decider_tests` proves 3 activity claims, 0 workflow
  claims and 4 takes per 3-activity workflow. It delivers a signal once when
  the epoch bumps just after the acknowledgement. One case has no owner at
  the acknowledgement. In the other case, the old owner holds the wake. A due
  timer fires through the scan, and the scan reads only owned and unstamped
  due rows. `a_dr_fenced_owner_decision_sends_one_fence_statement` proves one
  fence statement and one generation read per decision. Three more DR tests
  cover a bumped generation, a held generation row and a colocated shard.
  [`performance-owner-decider.md`](performance-owner-decider.md) records the
  assay 0014 runs and the fence bench.
- **Phase X.Y** (implemented): durable agents and agent meshes (epic #2262). The agent loop (#1973), the keyed entity (#1975) and the agent mesh join into one durable `Agent`. `docs/design/DESIGN-2262.md` is the spec. Each sub-issue below has its own red tests.

  ### A first-class durable `Agent` (issue #2263)

  - `autumn_harvest_agent::agent`: `Agent`, `AgentId` (`<kind>/<name>`, the
    workflow id), `AgentOp` (`user_message`, `control`), `Control` (`pause`,
    `resume`, `reset_memory`, `clear_transcript`), `AgentProfile` (one per kind,
    on the harness), `AgentState` and `AgentStatus`.
  - The workflow `agent` runs `Entity::run`. Each op runs one segment of the
    agent loop with the whole harness: tools, policy, approvals, budgets,
    memory, the loop guard and delivery.
  - The activity `agent_profile` reads the profile once per run. Replay reads
    the record. The activity `agent_memory_reset` clears the scope
    `agent:<id>`. `MemoryStore::clear` is a new method. Its default refuses.
  - The inbox kernel `agent::inbox::admit` holds work while the agent is
    paused, and runs it in order on resume.
  - A failed op keeps the transcript as it was, and keeps the labels and the
    tokens that it used.
  - Run ids are `<incarnation>:s<n>`. The state carries the tool-round counter,
    so approval names never repeat.
  - SQLite: `sqlite::send`, `sqlite::delete`, `sqlite::drive`,
    `sqlite::state` and `sqlite::current_run`.
  - `examples/agent_session_entity.rs` moves to the agent crate and runs on the
    new type. The §9 limit "the session entity is separate" is gone.

  No migration. No `WorkflowEvent` variant. An `agent_loop` history replays as
  it ran: the refactor changes no command of `agent_loop`.

  **Tests.** `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/durable_agent.rs`:

  - Two messages run one at a time, in order.
  - A restart at an approval asks no recorded model call again.
  - A process crash inside a model call runs only that call again.
  - The flow labels survive a checkpoint.
  - A paused agent holds its work and runs it in order on resume.
  - A failed op keeps the transcript and the labels.
  - Approval names never repeat across ops.
  - An unknown kind fails each op and keeps the agent.
  - A delete ends the life, and a new send starts another.
  - `reset_memory` clears the scope of the agent.
  - A recorded agent history replays.

  A mutation of each guarantee turns its test red.

  ### Mid-turn messages: queue, steer and interrupt (issue #2265)

  - `UserMessage::urgency`: `queue` (the default), `steer` and `interrupt`.
    `Agent::urgency_signal` names the signal that goes before the op:
    `agent.steer` with a `Steer`, or `agent.interrupt` with an `Interrupt`.
  - A durable agent races each model turn against `agent.interrupt`. The race
    records its winner, so replay takes the same branch.
  - `Tool::interruptible` (default `false`) and `FnTool::interruptible`. Only
    an opted-in tool call races an interrupt. Any other call runs to its end,
    and no later call of the round runs.
  - An approval wait ends as a rejection on an interrupt.
  - `AgentStop::Interrupted`. `ModelTurnRequest::interruptible` and
    `ModelTurn::interruptible` are left out at their defaults, so an
    `agent_loop` request records the same bytes as before.
  - A steer and its op dedupe through `AgentState::steer`, so each steer runs
    once.

  **Tests.** `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/agent_interrupts.rs`:

  - An interrupt during a model call cancels the call and records it.
  - An interrupted history replays.
  - An interrupt ends an approval wait as a rejection.
  - A stale interrupt does not stop the next op.
  - A steer joins the running op, and its own op does nothing.
  - A steer with no running op runs once, as a message.
  - A message acknowledged before a crash runs once.
  - Two simulator sweeps. No seed cancels a write tool halfway. Some seeds
    cancel an opted-in tool.

  A mutation of each guarantee turns its test red.

  ### Per-agent heartbeats and follow-ups (issue #2266)

  - `AgentHeartbeat`, `AgentProfile::heartbeat`, `HeartbeatSetting` and
    `Control::SetHeartbeat`. Each agent key has its own heartbeat, driven by
    its own durable timer through `Entity::run_with_wakes`.
  - `AgentOp::HeartbeatTick` and `AgentOp::FollowupDue` are inbox ops. They do
    not decode from a signal.
  - `AgentProfile::followups`: a booked follow-up is a deadline in the state.
    `AgentState::chain` keeps the chain cap across a checkpoint.
  - A tick is unattended and read-only unless it allows actions. A silent tick
    leaves the transcript as it was. `agent::wake::next_heartbeat` books the
    next tick strictly after the time a tick ran.
  - Each op records one `system_now` side effect and upserts the search
    attributes, `agent_next_wake_at` and `agent_wake_reason` among them.
  - `docs/agent-adapter.md` §10 narrows the "one heartbeat per deployment"
    caveat. It still holds for `heartbeat::schedule`. A durable agent runs its
    own heartbeat.

  **Tests.** `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/agent_wakes.rs`:

  - 1,000 agents with distinct intervals tick on their own schedule.
  - A tick and a message never overlap, in either order.
  - An unattended tick cannot run a write tool without `allow_actions`.
  - A restart during a wait ticks and reports once.
  - A paused agent skips ticks and catches up once.
  - The follow-up chain cap holds across checkpoints.
  - The next wake is listed.

  Unit and property tests pin the wake kernel.

  ### Durable peers with exactly-once messages that carry mandates (issue #2269)

  - `Peer::agent(name, description, &id)` and `Peer::reply_timeout`. A
    `delegate` call to a durable peer sends `AgentOp::PeerMessage` with a
    `PeerEnvelope` and waits on a durable promise for a `PeerReply`.
  - The send is `signal_external_workflow_by_id_with_idempotency` with the key
    `<from>:<seq>`. A durable sender sends `from` as
    `<agent id>@<incarnation>`. `AgentState::outbound_seq` keeps one sequence
    for each receiver.
  - The receiver keeps an applied set of each sender
    (`agent::dedupe::Inbound`): a floor and a set above it. It never drops a
    number for being under a high-water mark.
  - The receiver runs under `Mandate::accept` of its local mandate and the
    inbound one, and starts with the labels of the sender. The reply carries
    its labels back.
  - Each envelope carries the waiting chain. `Refusal::Deadlock` refuses a send
    to an agent that waits. `Refusal::PeerUnavailable` refuses a send to an
    agent with no run.
  - `ReportSource::Peer`.

  **Tests.** `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/durable_peers.rs`:

  - A peer message arrives once across a restart, and gets its answer.
  - Each receiver counts its own seqs.
  - The receiver does not take a new life of a sender for a duplicate.
  - The receiver drops a duplicate and keeps a late message.
  - A mandate cannot widen in either direction.
  - The labels of the sender taint the receiver.
  - An A→B→A request ends as a deadlock, with no timer.
  - A send to an agent with no run gets `peer_unavailable`.
  - The sender does not wait for a reply after its deadline.

  Unit and property tests pin the applied set. A mutation of each guarantee
  turns its test red.

  ### Keyed-entity wakes: run an op at a deadline (issue #2266, engine part)

  Part of epic #2262. ADR 0006 records the
  amendment. An entity can now run a heartbeat or a follow-up with no
  scheduler outside it.

  **API.** `Entity::run_with_wakes(handler, wake)` and `entity::Wake { at, op }`,
  built with `Wake::new(at, op)`. The hook `wake(&state)` runs before each
  step. It returns a deadline and an op, or `None`.

  **Semantics.**

  - `None` gives the step of `Entity::run`: a waiting op, else a wait for the
    op signal.
  - A wake makes the loop read the clock once with `ctx.system_now()`. A due
    wake runs before any waiting op, so a backlog cannot starve it.
  - A wake that is not due lets a waiting op run first. With no waiting op,
    the loop races the op signal against the deadline with
    `wait_for_signal_timeout`. A signal that wins runs as usual. A timer that
    fires runs the wake op.
  - A wake op is typed, so it does not decode and adds no op bytes. The
    handler, the `Ok` and `Err` rules, the op count, the snapshot, the
    published view and the checkpoint check apply to it as to a decoded op.
    A delete keeps its rules.

  **Invariants.** No new `WorkflowEvent` variant and no migration.
  `Entity::run` is a thin call into the same loop with no hook. It reads no
  clock and starts no timer, so existing entity histories replay with no
  change. A step with a wake records one `SideEffectRecorded` event of kind
  `Now`. A wait also records a timer. The hook must be a pure function of the
  state. A failed wake op keeps the old state, so the same wake is due again
  at once. The timer counts whole seconds, so a wake can run up to one second
  late.

  **Tests.** `entity::tests`:

  - A wake fires with no op waiting.
  - A queued op runs before a wake that is not due.
  - A due wake runs before carried and signalled ops.
  - A hook that returns `None` starts no further timer.
  - `run` records the pinned event shape, with no clock read and no timer.
  - A hook that never wakes records the same events as `run`.
  - A checkpoint carries the state, and the next run computes its wake from
    it.
  - Each wake run replays clean.

  ### The agent cost ledger on SQLite (issue #2275)

  Section 13 of the design note `docs/design/DESIGN-2262.md` of epic #2262. The SQLite
  backend now writes the agent cost ledger of issue #1996. Before
  this change, the SQLite agent path called the model with no activity
  context, so it wrote no ledger rows.

  **Table.** The SQLite schema gains `harvest_llm_ledger`, with the columns
  and CHECK bounds of the Postgres table. The key is `(exec_id, event_seq,
  call_index)`. `event_seq` is the `seq` of the completion event, as
  `event_id` is on Postgres. `recorded_at` is the drive clock at the
  completion, in epoch milliseconds, with an index for window reads. The
  table is new, so `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` adds it to an older file on
  the next open. `harvest_events` does not change, and no `WorkflowEvent`
  variant is added, so replay does not change.

  **Writes.** The runtime writes one row per call in the transaction that
  appends `ActivityCompleted` or `LocalActivityCompleted`. A crash before that
  commit writes no row, and the re-run writes the rows of its own attempt
  once. A failed, timed-out or oversized attempt writes no row, as on
  Postgres. Two sources feed it:

  - `ActivityContext::record_llm_call` in an `#[activity]` body, on the
    worker path and the local path.
  - The new `SqliteRuntime::register_activity_with_ledger(&info, body)`. The
    closure returns `Ok((output, Vec<LlmCall>))`.

  **Reads.** `SqliteRuntime::llm_ledger(exec)` and
  `SqliteRuntime::llm_ledger_between(from, until)` return `LlmLedgerRow`
  values. `SqliteReader` has both reads, and a file from before this change
  reads as having no rows. Retention removes the rows with their run.
  `autumn_harvest_sqlite` re-exports `LlmCall`.

  **Agent adapter.** `sqlite::register` registers `agent_model_turn` with the
  ledger variant. One builder, `AgentHarness::ledger_call`, makes the call for
  both backends, so one script gives the same rows. A response cache hit
  records no row. The §9 limit "The cost ledger needs Postgres" is removed
  from `docs/agent-adapter.md`.

  **Tests.**

  - `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/sqlite_ledger.rs`:
    - One row per model call of a three-turn script.
    - The same rows as the Postgres activity for the same script.
    - No row for a cache hit or a tool call.
    - A crash inside a model call, and one inside a tool call. Each runs in a
      child process that aborts. The resume writes exactly one row per turn.
  - `autumn-harvest-sqlite/tests/integration/llm_ledger.rs`:
    - A ledger closure, an `#[activity]` body and a local activity.
    - A failed attempt and its retry, a timeout and a restart.
    - An older file, the reader, a window read and retention.
  - Unit tests in the SQLite `llm_ledger.rs` and `worker.rs`:
    - The CHECK bounds match the core limits.
    - The model id charset and the per-attempt cap.
    - A rolled-back or failed finalize writes no row.

  ### A model per agent and per peer (issue #2271)

  - `AgentHarness::model_named(name, model)` adds a model to a registry.
    `DEFAULT_MODEL` names the model of `AgentHarness::new`.
  - `AgentTask::model`, `Peer::model`, `AgentProfile::model`,
    `AgentHeartbeat::model` and `HeartbeatTask::model` name a model. A child
    with no model keeps the model of its parent.
  - `ModelTurnRequest::model` records the name in the turn input, so replay
    asks the same model. An unknown name fails the turn with no retry.
  - The response cache key and the cost ledger use the id of the model that
    answers the turn.
  - `Mandate::models` is an allowlist that only narrows. A delegation to a
    peer on another model is refused as `Refusal::ModelForbidden`. A root run
    on a forbidden model fails before any model call. A durable receiver
    checks its own model against the mandate that it accepts.
  - `eval::compare` runs two candidates on one recorded run.
    `Candidate::model` and `Candidate::agent_model` set the model of each.
  - The §9 limit "All agents share the harness model" is removed from
    `docs/agent-adapter.md`, and the matching §12 limit from
    `docs/agent-mesh.md`.

  **Tests.**

  - `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/model_per_agent.rs`:
    - A parent and a child on two models record both ids in the ledger.
    - A child keeps the model of its parent.
    - The cache never serves the answer of one model to another.
    - A mandate that forbids a model refuses the delegation.
    - A root on a forbidden model fails before any call.
    - An unknown model fails with no retry.
    - A profile and its heartbeat name their models.
  - `durable_peers.rs`: a receiver on a forbidden model refuses the message.
  - `eval.rs`: two models compared on one source, and one agent of a tree on
    another model.
  - Mandate property tests cover the allowlist.

  ### Concurrent children (issue #2270)

  - `AgentTask::parallel_children` and `AgentProfile::parallel_children` let
    one model turn run up to that many delegations at the same time, bounded
    by `MAX_PARALLEL_CHILDREN`.
  - Each child of a batch runs as a child `agent_loop` run. The parent joins
    the runs and merges their usage, steps, labels and records in call order.
  - The siblings split the token remainder and the delegation remainder with
    `bounds::sibling_cap`. Each child starts with the labels of the tree.
  - `AgentReport::run_id` names the run, so a parent records the run id of a
    child run.
  - `eval::evaluate` answers each child run of a source with its recorded
    report.
  - ADR 0013 records why a child is a child run: two joined branches that
    each take many steps can swap results on replay. The §12 limit "children
    never run at the same time" in `docs/agent-mesh.md` is narrowed.

  **Tests.**

  - `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/fan_out.rs`:
    - Three children run as child runs, with exact replay.
    - With no bound, the inline path stays.
    - The bound splits a batch.
    - The token split and the delegation split.
    - The labels of every sibling reach the parent.
    - A child starts with the labels of its parent.
    - A durable agent fans out.
    - A simulator sweep over completion orders.
  - `eval.rs`: a fan-out source evaluates from its recorded children.
  - The wall-time test runs on Postgres workers in the `examples/agent-mesh`
    suite.

  ### Verus proofs of the agent kernels (epic #2262)

  The blue-team step of `docs/design/DESIGN-2262.md` asks for Verus proofs of the pure
  kernels. Four new files in `formal/verus/src/` mirror them:

  - `agent_inbox.rs` proves `agent::inbox::admit`. A spec models the inbox
    under any sequence of ops. The ops that ran, then the held ops, are
    exactly the work ops received, in arrival order. An acknowledged op is
    never lost, and none runs twice (invariant I2).
  - `agent_dedupe.rs` proves `is_new` and `next_floor`. After any order of
    numbers, the floor and the set above it equal the plain applied set. So
    the receiver never drops a new message as a duplicate. The bound on the
    set makes no false duplicate either.
  - `agent_wake.rs` proves `next_heartbeat`. A tick books the next tick
    strictly after the time that it ran. Messages never move a booked tick.
  - `agent_siblings.rs` proves `sibling_cap`. The shares of all siblings sum
    to the remaining tokens, and each share is the base share or one more.

  `next_heartbeat` now saturates by hand, because Verus has no spec of
  `i64::saturating_add`. The result is the same for every input. The guard
  `verus_proofs_coverage.rs` now reads the doc comments of
  `autumn-harvest-agent/src` too.

  Each proof was checked by a mutation of its spec or its copy that Verus
  then rejects.

  ### Each model turn records only its new messages (issue #2264)

  - `ModelTurnRequest::prefix` names the window that a turn adds to.
    `ModelTurnRequest::remember` keeps the window of a turn for the next one.
  - `transcript::chain` is a chained SHA-256 digest over the messages. The
    workflow hashes each message once.
  - `TranscriptStore`, `InMemoryTranscriptStore` and
    `AgentHarness::transcript_store` hold the windows. On a miss, a turn fails
    with `TranscriptPrefixMissing` before any model call, and the workflow
    sends it again in the full form.
  - `AgentTask::transcript_delta` turns it on, and `AgentTask::new` sets it.
    A recorded task has no flag, and `agent_loop` asks the patch gate
    `agent.transcript-delta`, so an old run replays as it ran.
  - A durable agent keeps the last sent window in `AgentState::sent`, so a
    later op sends a delta too.
  - The §9 limit "The transcript rides in history" in `docs/agent-adapter.md`
    is revised.

  **Tests.** `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/transcript_delta.rs`:

  - A 50-turn run stores at least 80% less history (86% measured).
  - A full-form history replays.
  - A delta history replays strictly.
  - A cold store falls back to the full form.
  - The cache key is the same in both forms.
  - Eval gives the same result.
  - A durable agent sends deltas across ops.
  - A trimmed transcript goes in the full form.
  - The request cap measures the whole window.
  - The in-memory store has a byte bound.

  ### Mesh-wide controls (issue #2272)

  - `AgentProfile::mesh` and `AgentTask::mesh` name the mesh of an agent. Each
    model turn and peer message carries it, and each run publishes the search
    attribute `agent_mesh`.
  - `MeshBudget` caps the tokens or the cost of a mesh for each day, month or
    fixed window. `AgentHarness::mesh_budget` and `AgentHarness::mesh_spend`
    set it up. The model-turn activity refuses a turn of a spent mesh with
    `MeshBudgetExceeded` before the model call.
  - A refused durable agent parks (`AgentStatus::Parked`). Its work waits, the
    refused message first, its ticks are skipped, and a wake at the period
    end opens it.
  - `sqlite::LedgerSpend` sums the cost ledger of the runs of a mesh.
  - `sqlite::pause_mesh` interrupts and pauses every running agent of a mesh,
    and returns a `MeshPause` audit record.
  - A memory entry keeps the flow labels of the run that wrote it
    (`MemoryBlock::labels`). A run that reads the snapshot takes them. The
    snapshot activity records `MemorySnapshot`, which is plain text when it
    has no labels, so an old history still reads.
  - `MemoryStore::apply_labelled` refuses a write from a run with labels by
    default, so a store that cannot keep labels never holds an untainted
    copy. `InMemoryMemoryStore` keeps labels.
  - `Control::ClearTranscript` keeps only the labels of the memory.
  - The §12 limit "A memory note carries no label" in `docs/agent-mesh.md` is
    removed.

  **Tests.**

  - `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/mesh_controls.rs`:
    - A mesh over its daily budget parks the next turn of every agent.
    - A parked agent opens when the period ends.
    - Another mesh keeps its own budget.
    - A pause stops every agent of a mesh within one tick.
    - A pause stops an agent that waits for an approval.
    - A pause leaves other meshes alone.
    - A note written under untrusted input taints the run that reads it. This
      holds for a store and for state memory.
    - A store that cannot keep labels refuses a labelled write.
  - Unit tests in `mesh_control.rs` cover the period windows and the caps.

  ### Agent memory as entity state (issue #2273)

  - `AgentMemory::State` keeps the memory blocks in `AgentState::memory`. The
    workflow runs the `memory` tool itself, so an edit commits with the op
    snapshot. No store and no edit key are involved.
  - The system prompt of an op holds the memory as it was when the op
    started, so a provider prompt cache keeps its prefix.
  - The memory lives in the entity snapshot events and the
    `harvest_entity_state` projection, which erasure and codec rotation cover
    (issue #2259).

  **Tests.** `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/memory_state.rs`:

  - An edit commits with the op and shows in the next op.
  - Memory reads are stable within a segment.
  - The memory is in the entity snapshot.
  - `ResetMemory` clears it.
  - A crash in a child process after the memory call leaves memory and
    history consistent. The edit applies once.

  ### Live tokens from inside the model-call activity (issue #2268)

  - `ActivityContext::publish_progress` sends a live, best-effort chunk while
    an activity runs. Nothing is stored: no event and no
    `harvest_stream_chunks` row. Each chunk carries the activity, the attempt
    and its index in the attempt, so a reader drops the text of a failed
    attempt. `ActivityContext::with_progress_sink` and `CaptureProgressSink`
    serve tests and embedded runtimes.
  - On Postgres a background task sends each chunk with `pg_notify` on the
    progress channel of the run. A full queue of 256 drops a chunk, so a slow
    database never slows the activity.
  - `GET /workflows/{id}/stream` sends an activity chunk as an `activity`
    frame with no `id:`. `ProgressNotifyPayload::activity` marks it, so the
    `seq` contract of the workflow chunks stays as it was.
  - `DurableCall::live` adds the `activity` frames to a durable route stream.
    One route then gives both layers: live tokens, and the durable text that a
    resume gets once. `DurableStreamListener::connect_live` listens on both
    channels of a run with one connection.
  - Agent: `AgentModel::chat_stream`, `AgentTask::stream`,
    `AgentProfile::stream`, `AgentHarness::live_sink`, `LiveEvent` and
    `TurnText`. Small deltas join until 256 bytes wait, or until 50 ms pass
    and the provider sends its next event. The workflow
    publishes the text of each finished turn with `publish_durable_progress`.

  **Tests.**

  - `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/activity_progress_db_tests.rs`:
    - A live chunk arrives before the activity completes, and nothing stores
      it.
    - A retried attempt tags its chunks with the new attempt.
  - `durable_stream_tests.rs`: a live listener keeps the activity chunks in
    order, drops workflow chunks, and puts a stored wake first.
  - `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/durable_stream_integration.rs`: one stream
    gives the live chunks with no id and the stored text once.
  - The `durable_route::stream` unit tests prove that a live chunk costs no
    table read and never moves the cursor.
  - `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/live_tokens.rs`:
    - Tokens arrive before the turn completes.
    - A retry starts the live text again.
    - Live text never reaches history.
    - A reconnect gets the durable text of each turn once.

  ### Agent lifecycle: idle, list, pause and erase (issue #2267)

  - An idle agent is a row in the database. A fresh runtime serves its next
    message and its next wake.
  - `agent_mesh` joins the agent search attributes, and `parked` joins the
    statuses.
  - Migration `20261023202848_harvest_agent_wake_index` adds the partial
    expression index `idx_harvest_we_agent_wake` on
    `(search_attrs ->> 'agent_next_wake_at')::numeric`. A list of the agents
    due to wake reads only those agents.
  - The `filter` grammar of `GET /workflows` takes `workflow_id` (`=`, `!=`,
    `IN`), so a caller lists every run of one business id.
  - `EraseOutcome::ledger_rows_deleted`: an erasure deletes the agent cost
    ledger rows of the run (issue #1996). The spend of an erased run leaves
    the budget sums.
  - CLI: `harvest agents list | describe | pause | resume | erase`. `erase`
    resets the memory and the workspace of a running agent, then deletes it.
    It erases each run of each life and prints one report.

  **Tests.**

  - `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/agent_lifecycle.rs`:
    - An idle agent needs no runtime and wakes on a message.
    - It wakes on its timer in a fresh runtime.
  - `workflow_filter_integration.rs`: the agent wake list reads
    `idx_harvest_we_agent_wake` with a range condition (`EXPLAIN`).
  - `llm_ledger_tests.rs`: an erase deletes the ledger rows of the run.
  - `autumn-harvest-cli`:
    - The request mapping, the filter literal and the erase report.
    - `agents erase` against a scripted server.

  ### Persistent workspaces (issue #2274)

  - `autumn_harvest_agent::workspace`: `Workspace`, `WorkspaceRef`,
    `WorkspaceMount`, `WorkspaceStore`, `WorkspaceBlobs`,
    `InMemoryWorkspaceBlobs` and `DirWorkspaceBlobs`.
  - A snapshot is content-addressed by the SHA-256 digest of its plain bytes,
    encoded by the payload codecs, and kept outside history. History records
    only its reference.
  - `AgentProfile::workspace` and `AgentHarness::workspace` turn it on.
    `Tool::uses_workspace` and `FnTool::uses_workspace` opt a tool in.
    `ToolContext::workspace` holds the files of one call. `SandboxTool`
    mounts the files and keeps its outputs.
  - `ToolOutcome::workspace` carries the new head. Only a recorded result
    moves the head, so the snapshot of a stale attempt never becomes it.
  - The end of each op that moved the head keeps one snapshot. The activity
    `agent_workspace_retain` deletes the others of its generation or older.
    `Control::ResetWorkspace` and the activity `agent_workspace_reset` delete
    them all. `harvest agents erase` sends the reset.
  - Caps: 64 MiB of file content and 10,000 files for each snapshot by
    default.

  **Tests.**

  - `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/agent_workspace.rs`:
    - A file from turn 1 is visible in turn 5 after a restart.
    - A stale attempt never becomes the head, and the op end deletes its
      snapshot.
    - A reset removes every snapshot, an orphan included.
    - The store holds only ciphertext.
  - Unit tests in `workspace.rs` and `sandbox.rs` cover the digest check, the
    caps, the path rules, the directory store and the sandbox mount.

  ### The agent-mesh capstone (issue #2276)

  - `examples/agent-mesh` runs an always-on support desk with three durable
    agents in one SQLite file. The triage agent wakes on a heartbeat. It asks
    the researcher and the critic as durable peers, under mandates that only
    narrow. A write waits for a person. The mesh shares one daily budget.
  - `--model claude` runs the agents on `autoresearch::claude::ClaudeModel`,
    which streams over Server-Sent Events. The offline model needs no key.
  - `docs/comparison.md` §12 compares durable agents, with each competitor
    claim cited.

  **Tests.**

  - `tests/e2e.rs`:
    - A check reports the inbox and files nothing.
    - An answer asks each peer once, waits for approval across a restart and
      files once.
    - A rejected reply is never filed.
    - A spent budget parks the mesh until the next day.
  - `tests/simulation.rs`: a seeded sweep with restarts, reordered steps,
    duplicate ops, clock jumps and a reckless model. Four invariants hold on
    every seed, and each nemesis fires on some seed.
  - `tests/postgres.rs`:
    - Three children of one turn overlap on the wall clock.
    - One slot runs them one after another.
    - The live text of a turn reaches a progress listener while the turn
      runs.
    - A durable peer on another shard gets one message and answers once.
    - An erased agent keeps no memory, stream chunk or transcript text in
      any table.
  - CI runs the offline suites, the README demo and clippy. The Postgres
    suite runs from its manifest row.

  ### Review fixes (epic #2262)

  A review from five angles found these. Each fix has a test.

  - **Mandates.** A read-only inbound mandate makes a durable receiver
    read-only. A peer segment books no follow-up. A `memory` call in a segment
    that may not write memory gets an error, whatever the policy says.
  - **Read-only delegation.** A `delegate` call to a durable peer sends the
    read-only flag of the sending segment. A writable peer cannot write for a
    tick, a follow-up or a read-only agent. Eight tests cover the paths.
  - **Peer replies.** Only the segment of a message answers it. A failed
    segment sends an error and no text. A full held queue answers a waiting
    sender at once.
  - **Heartbeats.** `Control::SetHeartbeat` only narrows the profile:
    `AgentHeartbeat::narrowed` and `MIN_CUSTOM_HEARTBEAT_SECS`. A tick books
    the next tick from its own end, so a long tick never starves messages.
  - **Durability.** `Control::Resume` stops when an op parks the agent again,
    so a spent budget never loops. A steer that a failed or silent segment
    took runs later as its own op. A failed profile lookup keeps the run and
    its state. A fan-out child run gets the waiting chain of its parent, so a
    send back up the chain is a deadlock.
  - **Clock.** A SQLite ledger body gets the drive clock of its claim, and the
    mesh budget window uses it. `LedgerSpend` reads rows with no upper bound.
    On SQLite, a live `system_now` returns the clock of its decision cycle,
    through `WorkflowExecuteSpanMeta::drive_clock`. An `_as_of` drive then
    keeps one clock, so a parked agent never wakes at once and parks again.
  - **Workspace.** A read-only run never moves the head. The state keeps the
    flow labels of the run that last moved it, and `ClearTranscript` keeps
    them. A store failure runs a workspace call again from the same head, up
    to three times. `DirWorkspaceBlobs` writes files that only the owner
    reads. A store with no keyed codec logs a warning.
  - **Transcript store.** A read checks the digest of the window, so a
    changed window is a miss.
  - **Erase.** `harvest agents erase` reads the `execution` object of the
    by-id answer. It pauses the agent first. It restarts an agent that ended,
    so its memory and workspace reset too. `stores_reset` reflects the final
    state, and `stores_error` names a failed reset.
  - **Live tokens.** The Postgres progress sink sends every chunk that waits
    in one `pg_notify` statement, so a burst of tokens costs one transaction.
    The sink gives its pool connection back when its queue is empty. When it
    cannot get a connection, every chunk that waits drops.
    `GET /workflows/{id}/stream` resolves the shard of a run at most once per
    keepalive. The Claude adapter decodes complete lines only, so a character
    or a `\r\n` pair split across network chunks stays whole. Upgrade every
    API server before a worker sends activity chunks: an older server sends
    an activity chunk as a `progress` frame.
  - **Capstone.** The offline desk model reads only the current op. A note
    search puts the best match first. A reply waits one day of desk clock for
    approval: `MeshConfig::approval_timeout`. The simulation checks the spend
    of each day apart, checks that triage applies each op key once, and
    asserts that each nemesis fires. A CI guard checks that each agent-mesh
    test target has a runner. A Postgres worker of the agents also polls the
    `default` queue, where the agent activities go.
  - **PR review.** A follow-up delay counts from the end of its segment, so a
    long segment never books a follow-up that is already due. Each
    `DirWorkspaceBlobs` put writes its own scratch file. Two attempts that
    save one digest at once then never mix their bytes.
  - **Workspace generations.** A late attempt of a retention could delete a
    newer head, because a key was the content digest only. The key now holds
    the generation of its segment, and `WorkspaceRef::generation` records it.
    Retention deletes only keys of the head generation or older, and a reset
    only keys below its own generation, plus keys in another form. A reset
    leaves an empty marker at its generation. The first generation of a life
    is above every key and marker in the scope: the new activity
    `agent_workspace_floor` reads it. A worker clock that reads low then
    cannot put a new life below an old one. The model
    `formal/tla/AgentWorkspaceRetention.tla` (lives, a clock floor and a
    missing marker as counterexamples) and the tests
    `a_stale_retain_never_deletes_a_newer_head`,
    `a_newer_head_with_old_content_survives_a_stale_retain`,
    `a_stale_reset_never_deletes_a_later_head`,
    `a_reset_marker_keeps_the_floor_of_an_empty_scope`,
    `a_late_retention_of_an_old_op_keeps_the_newest_head` and
    `a_reset_in_a_new_life_deletes_the_keys_of_an_old_life_on_a_fast_clock`
    cover it. A scratch name of `DirWorkspaceBlobs` holds a random UUID, so
    two hosts that share the folder never share one.
  - **Sandbox deletions.** A workspace file that a sandbox run deletes now
    leaves the workspace. Before, the old content came back on the next call.
    `SkippedOutput::is_absent` reads the skip reason. The constants
    `MISSING_OUTPUT_REASON` and `NOT_A_DIRECTORY_REASON` fix its text. A file
    over a size limit keeps its old content. The test
    `a_run_that_deletes_a_file_removes_it_and_a_skipped_large_file_stays`
    covers it.
  - **Eval fan-out.** `eval::evaluate` answers a child run of a fan-out with
    the recorded child that has the same delegation chain and task text.
    Before, it served the recorded results by start order, so a reordered or
    changed fan-out read the answer of another peer. A child with no match
    fails the candidate with `eval::NO_CHILD_RUN`. The tests
    `a_reordered_fan_out_answers_each_child_from_its_own_recorded_run` and
    `a_fan_out_child_with_no_recorded_run_fails_the_candidate` cover it.
  - **Budget refusal.** A mesh budget that refused the first turn of an op
    still kept its input in the transcript. A requeued message then reached
    the model twice, and each `Control::Resume` in the spent period added a
    copy. A refused first turn now keeps the transcript as it was, and a steer
    that it took runs later as its own op. The test
    `a_refused_message_leaves_the_transcript_as_it_was` covers it.
  - **Scratch files (issue #2315).** A `DirWorkspaceBlobs` put that stopped
    before its rename left a `.tmp-<uuid>` file that no operation could
    find, so `harvest agents erase` reported success over it. The store now
    lists scratch names, and retention and a reset delete one by the
    generation of its key. `erase` and the floor count them too. A reset
    puts its marker first, and a save above generation 0 that finds a later
    marker deletes its own key. `docs/agent-adapter.md` names the two
    windows that stay. Seven tests cover it, among them
    `a_reset_deletes_scratch_files_below_its_bound_and_keeps_a_newer_one`
    and `a_reset_on_the_dir_store_leaves_no_bytes_of_a_dropped_save`.

  ### Advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0387 (crypto-bigint 0.5.5)

  The advisory appeared during this PR and fails `cargo deny` on `trunk-dev`
  too. crypto-bigint 0.5.5 comes in through elliptic-curve 0.13, p256 and
  p384, which autumn-web 0.8.0 and jsonwebtoken 11.1.0 pin. Each crate of the
  chain is at its last release, so no bump is possible. `deny.toml` ignores
  the advisory with a verdict of "undetermined from this repo". Code in this
  workspace runs no P-256 or P-384 secret-key operation. The Web Push module
  of autumn-web does, when a host app turns it on. The entry names the revisit
  triggers.
- **Phase** (implemented): durable stream append skips the stored-row count — see issue #2083. `store::append_stream_chunks` counted every stored chunk of a run on each append. It now reads the lowest and highest real offset in one statement and skips the count while that span plus the new chunks fits the cap. Over the full lifetime of 1,000 heavy-tailed streams, the count statement drops from 45,438 calls and 4,332,498 buffers to 20 calls and 7,228 buffers, and total buffers fall 35.5%. The stored table is byte-identical (same md5). No migration, no event and no schema change. See `docs/performance-stream-append-count.md`.
- **Onramp** (implemented): chapter 9 snippets guarded in CI. Docs tooling only. `scripts/check-worker-routing-examples.sh` extracts the four Rust snippets of chapter 9 (activity `requires`, label map, `with_label`, `with_queue_weights`) and compiles them in CI's lint job. It also runs the example and passes the `requires` string to `eligibility::parse_requirements`, because the macro does not parse it. Baseline: 4 snippets, 0 errors, 18.2 min cold. The guard finds no defect today. It keeps the chapter from drifting from the routing API. No public API change.
- **Phase 2262.2320** (implemented): Failed agent children keep their reports — see issue #2320. A failed child of a fan-out no longer drops the reports of its later siblings. `fan_out` merges every successful report, then fails the batch with the first error in input order. The error text does not change.

  An inline `delegate` that fails now adds the usage of the child to the parent.
  A durable agent therefore keeps the tokens and the flow labels of a failed op,
  as `fold_segment` promises.

  The fix issues no command and adds no patch gate. It changes only the
  in-memory usage and labels of the parent.

  Tests: `fan_out.rs` (fan-out, inline, two failures) and `durable_peers.rs`
  (peer segment).

  Known limit: the failed slot itself still loses its usage. Issue #2328 tracks it.
- **Docs** (implemented): depth walk profile, negative result — see issue #2312. `payload_depth::nests_past_cap` runs on every successful activity result. A callgrind profile shows it at 10.6% of a harness that only clones and checks values. The one idea that the profile suggests saves at most 18.5% of the walk. No profile of a real completion exists, so the production impact is undetermined. No code changes.

  The profile harness is now in the tree as `benches/payload_depth_profile.rs`.
  `docs/performance-payload-depth.md` holds the numbers and the reproduce steps,
  so nobody repeats the profile.

  No migration, no route change, and no `harvest_events` change.
- **Fix** (implemented): det-check rejects a blank suppression reason — see issue #2314. `harvest det-check` accepted `// harvest-suppress: DET003 "   "`. The parser tested `reason.is_empty()`. It now tests `reason.trim().is_empty()`. A blank reason no longer suppresses a finding or appears in `--list-suppressions`. This matches `GuardrailSuppression::new`. No migration. No `WorkflowEvent` change.

  Tests: `parse_suppression_comment_rejects_a_whitespace_only_reason` and `parse_suppression_comment_keeps_a_padded_reason` in `det_check.rs`. `suppression_rejects_a_whitespace_only_reason` in `tests/integration/det_check_tests.rs` covers the same-line and previous-line forms. `blank_reason_suppression_is_not_listed_and_still_gates` in `det_check_cli.rs` covers the CLI gate and the suppression listing.
- **Feature** (implemented): Owner-local SQLite projection for SQL over entity state — see issue #2260. Stage 3b of epic #2247. A decision owner can keep the last state snapshot of each live entity in its disk cache file. User code then runs read-only SQL over the state of one entity with `Worker::query_entity_sql`. See `docs/adr/0012-owner-disk-cache.md` and the `entity_sql` module docs.

  - **Opt-in.** Build with the `owner-disk-cache` feature. Set
    `WorkerConfig::with_owner_disk_cache(dir)` and
    `WorkerConfig::with_owner_entity_sql(true)`. The projection acts only in
    owner mode, on the partitions that the worker owns. The switch with no
    directory fails the worker start.
  - **A projection, never a source of truth.** After each committed
    suspension, the owner reads the committed `harvest_entity_state` row of
    the run, one indexed read. It seals a newer snapshot into the
    `harvest_entity_projection` table of the partition file. A query reads
    that row only when the run and the event id match the Postgres row
    `harvest_entity_state`. Otherwise it reads the snapshot event from
    history, and an owner writes the row again.
  - **The disk cache rules apply.** The row lives in the stage 2 partition
    file. So the memory-only node key, the wipe at start and at a tenure
    end, the validity stamp, the purges and the reconcile pass all apply. A
    file that left the directory reads as stale, and the next store makes a
    new file.
  - **Read-only SQL.** Each query gets a fresh in-memory SQLite database with
    one table, `entity`. An authorizer allows reads and functions only.
    `ATTACH`, `VACUUM INTO`, pragmas and writes are refused, so no plaintext
    reaches the disk. A query stops after 50 million steps, after 5 s, or
    when SQLite memory grows by 64 MiB. A result stops past 10,000 rows or
    16 MiB. At most four queries run at a time, and a dropped caller stops
    its query. A blob comes back as a hex string. Parameters bind to `?1`,
    `?2` and so on.
  - **Any worker can query.** A worker that holds no tenure for the entity
    reads history and writes no file.

  **Tests.** `deleting_the_file_mid_run_rebuilds_from_history` is the red
  test of the issue. `an_erased_entity_leaves_no_local_bytes`,
  `an_erasure_purges_an_entity_that_a_missed_purge_left` and
  `a_rotated_codec_key_leaves_no_entity_ciphertext_on_disk` run the stage 2
  erasure and key-rotation tests on the projection. The stage 2 reconcile,
  foreign-terminal, lost-tenure and shutdown tests have projection twins.
  `a_killed_owner_leaves_no_readable_bytes` and
  `a_retired_codec_key_leaves_no_ciphertext` now store an entity row too.
  The `entity_sql` module tests cover the read-only rules and the limits.

  No migration. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. Off by default.
- **Engine** (implemented): Owner decider takes workflow tasks in claim order — see issue #2308. The owner decider of issue #2255 took workflow tasks in wake order and by `scheduled_at`. Under saturation, an older low-priority backlog could take every workflow permit before a newer high-priority task. A new start also competed equally with continuations.

  The decider now sorts its ready set by priority, then by the due time with
  the 30 s new-start handicap of issue #1824. A scan returns the first rows of
  that order. A wake reads its row's key with one statement, only when the free
  permits cannot cover every hint.

  **Migration.** `20261024184859_harvest_owner_decider_order` adds the partial
  index `idx_harvest_tq_owner_order` on `harvest_task_queue (decision_partition,
  (new_start AND attempt = 0), priority DESC, scheduled_at) WHERE state =
  'PENDING' AND task_type = 'workflow'`. The build is guarded, so an operator
  can build it `CONCURRENTLY` first. No `WorkflowEvent` variant, no replay
  impact.

  **Behavior change.** A worker with `priority_aging_secs` runs no decider. It
  keeps the owned claim of issue #2252, which applies the ageing boost. Owner
  mode is off by default.
- **Phase X.Y** (implemented): A failed fan-out child reports its usage — see issue #2328. A failed `agent_loop` run returned only an error string. A parent lost the usage and the flow labels of that run, and of its whole subtree.

  - `AgentTask::report_failure` makes a failed run end with a report. The report
    has `AgentStop::Failed` and `AgentReport::error`. It keeps the usage, steps,
    tool calls, delegations and flow labels of the run.
  - `fan_out` sets the flag on its children. It merges a failed report like any
    other, then fails the batch with the first error in input order. A nested
    failure keeps the usage of the whole subtree.
  - Top-level `agent_loop` callers still get `Err`.
  - Patch gate: `agent_child_failure_report`. The flag is part of the recorded
    child input, so a history from before the gate replays unchanged. The parent
    control flow does not change, so no further gate is needed.
  - Tests: `a_failed_fan_out_slot_keeps_its_own_usage` and
    `a_nested_failure_keeps_the_usage_of_the_whole_subtree` in
    `autumn-harvest-agent/tests/fan_out.rs`. Both failed before the fix.
- **Perf** (implemented): fan-out replay of `match_activity` is no longer quadratic — see issue #2330. `HistoryMatcher::scan_activity_terminal` walked from each schedule to its terminal. In a fan-out of N activities, each walk stepped over the later schedules and the consumed completions, so a replay cost O(N²). The settle then walked the same range again.

  A scan in a wide fan-out now reads a position index
  (`activity_scan_index.rs`). The index lists the stops and progress events of
  each activity, the interleaved commands and the barriers. Skip links pass
  over consumed entries. A scan leaves its walk only after an interleaved
  command, and only once the walks cost more than an index build. So a
  sequential history and a small fan-out build no index.

  At N=1000 the `fanout` bench costs 72% fewer instructions, and at N=2000 84%
  fewer. A sequential history costs 0.7% more. A fan-out of about 32 costs 52%
  more matcher instructions, about 45K. See
  `docs/performance-match-activity-fanout.md`. Issue #2338 tracks two other
  quadratic matcher paths.

  Replay semantics do not change. A differential property test compares the
  new scan with a copy of the old one over random histories, matcher calls and
